Having wrapped up her earlier adaptation, she had stopped recycling pre-transmigration novels and launched an original tale inspired by her own tangled path and the sight of Ye Anya and Cao Ban tying red silk beneath the Divine Willow—a story of star-crossed lovers fighting to break free of loveless marriages and claim their own happiness.
Three or four pages in, Matron Wei walked through the door.
Qianli Xun set down her brush and rose to greet her. "Same courtyard, yet I haven't seen you for days, Matron! Missed you."
Matron Wei glanced at the desk with a teasing smile. "Not having Kuqiao hide your drafts today?"
Pulling her into a chair, Qianli Xun laughed. "You knew all along and never told me, making me put on an act for nothing!"
Wondering how to break the news, Matron Wei let a heavy silence hang until her mistress noticed.
"Why so quiet, Matron?"
"There is something I weighed back and forth, Miss, and decided you must hear."
"What is it?" Qianli Xun leaned forward, intrigued.
"About last year's rumors."
"Those? Ancient history. Don't tell me people are gossiping again?"
"The person who spread them has come to light."
Before Qianli Xun could speak, Kuqiao bristled. "You know who it was, Matron? Tell us right now—I'll march over and curse him till his ears bleed!"
"Who was it, Matron? And how did you find out?" Qianli Xun pressed.
Matron Wei kept her gaze steady. "How I found out doesn't matter. What matters is what you plan to do once I name him."
"Need you ask?" Qianli Xun declared. "That bastard ruined my life! Two words: pay him back!"
"Yes! Revenge!" Kuqiao cheered.
"Out with it, Matron! Who is it?"
Hardening her resolve, Matron Wei spoke two words: "The groom."
Qianli Xun stared. "Chen Haoyu?"
Matron Wei nodded.
Kuqiao went dead silent as shock turned to fury on her mistress's face. Qianli Xun's fingers clamped onto the wooden armrest—CRACK! The carved arm snapped clean off in her grip.
Oh boy, Kuqiao thought. Young Master is dead meat!
Qianli Xun shot to her feet, paced two steps, and spun around. "If you know, Matron, with my father's reach he must have known long ago! He knew, and he still shoved me into this marriage blind! I'm marching back to Zhu Manor right now to have it out with him!"
Matron Wei stood and barred her way. "What's done is done, Miss. Raising a storm at Zhu Manor fixes nothing. Think about how to deal with the groom right here."
That snapped Qianli Xun's head clear. Making a scene at Zhu Manor would change zero. "Fine, my father gets a pass for now. Anyone else can walk, except Chen Haoyu! I'm settling the score for every slur this whole city threw at me! Kuqiao!"
"Here!"
"Go fetch Hongdou!"
Moments later Hongdou rushed in.
"Send men through every brothel and gambling den in Lin'an to track down Chen Haoyu," Qianli Xun snapped. "Report back the second you spot him. I'm going myself to thrash him black and blue and drag him home in ropes!"
"No need to search, Miss," Hongdou answered. "I already know where he is."
"Chunxiang Brothel?"
Hongdou nodded.
"Gather our people—we're hitting Chunxiang Brothel right now!"
Without another word, Qianli Xun stormed out of Suxin Thatched Hall.
Matron Wei sighed. "Well, here comes the fireworks."
"Matron," Kuqiao blinked, "why do you sound like you're looking forward to the show?"
"Nonsense! Gather those manuscript pages before anyone sees them, and swap out that broken chair."
Kuqiao caught Matron Wei's sleeve as she turned to go. "Matron, I'm terrified—Miss already went through one mutual divorce. Is she headed for a second?"
"Can't you wish your mistress well instead of waving 'divorce' around every five minutes?" Matron Wei chided. "This groom is a mess, sure, yet this second marriage is worlds apart from the first—because the Chen family is nothing like the Lins. Sit tight and watch."
Left alone, Kuqiao muttered to herself, "Matron Wei always talks in riddles, though if she isn't worried, Miss must be fine. Right—the groom's at fault, and Miss will tan his hide raw!" She set to stowing the drafts and fetching a new chair.
Marching toward the main gate with ten servants—three maids and seven men—Qianli Xun drew gawking whispers all along the paths.
Near the front gate, Chen Haodong strolled in from outside. One glance at her war party told him his trick had worked. Putting on an innocent smile, he stepped up. "Heading somewhere, Younger Sister-in-law? Quite the escort."
Hiding nothing, Qianli Xun snapped, "Going to fetch Chen Haoyu."
"Why go yourself when servants can handle it?" he baited her.
A sudden thought halted Qianli Xun: did the rest of the Chen family know about Haoyu's rumors while leaving only her in the dark? "Eldest Cousin, did you know Chen Haoyu spread those rumors about me last year?"
Right on target. Hiding his glee, Chen Haodong poured oil on the fire. "Since you already found out, no point hiding it—yes, everyone in Chen Manor knew. That's the exact reason our family overlooked your divorce and bad reputation. A man has to own his mistakes. Besides, last year Prefect Zhu marched in here waving a horsewhip, dragging Haoyu tied up like a hog, and forced Eldest Uncle and Aunt to seal the betrothal. They had no choice."
Whatever his motive, he had laid the whole timeline bare: Zhu Xiyan had known all along and dumped his "damaged" daughter fast to protect Zhu face without a single thought for her happiness.
Too furious even to answer Chen Haodong, Qianli Xun marched straight out the gate.
Chen Haodong called after her with glee, "He's at Chunxiang Brothel, Sister-in-law! Don't look in the wrong place!"
Mission accomplished, he sauntered back to his courtyard to enjoy the show.
#CH 224
#TITLE: Hog-Tied and Locked Up
Blinded by rage and caring nothing for gentlewoman decorum, Qianli Xun hopped down from the carriage and marched straight into Chunxiang Brothel with ten servants at her heels. Seeing their mistress unfazed, Hongdou and the other two maids dropped their own shyness and marched right in too.
Inside, the brothel hummed as usual—patrons watching dancers, clinking wine cups, flirting with courtesans. Every jaw hit the floor at the sight of a respectable lady striding through the doors with three maids and seven tough manservants.
Recognizing her at once, the madam muttered under her breath, "Mother of mercy—Young Master Chen's tigress tracked him all the way here!" She plastered on a smile and hurried up. "Looking for Young Master Chen, Young Madam?"
"Where is he?" Qianli Xun's face promised bruises by the dozen.
"Upstairs, with Chun Jinmo."
"Lead the way." Her voice ran ice-cold beneath the fire.
Hoping to give her regular a heads-up, the madam glanced up at the balcony where Scarface leaned and hollered, "Master Scar! Tell Young Master Chen his wife is here!"
Having already spotted them, Scarface bolted inside to warn him.
"Right this way, Young Madam," the madam said.
Before Qianli Xun reached the stairs, Chen Haoyu's voice barked from above: "Zhu Shuzhen! What are you doing in here? Go home right now!"
Looking up, Qianli Xun saw him clattering down the steps while tugging his robe straight—fresh from obvious filth—with his three hired bodyguards trailing behind.
Last year's slander boiled over at the sight of his smug, punchable face. Kicking off with her light-foot skill, Qianli Xun vaulted straight up the staircase, seized him by the collar, dropped back to the floor, and threw him flat on his back.
Humiliated before a packed hall, Chen Haoyu blustered from the boards, "Act tough all you want! I won't stoop to fighting you in public—wait till I get home and teach you a lesson!"
Having already tasted her seven servants' fists—and seeing her vault ten feet through the air—the three bodyguards traded one glance and bailed. They stepped briskly over to Chen Haoyu. "Family business, Young Master Chen—none of our affair. See you another day." They bolted out the door.
Left stranded, Chen Haoyu scrambled to his feet just as Qianli Xun barked, "Tie him up!"
Asheng whipped out rope, and with two other men trussed Chen Haoyu tight in three seconds flat.
"Zhu Shuzhen, you've lost your mind!" Chen Haoyu roared. "I'm your husband! Bullying your own husband in public—you'll make us a laughingstock!"
True enough, half the hall grinned over their cups.
Having zero desire to linger, Qianli Xun snapped, "Haul him out!"
Just as she turned, a soft female voice called from behind: "Please wait, Young Madam!"
Qianli Xun turned back. Down the stairs floated a slender beauty who swayed like a willow wand in the wind—Chun Jinmo, no doubt.
Stopping before her, Chun Jinmo dropped a deep curtsy. "Greetings, Young Madam."
"What do you want?"
"I have read your poems, Young Madam—gentle, poignant, full of tender longing. Meeting you in person today, you look nothing like your verse."
"Not in the mood for literary criticism. Goodbye." Qianli Xun turned again.
Chun Jinmo darted ahead to block her. "Please wait, Young Madam—I didn't stop you to talk poetry. I heard you and Young Master Chen signed a prenuptial contract not to interfere with each other. Why barge in today and treat your husband like a criminal?"
That Chen Haoyu had blabbed their private pact to a brothel girl pushed Qianli Xun past boiling. "Who the hell do you think you are, sticking your nose in my business? What contract? Never heard of it! Quit wasting my breath!"
As she turned a third time, Chun Jinmo ignored every stare in the hall and dropped to her knees before her.
"I didn't lay a finger on you—what are you kneeling for?"
"Young Madam, ever since I was sold to Chunxiang Brothel, Young Master Chen has been my only man, shielding me every day. If he stops coming, my life here will turn to misery. Have mercy and let him go—Jinmo will be in your debt forever!"
Seeing her kneel melted Chen Haoyu into a puddle of chivalry. "Look how pitiful she is, Zhu Shuzhen! You hate my guts—you're happier without me, and the Chen family has plenty of other sons, yet Jinmo can't survive without me! I mean the world to her. Untie me right now and quit making a scene!"
With her grudge burning white-hot, Qianli Xun stepped close to him. "Listen close: from today on, the more you want something, the harder I'll block it. Want to look after her? Then I'll make sure you never lay eyes on her again!"
Turning back to Chun Jinmo, she added, "Sure, you have it rough, and I'm not made of stone—yet I have no heart left to spare for you today. Did you ever wonder when I was the one needing pity? Where were you when the whole city tore me apart? What was Chen Haoyu doing back then? I'm no saint and no savior. Kneeling to me won't buy you a thing."
With that, she led her crew out of Chunxiang Brothel.
At the doors, Chen Haoyu craned his neck back to shout, "Hang in there! I'll be back soon!"
Sitting on the floor in tears, Chun Jinmo despaired—with a wife that fierce, holding onto Chen Haoyu was hopeless. Would she really have to serve thugs like Master Jiang?
The brothel madam hurried over and pulled her up. "Jinmo, girl, you're a courtesan—face facts. Any patron who calls your name and pays silver gets served, unless you luck out like Jinqiao and land a rich man to buy your freedom as a concubine. I heard you hinted at redemption to Young Master Chen plenty of times, and he never gave you a straight answer—he just comes here to play! With a wife like that, forget redemption. Find another patron who'll actually buy you out. Master Jiang isn't half bad—older and rough-looking, sure, yet he's dead serious about you! Look how many brawls he fought over you—and word is he doesn't even have a primary wife yet. Think of the chance waiting there!"
Chun Jinmo let those words sink in as she wiped her tears and walked back upstairs.
Back in Moxiang Courtyard, Qianli Xun sat behind her desk staring at Chen Haoyu, trussed in a chair before her.
Chen Haoyu kept up his cheeky swagger. "What're you staring at? Never seen a handsome man? Don't tell me you missed me while I was gone?"
"Hongdou!" Qianli Xun barked. "Slap him twice for me!"
"Zhu Shuzhen, did you eat bad mushrooms?" Chen Haoyu snapped.
Hongdou froze. "Miss, I dare not—he's the young master."
"Lay a hand on me and I'll sell you straight to Chunxiang Brothel!" Chen Haoyu threatened.
Hongdou shrank back.
"What is your game today, Zhu Shuzhen?" Chen Haoyu demanded. "We signed a prenuptial contract—hands off each other! Did a dog eat your precious contract spirit?"
Qianli Xun picked a sheet off her desk. "Here's your contract. Take a good look." Opening the bronze incense burner beside her, she rolled the sheet up and dropped it onto the glowing coals. Flames licked up and reduced the paper to ash in seconds.
Chen Haoyu's jaw dropped. Only when she clapped the lid back on did he find his voice. "You burned it! That makes the whole thing void! Hand back my properties, put my courtyard and rooms back the way they were, and get out to the back courtyard—I'm moving back in here!"
"You really are hilarious, Chen Haoyu. Think I burned that paper planning to hand your silver and rooms back? Dream on!"
"Aren't you scared I'll tell Grandmother and my parents so they haul you over the coals?"
"You'd have to make it out of this courtyard first!"
Sensing something far deeper than a passing spat—she had never bothered him before—Chen Haoyu damped down his bluster. "Did you swallow gunpowder today? Since we wed I haven't done a thing to cross you. Why come at me like this?"
That lit the fuse. "Haven't done a thing? Forgotten your filthy handiwork already?"
A chill ran down Chen Haoyu's spine. Burning the contract, raging like a storm—had she found out about the rumors? "Wait... did you hear something?"
Qianli Xun shot up, fists clenched, stalking toward him. "Last year you spread slander across Lin'an, wrecked my betrothal, and turned me into the city's laughingstock! Today we're settling that tab!"
Terror iced his veins—she knew! Seeing her fist whistle straight at him, he squeezed his eyes shut. CRACK! He hit the floor in a heap of splinters—she had smashed the chair right out from under him.
Exhaling in relief, he cracked his eyes open and scrambled for excuses. "You started it by bullying me nonstop! If you hadn't pushed me around, I never would've spread those rumors! Besides, people didn't just gossip because of me—you wrote 'falling asleep in his arms, fully dressed' yourself..."
"Hongdou! Slap him right now!" Qianli Xun thundered.
Ordered a second time, Hongdou dropped all hesitation and stepped up. "Young Master, even if you sell me to a brothel, I'm hitting you for Miss!"
SMACK! SMACK! Two ringing slaps landed square across Chen Haoyu's cheeks.
Watching from the side, Kuqiao felt both fierce satisfaction for her mistress and a wince for the stinging red prints blooming on his face.
Hands tied behind his back, unable to rub his throbbing cheeks, Chen Haoyu hissed, "You little wench! Why swing so hard?"
Qianli Xun crouched down and tapped his reddened cheek. "I meant to beat you senseless and downgraded it to two slaps—that's mercy! Still complaining?"
"Zhu Shuzhen! I'm divorcing you! I'll write you a letter of repudiation!"
"Divorce me? Not a chance. From here on out, I have two goals in Chen Manor: live well, and make your life hell."
Fear crept into his eyes. "W-what are you planning to do to me?"
Qianli Xun spoke slow, biting off every syllable. "Everything you love doing, I will forbid. Everything you hate doing, I will force down your throat."
"You—you—" Chen Haoyu choked, speechless.
Qianli Xun rose. "Guards! Haul him back to Boya Study and lock him in!"
Asheng and another servant hoisted him up, marched him to Boya Study in the back courtyard, and cut his ropes. The instant his arms came free, Chen Haoyu lunged to hit Asheng and bolt—only for Asheng to block the doorway. "Behave, Young Master. Crossing Miss won't end well."
Outside, wooden shutters slammed shut, followed by the bang of hammers nailing boards over every window.
"Stop that right now!" Chen Haoyu roared at the panes. "I own this courtyard!"
Then the door pulled shut behind Asheng and a heavy padlock clicked home.
"Zhu Shuzhen! We aren't done!" Chen Haoyu yelled at the wood. "Just you wait! This is Chen Manor, not Zhu Manor—and not your Wangyue Pavilion!"
A whisper floated through the boarded window. "Young Master? Young Master, are you alright?"
For the first time in his life, Qinggua's voice sounded like heavenly music. Chen Haoyu pressed his face to the crack. "Qinggua! Thank goodness! That tigress is torturing me! Run tell Old Madam Xia, Father, and Mother right now—tell them I'm repudiating her! Go!"
"On my way, Young Master!"
Qinggua scampered into the front yard—only to freeze short of the pond as Qianli Xun's voice sliced across the grass. "Qinggua! Running off to tattle for your master?"
"N-no, Young Madam!" Qinggua stammered. "I just wanted a bigger yard to practice Phantom Sidestep!"
"You've drilled it enough. Worried you have nowhere to sleep tonight, so from now on you're staying in Boya Study with Chen Haoyu." To stop him from running his mouth, locking both up was the only fix.
"Young Madam, he's the one who messed up—don't drag me in! The West Courtyard is fine by me!"
"Your master gets lonely in there. Keep him company." She nabbed Qinggua by the scruff and marched him to the back courtyard.
Hearing the padlock click open, Chen Haoyu lit up—sure Grandmother had stormed over to free him. Instead, Qinggua flew headfirst through the gap and the door slammed shut once more.
Qianli Xun's voice drifted through the planks. "Didn't want you lonely, Chen Haoyu—sent you a cellmate."
Chen Haoyu threw himself at the door, pounding with both fists. "Zhu Shuzhen! The second I get out of here, I'm divorcing you!"
#CH 225
#TITLE: Matron Wei Soothes Worried Hearts
After pounding the door and shouting himself hoarse to zero effect, Chen Haoyu spun around looking for a punching bag—and locked onto Qinggua standing there with an innocent blink.
"I sent you to fetch Grandmother, Father, and Mother! How did you wind up locked in here too?"
"Don't blame me, Young Master! Young Madam is sharp as a hawk—spotted me before I cleared the front yard and tossed me right in."
"Idiot! Couldn't you make up an excuse?"
"I tried! She didn't buy it and said to keep you company." Qinggua stepped closer. "Honestly, Young Master, why not play nice from now on? When Young Madam says east, don't go west. Fighting her only gets you hammered—and drags me down with you..."
Already fuming, Chen Haoyu swung a full-power kick straight at him. "Daring to talk down to me now? I'll kick the hide off you!"
Qinggua glided sideways in a neat arc. Chen Haoyu's foot hit air, almost pitching him onto his nose. Another kick—missed! Three, four more—every one whiffed past Qinggua like smoke.
Fed up with kicking, Chen Haoyu lunged in with a grappling hold and twisted Qinggua's wrist. "Dodge that! Where'd you learn that footwork?"
"Mercy, Young Master, mercy! Young Madam taught me Phantom Sidestep!"
"Zhu Shuzhen again!" Letting go, Chen Haoyu planted a parting boot squarely on Qinggua's backside before he could turn. "Take that!"
Qinggua stumbled forward onto the floorboards unhurt, sitting up with a sigh. "Quit picking on me, Young Master. Beating me black and blue won't get you out this door. Shouldn't we figure out how to escape?"
Knowing Qinggua wasn't to blame, Chen Haoyu dropped into a cushioned chair and switched gears. If he got word to his parents and grandmother, family pressure would force Zhu Shuzhen to unlock the door. "Which of the courtyard servants are you tightest with?"
Qinggua puffed up. "All of them! While you were gone, I drilled with them in the West Courtyard every day—just Phantom Sidestep, since Young Madam says I lack aptitude for real boxing. Hanging out daily made us pals. You know what, Young Master? I—I think I fell for Hongdou, and she might like me too..." A blush crept up his neck.
Chen Haoyu snorted. "Hongdou falling for a mug like yours? Quit dreaming! Focus—which of those ten servants will sneak a message out for us?"
Deflated, Qinggua pouted. "You never give me an ounce of credit! First time I like a girl and you stomp right on it. Look how well Young Madam treats her people—you ought to learn from her!"
"Since when do you lecture your master? Stick to business or I'll smack you!"
"I get along with all ten," Qinggua muttered, "only they answer to Young Madam. None of them will take orders from me."
Chen Haoyu jumped up and grabbed Qinggua's shirtfront. "All that jawing for a dead end? Fine—your punishment is to stand by that door and yell, 'Zhu Shuzhen, I'm divorcing you!' Don't stop till I say so!"
He shoved Qinggua straight to the door. "Shout!"
Sprawled on the floor, Qinggua groaned, "She's married to you, Young Master, not me! How can a servant yell her full name and shout about divorce?"
Chen Haoyu raised a boot. "Shout, or I'll stomp you flat!"
"I'll shout, I'll shout!" Scrambling up, Qinggua leaned against the door and muttered, "Zhu Shuzhen, I'm divorcing you."
"Louder!"
"Zhu Shuzhen, I'm divorcing you!"
"Louder still!"
Squeezing his eyes shut, Qinggua bellowed at the top of his lungs: "Zhu Shuzhen! I'm divorcing you!" Over and over he went.
Satisfied, Chen Haoyu sauntered into the inner bedroom and flopped onto the bed for a nap.
Across the back yard in Jingyi Hall, Matron Wei sat listening to the ruckus outside. Rising to her feet, she murmured, "Time I paid Old Madam Xia a visit."
Meanwhile, inside Old Madam Xia's rooms where the three daughters-in-law sat chatting, a maid burst through the doors gasping, "Old Madam! Old Madam! Trouble! Huge trouble!"
"Watch your tongue!" Old Madam Xia scolded. "What's all the panic? Catch your breath and speak plain."
Slowing down, the maid reported, "Just now I saw Second Young Madam march Second Young Master through the gates tied up with ropes! Looks like he's in for it!"
Old Madam Xia's heart jumped, and Yao Qingyan went pale with worry.
Knowing her son's scheme had hit home, Madam Bao feigned outrage. "How outrageous! A brand-new bride tying up her own husband? You must step in, Mother, before the whole city thinks Chen men get pushed around by women!"
Madam Cui chimed in. "First Sister-in-law, you have to teach that Zhu girl proper wifely conduct. Wild as Haoyu is, his parents are right here—it's not her place to tie him up!"
Checking her own worry, Old Madam Xia spoke firm. "Quit stirring the pot, you two. I put Shuzhen in charge of disciplining Haoyu, so I trust her. No matter how she handles him, neither Jianglin, Qingyan, nor I will meddle."
Yao Qingyan bit down her urge to run over. "I'll abide by Mother's word."
With both grandmother and mother too anxious to chat, Madam Bao and Madam Cui lost their audience and took their leave together.
Outside the courtyard, Madam Bao sighed in mock pity. "Whatever made Eldest Brother and Sister-in-law pick that Zhu girl? Poetess or not, rotten temper and ruined name."
"Drop the act, Second Sister-in-law," Madam Cui shot back. "Haoyu marrying poorly only helps Haodong—you must be laughing up your sleeve."
"Nonsense! Even if Haoyu married a saint, he couldn't touch my Haodong, who's learned business beside his father and uncles since boyhood. Can't help it if Haoyu only chases skirts and your Haofei won't touch a ledger, dumping the whole load on my boy."
Stung by the jab at Haofei, Madam Cui stiffened. "I have errands. Excuse me."
Watching her stalk off, Madam Bao sniffed to herself. "Merchants for generations, yet instead of teaching their boy trade, they dream of him passing imperial exams! Fat chance!" Eager to carry the good news to her son, she hurried off, passing Matron Wei on the path without a second thought.
Inside Old Madam Xia's room, heavy silence pressed down while grandmother and mother wrestled with their nerves. A maid announced at the door: "Old Madam, Eldest Madam, Matron Wei from Second Young Madam's courtyard requests an audience."
Color rushed back to both women's faces. "Bring her in at once!" Old Madam Xia ordered.
Matron Wei stepped in and curtsied. Old Madam Xia bade her sit. "First time you've visited my courtyard since Shuzhen married in."
Reading the knot of anxiety on both faces—eager to hand discipline to Shuzhen until the moment the whip actually fell—Matron Wei replied smoothly, "My oversight, Old Madam. Please forgive me."
"No blame—running Shuzhen's courtyard keeps you plenty busy."
Seeing the forced smile beneath Old Madam Xia's polite tone, Matron Wei moved straight to ease their hearts. "Today I finally found a spare moment to pay my respects and speak about Miss and the young master."
Both women blurted in unison: "How is Haoyu?"
"Look how worried you two are—afraid Miss is abusing him?"
"Not abuse," Yao Qingyan murmured. "I just can't bear seeing him suffer."
Old Madam Xia sighed. "Spoiled him from the cradle—can't stand seeing him take a single knock. Even knowing it's for his own good, my heart still aches."
"All the more proof you chose right putting Miss in charge," Matron Wei said. "Right now she has him locked in the back courtyard with the windows nailed shut and the door padlocked, sending servants in with food and water..."
Again both gasped in unison: "How can she do that?!"
"Disciplining him is one thing, yet locking him up like that?" Yao Qingyan fretted. "How can Haoyu stand it?"
Seeing their panic, Matron Wei played the trump fact. "Earlier today, Madam asked me to persuade Miss to rein the young master in, yet Miss had zero interest. She didn't change her mind because of my silver tongue—she changed it because she learned something."
"What did she learn?" Old Madam Xia pressed.
"That the person who spread those rumors about her last year was the young master himself."
Old Madam Xia and Yao Qingyan traded stricken looks. "Ah! Paper can't wrap fire forever," Old Madam Xia groaned. "Maybe it's better she knows, yet poor Haoyu is in for rough waters! Please go back and talk her down—discipline is fine, just don't let her hurt him bad."
"He did her a terrible wrong," Yao Qingyan added in alarm. "I'm terrified she won't hold back her fists!"
"If you trust Miss to reform him, you have to trust her all the way," Matron Wei reassured them. "I watched her grow up. Her heart is upright and pure, kind to the bone—"
"Yet Wenxin told me she turned fierce after losing her memory, nothing like before!" Yao Qingyan broke in.
"Fierce outside or not, Madam, her kindness hasn't changed an ounce. Haven't you felt that yourselves these past days?"
Both women nodded.
"However furious she is over him ruining her name and wrecking her Qiao betrothal, she won't maim him with her fists—just teach him a sharp lesson. Put your minds at ease and pretend you know nothing, just like when he vanished outside for days on end. Think of the scrapes he got into out in town—Master Jiang's trap, coming home bruised—didn't he bounce right back?"
Remembering those close calls, both women exhaled.
Yao Qingyan steeled her heart. "Matron Wei is right. I'll pretend he's off gallivanting."
Still, one worry nagged Old Madam Xia. "From what you say, she locked him up for revenge, not to reform him. What if we don't get the outcome we want?"
"Whether revenge or reform, Old Madam, the methods are the same, and so is the outcome," Matron Wei smiled. "Sit back and watch Miss turn out a grandson to make you proud. Who knows—just as Madam said, knock two stubborn rocks together long enough, and sparks might really fly!"
That broke both women into genuine laughter, sweeping their gloom clean away.
Before leaving, Matron Wei gave one final warning. "While Miss disciplines him, neither of you may step in. No matter how he begs for rescue, harden your hearts and ignore him. Soften even once, and all her work goes up in smoke."
Steeling their resolve, both women nodded in firm agreement.
#CH 226
#TITLE: Hongdou Delivers Dinner to Boya Study
By dusk Qinggua's voice had worn down to a dry croak, yet he dared not stop whispering, "Zhu Shuzhen, I'm divorcing you..."
Then snores rumbled from the inner room. Relief flooded Qinggua's face. "Young Master's asleep! Time for a breather—my throat's parched." Pouring tea at the table, he touched the rim to his lips and grimaced. "Stone cold, and nobody brought hot water. Too thirsty to care."
Gulping it down, he peered through a crack in the boarded window. "Pitch dark outside and my stomach's growling—where's dinner?"
Right on cue, the padlock rattled. Qinggua bounded to the door as Hongdou stepped inside, food carrier in one hand, hot teapot in the other.
"Hongdou! You're here!" Taking the teapot to set on the table, Qinggua eyed the open door for a dash—only for it to click shut behind her.
Hongdou unpacked two plates of plain vegetables and two bowls of rice. "Miss sent dinner. Go wake the young master."
Already roused by the lock, Chen Haoyu stalked out of the bedroom and glared at Hongdou. "The second I get out, I'm selling you off to pay you back for those two slaps!"
Backed by her mistress, Hongdou did not flinch. "Miss holds my deed of sale, Young Master. Nothing you can do to me."
Stung by a maid's lip, Chen Haoyu snapped, "Go tell Zhu Shuzhen I'm repudiating her!"
"You had Qinggua hollering it all afternoon—every soul in Moxiang Courtyard heard, Miss included! Miss said whatever you want, she'll do the exact opposite. Want to divorce her? Forget it!"
Chen Haoyu drew back a fist. Qinggua jumped between them. "Easy, Young Master! Don't fight Hongdou—she brings our food!"
Furious at his own servant taking sides, Chen Haoyu forgot the boy's new trick and fired off a reflex kick.
Qinggua slipped past it without breaking a sweat. "No use kicking me, Young Master. I only held back out of loyalty—anyone else, I'd have tossed on the floor."
Outmatched by Hongdou and unable to land a kick on Qinggua, Chen Haoyu had lost his last punching bag. Clenching both fists, he snarled, "Zhu Shuzhen, we aren't through!"
Amused, Hongdou said, "Better eat, Young Master. I'm waiting to take the dishes back."
Seeing rage got him nowhere and hunger gnawed his belly, Chen Haoyu slumped into a chair—and balked at the spread. "Two dishes? I never eat less than five dishes and a soup! Tell Zhu Shuzhen to send more!"
"Miss said every complaint shrinks the portions."
"Forget I spoke!" Grinding his teeth, he lifted his chopsticks, poked through both plates, and groaned. "All greens? Not even a shred of meat?"
"Miss ordered a strict vegetarian diet while you're locked up."
Too mad to waste another word, Chen Haoyu shoveled rice into his mouth.
Starving himself, Qinggua pulled out the chair across from him and reached for his chopsticks.
Chen Haoyu flared up. "Who said you could sit at my table?"
Deflated, Qinggua laid his chopsticks down, rose, and swallowed hard over the steaming bowls. "I yelled my throat raw for you all afternoon, Young Master! At least throw me a bite!"
"Miss specifically ordered that Qinggua eats at the same table with you," Hongdou cut in.
"Hear that, Young Master? Young Madam's orders!"
Chen Haoyu had almost softened at Qinggua's sad face, yet hearing Zhu Shuzhen's name stiffened his spine. "You're my servant—you obey me, not Zhu Shuzhen! Sit down and I'll tan your hide!"
Backing off, Qinggua stood watch in agony, heart dropping with every mouthful his master took. To his relief, half of both dishes stayed untouched when Chen Haoyu rose, shot Hongdou a glare, and retreated to the bedroom. Qinggua dove into the leftovers like a starving wolf.
Afterward, helping Hongdou stack bowls into the carrier, Qinggua tested the waters. "Hongdou, what do you think of me?"
"Passable," Hongdou said, packing the bowls.
"What does 'passable' mean?"
"Not great, not awful."
Not thrilled with that rating, Qinggua pushed on. "Do you like a 'not great, not awful' guy like me?"
Too blunt to misread, Hongdou stayed unfazed since she felt no spark for him. "What's bouncing around in that head of yours, Qinggua? Plenty of maids in Chen Manor—somebody's bound to like you."
Handing her the cold teapot, Qinggua held his ground. "I don't care about anybody else. Do you like me?"
Lifting carrier and pot, Hongdou teased him. "Do I like you..."
Qinggua's face lit up.
"...or not like you..."
His heart sank.
"...truth is, I don't know myself."
Crestfallen yet stubborn, Qinggua walked her to the door. "I'm a good catch! Hang around me more and you'll see—marry me and I'll treat my wife like a queen."
Hongdou laughed. "Since you're such a prize, I'll advertise you around Moxiang Courtyard—and all over Chen Manor if need be. Bound to find you a bride!"
Before he could protest, the door opened and shut, the padlock clicking back into place.
Qinggua called through the planks, "Hongdou! Won't you be my wife?"
No answer came from outside—only a dry scoff from behind him. "Have you no shame? She turned you down flat and you're still barking shameless lines at a closed door! I'm blushing for you!"
Qinggua jumped and spun around. "Quit creeping up behind me like a ghost, Young Master! Almost gave me a heart attack!"
"Daring to gripe at me now? Tired of working here?"
Stuck indoors with time to burn, Chen Haoyu dropped into a chair. "Come sit and chat with me."
Flattered, Qinggua hopped onto a stool. "What about, Young Master?"
"Chasing Hongdou like that won't get you anywhere."
"Then teach me how!"
"Know why women flock to me?"
That stumped Qinggua. Searching his memory, he answered honest, "Young Master, I've never seen a girl fall for you on her own—only country maidens you hauled home to wait on you, like the old maids in Moxiang Courtyard and the other estates..."
Chen Haoyu shook a fist. "Spout more trash and taste my knuckles!"
Qinggua ducked back. "Just stating facts!"
Lowering his hand, Chen Haoyu muttered, "Sure, I was wild back then, yet I quit doing that half a year ago! Can't a guy turn over a new leaf?"
"Come to think of it, true—last year you switched to haunting Chunxiang Brothel. Must have better girls there. Got a sweetheart there, Young Master?"
Chun Jinmo crossed Chen Haoyu's mind. "Sort of. Wait—we were talking about you! How'd it turn on me?"
"You asked why girls like you! In my book, they only liked your silver."
"Bingo!" Chen Haoyu snapped his fingers. "Get rich, and you won't have to chase Hongdou—she'll throw herself at you!"
Qinggua shook his head. "Not true, Young Master. You're loaded, yet Young Madam couldn't care less—even locked you up! Anyone who chases your silver isn't sincere. Even if I had silver, I'd pretend I was broke so I'd know Hongdou loved me for real."
Those blunt words hit a sour chord in Chen Haoyu. Deep down, knowing every snatched village girl and brothel courtesan yielded only to his coin was why he had never truly given his heart to anyone. Buying compliance grew hollow fast; he had only indulged to stave off boredom.
Seeing his master fall quiet, Qinggua fretted, "Did I put my foot in it again? Mad at me, Young Master?"
To his surprise, Chen Haoyu spoke calm. "Looks like you understand love better than I do. Forget my advice—court Hongdou your own way. Still, anyone can see she isn't into you. Don't waste your breath."
"Thanks for the tip, Young Master! Today was just a warm-up. Once we get out, I'll bring out my full charm—Hongdou will be mine sooner or later!"
Letting the boy keep his dreams, Chen Haoyu turned back to escape. Night had fallen, yet neither Grandmother nor his parents had shown up—even though a maid from Old Madam Xia's own yard had watched him get marched in trussed with rope!
"Qinggua, why hasn't Grandmother come to rescue me?"
"Maybe she doesn't know you're locked up."
"Her own maid saw Zhu Shuzhen haul me in! Usually Grandmother storms over inside ten minutes. Did something big happen while I was away?"
Qinggua racked his brain. "Actually, yes—huge stuff!"
"Like what?"
"While you were gone, Young Madam hired a storyteller to come every day and tell Old Madam Xia stories till she laughed her head off! Today she even brought an old blind drummer, and Old Madam Xia ate extra bowls of rice! And the biggest thing of all..."
Alarm pricked Chen Haoyu. "What?"
"Young Madam patched up the rift between Old Madam Xia and Eldest Master and Madam! Now Second Master, Third Master, and all the aunts drop by every day too. Old Madam Xia's yard is packed nonstop, and everyone praises Second Young Madam to the skies!"
Chen Haoyu slammed his fist onto the table. "Sneaky! Beyond sneaky! Bought off my whole family behind my back! No wonder nobody lifted a finger for me! One clever granddaughter-in-law and Grandmother stops spoiling me? Mother forgets me?"
Qinggua snickered into his sleeve.
"I'm fuming and you're laughing? Begging for a beating?" Chen Haoyu barked.
Qinggua hopped clear—only for Chen Haoyu to crack a wry grin. "Relax, just messing with you. Sit back down; I'm bored stiff."
Easing back onto his stool, Qinggua chuckled. "Couldn't help laughing—you actually called Young Madam a 'clever granddaughter-in-law'!"
"Listen closer—that wasn't praise! Enough talk, help me break out. Here's a plan: use that face of yours to sweet-talk one of Zhu Shuzhen's maids into unlocking the door! Forget Kuqiao and Hongdou—what about the other two plain maids? Bet you can hook one easy."
Qinggua winced. "My looks don't hold a candle to yours, Young Master! Besides, those two aren't my type—and none of Young Madam's maids are pushovers."
"What, want me to seduce them myself?"
"If you tried, Young Master, guaranteed success!"
Chen Haoyu raised a hand. "Asking for a smack?"
Qinggua ducked with a grin. "Heh, I'm just plain-looking!"
Dropping his hand, Chen Haoyu sweetened the pot. "Lend me a little charm, and once we're out, I swear I'll help you win over Hongdou."
Qinggua's eyes lit up. "Really? Don't lie to me, Young Master!"
"A gentleman's word is bond!"
"Deal! I'll sacrifice myself for you, Young Master!"
"Now you're talking!"
#CH 227
#TITLE: Discipline as Cover for Revenge
Having marched Chen Haoyu home in ropes from Chunxiang Brothel, Qianli Xun feared zero backlash from the Chen elders. Part of her hoped they would storm over so she could demand why they had pushed this marriage knowing full well Chen Haoyu had ruined her reputation.
Night fell without a single elder knocking at her gate—not even doting Old Madam Xia, whose maid had witnessed the whole scene. Unable to fathom why, Qianli Xun gave up guessing.
With the culprit locked away, her white-hot rage cooled into a dull, heavy ache. Too drained to write, she sat at her desk remembering how dark last year's slander had been—the nights of tears, the sense that her whole future had crumbled to ash. All of it by Chen Haoyu's hand, and now she bore his name. Thank heaven she had never consummated the marriage, or she would have regretted it to her dying day.
Thinking back on those bleak months brought her family, Mengrong, and Shen Jianchen into focus. Family warmth had kept her standing; even strict Zhu Xiyan had quietly allowed her mother, brother, and sister-in-law to visit Wangyue Pavilion, loving her in his clumsy, face-obsessed way—including this Chen match. Matron Wei had stopped her from storming Zhu Manor, and now the urge had passed; screaming at her father would not turn back the clock.
During those dark days, Mengrong had visited Wangyue Pavilion two or three times—few visits, yet enough to prove the world had not abandoned her, sitting beside the brazier trading secrets. That was when Qianli Xun had vowed to treat Mengrong as her best friend for life.
Once she learned Prince Yi was Shen Jianchen, his odd kindness back then made complete sense—gifts, treats, waiting outside Wangyue Pavilion in his carriage while Mengrong visited. A debt of feeling she could never repay in this lifetime. For Mengrong's sake she had turned him down flat, yet she could not deny that having a prince cherish her while the whole city spat on her name had buoyed her pride when she needed it most.
"Kuqiao, go fetch that gift Prince Yi sent to Wangyue Pavilion last year."
Kuqiao racked her brains. "Miss, I don't recall Prince Yi sending a gift."
"That peeing clay figurine."
Recognition clicked. "Oh! That bare-bottomed clay boy! What do you want with it, Miss?"
"Stop asking and go find it."
Thinking back—her mistress had looked at it once and told her to pack it away—Kuqiao figured it might have come over with the move. "I'll check the storeroom where I tuck things you don't use."
Left alone, Qianli Xun felt sorrow welling up, spread a fresh sheet of paper, and brushed out Zhu Shuzhen's quatrain:
"Springs come, springs go, how many have passed, / Yet none ever held as much bitterness as this year. / Lonely moon perched above the crabapple bough— / Shining down on this quiet night, what do you ask of me?" [TN: Translator's rendering of Zhu Shuzhen's "Miscellaneous Spring Verses, No. 1"]
She had just lifted her brush when Kuqiao returned holding a small wooden box and set it beside her. "Had to dig forever to unearth it."
Picking up the wet verse to blow the ink dry, Kuqiao said, "I'll set this aside for Nan Shuang or Huayu next time they come." Her eyes caught the word "bitterness" in the wet ink. "Miss, do you hate Young Master?"
Pulling the box close, Qianli Xun lifted out the cheeky bare-bottomed clay boy, and an involuntary smile touched her lips—it really was too comical not to grin at. "Hate him? Of course I hate him. He put me through hell."
Seeing her smile even as she spoke, Kuqiao relaxed; she cared far less about Chen Haoyu's bruises than about her mistress drowning in hatred during a second marriage. "If you're smiling, Miss, I'm happy."
Stowing the dried poem, Kuqiao noticed her mistress still gazing at the clay figurine, which reminded her of the figurine Bai Feng had given her. "Wonder when Bai Feng and Prince Yi are coming back to Lin'an?"
That hit straight at Qianli Xun's own secret ache—torn between wanting him back and dreading how to face Mengrong. "I'd rather they stayed in Bianliang and never came back."
Sensing the raw nerve, Kuqiao changed track. "Miss, do you mean to keep Young Master locked up forever?"
Qianli Xun tucked the figurine back in its box and shut the lid. "Locked up for now. Haven't decided how long."
Suddenly Kuqiao began to sniffle.
Qianli Xun turned. "What's got you crying out of nowhere?"
"I'm heartbroken for you, Miss!" Kuqiao sobbed. "Your first marriage was misery, you fought so hard for a mutual divorce, and now you're married to the very man who started those rumors! How are you supposed to live?"
Kuqiao's tears tugged at Qianli Xun's own gloom. Dry-eyed yet subdued, she murmured, "I'll make Chen Haoyu pay."
"Yet he's your husband now!" Kuqiao wept. "To the world you're one household—you rise together and fall together! If he pays a heavy price, won't it drag you down too? My heart aches for you!"
"Quit crying—you're giving me a headache." Handing the box back, she said, "Put this on the shelf where I can grab it anytime."
Wiping her cheeks, Kuqiao set the box on the shelf.
"Go get some sleep. I want to sit alone for a bit."
Obeying, Kuqiao withdrew to Yuening Room.
Feeling stifled indoors, Qianli Xun stepped out into the yard and strolled to the pond. Small lotus pads floated dark across moonlit ripples, reducing the pool to silver shimmer and ink-black shadow.
Kuqiao's point—"rise together, fall together"—rang true. Dislike Chen Haoyu as she did, marrying into this house had been her own final call. Out of weariness, acceptance, or the wish to hand Mengrong back her brother whole, she had meant Chen Manor to be her final harbor—never once picturing a second divorce. Hearing Chen Haoyu bellow about repudiating her today had not frightened her, yet it had jarred her peace.
How could she avenge herself without burning down the roof over her own head?
Then she remembered Old Madam Xia and her in-laws handing her authority to reform Chen Haoyu. A cool smile curved her lips. "Fine—I'll avenge myself under the banner of 'disciplining' him! Pray you stay stubborn forever so I can 'discipline' you for life. And if you somehow turn decent, I become the Chen family's hero, rock-solid in this house!"
Trying to picture slick, loafing Chen Haoyu turned respectable—like Wenyuan or Shen Jianchen—made her chuckle aloud. Her mood lifted. Tomorrow she would call on the elders and lay out her "reform plan" upfront, reassuring them so nobody interfered with her payback.
Across the courtyard in Yuening Room, Kuqiao watched her mistress by the pond through the window, sighed, shut the casement, and turned to Hongdou. "I'm terrified Miss will end up in a second divorce."
Lying awake in the second servant bed, Hongdou shook her head. "Relax, Sister Kuqiao. Miss gets along great with every elder here—the Chen family would never let her go."
Kuqiao sat on the edge of Hongdou's bed. "He spread those rumors; Miss won't go easy on him. Yet Young Master is Old Madam Xia's treasure and Eldest Madam's darling son! Liked as Miss is, blood runs thicker than water."
Hongdou rolled over. "Quit borrowing trouble! Matron Wei isn't sweating—why are you?"
True enough: since Chen Haoyu had been dragged home, Matron Wei had stepped out once and stayed cool as cucumber since. Kuqiao relaxed a notch. "Did Young Master keep cursing Miss when you brought dinner?"
"Nonstop! Swear they must've been bitter enemies in a past life shoved under one roof in this one. Wonder who'll win?"
"Need you ask? Miss will wipe the floor with him—boom, crash, done!" Kuqiao crowed, anxiety forgotten.
Hongdou sounded wistful. "What's the fun in husband and wife fighting nonstop? I want Miss happy with a decent husband. Eldest Master and Madam are such good people—why didn't their son turn out like his father? Imagine how sweet life would be if Young Master treated Miss half as well as Eldest Master treats Madam!"
Yawning wide, Kuqiao snuffed the candle, shed her outer jacket, and climbed under her quilt. "No use worrying—just pray Young Master shapes up fast so Miss gets some peace."
That evening, when Chen Jianglin returned from the tea shop, Yao Qingyan recounted the whole day's drama.
"Good!" Chen Jianglin beamed. "Lock him up! I've wanted to do that for years—only held back because of you and Mother."
Helping him shed his outer robe, Yao Qingyan said, "Mother and I nearly panicked when we heard, till Matron Wei came over to calm us down and told us Shuzhen found out Haoyu started those rumors—that's why she locked him up."
Sitting on the bed edge, Chen Jianglin sighed. "Paper can't hide fire. Better she knows now. After a stunt that low, locking him up is mercy—I'd take a whip to his hide myself."
When Yao Qingyan bent to unlace his boots, he waved her off. "I'll get my own boots—you climb in and rest."
Taking off her hairpins at the vanity, Yao Qingyan shed her robe, blew out the lamp, and slipped under the covers. "I'm more scared of her fists than a whip. What if she beats Haoyu half crippled?"
"Relax! Tough as her fists are, has she swung once since arriving? Quite the opposite—courteous, sharp, and warmhearted. Barely days in the house and the whole atmosphere changed for the better."
"So she brought us good fortune?"
"No doubt! Starting to think heaven broke off her Lin marriage and blocked the Qiao match just to save her for our family! Hahaha!"
"Speak for yourself—the Zhus and Chens only matched up because of Haoyu's loose mouth."
"Which proves fate forced Haoyu to earn himself a brilliant wife! Hahaha!"
Half-skeptical yet amused, Yao Qingyan smiled in the dark, silently wishing her son and daughter-in-law might grow closer with time.
#CH 228
#TITLE: One Branch Frets While Another Laughs
Where one branch worried, another celebrated. Inside Chen Jiangshu's quarters, all three family members sat beaming.
"Ha!" Chen Haodong gloated. "Locked up tight—no more roaming around free as a bird! Feels great! Why should I slave away earning silver for this house while he burns money like water without lifting a finger? That tigress came through big-time."
"Good news indeed," Chen Jiangshu mused, "yet it puzzles me why Mother and First Sister-in-law haven't lifted a finger. Don't they know?"
"Oh, they know!" Madam Bao said. "A maid ran right in and reported it while I was sitting there. You should have seen their faces!"
"Then why didn't they march over to stop her? Not like them at all."
"Bet the Zhu girl's fists scared them off," Madam Bao guessed.
Chen Jiangshu shook his head. "Mother's seen half a century of storms—no young girl scares her off. Last time you and Third Sister-in-law riled her up, she marched right over without blinking."
"Well, you've got me stumped then," Madam Bao admitted.
"My guess," Chen Haodong reasoned, "is that because the Zhu girl smoothed things over between Grandmother and the elders, Grandmother and First Aunt held back to give her face. All the better! If they meddled and forced her to let Haoyu out, my plan would flop."
"Makes sense," Chen Jiangshu nodded. "Just hope they don't lose their nerve and step in tomorrow."
"Even if they try, they won't stop her!" Madam Bao laughed. "That Zhu girl has fists like iron and a tongue like a razor! Last time Grandmother stormed over with three solid charges, she spun them all around until Grandmother walked out nodding! Now that she knows Haoyu started those rumors, with that rage fueling her, neither Grandmother nor First Sister-in-law can budge her."
Amused by Madam Bao's breakdown, father and son laughed aloud. Chen Jiangshu praised her, "Spot on, wife! Never again will I say women are shortsighted."
"Mother comes from a scholar family and reads plenty," Chen Haodong chimed in. "Of course she sees straight through things."
Praised by the two men who mattered most to her, Madam Bao glowed with pride.
Since night had deepened, Chen Haodong bade his parents good night and walked back to his own courtyard. Riding high on good news, desire stirred in him, yet it was too late to visit Chun Jinchan.
Glancing up at Ye Anya's darkened room—the lamp already out—annoyance spiked inside him. His own wife crawling into bed without waiting up for him!
He rapped sharp on the door. Knock, knock, knock!
Still awake beneath her quilt while Xiaocui slept in the side room, Ye Anya guessed who stood outside and tugged the blanket over her head without budging.
Knock, knock, knock! Silence inside. Infuriated, Chen Haodong kicked the door wide open, marched around the folding screen in the dark, and yanked Ye Anya up by the arm. "Why didn't you open the door?"
Numbed by countless beatings, Ye Anya showed no fear. "Need you ask?"
CRACK! His palm whipped across her cheek. "You're my wife! Your job is waiting up every night to undress me and serve me, instead of going to sleep alone like I don't exist! Act half decent and I wouldn't lay a hand on you!"
Ye Anya gave a cold laugh. "Even before our wedding I heard you were bedding brothel girls. The sight of you turns my stomach—why would I wait on you?"
He shoved her back onto the mattress and pinned her down. She did not struggle, turning her head away with an expression carved from ice. Even in moonlight through the window, the chill off her face stung him.
"I'm a man—playing with a few women outside is nothing! Look at Lin Jue's wife—sweet, dutiful, even spent her own dowry to buy Chun Jinqiao out of the brothel for him..."
Pah! Ye Anya spat straight into his face. "Dream of me acting like that in your next life—no, not even then!"
Wiping her spit off his cheek, Chen Haodong sneered, "The colder you act, the more I want to take you. Since I'm in a good mood tonight, I'll go gentle."
Closing her eyes, Ye Anya endured while he took his pleasure. Not once since their wedding night had she known a single shred of joy. When would this nightmare end? Thinking of Shuzhen—bold enough to drag Haoyu out of a brothel and lock him behind nailed windows—sparked admiration and resolve. Tomorrow she would go talk to her.
Meanwhile, in Third Master Chen Jiangmu's room, husband and wife chatted while getting ready for bed.
Sitting at the vanity pulling out her hairpins, Madam Cui remarked, "Eldest Brother and Sister-in-law never should have agreed to that match. Look at poor Haoyu suffering now."
Soaking his feet in a hot wooden basin poured by a maid, Chen Jiangmu shrugged. "You know why—Prefect Zhu marched right to the door. What choice did Eldest Brother have? Wedding's done; nothing to do but live with it."
Setting her pins in the box, Madam Cui knelt beside him and dipped her hands into the basin to wash his feet. "Still can't believe Haoyu spread last year's rumors! Why on earth would he target the Zhu girl when they barely knew each other?"
Eyes shut, enjoying his wife's gentle rub, Chen Jiangmu muttered, "Haoyu roams outside day and night—who knows what trouble he stirs up?"
"Thank goodness our Haofei is sensible," Madam Cui sighed, rinsing and kneading his ankles. "Never gave me a day's worry—nose buried in his books."
"Part of me wishes he'd learn trade instead, yet his heart's set on studying."
Finished washing, Madam Cui stood, dried her hands on a towel from a maid, while Chen Jiangmu wiped his feet dry. Once the maids withdrew, they snuffed the lamp and lay down.
"Both of Haofei's older cousins have their own edge," Madam Cui sighed in the dark. "One charms Old Madam Xia, the other's a wizard at trade. Competing head-on in Chen Manor is hopeless—and neither you nor our son has the stomach for cutthroat fights. Earning an imperial degree opens a whole different path! Merchants always rank below officials. If Haofei passes the exams, we'll be parents of a court official—think of the prestige!"
Rolling onto his side with his back to her, Chen Jiangmu mumbled, "True enough. That's why I back him even if I'd prefer trade."
"Who do you figure ends up inheriting the Chen estates?" she asked.
Chen Jiangmu yawned. "Count Haofei out."
"Between Haodong and Haoyu—who do you want?"
"Isn't it obvious?" he slurred.
"You mean Haodong?" Only steady snores answered her. Madam Cui murmured into the dark, "The way things stand, Haodong has it locked up."
Early the next morning, the moment Chen Haodong left for the silk shop, relief washed through Ye Anya. Deep down she wished he stayed gone forever—roaming like Haoyu would be pure heaven. Too restless to sleep in, she ate an early breakfast and walked to Moxiang Courtyard with Xiaocui.
Just then Qianli Xun was heading out the gate herself, primed to confront the Chen elders about Haoyu's rumors and lay out her "reform" terms. Spotting Ye Anya approaching, she beamed. "First Sister-in-law! Stopping by this early must mean something important. My errand can wait—come chat!"
Ye Anya felt a flash of envy at her resilience. Yesterday Shuzhen had marched her husband home in ropes breathing fire; today not a trace of anger clouded her bright face. How could a spirit this sunny pen such heartbroken verse? Maybe pouring sorrow onto paper kept her heart clear.
"Hope I'm not interrupting anything," Ye Anya asked with shy caution.
Taking her hand to pull her inside, Qianli Xun laughed. "Nonsense—you're welcome any hour!"
Guessing Ye Anya had private matters to share, Qianli Xun guided her straight past the outer hall into the inner chamber, where a low square tea table with squat wooden stools sat atop a woven rug. Without needing to be told, Kuqiao stayed in the outer hall to whisk tea.
Settling down, Ye Anya led with yesterday's news. "I heard you locked Haoyu up! What nerve—aren't you worried Grandmother and First Uncle and Aunt will come down on you?"
"If you already heard, Grandmother and my in-laws must know too," Qianli Xun reasoned. "Not one has knocked on my door yet—which means either they know they're in the wrong, or they secretly approve."
Careless of the elders' views, Ye Anya gazed at her in awe. "You're so fearless and strong, Sister—doing whatever you please. I envy you more than words can say."
"Didn't you know folks call me a tigress behind my back?" Qianli Xun quipped.
"Whatever they mean by it, I take it as high praise!" Ye Anya smiled. "How many wives in this world have the guts to drag their husbands out of a brothel in ropes and lock them up? That spine deserves respect."
"You're the only soul in Chen Manor who thinks so."
Dropping small talk, Ye Anya drew a steadying breath. "Shuzhen, last time I visited I wanted to ask your advice, yet lost my nerve since we'd just met. Today I'm swallowing my pride to ask straight out—please help me."
Remembering the embrace beneath the Divine Willow, Qianli Xun stayed careful. "Ask away, Sister-in-law."
Ye Anya met her eyes. "You went through a mutual divorce once. Could you tell me how you managed it?"
Right then Kuqiao walked in carrying two bowls of freshly whisked tea—catching that exact sentence. Her mind flashed straight back to the Divine Willow. Knowing she had walked in on dynamite, she set the bowls down without a peep.
"Kuqiao," Qianli Xun said, "wait in the outer hall and keep everyone out."
Ye Anya nodded to Xiaocui, who stepped out alongside Kuqiao.
Studying the desperate hope in Ye Anya's eyes, Qianli Xun trod with care; she wanted full context before speaking a word that might upend someone's life.
"A few days ago, I visited the Divine Willow outside town," she began, "and stumbled onto quite a sight..."
Catching her meaning at once, Ye Anya dropped all pretense. "Since you saw us, you know why I'm asking about mutual divorce."
"How long has this been going on?"
"Before I ever married into Chen Manor, he and I loved each other," Ye Anya confessed. "Yet the Ye and Cao families have feuded for generations. My father flatly forbade it and betrothed me to the Chens. Part of me tried to resign myself—until the day before the wedding, when Xiaocui learned Chen Haodong was spending time with a courtesan. Disgust took root in my bones, and since crossing this threshold I haven't stopped loathing him for a single day."
She pushed up her sleeve, baring mottled purple and yellow bruises along her forearm. "Because I stay cold to him, whenever Chen Haodong wants... what he wants, he uses his fists. I'm black and blue year-round. I can't survive another day like this. I want a mutual divorce—I just have no idea where to start, so I came to ask you."
Qianli Xun reached across and drew Ye Anya's sleeve back down over the bruises. "I had no idea you were going through hell like this, Sister-in-law. Are you dead set on divorce?"
Ye Anya nodded hard. "My mind is iron. That's why I dared ask."
Having fought through a Song-era divorce herself, Qianli Xun looked at fragile Ye Anya and felt her chest tighten with dread. "A mutual divorce is brutal, Sister-in-law. Think ten times before stepping onto that path."
#CH 229
#TITLE: Laying Out the Ugly Truth Upfront
Ye Anya drained her tea bowl in one gulp, dabbed her lips with a silk handkerchief, and spoke with quiet grit. "Don't worry for me, Sister. If you wish me well, tell me how to break free of this marriage."
Reflecting on her own turbulent path since transmigrating, Qianli Xun felt a deep pang. Compared with Ye Anya, she had been lucky—neither Lin Jue nor Chen Haoyu could lay a finger on her, whereas her sister-in-law suffered Chen Haodong's fists helplessly. She owed her the unvarnished truth.
"For a woman in this era, a mutual divorce is uphill murder. I threw everything I had at it, and in the end I only escaped Lin Manor because Prince Yi stepped in to pressure my father and Lin Jue."
"Prince Yi stepped in?" Anxiety tightened Ye Anya's brow. "So it's that hard..."
Qianli Xun sipped her tea. "Yes. Sometimes I wonder if I'd ever have broken free of Lin Jue if Prince Yi hadn't come to Lin'an." Thoughts of Shen Jianchen flickered through her—helping her divorce the moment they met, persuading the Qiaos to propose, helping squash last year's rumors...
Seeing her pause, Ye Anya asked with gentle care, "Was Prince Yi already in love with you back then?"
After the wedding-day raid, the question came natural enough. Wanting to stay honest without fanning gossip, Qianli Xun answered steady, "Asking that means you heard about the raid on my wedding procession. What Prince Yi felt back then I couldn't say, yet nothing improper ever passed between us. Princess Jiahe was my dearest friend—I could never betray her. What happened on my wedding day caught me completely off guard."
Ye Anya sighed. "We're two miserable souls."
Steering clear of Prince Yi, Qianli Xun pulled back to divorce. "If you really want a mutual divorce, Sister-in-law, you don't just need Eldest Cousin's signature—both families' elders must consent. If even one side digs in its heels, it's dead in the water."
Twisting her handkerchief in silence, Ye Anya looked weighed down with dread. Qianli Xun figured she might back off.
Instead, Ye Anya lifted her head. "I'll find a way to wear down every last one. And if all else fails, I'll push Chen Haodong to repudiate me."
Remembering Kuqiao's warning from her earliest days here, Qianli Xun leaned forward fast. "Do you have unmarried sisters at home?"
"Two younger sisters."
"Then under no circumstances can you let your husband cast you out with a letter of repudiation!"
"I know being repudiated ruins my sisters' marriage prospects," Ye Anya said, voice steady. "Still, I can't endure one more year of this cage. At worst, the Ye family can disown me."
Moved by the iron beneath her fragile frame, Qianli Xun clasped her hands. "You're one in a million in this age, Sister-in-law. Just promise me one thing: whatever move you make, plan every step tight—and protect yourself first."
Ye Anya squeezed back. "Thank you, Shuzhen. Seeing you gave me the courage to fight for freedom."
Qianli Xun fell quiet, unsure whether inspiring her sister-in-law was blessing or curse in a world stacked this hard against women.
With everything said, Ye Anya rose to leave. Walking her outside Moxiang Courtyard, Qianli Xun watched her go and whispered a silent wish: May First Sister-in-law find happiness. Why not wish for her divorce to succeed? Because either way—free with the man she loved, or trapped enduring—happiness was what she needed most.
Setting Ye Anya's troubles aside for her own business, Qianli Xun headed straight for Old Madam Xia's courtyard. Since her father- and mother-in-law now visited every morning after breakfast, she could catch all the elders in one room and say her piece once instead of making rounds.
Reaching the gate, lively voices floated out from inside. When a yard maid stepped up to announce her, Qianli Xun waved her back. "No need—I'll walk straight in." She wanted to catch their unfiltered faces before anyone could compose a polite mask.
Second Uncle's voice rang loudest as she stepped across the threshold. Every tongue froze the instant she appeared.
Old Madam Xia, Yao Qingyan, and Chen Jianglin all greeted her with warm smiles—relieving Qianli Xun, though she was ready to confront them over Haoyu's rumors either way. Second and Third Aunt wore pinched expressions half-gloating for drama; the two uncles masked their reactions better, yet their eyes flicked up and dropped fast—proof everyone knew Chen Haoyu was locked up.
"Shuzhen! Come sit," Old Madam Xia called out.
Instead of sitting, Qianli Xun dropped straight to her knees, with Kuqiao kneeling right behind her.
"What are you kneeling for?" Old Madam Xia asked.
"Grandmother, yesterday I dragged Chen Haoyu home from a brothel in ropes and locked him in the back courtyard. In my eyes I did nothing wrong, yet the elders may see it different, so I kneel first to accept any blame."
Before Old Madam Xia could speak, Third Uncle Chen Jiangmu jumped in hot. "If you know you crossed a line, hurry up and let Haoyu out! Better than kneeling here putting on a show—"
Old Madam Xia raised a hand, cutting her third son off mid-sentence. "What crime did you commit? Get off your knees!"
Qianli Xun rose with Kuqiao, who beamed inside at seeing her mistress cleared.
Qianli Xun pressed on purpose. "Grandmother, Father, Mother—you truly don't fault me?"
"When did we ever fault you?" Chen Jianglin replied. "We handed you full authority to discipline Haoyu. Handle him however you see fit."
"We heard yesterday and didn't lift a finger to stop you," Yao Qingyan added. "That proves we stand behind you. Discipline him your own way."
Old Madam Xia grinned. "I give you my word right here: while you reform Haoyu, none of us three will undermine you."
Her father-in-law's backing she had expected; Old Madam Xia and Yao Qingyan giving her blank-check approval without even a single plea for mercy caught her by surprise.
Exchanging a smirk with Chen Jiangshu, Madam Bao could not resist poking the pot. "Funny—yesterday Mother and First Sister-in-law looked fit to faint when they heard Haoyu was tied up! Why so breezy today? Oh, right—when I stepped outside yesterday, I saw Matron Wei heading in! Must have talked you both round. That matron beside Shuzhen sure works magic!"
Whatever poison Madam Bao aimed to drip, she just solved Qianli Xun's mystery: Matron Wei had smoothed the whole path behind the scenes! Thank heaven for Matron Wei.
"Shuzhen isn't your daughter-in-law—butt out!" Old Madam Xia snapped at Madam Bao. Madam Bao pursed her lips and went mute, while Madam Cui swallowed her own comment whole.
Beaming again, Old Madam Xia gestured to a chair. "Sit down, girl! Tiring standing there."
Qianli Xun stayed on her feet. Since discipline was settled, she moved straight to her real grievance—even if venting changed nothing, she refused to choke it down. "Better I stay standing, Grandmother. What I say next may displease you."
Guessing at once, Old Madam Xia beat her to it. "About Haoyu spreading those rumors?"
"Yes."
"All water under the bridge," Old Madam Xia waved it off. "You're married in now—we're one family. No need digging up old dirt."
That warm phrase—"one family"—nearly dulled Qianli Xun's fire until Chen Haoyu's smirking mug flashed in her mind. "I want to know one thing: knowing full well Chen Haoyu spread slander and wrecked my happiness, why did the Chen elders still agree to this betrothal? Shoving two bitter enemies into marriage—isn't that ruining my life?"
Her blunt volley landed like a thunderbolt, leaving some elders squirming and others lapping up the show.
Chen Jianglin let out a heavy sigh. "We understand your anger, Shuzhen. Yet that day Prefect Zhu marched Haoyu in trussed with ropes and told us what he'd done. I was furious and frantic; when Prefect Zhu proposed the match, it struck me as the right way to make amends. Haoyu caused the harm, so he had to own the responsibility."
"Plenty of ways to take responsibility! Why pick a betrothal? Pushing me into a fire pit and calling it noble!"
Yao Qingyan stood and took Qianli Xun's hands. "How is Chen Manor a fire pit? Since marrying in, have you suffered a single wrong or hardship here?"
Fair point—the family had treated her well, even Old Madam Xia's little test had been playacting. Still, the knot in her chest refused to untie. "Chen Manor is fine and the elders are kind, yet Chen Haoyu... we're oil and water, nowhere near the kind of man I want."
"Then whip him into the man you want!" Yao Qingyan laughed. "Won't that be perfection?"
Old Madam Xia and Chen Jianglin chuckled along.
Inside, Madam Bao sneered: Couldn't raise their own son, now expecting a new bride to fix him! What a joke!
Madam Cui scoffed to herself: Never heard of a wife reforming a rake! If that Zhu girl straightens Haoyu out, I'll write my maiden name Cui upside down!
Chen Jiangmu thought it pure nonsense yet kept his mouth shut seeing his eldest brother smiling.
Unable to hold back longer, Chen Jiangshu spoke up. "Mother, Eldest Brother, why not put Haoyu in our shops under my wing to learn trade? I can keep him in line—sounds better to outsiders than letting a brand-new bride discipline him. Tough as Shuzhen's fists are, fists alone don't build character."
Madam Bao knew her husband meant not a word of that offer—just a slick dig implying Eldest Brother failed as a parent and dumped the mess on a girl.
"Shuzhen is the best choice," Old Madam Xia ruled flat. "Case closed. Not another word."
Since his offer was pure theater anyway, Chen Jiangshu bowed right out. "Whatever Mother sees fit."
Old Madam Xia turned gentle toward Qianli Xun. "I know you resented this wedding, Shuzhen, and hearing Haoyu spread those rumors made you boil over. Yet nobody held a blade to your throat to make you step into that bridal sedan. Maybe it really is fate—an ill-fated tie now, sure, yet Grandmother believes you can turn an ill fate into a good match."
Squeezing her hands, Yao Qingyan echoed, "Mother's right—ill fate can turn golden! Put those rumors behind you, Shuzhen; bright days lie ahead. If anger still burns in you, use disciplining him to let off steam..."
Qianli Xun marveled at their rosy daydreams—expecting her to reform a rake and fall in love to boot! Still, Yao Qingyan's last words gave her the exact opening she needed to lay down ground rules upfront.
"Since Mother puts it that way, I'll hold you to it," Qianli Xun declared. "From now on I'll treat disciplining Chen Haoyu as letting off steam. If I fail to mold him into the paragon you elders dream of, please don't regret today's choice."
Chen Jiangshu grinned inside: Vent all you want—the worse for Haoyu, the better for my son!
Madam Bao crowed silently: Nice job digging your own hole, First Sister-in-law!
Third Uncle and Aunt exchanged appalled looks at the bride's cheek, keeping quiet while enjoying the spectacle.
Yao Qingyan let go of Shuzhen's hands with a sudden twinge of nerves. "I only meant it as a figure of speech—don't take 'letting off steam' too far!" Returning to her chair, she shot an anxious look at Chen Jianglin.
Qianli Xun saw her words had stung, yet better to put the ugly truth upfront. She had zero plans to play dutiful tutor—only to settle her score. If Haoyu stayed a hopeless bum at the end of it, nobody could come blaming her.
#CH 230
#TITLE: Qinggua Seduces Ugly Maid
Catching Yao Qingyan's anxious glance, Chen Jianglin cleared his throat to steady his wife and reassure Shuzhen at the same time. "Ahem! In the short time since Shuzhen married in, she helped us three brothers understand Mother's heart. That alone proves she is thoughtful and kind to the core..."
"Kind to the core" echoed Matron Wei's assurance from yesterday, easing Yao Qingyan's panic at once: True—Shuzhen has a good heart; she won't actually abuse Haoyu. Why am I fretting?
Chen Jianglin went on. "Nothing under heaven is impossible to a willing heart, and I trust Shuzhen. Even if she can't reform him, I won't blame her or feel an ounce of regret. Only two outcomes exist: reform him, and we all rejoice; fail, and I wash my hands of him—every child walks their own fate. All I ask is that after I'm gone, whoever leads the Chen clan spares Haoyu a bowl of hot rice, and that you don't abandon him, Shuzhen."
Fair and heartfelt words that left Qianli Xun with zero stomach to vent further. Chen Haoyu had spread the lies, not these elders; taking her grudge out on them made no sense.
Catching the subtext in Chen Jianglin's speech—he never counted on Haoyu inheriting the clan, and Haofei cared only for books, leaving the throne wide open for Haodong—Chen Jiangshu and Madam Bao traded pleased smiles.
Chen Jiangmu spoke up in protest. "What kind of talk is that, Eldest Brother? This is the Chen clan! How could Haoyu ever be reduced to begging for hot rice? Even if he roams his whole life, whenever he walks through the door he'll feast on fish and meat!"
"Right, right!" Madam Cui chimed in. "How could Eldest Brother, First Sister-in-law, or Mother ever let Haoyu go short? You'll leave him plenty—his cousins won't neglect him either, and besides, his own wife holds a small fortune between her dowry and Haoyu's properties! She's one of the wealthiest young ladies in Lin'an; Haoyu won't suffer a day."
Watching her granddaughter-in-law's flat face, Old Madam Xia sensed she still had zero enthusiasm for reforming Haoyu, and disappointment tugged at her. Irritated by Third Son and his wife's chatter, she snapped, "Enough! I'm not in my coffin yet, and you're already planning Haoyu's leftovers? As the proverb goes, a worthy wife beats ten thousand acres of fertile land. Marrying Shuzhen is the blessing Haoyu earned in a past life—with a wife like her, why worry about his future?"
Worthy wife, sure, Qianli Xun thought wryly, except marrying a scoundrel I hold a grudge against forces me to play tigress!
Madam Bao bristled inside: Worthy wife? She's a full-blown tigress!
Madam Cui sneered silently: Looks delicate enough till she swings her fists! Never heard of a 'worthy wife' trussing her husband up and locking him away—Old Madam Xia's bar sure dropped low!
"Shuzhen," Old Madam Xia continued, "if you're happy with your in-laws and with me, let go of Haoyu's old rumors. Good or bad, the past is gone—eyes forward. Focus on disciplining Haoyu; skip daily morning greetings to me, this big house has plenty of company already. Don't worry about entertaining me either—the storyteller knows the way to my yard by heart now. No need reporting how you handle Haoyu; do as you please. Run along now."
She sent Shuzhen off before raw resentment pushed her into sharper remarks that would only hand Second and Third Aunt free gossip—both daughters-in-law were devoted to their husbands yet petty enough to relish anyone else's stumble.
With nothing left to say, Qianli Xun curtsied and withdrew. Walking back, she felt the trip had been pointless: Matron Wei had already cleared the way, while her own bottled anger still had nowhere to go. Since Old Madam Xia excused her from greetings, better to stay out of sight until her temper cooled, and focus on dreaming up ways to torture Chen Haoyu under the banner of "discipline."
Earlier that morning, when Hongdou delivered breakfast to Boya Study, Chen Haoyu had shot Qinggua a signal as soon as they finished eating.
Taking the cue, Qinggua sidled over while Hongdou stacked bowls. "Hey, could you send Chouya over later?"
"Why call Chouya?" Hongdou asked.
"Don't get the wrong idea—not because I like her! Just need a quick word."
Well aware Chouya carried a torch for Qinggua, Hongdou welcomed the chance to steer Qinggua off her own back. "Sure, I'll send her over, though she can't come inside—you'll have to talk through the window."
"Fine by me—window works!" Qinggua escorted her to the door until the padlock clicked shut.
"Why pick Chouya?" Chen Haoyu asked.
Turning back, Qinggua grimaced. "Tall order you gave me, Young Master! Had to pick the easiest target. Hear a name like 'Ugly Girl' and you know she'll fall for sweet talk fast."
"What's the other maid called?"
"Amei."
"Amei—sounds pretty."
"Plain enough, nowhere near Hongdou. She's Asheng's younger sister."
"Brother and sister both slaving for Zhu Shuzhen—hopeless."
Qinggua pushed back. "Growing up rich, you don't know how hard poor folks have it, Young Master. Poor families jump for joy landing a spot in a wealthy manor—especially under a good mistress like Young Madam! Getting trained in martial arts side by side—folks would kill for that."
"Shoo, shoo! Quit praising Zhu Shuzhen to my face! You work for me—don't let her buy you off!"
"Don't worry, Young Master, I'm loyal to the bone."
Right then a voice floated outside the boarded window: "Qinggua? Sister Hongdou said you wanted me?"
Chouya was hardly hideous—just plump with narrow, squinting eyes that looked less striking than the other maids, earning her the blunt nickname.
"She's here! Turn on the charm!" Chen Haoyu whispered, settling into a chair to watch the show.
For his master's sake—and his own shot at winning Hongdou—Qinggua steeled himself and leaned close to the planks. "Chouya, Young Madam locked me in here, and after eight or nine shichen without seeing you, I asked Hongdou to call you just so I could hear your voice."
Chen Haoyu raised a brow: Look at Qinggua spinning lies without blinking—gotta watch this kid! Ugh, syrupy enough to rot teeth!
A shy whisper floated back through the cracks. "I thought you had eyes for Sister Hongdou... never dreamed you felt that way about me. Truth is, I like you too."
Qinggua froze—faking romance had hooked a genuine heart! He had never guessed she actually fancied him, leaving him tongue-tied.
Pumped up, Chen Haoyu sprang over and hissed in his ear, "Keep talking! She's hooked—this is in the bag!"
Nudged by his master, Qinggua stammered, "Then... we feel the same way..."
"Get to the point!" Chen Haoyu prodded.
"I'm dying to see you, Chouya, yet I'm stuck in here! Could you unlock the door for me?"
A brief hesitation outside. "I want to see you too, yet Miss locked you up—what if I beg her to let you out when she gets back?"
"No use! Young Madam will never let me out! Who knows how long I'll rot in here without seeing you? I miss you, Chouya."
"I miss you too..."
"I didn't even do anything wrong, and she locked me up for nothing, tearing us apart..."
"Wait right there, Qinggua! I'll sneak the key and let you out!"
As her footsteps faded, master and servant slapped palms in triumph.
"So who sneaks out, Young Master—me or you?"
"Me, obviously! Wait—should I run straight to Grandmother and Father, or bolt outside the manor? Forget the elders—straight outside where Zhu Shuzhen can't find me! Done!"
Moments later, the padlock clicked. Both lunged for the door, coiled to bolt—only for Chouya to slip through the gap and kick the door shut behind her, sealing off any sprint.
Throwing her arms straight around Qinggua, she beamed. "Qinggua! I'm so happy you like me too!"
Pinned in her bear hug, Qinggua stiffened, gritting his teeth for freedom's sake.
Seeing the bolt unlatched from inside, Chen Haoyu lunged for the handle while Chouya was distracted—only for Chouya to swing right in front of the door still clutching Qinggua. "Going somewhere, Young Master?"
Marveling at the steel in Zhu Shuzhen's maids, Chen Haoyu bluffed with a smirk. "Don't let me out and I'll order Qinggua to dump you! He's my servant—he obeys every word I say!"
Releasing the hug to clasp Qinggua's hand, Chouya held firm. "Quit trying to scare me, Young Master. Qinggua and I love each other—nobody can tear us apart!"
"Let me out," Chen Haoyu coaxed, "and I'll give you two my blessing!"
"Don't need your blessing, Young Master. I'm only taking Qinggua out—you stay put inside."
Seeing the stalemate, Qinggua spoke up. "Let go a second, Chouya, let me have a quick word with Young Master."
She obeyed at once. Leaning close to Chen Haoyu's ear, Qinggua murmured, "Sit tight, Young Master—let me slip out first and fetch rescue from outside!"
Chen Haoyu nodded and waved to Chouya. "Fine, take Qinggua. I'll stay in here enjoying my vacation."
He watched the strip of daylight flash open and vanish as the heavy padlock clanked shut again, then hurried to the door and yelled through the crack, "Qinggua! Don't forget Grandmother!"
"Got it, Young Master!" Qinggua called back.
Outside, Chouya clung to his arm. Helpless, Qinggua nudged her. "Hurry and put the key back before anyone notices!"
She let go at last. "While Miss is out, go hide in the West Pavilion and wait for me! I'll slip the key back to Asheng in the West Courtyard."
The second Chouya darted off, Qinggua bolted straight out of Moxiang Courtyard toward Old Madam Xia's quarters. Halfway there, he spotted Qianli Xun and Kuqiao strolling back toward him, dove behind an ornamental rockery until they passed, and sprinted on.
