Back in Old Madam Xia's room, the elders had moved on to family chatter while waiting for the storyteller; all three brothers had cleared their morning schedules to listen with their mother.
Bursting past the empty yard straight through the hall doors, Qinggua threw himself onto the floor and squeezed out loud wails: "Old Madam! Save Young Master! Young Madam locked him up! No freedom! Boo-hoo-hoo!"
Chen Jiangmu bristled. "Haoyu's wife went way too far! Mother, since we're all here, lead us over and order her to release him!"
"Yes, Mother, go help Haoyu!" Madam Cui urged.
Old Madam Xia raised a hand to halt them. "Quit howling, Qinggua. Go back and tell Haoyu that from today on, neither his parents nor I will meddle in his courtyard. Sink or swim, his fate is his own."
Qinggua's sobs cut off dead. Blinking in shock, he stammered, "Old Madam, you can't abandon him! Young Madam's fists are lethal—Young Master might not survive!"
Chen Jiangshu and Madam Bao stayed stone-faced while cheering inside—perfect!
Seeing Old Madam Xia mute, Qinggua crawled toward Chen Jianglin. "Master! He's your own flesh and blood—you can't leave him in there!"
"Tell Haoyu I'm thrilled he's locked up," Chen Jianglin replied flat. "Why would I rescue him? He made his bed; let him lie in it."
Desperate, Qinggua swung to Yao Qingyan. "Madam—"
Hardening her heart, Yao Qingyan cut him off. "Save your breath! Dead or alive, Haoyu is his wife's responsibility. Never bring Moxiang Courtyard drama to my door again!"
"Guards!" Old Madam Xia barked. Two servants hurried in. "Haul Qinggua out."
Dragged out past the gate just as the storyteller arrived, Qinggua lingered until lively narration drifted out from inside, let out a long sigh, and slunk away.
#CH 231
#TITLE: The Torture Plan Begins
Walking back into Moxiang Courtyard from Old Madam Xia's rooms, Qianli Xun crossed paths with Chouya hurrying past, cheeks flushed bright as peach blossoms.
"Miss," Chouya curtsied with guilty haste.
"What's the rush?"
"N-nothing, Miss! Got chores—won't keep you!" She scurried off.
Watching her bolt, Qianli Xun raised a brow. "What's gotten into Chouya today?"
"Looked scared you'd scold her," Kuqiao guessed.
"Nah—looked more like she's rushing off to meet a secret boyfriend!" Qianli Xun teased.
Brushing it off, they reached Suxin Thatched Hall, where Qianli Xun remembered her captive. Time to kick off payback. "Fetch the key to Boya Study."
While Kuqiao ran to the West Courtyard, Qianli Xun strolled into the back yard. Glancing at Jingyi Hall's closed doors—Matron Wei must have gone out early to check shops—she felt a swell of quiet gratitude for how thoughtfully the old matron cleared every thorn from her path.
Facing Boya Study next, she figured leaving Chen Haoyu cooped up did not scratch her itch for vengeance. Better to lay out her custom torment plan face to face.
Kuqiao returned with the key and unlocked the heavy padlock.
Inside, Chen Haoyu had been pacing the outer room waiting since Qinggua left. Hearing the lock click, his face lit up—Grandmother had come to rescue him! Bounding to the door, he braced for her doting hugs—only for Zhu Shuzhen and Kuqiao to step in, empty yard behind them.
Qianli Xun shot him a cool smirk. "Still hoping the Chen elders will ride in on white horses? News flash: they handed me full authority to discipline you, and I plan to enjoy every minute of making your life miserable."
"Liar! Grandmother spoils me rotten and Mother's softhearted—they'd never hand me over to you!" Seeing the door standing wide open, he made a break for it.
Qianli Xun slid straight across the threshold. "Trying to bolt? Dream on. Door can stand wide open all day—with me standing here, you aren't clearing a single inch."
Trembling with rage, Chen Haoyu stabbed a finger at her before dropping back into a chair to catch his breath. "Fine—what's your price to let me out?"
"I came here to let you out today."
Hopeful yet wary, he squinted. "Since when are you that nice?"
"Oh, I'm not nice at all." Turning to Kuqiao, she said, "Take notes while I talk."
Kuqiao settled at the desk and smoothed out a fresh sheet.
Qianli Xun faced Chen Haoyu. "Starting today, you can step out of Boya Study—yet you do not set one foot outside Chen Manor."
"Says who?!"
"Says my fists, and says the Chen elders who handed me the whip."
"I don't buy your one-sided story!"
"Believe it or not, behave yourself and listen."
Chen Haoyu clapped both hands over his ears. "Not listening! Not listening! What are you gonna do about it?"
Tired of the noise, Qianli Xun flashed forward and tapped two acupoints. Instantly he froze stone-still and mute, reduced to glaring daggers.
"Much quieter. Now let's review your reform program. First: your monthly allowance is slashed to zero. Want spending money? Earn it yourself."
Unable to speak, Chen Haoyu clenched his fists inside: Zero?! Cutting off even twenty taels! Never earned a copper in my whole life!
"Second, here is your wage sheet," Qianli Xun ticked off. "One: run ten laps around Chen Manor's main loop every day for ten wen. Two: memorize assigned classics and poems each day for thirty wen. Three: complete one daily chore for fifty wen. Four: say 'I'm sorry' to someone you bullied for one tael of silver."
All four popped into her head on the spot—half torment, half boot camp, every single item guaranteed to make him squirm. "Four items to start; I'll add more whenever inspiration strikes. Got all that down, Kuqiao?"
"Every single word, Miss."
"Good. Time for Chen Haoyu to put his thumbprint on it."
Frozen solid, he could only watch in crimson-faced fury while she pried his thumb open, smeared it in the red ink paste Kuqiao held up, and stamped it square onto the paper.
Then she tapped his acupoints free.
The second he could move, Chen Haoyu swung a fist at her. "Zhu Shuzhen! I'm not doing a single damn thing on that list!"
Catching his wrist mid-swing, Qianli Xun twisted his arm behind his back. "Glad you reminded me—penalties! Skip one task, and you empty my chamber pot for one day! Skip two, two days! Skip all four, ten straight days! Refuse altogether, and you're my personal chamber-pot boy for life!"
Wincing in her grip, he spat back, "Chen Manor has plenty of clean latrines—nobody keeps chamber pots for big business, only urinals! Tough luck!"
"Easy fix!" Qianli Xun grinned. "Just for you, I'll start using a chamber pot exclusively—stink your nose right off!"
Outmatched in muscle and mouth alike, Chen Haoyu switched to groveling. "Okay, okay, I apologize, Zhu Shuzhen! Spreading those rumors was my fault—beat me or curse me all you like, just don't cripple me!"
Seeing him fold, Qianli Xun let him go. "Kuqiao, go fetch Hongdou."
Adding the penalty clauses onto the thumbprinted sheet, Kuqiao hurried off.
Relieved the door stayed unlocked, Chen Haoyu slumped back into his chair. "Biggest mistake of my life was marrying you, Zhu Shuzhen. Bet you regret marrying me too?"
Having sworn never to look back once she made her choice, Qianli Xun snapped, "Whether I regret it or not is none of your damn business!"
"Oh, you regret it alright," he prodded. "Why don't we get a mutual divorce so you're free? Look how crazy Prince Yi is over you—he won't blink twice at a second divorce. Come on, let's sit down and talk divorce like adults."
Those two words—"mutual divorce"—sent an unexpected pang through Qianli Xun's chest. She had fought so hard through her first divorce hoping for peace, only to hear her second husband tossing the same words right back. She had no stomach left for another divorce battle; the first had already wrung her dry.
Spotting sadness flicker across her face, Chen Haoyu beamed and pushed his luck. "Wait—don't tell me you fell for me and can't bear to leave? Makes sense—tall, dashing, irresistible to every woman alive! Since you like me, drop the torture and treat me sweet; get me in a good mood and maybe I'll fall for you too, haha—"
Shaking off her gloom in disgust at his oily leer, Qianli Xun snapped, "Shut your filthy mouth! Want a divorce? Then I'll never grant you one! Maybe once I finish torturing you and my temper cools, I'll think about it!"
Seeing anger got him nowhere, he kept teasing. "Word is you moved heaven and earth to divorce Lin Jue, yet when I hand you divorce on a silver platter, you say no! If that isn't love, what is? I never turn down a pretty woman—go on, throw yourself into my arms!"
Nothing triggered Qianli Xun faster than a lecherous smirk. Her fist snapped out—WHAM!
A purple shiner bloomed straight around Chen Haoyu's left eye. Clutching his face, he yelped, "Are you crazy?!"
Pulling back her fist, she snapped, "You're the crazy one! Tease me with that sleazy face again and see what happens!"
Sweat stinging his bruised cheek, he dropped his hand and muttered, "Act like this and heaven knows what Qiao Wenxian and Prince Yi saw in you..."
Hongdou and Kuqiao walked back in, fighting back giggles at the comical purple bruise ringing the young master's eye.
Kuqiao picked up the contract from the desk while Hongdou asked, "Your orders, Miss?"
"Assign two men to shadow Chen Haoyu from this moment on and make sure he finishes every task on this list every day."
"Right away, Miss." Taking the sheet from Kuqiao to memorize, Hongdou hurried out to pick the watchers.
"Can I step outside now?" Chen Haoyu asked.
"Not until your babysitters get here."
So long as the padlock stayed off, he could run straight to Grandmother and weep his case—wait. Where on earth was Qinggua? He had been gone for ages, yet no elder had shown up! Had Zhu Shuzhen actually bought off his whole family?
"Did Grandmother and my parents really put you in charge of disciplining me?"
"Every word," Qianli Xun said with smug pride. "Promised not to meddle, too."
"Don't believe you!"
"Suit yourself. Think I'd unlock your door if I worried about you crying to the elders?"
Hongdou returned with Asheng and another servant. "Miss, Asheng and Sanbao will guard Young Master from now on." Returning the sheet to Kuqiao, she added low, "Both memorized every rule."
Satisfied, Qianli Xun gave her orders. "Stick to the young master like shadows. Don't let him set foot outside Chen Manor; inside the gates he can roam free. Daytime he stays out of Boya Study; at night, once he turns in, lock the door again so he doesn't sneak out after dark."
"Understood, Miss!" both answered.
With everything set, Qianli Xun gave Chen Haoyu a curt huff. "You're free to go."
Without waiting a second, Chen Haoyu vaulted out the door and drank in a deep lungful. "Sweet air of freedom!" Spinning back, he jabbed a finger at her. "Just you wait, Zhu Shuzhen—I'm heading straight to Grandmother!"
Asheng and Sanbao fell right in step behind him toward the front yard.
Her revenge plan was rolling, yet Qianli Xun felt zero joy. Mentioning divorce and Prince Yi had brought Mengrong straight back—the real reason she had accepted Chen Haoyu and refused to divorce again. Mengrong's wedding-day words of hatred still echoed in her ears, freezing every hidden longing inside her chest.
Walking back to Suxin Thatched Hall, she sat staring blankly at her desk while Kuqiao tucked the contract away and kept quiet watch beside her.
#CH 232
#TITLE: No Rescue in Sight, Running Laps Instead
After striking out at Old Madam Xia's courtyard, Qinggua dared not return to Moxiang Courtyard—and clean forgot his date with Chouya—instead idling around the manor gardens until dusk.
Wandering west, he glanced up, spotted Chouya waiting in the West Pavilion, and winced: Tried to help Young Master and got myself hooked instead! Better disappear—stand her up and she'll get the hint.
Doubling back to Moxiang Courtyard, he slipped behind the fresh bamboo groves flanking the gate to wait for a chance to warn his master. Moments later, out strode Chen Haoyu with Asheng and Sanbao right behind him. Figuring the coast was clear, Qinggua popped out from the stalks. "Young Master! Young Madam let you out?"
Blaming Qinggua for failing to fetch rescue, Chen Haoyu cocked a leg—then checked himself remembering Phantom Sidestep—and swung a fist instead. "Sneaking out early to enjoy yourself while leaving me locked up? I'll tan your hide!"
Qinggua dodged aside. "You're out now, Young Master—why stay mad?"
"What good is getting out with these two glued to my back?"
Qinggua eyed Asheng and Sanbao with a grin. "Beats staring at boarded windows!"
"Shut up and come with me to Grandmother's!" Chen Haoyu marched off.
Qinggua jumped in front of him. "Don't waste the trip, Young Master! I already went! Old Madam Xia said she's washing her hands of your courtyard; Master said he's glad you're locked up and you brought it on yourself; Madam said dead or alive, you're Young Madam's business!"
Convinced Qinggua was lying, Chen Haoyu shoved him aside and strode straight to his grandmother's courtyard.
Inside, the storyteller had gone and the second and third branches had left, while Chen Jianglin and Yao Qingyan stayed chatting with Old Madam Xia. A maid hurried in. "Old Madam, Second Young Master is out and heading this way!"
"Bolt the courtyard gate," Old Madam Xia ordered. "Tell him to quit bothering me."
"Yes, Old Madam."
Seeing the ache on Yao Qingyan's face, Old Madam Xia added, "Lock your own courtyard gate when you go back too. Don't soften—soften once and we throw everything away." Pressing a hand over her chest, she murmured, "My heart hurts too, yet we have to endure for Haoyu's own good."
Yao Qingyan bit her lip and stayed silent.
"My fault for failing to raise him right and putting you both through this," Chen Jianglin said. "Everything rides on holding firm now." Both women nodded.
Reaching the bolted gate, Chen Haoyu ordered Qinggua to pound on it. No bolt slid; a maid called through the wood: "Please go back, Second Young Master. Old Madam Xia will no longer meddle in your affairs."
"A servant talking back to me?" Chen Haoyu barked. "Wait till I have Grandmother sell you off tomorrow!"
"I wouldn't dare, Second Young Master—those are Old Madam's own orders."
Switching straight to waterworks, Chen Haoyu wailed at the gate: "Grandmother! Don't abandon me! That tigress let me out, sure, yet she's pure poison! Two thugs tailing me nonstop, mountains of chores—and worst of all, she's forcing me to empty her chamber pot! Boo-hoo! Save me or I'll drop dead!"
Inside, Yao Qingyan gasped. "Empty a chamber pot?! Haoyu's never even dumped his own washbasin—how can Shuzhen make him do something so filthy?"
Old Madam Xia half-rose in distress—"Unthinkable! Unthinkable!"—before forcing herself back onto the couch. "Endure it! Maid, bring cotton to plug my ears!"
Even with cotton tucked in her ears, his wails seeped through, forcing her to clench her jaw. Yao Qingyan swallowed her own protests. Only Chen Jianglin sat unmoved. "Endure bitter trials to stand above others. Too little hardship turned Haoyu rotten; if he keeps going like this he'll end up lower than a night-soil man. Emptying a chamber pot is letting him off easy!"
Getting zero response, Chen Haoyu cranked up the sobs: "Grandmother! Zhu Shuzhen is getting revenge! Yesterday Hongdou slapped me twice—my face still throbs! Just now she punched me right in the eye, didn't even give me salve, and cut off my whole allowance! Boo-hoo!"
Still dead silence. Dropping the sobs, he shouted, "If Grandmother won't stand up for me, I'll go find Mother!"
The maid's voice drifted back through the gate: "Eldest Master and Madam are right inside, Second Young Master. They told me to tell you to go back and obey Young Madam."
Every lifeline snapped at once. For the first time, Chen Haoyu felt the full weight of Zhu Shuzhen's genius at winning over his family.
Asheng stepped forward. "Time to run your laps, Young Master. Skip them and it's chamber-pot duty."
Chen Haoyu threw a punch straight at him. "A servant bossing me around?!"
Asheng caught his fist midair. "Save your breath, Young Master."
Spinning, Chen Haoyu swung at Sanbao, who slipped aside with ease. "No point, Young Master."
Abandoned by family, outmatched by both guards, rage boiled over—and he fired a reflex kick at Qinggua.
Qinggua hopped sideways, flustered enough to shove his master by accident. Chen Haoyu stumbled sideways, almost biting the dirt.
"Qinggua! Tired of living?! You just pushed me!"
"Accident, Young Master, slipped—don't take it to heart!"
Lunging to throttle Qinggua for daring to touch him, Chen Haoyu ran straight into Asheng stepping between them. "Don't waste more time, Young Master—start running."
Qinggua breathed a silent thank-you; without Asheng, he would have been pounded flat.
Friendless and outgunned even by servants, Chen Haoyu hit rock bottom for the first time in his life and sank into a squat on the paving stones.
Concerned, Qinggua crept closer. "Are you alright, Young Master?"
SMACK! Chen Haoyu slapped him across the cheek.
Clutching his stinging face, Qinggua whimpered, "Bullying me again!"
Having vented that pinch of spleen, Chen Haoyu stood up. "If I can't beat you, who else—those two?"
Imagining a reeking chamber pot nearly turned his stomach. A wise man does not fight losing odds—time to run. "Hey! Chen Manor's huge—where do I run?"
"I'll set the pace up front, Sanbao brings up the rear, you run in the middle," Asheng laid out.
Refusing to suffer solo, Chen Haoyu jabbed a finger at Qinggua. "You—run with me!"
"Young Master, I hate running—too exhausting!"
"Look at them—not even my servants, running along anyway, while my own boy plays turtle! Move it, or forget my help chasing girls!"
For Hongdou's sake, Qinggua caved. "If you're running, Young Master, I'm right beside you!"
Down Chen Manor's broad main avenues they jogged: Asheng leading, Sanbao behind, master and servant panting between them. Servants stopped to whisper and point; near Xinglong Pavilion on the west road, cheeky clerks who feared no young master hollered out, "Out for a jog, Second Young Master? Since when did you take up fitness?"
Too winded to swear back, Chen Haoyu gasped at Asheng, "Can—can we—take a breather?"
Without looking back, Asheng kept striding. "Not even one lap down and you're wheezing, Young Master! Ten laps to go—push through and it gets easier!"
Suddenly a fierce female shout split the air behind them: "Qinggua! Freeze right there!"
Everyone skidded to a halt and spun around, Chen Haoyu thrilled for any excuse to catch his breath.
It was Chouya. After waiting half the morning in the West Pavilion, realization had dawned that Qinggua had played her heart just to break out. Boiling mad, she had marched onto the main road hunting answers and caught him jogging right past.
Seeing her furious glare tickled Chen Haoyu. "Oh boy, Qinggua—you're toast."
"I only put my charm on the line for you, Young Master!" Qinggua hissed back. "Quick—give me a way out!"
"Wise men dodge immediate storms," Chen Haoyu whispered. "Sweet-talk her for now."
Putting on a sheepish grin, Qinggua trotted over. "Sorry to stand you up, Chouya! Not that I skipped the pavilion—look, Young Madam let Young Master out and ordered me to jog with him!"
Chouya narrowed her eyes. "Really?"
"Would I lie? Ask Young Master!"
"You two breathe through the same nose—I'm asking Sanbao! Sanbao, did Miss order Qinggua to run with Young Master?"
"Miss only ordered Young Master to run," Sanbao answered deadpan. "Young Master dragged Qinggua along himself."
Chouya whipped back to Qinggua, fists balled. "Lying to me again!"
Terrified, Qinggua stammered, "Didn't lie—I can't disobey either master or mistress!"
"What about saying you liked me?" Chouya demanded, caring zero about their audience. "Was that a lie too?!"
Chen Haoyu beamed like a front-row theatergoer—nothing spiced up dull jogging like live romance drama! Asheng breathed a quiet sigh of relief, glad Qinggua wasn't after Hongdou after all.
Qinggua weighed his two options in a split second: confess and get pounded flat now, or play along and stay stuck with Chouya forever. Before he could blurt the truth, Chouya laid down the law: "If you lied to me, I'll shadow you every waking hour so you never marry anyone else—wherever you run, I follow until you marry me!"
Even Chen Haoyu grimaced on his behalf.
"Chouya's dead sincere, Qinggua—don't play games with her," Sanbao chimed in.
"Don't worry, Chouya, Qinggua takes love serious," Asheng piled on.
Deciding survival beat long-term strategy, Qinggua flashed a weak grin. "Every word I told you came straight from my heart, Chouya! Hurry on back—I have to run with Young Master, or if he flunks his laps and gets stuck emptying chamber pots, guess who ends up doing the dumping?"
Hearing he hadn't denied it made Chouya beam. Holding back the urge to hug him in front of everyone, she blushed. "Alright—keep jogging with Young Master. I'll head back!" She scampered off in shy joy.
"Show's over, Young Master," Asheng called. "Back to running!"
Half-disappointed the comedy ended so soon, Chen Haoyu groaned and dragged his sore legs back into a trot along the manor road.
#CH 233
#TITLE: Resistance Gets Him Nowhere
Chen Manor sprawled wide enough to wind a man after three laps, let alone ten. By the final two rounds, Chen Haoyu and Qinggua were gasping on leaden legs, reduced to a crawl while Asheng and Sanbao kept pace at a brisk walk.
"Young Master," Qinggua wheezed, "Young Madam only made you run—can I sit out?"
"No... way!" Chen Haoyu panted. "Running solo is... too embarrassing! Keep moving!"
Qinggua shut up and shuffled on. Rounding a bend, they spotted Chen Haodong standing dead center in the lane, beaming from ear to ear.
Chen Haodong was having the time of his life: Watching you get put through the wringer feels amazing! Time to stir the pot and push you straight into another clash with that tigress!
Spotting his eldest cousin like a drowning man grabbing driftwood, Chen Haoyu found a fresh burst of wind, jogged forward, and threw his arms around him. "Big Brother Dong! Ran half the morning and not one elder lifted a finger for me—only you care!"
Putting on a warm show of outrage, Chen Haodong patted his back. "The second I heard, I rushed straight to Grandmother's, only to find her gate bolted—and Eldest Uncle and Aunt's locked tight too! None of the other elders dared cross Old Madam Xia, so I waited out here to help you figure a way out."
Asheng and Sanbao stood back respectfully without interrupting, giving Qinggua a welcome chance to flop down and catch his breath.
Letting go, Chen Haoyu pleaded, "Give me a plan! How do I dodge that tigress's punishments?"
Instead of answering right away, Chen Haodong peered at his bruised left eye with keen relish. "What happened to your face?"
"That tigress punched me!"
Keep hitting him—beat him black and blue! Chen Haodong cheered inside while putting on a stern mask. "Wait here while I give those two a piece of my mind."
Marching over to Asheng and Sanbao, he barked, "Blind, insolent servants! Daring to bully Chen Manor's Second Young Master in broad daylight? Who gave you the gall? Wait till I report to Old Madam Xia and have you both sold to the countryside for good!"
Before Sanbao could talk back, Asheng raised a hand and answered calm. "Eldest Young Master may not know—our mistress received full permission from Old Madam Xia, Eldest Master, and Eldest Madam to discipline the young master, and ordered us to supervise."
Feigning wrath, Chen Haodong snapped, "Step aside and wait right here! My brother and I are sitting in that pavilion to talk. If Second Sister-in-law has a problem, send her to me!"
Steering Chen Haoyu toward the nearby pavilion, he drew a big thumbs-up from his cousin. "Awesome, Big Brother Dong!"
"Honestly, Haoyu, you're shaming every Chen man," Chen Haodong chided as they sat. "Let me teach you how a real man handles his wife."
Chen Haoyu sighed. "Not like I want to lose face—Zhu Shuzhen is a monster, and her lackeys too! Can't beat those two and can't outrun them, so I had to play nice."
Chen Haodong leaned in to fan the flames. "A real man never rolls over—you push back! Tough as she is, she won't dare cripple you or put your life in danger. Use your head: why did Grandmother and Aunt wash their hands of it? Because they know for a fact she won't actually hurt you! So what are you scared of? Refuse everything flat!"
Light dawned on Chen Haoyu's face. "Genius! Why didn't I see that? No wonder Sister-in-law is so gentle and obedient around you! Forget that last lap—I'm marching straight back to defy Zhu Shuzhen to her face!"
"That's the spirit!" Chen Haodong applauded. Watching his cousin stride off puffed with swagger, he chuckled to himself: Go lock horns with your wife so I can sit back and enjoy the fireworks!
Seeing his master return, Qinggua bounced up. "Rested enough, Young Master? One lap left—I'll jog it with you!"
"Who said I'm running?" Chen Haoyu jabbed a finger at Asheng and Sanbao. "Listen up! I'm skipping the last lap and going back to Moxiang Courtyard. Let's see what Zhu Shuzhen can do about it!"
Unwilling to rough up their young master, the two servants trailed behind with helpless looks. "Young Master," Asheng cautioned, "skipping tasks means emptying chamber pots."
Chen Haoyu spun around. "Empty my foot! I'm not touching a chamber pot! What's she going to do about it?"
Trotting alongside, Qinggua whispered, "What did Eldest Young Master tell you to make you so bold all of a sudden?"
"Pure gold," Chen Haoyu grinned.
Back inside Moxiang Courtyard, three unfamiliar maids stood lined up in a row. Chen Haoyu dimly recognized them from Third Uncle's yard—girls he had once flirted with—yet ignored them as he turned toward the back courtyard.
A maid stepped straight across his path. "Young Master, Miss instructed that once your run ends, you apologize to these three maids, recite the Analects and Wang Wei's poems, and sweep Miss's room."
About to blow up, Chen Haoyu remembered his cousin's gold nugget—she would not dare hurt him—and broke into an easy smirk. "What's your name? Don't think I've seen you."
"I'm Amei. I fought Master Jiang's men for you and came to the brothel with Miss to haul you back—you just never noticed. Hardly surprising since you've barely slept at home since the wedding."
"Ah, Amei." He jabbed a thumb back at Asheng. "His little sister! Think you two siblings can boss me around? Dream on. Tell Zhu Shuzhen I'm not scared of her—whatever she tells me to do, I'm doing the exact opposite!"
Turning again toward Boya Study, Qianli Xun's voice sliced across the yard: "Chen Haoyu! Dying to empty my chamber pot? Never knew you had such quirky hobbies!"
He halted and faced her square. "Let me repeat myself: I'm not lifting a finger on your list, and I'm sure as hell not touching your chamber pot!"
Qianli Xun flashed forward and pinned his arm behind his back. "Doing it or not?"
Wincing through the twist, he yelled, "Not doing it! You don't dare maim me or kill me—I'm not scared of anything! Try me!"
Caught off guard that he had spotted her hard limit, Qianli Xun shoved him loose. "You don't have a single copper on you—don't you want to earn silver?"
Rubbing his shoulder, he sneered, "I can't leave the house anyway—free food and roof right here! Why bother earning silver?"
"Then I'll keep you locked in Moxiang Courtyard forever!"
Gleeful at backing her into a corner, Chen Haoyu grinned. "Fine by me! I'll become a stay-at-home hermit! Partied enough, tasted every delicacy, seen every sight—never tried staying indoors forever, so consider it a fresh experience!"
Dead pig unafraid of boiling water—he had nailed her blind spot. Qianli Xun paused two seconds, then found the kill shot.
"Refuse my rules, and I'll have a wooden placard painted reading 'I AM A MASSIVE SCUMBAG,' hang it around your neck, truss you up in ropes, and have my servants parade you around Chen Manor first—then through every busy street in Lin'an every single day! Your pick: follow the list, or enjoy your daily city parade?"
Chen Haoyu exploded, jabbing a shaking finger at her. "Y-you! What good does parading me through the streets do you?! I'm your husband on paper!"
The wilder he got, the wider Qianli Xun smiled. "Key words: on paper! Your humiliation, not mine! As long as I settle the score for last year's slander, I sleep great! Since the day I married in, did you ever think of me as your wife while camping out at Chunxiang Brothel? Why should I care about your face?"
Scrambling for another deflection, he put on an arch grin. "Wait—don't tell me you really fell for me? Hard to blame you, given how dashing I am—"
"Which ear heard me say I like you? I only like watching you squirm!" Cutting him flat, she barked, "Asheng! Go grab a wooden board!"
"Zhu Shuzhen, are you serious?!" Chen Haoyu roared.
Stepping right up to him, Qianli Xun cracked her knuckles. "Dead serious! Care for a matching shiner on the other eye?"
Three rounds in, and Big Brother Dong's grand strategy lay in smoking ruins. Knowing this woman never bluffed—paraded through Lin'an wearing a scumbag sign would kill his social life forever—he folded.
"Fine, fine, put the board away! I'll play ball! I spread your rumors, I screwed up—consider this paying my debt!"
"Should've said that five minutes ago," Qianli Xun quipped. "Amei, take him over to apologize to those three maids."
"Right this way, Young Master."
Burning with humiliation yet out of moves—blaming Zhu Xiyan all over again thanks to Master Jiang's lie—Chen Haoyu muttered over his shoulder, "Your father's a sly old fox, Zhu Shuzhen! Ruined my life!"
Clueless what he meant, Qianli Xun brushed it off. "Quit stalling and apologize!"
Stopping before the three maids, Chen Haoyu glared up and down. "All I did was pinch your cheeks and hold your hands once, and I have to apologize? Spill it—how'd that tigress dig you three up?"
"Hongdou passed word that Second Young Master planned to apologize to every servant he'd ever wronged," one maid giggled. "We came out of sheer curiosity to see it with our own eyes!"
"Curious for you, agony for me—apologizing to servants! What's this world coming to?"
"Apologize, Young Master," Amei prompted.
"Quit nagging!" Shooting a look at Qianli Xun's icy stare, he gritted out, "I'm sorry."
Never having heard a master say sorry before, all three maids burst into giggles.
"One won't do—three maids, two more left," Amei reminded him.
"I'm sorry! I'm sorry!"
Laughing, one maid teased, "Watch your hands around us from now on, Second Young Master, or you'll spend all year saying sorry!" With that, all three trotted off thrilled.
Chen Haoyu spun back. "Satisfied, Zhu Shuzhen?"
"Just getting warmed up—nowhere near satisfied."
Envious of the three maids, Qinggua bounced over to Qianli Xun. "Young Madam, can I get in line for an apology too?"
"Of course! He bullies you nonstop—owes you a mountain of apologies."
Qinggua lit up.
Watching his own personal lackey jump into the apology line right in front of him snapped Chen Haoyu's last thread of dignity. Lunging forward, he threw a wild kick—whiffed clean past Qinggua—and crashed flat onto the ground from his own momentum.
Qinggua hopped back to help him up. "Still kicking me, Young Master?"
Chen Haoyu grabbed Qinggua's collar from the floor. "Anybody else gets an apology—not you!"
"Young Madam already said yes!"
Tightening his grip, Chen Haoyu hissed, "You're MY servant! You listen to ME!"
Qinggua gave a reluctant nod.
Bored with their antics, Qianli Xun turned and walked back indoors; Kuqiao shot Asheng a look and followed.
Shoving Qinggua off, Chen Haoyu climbed up with Qinggua steadying his arm. "Back to Boya Study for memorization, Young Master," Asheng prompted.
Waving a fist at both guards, Chen Haoyu growled, "Wait till the day I flatten both of you ghosts!" Still, beaten for now, he had to study—and needed an outlet first. "Qinggua, walk in front of me."
"Why?"
"Do as I say and quit yapping!"
Unsuspecting, Qinggua stepped ahead. Focusing every ounce of venom into his right leg, Chen Haoyu booted him square in the seat of his pants. "Take that, Zhu Shuzhen!"
#CH 234
#TITLE: A Single Tear Reveals True Feeling
With no eyes on his backside, Qinggua took the kick full force and pitched forward off balance, headed straight for a face-plant into the stones.
In a flash, Chouya darted out and caught him by the arms. "Qinggua! You okay?"
"Whew—thanks, Chouya!"
"Don't mention it." Releasing him, Chouya bobbed a crisp curtsy toward Chen Haoyu. "Young Master, please stop bullying my Qinggua from now on."
Having failed even to vent his spleen and now lectured by a maid, Chen Haoyu felt a crush of humiliation unlike anything in his spoiled life. Looking around—a courtyard no longer his, servants all loyal to Zhu Shuzhen, even lowly Qinggua defended while he stood completely alone—heat stung his eyes until his rims flushed red. Without another word, he turned and walked toward Boya Study with Asheng and Sanbao trailing behind.
Chouya blinked after him. "Qinggua, did you see that? Did Young Master just cry?"
"Huh? Young Master crying? No way! He makes other folks cry—never shed a tear in his life!"
Amei walked over. "I saw it too—eyes bright red, looked crushed. Can't blame him, going up against someone as tough as Miss."
Ignoring Amei, Chouya tugged Qinggua's sleeve. "Meet me at the West Pavilion when you get a break."
"No shame at all, Chouya—I'm standing right here!" Amei teased.
"Then make yourself scarce!" Chouya nudged Amei off, who laughed and wandered back to the West Courtyard.
Worried over his master—and eager to shake Chouya—Qinggua backed away. "Got to go check on Young Master!" He sprinted toward the back courtyard.
Too busy with chores to chase him, Chouya muttered at his fleeing heels, "He kicks you all day and you still chase after him! Begging for bruises—see if I save you next time!"
Walking back to Boya Study, Chen Haoyu fought to blink back the sting, yet one hot tear slipped down his cheek. Halting to brush it away with his sleeve, an old drinking boast from Juxiang Tower flashed straight back into his head.
One night, lounging with a pack of rich playboys swapping crass jokes, the talk had drifted to true love. Every rake around the table named some girl who had once stolen his heart—everyone except Chen Haoyu.
"With all the blossoms you've plucked, Brother Chen, didn't even one move your heart?" a friend had asked.
One courtesan under each arm, Chen Haoyu had leered, "I just like playing with them—who bothers with true love?"
"Still, what kind of woman would actually make you fall for real?" another friend pressed, joined by a chorus insisting he answer since everyone else had spilled.
Waving both courtesans away to the corner, Chen Haoyu had turned half-serious. "Can't remember how much I cried as a toddler, yet since I grew sense, I've never shed a tear. If any girl ever makes me cry, that's the one I'll fall for."
"What if she's ugly as sin?" someone jeered.
"With my standards, an ugly face never even enters my sight—how could she make me cry?"
Standing in the back yard now, Chen Haoyu stared at his damp sleeve and froze: Wait... did I just fall for that tigress?!
He shook his head hard. Impossible! We're mortal enemies! Why on earth did I shed a tear then? No, no—drunk talk doesn't count!
Shaken, he crossed the threshold into Boya Study while Asheng and Sanbao took posts outside.
Hongdou stood tidying the desk and curtsied. "Young Master, Miss picked out this stack of books for you. Start with the Analects and Wang Wei's poems—five chapters of the Analects and five poems every day. Once finished, report to Suxin Thatched Hall for Miss to test you."
Staring at the towering stack of volumes gave Chen Haoyu an instant migraine, sweeping away his strange mood: Hateful tigress! Fall for her? Never in a million years!
"Better get started, Young Master," Hongdou nudged.
Rubbing his hollow belly, he grumbled, "Ran all morning on empty—feed me first, memorize after."
"Start reading now; I'll bring your lunch."
After Hongdou left, Qinggua crept in and blinked at the unprecedented sight of his master seated before a pile of books. Grinning, he edged closer. "Young Master, Chouya and Amei swear you cried out there—true?"
"Scram! Quit bugging me! None of your business if I cried!"
"So it IS true! I know you're miserable, Young Master, yet with the elders sitting out and Young Madam fierce as iron, you're stuck eating dirt. Want to hear an idea?"
Glaring at the books, Chen Haoyu sighed lifelessly. "What bright idea could you possibly have?"
Qinggua leaned over the desk. "Going head-to-head flopped—why not try going soft?"
Chen Haoyu's eyes snapped up, gleaming. "Didn't know you had brains in there! Spill it!"
Thrilled not to get yelled at, Qinggua hit his stride. "You two are husband and wife! Turn on the charm and treat her sweet! Tough as she is, she's still a woman—women melt over soft words and gentle care. Coax her enough and her heart softens; how could she keep swinging fists? Act like a model husband, and once she sees your good side, she'll want a real marriage and quit torturing you!"
Chen Haoyu chewed on that. "Sweet talk I can manage—never tried being a good husband, though. How's it done?"
"Look right at Eldest Master! Treat Young Madam the exact way your father treats Eldest Madam!"
"Brilliant! My own father is a walking textbook—I'll copy him!" Chen Haoyu slapped the desk in excitement—until his gaze dropped back to the stack of books and deflated. "Still stuck memorizing these, though. Do I read or not?"
"Read!" Qinggua flipped the top book open before him. "Think about it: has Eldest Master ever crossed Eldest Madam?"
"Well, no—only Mother never bullied Father! That tigress is flat-out bullying me, and I hate books!"
"Cool down, Young Master." Patting his master's back gently, Qinggua reasoned, "Ask yourself why she's coming at you so hard. Because you wronged her first—every servant in Chen Manor knows you started last year's rumors!"
"Even you know about that?!"
