That hit home hard. Without his rumor campaign, that line would have stayed inside poetry circles instead of becoming market-stall filth. The guilt really did sit squarely on his shoulders.
"Alright, alright, my bad—I'll memorize!" Cracking open the pages, he groaned at how long-winded ancient sages were, leaving endless headaches for descendants.
Hongdou arrived with lunch; the instant Chen Haoyu stuffed his belly, drowsiness knocked him flat, face planted across the open Analects snoring away. Qinggua sighed and nodded off on his feet beside him.
A sharp poke jerked Qinggua awake—Chouya stood beside him whispering, "Come to the West Pavilion with me!"
Uninterested in Chouya and afraid Hongdou would see them together, Qinggua steered her away from his sleeping master and cooked up an instant escape hatch. "Stop coming to find me, Chouya."
"Why?"
"Young Master's miserable under Young Madam's thumb—how can I be in the mood for romance?"
"He's him and you're you!"
"Wrong! When Young Master hurts, I hurt!"
"So you'll only meet me in the West Pavilion once Miss and Young Master make up?"
Qinggua nodded fast.
"That'll take till doomsday!" Chouya sighed.
"Your pick: leave me alone, or help Young Master patch things up with Young Madam!"
"Patch things up? Impossible! Guess I have to stay away..." Shoulders slumped, Chouya drifted out.
Grinning at his own genius for brushing her off, Qinggua paused—wait: if Chouya thought reconciliation was impossible, would his soft-approach plan flop too?
Right then his master mumbled in his sleep: "Zhu Shuzhen... just wait... I'll beat you till petals scatter..."
Just a dream. A beat later, four soft syllables drifted off Chen Haoyu's lips: "I... like... you..."
Eyes popping wide, Qinggua leaned close. "Who do you like, Young Master?"
Slurred yet unmistakable, Chen Haoyu murmured, "Zhu... Shuzhen..."
A grin spread across Qinggua's face. "Well I'll be! Young Master secretly fell for Young Madam without even realizing it while awake! Hope they hit it off fast so us servants get our normal lives back!"
In his dream, Zhu Shuzhen landed a haymaker knocking him down a pit, jolting him upright with a gasp. Rubbing his eyes, he asked, "What hour is it?"
"Hour of the Monkey—mid-afternoon."
"Already?! I didn't memorize a single line! Now what?"
"Better cram fast!"
Before he could crack a page, Hongdou walked in. "Study hour's up, Young Master. Time to recite for Miss."
"Give me a little longer?"
"No! Miss's schedule is iron!"
"Fine, quit yelling!" Dragging his feet out the door, Chen Haoyu left Qinggua trailing behind wincing—zero lines memorized meant a royal chewing-out ahead.
#CH 235
#TITLE: Soft Tactics, Soft Tactics, Soft Tactics
Stepping into Suxin Thatched Hall, where ink and old paper scented the air, Chen Haoyu noticed for the first time how pleasant the smell was. Seated by the tea table sipping her bowl, Zhu Shuzhen without a scowl looked breathtaking—small wonder Prince Yi had lost his head over her, when even Chen Haoyu's own chest skipped a beat.
Shaking his head hard to snap out of it, he thought: What's gotten into me? Focus!
"Young Master is here, Miss," Hongdou announced.
Qianli Xun set down her bowl. "Got it. Go handle your chores."
Unable to peel his eyes off her, Chen Haoyu mused inside: If this tigress ever softened up, she'd make one heck of a wife—brilliant, skilled in martial arts, ready to back me up if anyone picks on me outside...
"What're you gawking at, Chen Haoyu?"
Her sharp bark jolted him back to earth. "I came to see you—who else should I look at, Kuqiao or Qinggua behind me?"
Skipping banter, Qianli Xun asked, "Well? Recite what you memorized."
"Too short on time—didn't memorize any."
"What? Not a single line?! Over a full hour and not even one poem?!"
Chen Haoyu nodded.
"Kuqiao! Fetch the wooden ruler!"
Kuqiao brought the ferule and handed it over. Rising, Qianli Xun stepped up to him. "Hold out your hand!"
To his own astonishment, Chen Haoyu stuck his palm straight out like a scolded schoolboy.
Caught off guard by his total lack of pushback, Qianli Xun blinked. "What's gotten you so docile all of a sudden?"
Seizing his cue, Chen Haoyu rolled out the soft approach. "No more fighting you. Whatever you tell me to do, I'll obey."
That sucked every drop of fun out of hitting him. "Why waste effort smacking your palm when I still need your hands to clean my room?"
Yes! Soft tactics worked like magic! Behind his back, Chen Haoyu slipped Qinggua a sly thumbs-up, making the boy beam with pride.
Handing the ruler back to Kuqiao, Qianli Xun returned to her desk. "Dust every corner of my rooms inside and out—no help from Qinggua. And stay at least three feet away from my writing desk."
Keeping his tone breezy and compliant, Chen Haoyu said, "Dusting's a cinch, I'll handle it solo—just let Qinggua rinse out the rags for me, okay?"
Baffled by his sudden personality transplant, Qianli Xun waved him off. "Quit yapping and get to work." Picking up her brush, she went back to her huaben as though he weren't there.
Qinggua rolled up his master's sleeves and handed him a damp cloth. Wiping shelves and screens with surprising care, Chen Haoyu stole glances at Zhu Shuzhen—absorbed over her manuscript, looking nothing at all like a tigress.
His mind jumped back to last year on West Lake, seeing her nestled soft in Qiao Wenxian's arms at the prow of a boat. Back then he could not fathom how a fierce bruiser melted so tender beside a fragile scholar; now he understood—love brought out a woman's softness. Now that fate had landed her under his roof, if she ever fell for him, maybe she would turn into a purring kitten too!
Then gloom hit him. Look at her past suitors: Qiao Wenxian had poetic genius and looks that made Lin'an girls swoon; Prince Yi had royal rank and lethal fists. What did Chen Haoyu bring to the table?
Glancing over at homely Qinggua—built for Chouya yet fearlessly chasing Hongdou—sparked a boost of nerve. He crooked a finger and dropped his voice as Qinggua leaned in.
"Quick question: if folks told you you're way out of Hongdou's league, would you still chase her?"
"Of course! Who cares what folks say? I like her—nothing else matters!"
Chen Haoyu shot him a second thumbs-up, leaving Qinggua over the moon.
Qinggua's grit lit a fire under Chen Haoyu. Why overthink? Brilliant as Qiao Wenxian and Prince Yi were, heaven still handed her to Chen Haoyu! Roll up his sleeves and go for it—no reason he couldn't win her heart!
Pumped with fresh resolve, he scrubbed every nook and beam outside her desk perimeter for half an hour straight. Kuqiao ran a fingertip along a windowsill, checked it, and admitted, "Who knew besides haunting brothels, Young Master dusts as well as any maid!"
"Watch that tongue! Starting today I'm done with brothels. I'm a married man now—hanging around brothels invites gossip and hurts my wife's feelings."
Glancing toward Zhu Shuzhen, she acted deaf to his noble speech, setting her brush down only to say, "Qinggua, go call Asheng." Kuqiao quietly stowed her pages.
Waiting for Asheng, Chen Haoyu watched her open a volume and lose herself in the text. What was so gripping inside ink and paper? To win her over, he needed book learning too—starting tomorrow he'd memorize for real and blow her mind!
Asheng stepped in. "Your orders, Miss?"
"Report on Chen Haoyu's running."
"Eight and a half laps total, Miss," Asheng answered straight. "Stopped twice—once to watch a spat, once to sit in a pavilion with Eldest Young Master."
Qianli Xun's face turned stern. "Two out of four tasks finished. Chen Haoyu, starting tomorrow morning, two straight days of emptying my chamber pot. Understood?"
Tempest flared in his gut—only for Chen Haoyu to hammer it down with a silent chant: Soft tactics, soft tactics, stay soft! Soft tactics, soft tactics, stay soft!
Magic—his temper cooled flat. Flashing a sunny smile, he said, "Whatever you say, Wife. I'll obey every word."
Caught off balance, Qianli Xun bristled. "Don't call me 'Wife'!"
"What should I call you then, Wife?"
"Still saying it?!"
"Shuzhen."
"Swallow something funny? Put my surname back on!"
"Zhu Shuzhen."
Same three syllables as before, yet rolling off his tongue with an eerie warmth that set Qianli Xun's radar pinging. One single day of punishment couldn't transform a lifelong rake—this had to be a new angle. Hard fights she knew how to smash; soft pliancy threw her completely off rhythm. Stay sharp—don't fall for his act!
"Kuqiao, bring his wages."
Kuqiao counted coins into his palm. "One tael of silver and fifty wen, Young Master. Miss keeps her word, and expects you to serve your penalty tomorrow."
Riding the momentum of soft tactics—and his own genuine stirring feelings—Chen Haoyu pushed all-in, handing the coins right back to Kuqiao. "This is punishment—how could I take payment? Keep every copper; I accept my penalty gladly."
Both Kuqiao and Qianli Xun stared in shock.
"What do I do with this, Miss?" Kuqiao asked.
Refusing to buy his saint act, Qianli Xun countered, "Take it to the West Courtyard and split it among the servants—tell them Chen Haoyu earned them a bonus."
Catching the bait to make him snap, Chen Haoyu ran his silent mantra twice—Soft tactics, stay soft!—and beamed wider. "Right! Listen to Young Madam and pass it around! I'll earn you guys silver every day—even more tomorrow! Don't leave out my boy Qinggua!"
"Thank you, Young Master!" Qinggua cheered.
Thrown completely off stride by his sudden thick skin, Qianli Xun pivoted to tomorrow's schedule. "Besides emptying my chamber pot, finish your laps and memorization. For your chore..." She eyed the sprawling yard. "Sweep the entire main courtyard—Asheng inspects. Fail, and more chamber pots. As for your apology..." Her gaze landed on Qinggua. "You bully Qinggua nonstop. Tomorrow apologize to him in front of every servant in Moxiang Courtyard."
Fearing his master would blow a gasket, Qinggua jumped in. "Forget me, Young Madam! Bullying other servants is wrong, yet kicking me is his right!"
One quick silent mantra—Soft tactics, stay soft!—and Chen Haoyu smiled easy. "Don't talk like that, Qinggua. Tomorrow I'll apologize to you fair and square."
Keeping her chilly mask up, Qianli Xun still noticed the purple swelling around his eye. "Kuqiao, grab a jar of bruise salve."
Kuqiao pocketed the silver, fetched a porcelain jar from the inner room, and handed it to him. "One coat tonight, Young Master, and that bruise will vanish by morning."
Chen Haoyu clutched the jar like pure gold—her very first show of concern! At this rate, victory was right around the corner!
Unwilling to face this unsettling new Chen Haoyu another second, Qianli Xun waved him away. "Get back to Boya Study and quit annoying me."
Once they left, Kuqiao spoke up. "Miss, doesn't Young Master feel like a completely different person?"
"Illusion—pure act!" Qianli Xun scoffed. "How could Chen Haoyu reform overnight? Just a new ploy. Give him two days and the mask drops. Besides, my grudge isn't settled yet—I don't want him reforming this fast!"
"Yet he's your husband, Miss," Kuqiao reminded her. "Him turning decent only helps you."
"What—don't you want me getting payback?"
"Of course I do! If anyone else had spread those rumors, I'd slap them raw myself! Only he's the groom—I don't want you going through a second divorce. If he turns into a good man and treats you right, isn't that the best outcome?"
"Even if he turns into a saint, it means nothing to me." Living under one roof without killing each other was her ceiling; falling for Chen Haoyu was out of the question.
Back in Boya Study after nightfall, Qinggua dabbed salve across his master's shiner. "Your soft words worked wonders, Young Master! Young Madam couldn't even stay mad at you!"
"Credit goes to your sharp head," Chen Haoyu beamed. "Once my life gets back to normal, I'll reward you big."
"Skip the reward—just keep your word and help me land Hongdou!"
Chen Haoyu winced. "Hongdou's clearly not biting. Pick someone else—Chouya practically throws herself at you!"
Capping the salve jar, Qinggua shook his head firm. "Don't want easy—I want Hongdou!"
"Alright, alright—once I win over Zhu Shuzhen, I'll play matchmaker for you."
Today marked the biggest turning point of Chen Haoyu's life, one he would never forget—nor the very first woman who had ever brought a tear to his eye. Asked why that old drunken vow held true, he couldn't explain; tossed off half-joking back then, today it had come real. Falling for someone felt wonderful—even her fiercest quirks looked adorable now.
Sitting there, Chen Haoyu let out a goofy chuckle. "Heh heh..."
Watching him grin like a loon, Qinggua shook his head: Dumping chamber pots at dawn tomorrow, and he's sitting here giggling!
#CH 236
#TITLE: A Bouquet of Roses to Declare His Heart
Only when Asheng pulled the doors of Boya Study shut and clicked the padlock home did Chen Haoyu snap out of his dreamy grin. "Locking me in again? Must be scared I'll sneak off to Chunxiang Brothel! Just admit you like me already! Relax—even if you chased me toward Chunxiang Brothel with a broom, I wouldn't go!"
Qinggua pressed a palm to his master's forehead. "No fever... why are you talking crazy?"
Chen Haoyu swatted his hand away. "Quit poking me! Why would I have a fever?"
"You think Young Madam locking your door means she's jealous about Chunxiang Brothel?"
"What else?"
"Do soft tactics fry your brain or something?" Qinggua fretted.
"Not crazy talk—truth!"
"You're really quitting Chunxiang Brothel for good?"
Resting his chin in his palm with a goofy smile, Chen Haoyu sighed, "What's fun about a brothel? Played out! Right now all I want is staying home in Moxiang Courtyard."
Certain now, Qinggua beamed. "Wonderful—peaceful days ahead for us!"
"Flipping fast, aren't you? One second ago you thought I was delirious!"
Edging back out of arm's reach, Qinggua asked, "Young Master... did you actually fall for Young Madam?"
Far from taking offense, Chen Haoyu blinked. "Shows that plain, huh? Even you spotted it! Who'd ever believe I fell for that tigress? Feels like a dream even to me."
"Feels unreal to me too!" Pouring a bowl of tea for his master, Qinggua marvelled, "Cursing her blue at noon and head over heels by night—isn't that awful fast?"
"Ever hear the phrase 'changing in the blink of an eye'?"
Remembering the afternoon nap, Qinggua hinted, "Think back, Young Master—maybe you fell for her way earlier and just didn't realize it."
Replaying the past year—getting thrashed at Yongtai Teahouse, bumping into her in the bamboo grove, spending months obsessing over how to get even while "Zhu Shuzhen" looped nonstop through his skull—Chen Haoyu realized no woman had ever occupied his thoughts half that much. Maybe she had sneaked into his heart all along behind his grudge, until one single tear of wounded pride today tore off the blindfold.
"Since when did you get so good at reading me?" he marveled.
Glowing with pride, Qinggua spilled the rest. "When you napped across the desk today, you called Young Madam's name in your sleep and said you liked her—I was standing right beside you!"
Chen Haoyu beamed brighter than ever—falling in love for the very first time and having accidentally married her already! "Qinggua, starting tomorrow I'm turning over a brand-new leaf to blow Zhu Shuzhen's socks off!"
"Why wait till tomorrow? Your sweet talk today already had her reeling!"
"Heh heh! Found her Achilles' heel at last! Keep pouring on the soft charm till she melts into a sweet little bride curled up in my arms—using those fists to guard me instead of clobbering me! Heh heh..." Drool practically glistened at the corner of his mouth.
At crack of dawn, Asheng and Sanbao unlocked Boya Study and hauled Chen Haoyu out of bed. Never an early riser, he swallowed his urge to curse, thought of his new feelings, sprang up bright-eyed, dressed with Qinggua's help, and tied cloths across both their noses and mouths.
Outside Suxin Thatched Hall, Asheng tapped the door. Kuqiao cracked it open, set a chamber pot on the step without a word, and shut the door again.
A wave of foul reek rolled out. Asheng and Sanbao plugged their noses and spun away; even through cloth masks, master and servant gagged.
Chen Haoyu muttered inside: Smell like that doesn't match a face that pretty—ah well, love overlooks little flaws! "What are you staring at, Qinggua? Grab the pot and dump it!"
Obeying with watering eyes, Qinggua hauled the pot off toward the latrines while the stench drifted away behind him.
Indoors, Kuqiao waved a lit incense stick through the room, groaning, "Reeks to high heaven! We really doing this again tomorrow?"
Dressed early and staring blankly at the tea set, Qianli Xun answered, "One more day."
"Praying Young Master aces every chore today, or I'll be stuck digging up foul manure every dawn till Suxin Thatched Hall turns into Stink-Pot Hall!"
Her complaint hit close to home—Qianli Xun's own stomach still churned from the smell. Still, she sat quiet, lost in thought.
Noticing her mistress hadn't moved or spoken since waking, Kuqiao paused with the incense. "Look down, Miss—feeling unwell?"
Qianli Xun looked up. "Kuqiao, am I right or wrong taking revenge on Chen Haoyu?"
"Right, of course! He spread those rumors—deserves every bit!"
"Then why don't I feel even a shred of joy?"
"Because your heart's too kind to enjoy watching folks suffer."
Qianli Xun examined her chest—not just kindness. "Making him dump a chamber pot stinks him out, yet stinks us out too. Hurting someone bounces right back on yourself. Wonder if it's even worth it?"
"Giving up on payback, Miss?"
"No..." After a quiet beat, she sighed. "Just wondering what it buys me when I don't feel one ounce happier."
With no answer for that, Kuqiao set the incense down once the coast cleared outside and threw open the doors and windows for fresh air.
After breakfast, Chen Haoyu hit the main loop—and surprised himself by running with zest, finding the jog grew lighter lap by lap. Passing Chen Haodong halfway around, he waved without slowing: "Gotta finish my laps, Big Brother Dong, or it's chamber-pot duty! Catch you later!"
Watching his cousin jog off grinning, Chen Haodong frowned: Why's he beaming while serving punishment? Did my advice flop? Infuriating! Gotta cook up something nastier to make that tigress shred him!
Passing the gardeners' quarters beside a blooming rose patch—flowers he had walked past a hundred times without blinking—sparks lit in Chen Haoyu's eyes. "Qinggua! Go tell the gardener to cut me a bouquet of roses!"
Thrilled for an excuse to ditch jogging, Qinggua darted off. The gardener snipped a lush bunch and tucked them into a plain porcelain vase with water to guard against thorns. Figuring his master still had five laps left, Qinggua slipped into a hidden wooden corridor, set the vase on a bench, and dozed off against a pillar—until a splat of bird droppings hit his cheek! Wiping his face with leaves and eyeing the sun, he grabbed the vase and sprinted back to the finish line.
Right on cue, Chen Haoyu jogged up with Asheng and Sanbao and collapsed onto a roadside boulder. "Solid effort today, Young Master," Asheng praised.
Spotting Qinggua hurrying over with the roses, Chen Haoyu grinned. "Gorgeous blooms—crummy vase. Swap it for the celadon vase back in Boya Study."
Catching his breath, he swapped the flowers into the fine green vase, carried it himself to Suxin Thatched Hall, and waved his two shadows back. "Scared I'll bolt? Wait outside—Qinggua's enough."
Stepping inside, he found Kuqiao whisking tea and Zhu Shuzhen absorbed in writing, neither noticing him. Cradling his roses, Chen Haoyu gazed at her with pure delight, kicking himself for all the months wasted feuding with her.
Turning with a finished tea bowl, Kuqiao spotted him grinning like an idiot over a vase of roses. "When did you walk in, Young Master?"
"A moment ago—didn't want to disturb your mistress."
Qianli Xun set down her brush and looked up. "What do you want?"
"Brought you flowers."
Seeing the roses and hearing that caught Qianli Xun flat-footed.
"Go set them on Young Madam's desk, Qinggua," Chen Haoyu ordered.
Snapping out of her daze as Qinggua approached, Qianli Xun flipped her manuscript face down just before the celadon vase landed on her desk. Kuqiao stood frozen holding the tea bowl.
Plenty of guys had brought Qianli Xun flowers before her transmigration—roses didn't melt her knees—yet coming from Chen Haoyu, the move baffled her. "What game are you playing now, Chen Haoyu?"
Before speaking, he broke into a dopey grin. "Heh heh heh..."
"Quit giggling and spit it out!"
Reining in his grin, he asked, "This obvious and you still can't tell?"
"Tell what? Speak up or get out!"
"Even your scowl looks gorgeous! Since you want it plain, I'll swallow my pride and say it right in front of the servants: Zhu Shuzhen, I like you! Heh heh heh..."
Kuqiao's eyes popped wide, bowl still hovering midair.
Convinced it was pure theater, Qianli Xun scoffed. "Think a cheap trick like this makes me let you off? Dream on!"
Not even needing his silent mantra today, he beamed right back. "Fair enough—we fought too long for you to buy it overnight. Give it time and you'll see it's real. Heh, who knew I'd end up married to the woman I love? Neither Qiao Wenxian nor Prince Yi got this lucky! Heh heh..."
His goofy grin gave Qianli Xun goosebumps: Real or fake, don't buy a single word! "Stop laughing!"
He snapped his mouth shut on command. Kuqiao finally set the tea bowl on the desk.
Gulping the whole bowl down to hide her unease, Qianli Xun set it back down. "Per yesterday's schedule, you owe Qinggua an apology. Do it right now in front of me."
Expecting him to bristle now that the moment arrived, she blinked as he agreed without a hitch.
"Sure thing!" Turning to Qinggua, he spoke warm and clear. "Qinggua, I bullied you nonstop—my fault. Right here in front of Young Madam, I'm sorry. Never laying a hand on you again. Know one thing, though: rough as I was, in my heart you've always been my one true sidekick."
"One true sidekick" broke Qinggua into instant sobs. "Young Master! Never knew I meant that much to you—kick me all you want, I'll take it glad! Boo-hoo..."
"Call you a glutton for punishment and you prove it! My word stands—not one punch or kick ever again." Turning back to Qianli Xun, he asked, "Apology done—happy?"
Reminding herself this was all an act—who on earth coached him into this unbreakable soft shell?—Qianli Xun nodded crisp. "Fine, task two passed."
"Aced task one too—even Asheng praised me! Whatever you order from now on, zero backtalk. Though..." He grinned slyly. "That chamber pot this morning sure packed a punch—heh heh! Still didn't mind, heh heh..."
"If we're done, get out and stop bothering me!"
"Yes ma'am! Off to memorize! Heh heh..." He bounced out the door whistling on air.
#CH 237
#TITLE: The Servants Hold a Strategy Huddle
Watching him skip out, then eyeing the bright roses on the desk, Kuqiao ventured, "Miss... could Young Master actually be in love with you?"
Staring at the petals, Qianli Xun scoffed. "Don't buy a word—just another scheme! Too bad I'm not brainless enough to fold over a bunch of flowers and a sleazy grin."
"Still, he looked like he was having a blast—didn't look tortured at all."
"Means my punishments are too soft," Qianli Xun mused. "Need to think up something heavier."
Half agreeing, half doubting, Kuqiao stayed silent.
"Toss those roses out."
Scooping up the vase, Kuqiao protested, "Too pretty to dump in the trash! If you don't want them, I'll put them in Yuening Room."
Just after setting the vase in Yuening Room and stepping out, Chouya nabbed her sleeve. "Sister Kuqiao, quick huddle!"
"About what?"
"Huge business!"
"Spill it or I'm leaving."
Chouya leaned to her ear. "About whether Miss and Young Master live happy ever after!"
That hooked Kuqiao at once. "Where?"
"West Courtyard."
"Wait—let me make an excuse to Miss so she doesn't come looking."
Popping back into Suxin Thatched Hall, where Qianli Xun was absorbed writing, Kuqiao said, "Miss, Chouya needs a hand in the West Courtyard—be right back."
"Go ahead," Qianli Xun murmured without looking up.
In the West Courtyard, instead of Qin'an Lodge, Chouya beckoned from the doorway of the servants' dining room. "Thought it was just us two," Kuqiao laughed walking over. "Looks like a full house!"
"Everyone except the three men out on errands with Matron Wei," Chouya said.
"Funny—since when did you get so invested in Miss's romance?" Kuqiao teased.
Chouya flushed crimson. "Miss's happiness IS my happiness! Qinggua swore he'll only get together with me once Miss and Young Master make up!"
"Ha! Selfish motives after all!" Kuqiao teased while Chouya grinned shyly.
Inside sat three dining tables with Jiaxiang and Fulu already waiting; both rose at once to greet Miss's head maid. Moments later Hongdou, Amei, Qinggua, and Asheng filed in, filling the room with chatter.
Bold as brass, Chouya grabbed Qinggua onto the bench beside her, forcing him to watch Hongdou sit snug beside Asheng.
Scanning the room, Kuqiao asked, "Asheng, Qinggua—if you're both here, who's watching Young Master?"
"Sanbao's got him covered," Asheng said.
"Relax, Sister Kuqiao," Qinggua piped up. "Young Master's meek as a lamb now—buried nose-deep memorizing books! Never seen him study this hard in my life!"
"Awesome!" Chouya clapped. "Push a tiny bit more and they'll patch things up—then Qinggua and I can..." She broke off blushing.
Light dawned on Qinggua—his excuse to brush Chouya off had sparked an entire staff summit! Torn between wanting his master happy and dreading becoming Chouya's captive, he glanced across at Hongdou chatting happily with Asheng without sparing him a blink.
"Who's chairing this meeting?" Kuqiao asked.
"Chouya called it—she chairs," Hongdou nominated.
Sitting tall—finally giving Qinggua breathing room—Chouya took charge. "Aside from Qinggua, we all belong to Miss and want her happy. She started punishing Young Master over last year's rumors, yet instead of cheering up, she looks glummer than before—Sister Kuqiao sees her closest, right?"
Kuqiao sighed. "Who could smile finding out they married the man who slandered them? Top priority is helping Miss get past this wall. I don't want her suffering a second divorce—in-laws as good as Eldest Master and Madam don't grow on trees!"
A chorus agreed: "Right, no second divorce!"
Qinggua grinned. "Actually, huge leap forward already! Sister Kuqiao heard Young Master confess to Young Madam today!"
Every jaw except Kuqiao's dropped. "What?! Young Master confessed?!"
"Happened right in front of me," Kuqiao confirmed, "except Miss didn't buy it and wants to crank up the torture! Heck, even I can barely wrap my head around it."
"True as gold!" Qinggua insisted. "Talked in his sleep saying he liked her! Even took my advice to drop the tough act, use soft words, and learn from Eldest Master—old Young Master would've kicked me across the yard for suggesting that! If that isn't love, what is?"
"Guess he really fell for her," Kuqiao conceded, thinking of the shadow still sitting in her mistress's heart. "Trouble is, Miss doesn't feel a spark for him yet."
Asheng cut straight to the core. "Young Master's already turned around; now it's all on Miss. Get her to like him back, and smooth sailing ahead!"
"Quiet till you hit the bull's-eye," Hongdou praised with a warm glance.
Watching them make eyes soured Qinggua's mood. "Only hit the bull's-eye because I laid the groundwork!"
Ignoring him, Hongdou pitched a plan. "Starting today, let's back Young Master up—hunt for his good points and drop compliments in front of Miss every chance we get! Especially you, Sister Kuqiao—praise him enough and Miss's view of him will soften bit by bit."
"Will that work?" Amei wondered. "Miss hates rumormongers—she won't fold easy."
"No better plan on the table," Kuqiao reasoned. "Worth a shot!"
Chouya seconded first, followed by unanimous nods. Wrapping up the huddle, Chouya declared, "Solid meeting! Three words to live by: Praise Young Master! Qinggua, tell Young Master to put his best foot forward so we actually have material to praise!"
Eyes glued on Hongdou, Qinggua muttered, "Count on it."
Walking back to Boya Study together, Qinggua couldn't resist poking Asheng. "Say, Asheng—got a crush on Hongdou?"
Caught flat, Asheng admitted honest, "Yeah... I like her."
Qinggua spun a tall tale on the spot. "Hate to break it to you, pal—Hongdou likes ME."
Asheng blinked in alarm. "Thought Chouya liked you! She was practically sitting in your lap!"
"Just because Chouya likes me doesn't ban other girls from liking me! I'm single!" Bluff delivered, Qinggua bolted inside before Asheng could press him.
Standing guard outside, Asheng chewed on that in distress until Sanbao noticed his sour mug. "What's eating you, Asheng?"
"Sanbao, think Hongdou likes Qinggua?"
"No way!" Sanbao snorted. "Chouya's crazy for Qinggua—Hongdou likes ME!"
Asheng froze—asked one question and uncovered a second rival! Time to confess to Hongdou fast before somebody beat him to it!
Inside Boya Study, Qinggua found his master reciting aloud with intense focus. Setting down tea, he waited till Chen Haoyu finally closed the volume and chided him: "Gone half the day—sneaking off to meet Chouya?"
"Please! If I sneak off, it's for Hongdou! Great news, Young Master: every servant in Moxiang Courtyard just vowed to sing your praises to Young Madam! Show off your best qualities so they have ammo!"
"Wait—Zhu Shuzhen's own loyal pack backing ME?"
"They want Young Madam happy without another divorce. Once I told them you fell for her, they jumped on board!"
Chen Haoyu sprang up. "Let's go show Zhu Shuzhen my killer talent right now!"
"Which talent?"
"Photographic memory!"
Stepping out, Chen Haoyu waved back at Asheng and Sanbao. "No need shadowing me—not going anywhere!"
Still bound by orders, both trailed along—Asheng scanning hard for praiseworthy traits and drawing a blank beyond decent looks. "Sanbao, see any good points on Young Master?"
"Drawing a blank," Sanbao whispered back.
"Does being handsome count?"
"Guess so."
Leaving the guards outside Suxin Thatched Hall, Chen Haoyu stepped in and felt a dip of disappointment seeing the writing desk empty—until he turned and spotted her seated at the tea table holding a bare-bottomed clay figurine, smiling softly.
The sight rooted him to the floor—she looked radiant when she smiled! Why on earth did I ever roam outside with a bride like this at home? Yesterday I cursed Zhu Xiyan; today I want to buy him a drink!
"Young Master is here," Kuqiao prompted gently.
Eyes glued to her face, Chen Haoyu spoke warm. "Like clay dolls? I'll buy you dozens—fill the whole room!"
Handing the figurine to Kuqiao to stow, Qianli Xun rose and met him. "Broke to the bone, and you're buying me a roomful? Check your own pockets before bragging."
"The day your temper cools and you let me outside, I'll ask Father to put me to work in family trade—earn real wages and buy you anything you want!"
Two days of boot camp and he was volunteering for work? Real or fake, she jabbed right back. "I'm richer than you—need your silver? One clay doll is cute; a whole room turns my hall into a toy stall!"
"Mad again? My bad, alright? Cool down and sit—listen to me recite!"
With his endless patience blocking every jab, Qianli Xun swallowed her snark. Fine—let's see what he actually memorized, and tear him apart when he stumbles!
#CH 238
#TITLE: Everyone Sings the Groom's Praises
Chen Haoyu launched into the Analects, Book One—not just the first ten passages she expected, rather the entire opening chapter word for word! Unfamiliar with the full text herself, Qianli Xun had to crack the volume open to follow along, amazed as he rattled off every line without a single stumble.
Finishing, he beamed with pride. "Well? Pretty sharp, huh? Blew past the quota!"
Closing the Analects, Qianli Xun sniffed, "Nothing to brag about—bet your childhood tutor drilled that into your skull years ago."
"Sure I sat in a schoolroom as a kid, yet my head was out the window! Knew the title 'Analects,' never remembered a single line inside—ask Big Brother Dong if you doubt me!"
Figuring his star performance earned a breather, he aimed his backside at a chair—only for Qianli Xun to bark, "Not done reciting—stay on your feet!"
Standing straight again, he wheedled, "Go easier on your husband, huh? A little gentleness goes a long way."
Qianli Xun stood and circled him twice, sizing him up: Guy actually has solid brains when he applies them—might make something of himself after all.
Her faint fragrance drifted close as she circled, leaving Chen Haoyu dizzy with hope—studying him this close, was she warming up? "Well? Pretty solid catch, right? Hit the jackpot marrying me!"
Where on earth did this guy inherit shameless confidence like that? Certainly not from his parents! "Quit yapping and recite your poems!"
"Hate poetry, so I only did the exact quota," he prefaced, then rolled straight through ten Wang Wei classics including "Autumn Evening in the Mountains" and "Farmhouse on the Wei River" without missing a syllable.
Impressed despite herself, Qianli Xun decided the syllabus was too soft—time to crank up the pain. "Way too easy! From now on, memorize the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries!"
Chen Haoyu blinked. "Complete Library of the what? Never heard of it."
Oops! Transmigration brain-fart—that colossal anthology belonged to the Qing dynasty, centuries in the future!
Refusing to admit a slip, she doubled down. "Loafing around all day, how many books could you know? Forget it—I'll go easy on you: memorize Records of the Grand Historian!" Han dynasty—safe! Massive, dense chapters—guaranteed torture!
Sure enough, his face fell. "You already stacked a mountain of books on my desk! Why swap now? Records of the Grand Historian runs miles long—you're doing this on purpose!"
The more he groaned, the brighter she smiled. "I hold the whip, I pick the syllabus! Can't I change my mind?"
"Fine, fine—on one condition!"
Qianli Xun's eyes blazed wide. "You dare name conditions?! When you spread rumors and the whole city tore me apart with nowhere to turn, who gave ME conditions?! Now memorizing a few books makes you whine? Forget it—no conditions granted!"
Guilt pricked Chen Haoyu at the reminder of last year's cruelty. "Alright, alright, no conditions. Torture me however you want—I'll take it till your anger cools. Just tell me how long that takes?"
"My anger will NEVER cool—not for a whole lifetime!"
Instead of flinching, a goofy grin split his face. "A whole lifetime?! Means you're staying with me forever! Heh—luckier than Qiao Wenxian and Prince Yi combined! Heh heh..."
Her fury splashed like a pebble dropped into a deep pond, leaving zero ripples while sinking her own spirit. Afraid staring at his beaming face any longer might weaken her grudge, she spun her back to him. "Drop the act! Think I can't see through your new tactic? Won't work on me!"
"Think whatever you like—off to sweep the yard so the servants get a fat bonus! Wouldn't dream of making you mad again, heh heh!"
Heading out just as Hongdou and Amei walked in carrying lunch trays, he pressed his luck. "Since I nailed my tests today, Zhu Shuzhen, can I eat lunch with you?"
She whipped around. "Keep dreaming! I'd rather share a table with a street beggar than eat beside you!"
Unfazed, he grinned back. "No sweat—plenty of time ahead. Since you're sticking with me for life, we'll share a table sooner or later!" He strolled out before she could fire back.
Laying out the dishes, Hongdou and Amei traded a quick look before Hongdou began, "Lunch is ready, Miss. While you eat, let me report on Young Master's morning."
Unbothered, Qianli Xun sat down.
"Young Master spoke polite and respectful to every servant today, and studied dead serious without nodding off once," Hongdou praised.
"Didn't kick Qinggua a single time either," Amei added. "Really looks like he's turned around!"
Missing the coordinated campaign at first, Qianli Xun cautioned, "Bought off already by a few copper coins he earned? Don't trust a two-day front! A long road tests a horse's stamina, and time tests a man's heart. Wait and see. Run along—Kuqiao can serve me."
Shooting Kuqiao a quick glance, both maids withdrew.
Laying out chopsticks and ladling soup, Kuqiao hunted for a natural opening to slip in her own praise. "Miss, haven't seen Matron Wei for two straight days."
"Out running business errands dawn till dusk," Qianli Xun said between bites. "Haven't seen her myself."
Kuqiao put on a dramatic sigh. "Old saying goes men handle outside affairs, women handle indoors. If you had a capable man by your side, Matron Wei wouldn't have to wear herself out running around town."
Qianli Xun set her chopsticks down. "Since when did you pick up narrow ideas like that, Kuqiao? What's wrong with women? We hold up half the sky! Who matches Matron Wei's brains? And I'm the Poetess of Jiangnan! Meanwhile look at Chen Haoyu—born male, empty-headed rake chasing brothels and hoodlums! If the world ran on men like him, better off handing everything to women!"
Hearing him mentioned handed Kuqiao her bridge. "Young Master isn't that awful—did awesome today, swore off brothels, even wants to learn Chen trade! Must be your brilliant discipline transforming him!"
Qianli Xun lowered her soup spoon. "Use your head: twenty years a playboy, reformed in forty-eight hours? Who buys that? When things flip overnight, there's a catch—he's plotting something!"
Half-persuaded yet remembering Qinggua's secret, Kuqiao ventured, "Heard something from Qinggua—not sure if I should mention it..."
"Already brought it up—spill it."
"Ran into Qinggua in the West Courtyard. He told me Young Master called your name in his sleep yesterday and said he liked you..."
Qianli Xun paused mid-spoonful and set it back in the bowl. "You believe Qinggua?"
"He also said Young Master turned around because he fell in love with you..."
Qianli Xun fell silent, resuming her soup at half speed. Having planted the seed, Kuqiao stayed mute.
Finishing lunch without another word, Qianli Xun retreated to her bedroom. After eating with the staff in the West Courtyard—passing Chen Haoyu hard at work sweeping the front yard while waving off Qinggua's help under Asheng and Sanbao's gaze—Kuqiao returned and found her mistress lying fully clothed on top of the quilt.
"Let me help you slip off your outer robe for a nap, Miss."
Sitting up, Qianli Xun shook her head. "Can't sleep. Come out with me."
"Where to?"
"The Divine Willow."
Whenever heavy thoughts weighed on her mistress, the Divine Willow was her refuge. Kuqiao asked no questions and fetched her cloak.
Crossing Moxiang Courtyard, Qianli Xun watched Chen Haoyu's broom sweeping crisp strokes across the paving stones—nothing about his focus looked staged. Could he really have changed out of love for her? If so, where on earth was she supposed to aim her grudge?
Asheng and Sanbao stepped over to bow. "Young Master's putting real muscle into it, Miss," Sanbao praised. "Spotless wherever he swept!"
"Plus," Asheng chimed in, "never noticed before how strapping Young Master is—tall, broad-shouldered, handsome face too!"
Realization snapped shut—her whole staff was running a PR campaign for Chen Haoyu! Putting on a stern glare, she demanded, "Whose payroll are you two on—mine or Chen Haoyu's?"
"Yours, Miss, of course!"
"Then quit pitching for him!" Both guards fell mute as she strode past the gate.
"Easy does it—slow and steady," Asheng sighed once she cleared earshot. Sanbao nodded.
Overhearing everything, Chen Haoyu grinned over his broom. "Appreciate the assist, boys! Keep putting in good words—I won't forget you!"
"Our words only go so far, Young Master—you have to earn it," Asheng advised.
"On it!" Chen Haoyu bent back to sweeping with fresh fire.
Heading toward the front manor gate, Chouya bounced straight into her path coming back from reporting kitchen orders. "Heading out, Miss?"
"Quick walk." Qianli Xun stepped around her—only for Chouya to dart ahead blocking the lane.
"Miss, gotta tell you something urgent!"
"What?"
"Young Master changed—so much better than before!"
Another cheerleader! Had Chen Haoyu hypnotized her entire courtyard? Without wasting a syllable, Qianli Xun sidestepped her and marched out.
"Not lying, Miss! Scout's honor!" Chouya hollered at her back until Kuqiao waved frantically for her to zip it and run back.
Riding out toward the Divine Willow, silence filled the carriage. Stepping outside Chen Manor for the first time since the wedding, street bustle felt almost foreign. When she first learned Chen Haoyu had spread last year's rumors, she had dreamed up punishments expecting his fury and misery to heal her own wounds. Instead, his cheerful surrender—and confessed affection—left her emptier than before. Even heaven seemed to deny her a clean shot at payback.
#CH 239
#TITLE: Light as Air Once Let Go
At the trailhead, the driver halted and set down the footstool. Kuqiao stepped down first and offered her hand. Sensing her mistress's brooding silence all ride, she guessed the cause: watching Young Master turn sweet robbed Miss of a target for her bitter grudge.
Seeing Kuqiao's careful concern, Qianli Xun laid her hand lightly on hers to reassure her as she stepped out.
Crowds of pilgrims—men, women, young, and old—streamed up and down the mountain path toward the nunnery. Before her transmigration, Qianli Xun had scoffed at superstition; now she judged no one. Everyone needed a spiritual anchor, just as she came back to the Divine Willow whenever her chest grew heavy.
Strolling toward the tree, far fewer willow catkins drifted on the breeze. Counting the days, over half a month had passed since Prince Yi and Mengrong left for Bianliang, and since she had married into Chen Manor. Were they exchanging vows right now, or already riding back? Either way, she hoped wedded happiness would melt Mengrong's hatred away.
Wait—why wish Mengrong would drop her hatred while she herself clung tight to hating Chen Haoyu? All ride out here she had been cooking up wilder tortures—dangling him down a well for three days, burying him neck-deep by a country road for passersby to poke, stripping him to his undershorts with charcoal smeared across his face and acupoints locked to beg on the street—all over last year's rumors!
Reaching the willow, four young couples stood tying fresh red silk ribbons onto low boughs; the canopy held half again as many ribbons as before, spring stirring young hearts across Lin'an. Watching them tie their wishes hand in hand sparked a quiet ache. Back during her whirlwind romance with Wenyuan, they had never bought a red ribbon at the nunnery to hang here—maybe if they had, fate wouldn't have tossed her onto this tangled road.
Once the couples wandered off and quiet returned, Qianli Xun stepped closer. Cool shade radiating off the ancient trunk eased a fraction of the heat in her chest—yet the grudge still lingered underneath.
"Tell me what to do, Divine Willow," she murmured aloud. "Marrying a man I disliked was bad enough; learning he spread those rumors makes me want to slice him into pieces..."
Knew it! Kuqiao thought behind her.
"Yet overnight he flipped completely—stopped fighting, took every punishment smiling, even..." She skipped mentioning his confession. "Now I can't bring myself to strike hard, yet letting my grudge fizzle out leaves a bitter knot in my gut."
A warm gust swept the drooping fronds, swaying red ribbons until several tangled softly around neighboring twigs in the slanting gold sunlight. Moved by the scene, Qianli Xun recited Zhu Shuzhen's quatrain:
"Tall strands, a thousand threads spun fine in warm wind, / Draped in mist and haze east of the market bridge. / Knotting silent resentment inside the slanting sun, / Snapping parting sorrow amid the fine spring rain." [TN: Translator's rendering of Zhu Shuzhen's "The Willow"]
"Fine verse!" a familiar voice chimed from behind.
Turning, Qianli Xun greeted the elderly nun from the mountain nunnery—still unaware she stood before Master Jingguang herself. "Greetings, Venerable Master! Fate brings us together again."
Fingering her prayer beads with palms pressed together, Master Jingguang chanted, "Amitabha. Fine verse indeed, Lady Benefactor, though ill-matched to the scene. This willow stands by a lakeside pond outside the city—why speak of 'east of the market bridge'? Clear bright skies overhead—why 'fine spring rain'? That closing line speaks of parting from lover or friend, yet you came here parting from no one."
"Just recited whatever popped into my head, Master—no need to dissect it."
"Popped into your head? Hardly. 'Knotting silent resentment inside the slanting sun'—resentment knots your heart, so you pour it into verse seeking release. Yet venting never heals a heart gripped by anger."
Struck straight to the quick, Qianli Xun asked, "Then what heals it, Master? Please enlighten me."
"Not enlighten—merely share the Buddha's words. Only one remedy cures wrath and resentment: forbearance."
"Expect me to just swallow it? No way! I can't bear watching the man who hurt me walk away unscathed—I want payback until he begs on his knees!"
"You refuse forbearance because you have not grasped the unarisen nature of wrath," Master Jingguang explained. "What arises only from conditions has no true self-nature—it is an illusion. Why let an illusion torment you?"
"Illusion?" Qianli Xun shook her head. "My pain feels solid enough, and Chen Haoyu spread those rumors for real—every soul in Lin'an heard them! Too lofty for a mortal like me—I can't call real wounds an illusion."
"Have you already taken revenge on the one who stirred your wrath?"
"Sure have—except I'm too softhearted to go brutal, so he's grinning through it! Leaves me itching to hit harder, yet unable to stomach cruelty."
Beside her, Kuqiao prayed silently for the old nun to break through her mistress's knot.
"You possess a kind heart, Lady Benefactor—that kindness drew our paths together beneath this willow to hear the Dharma," Master Jingguang said. "Tell me: since starting your revenge, have you felt happy?"
Qianli Xun searched her chest—from dragging Chen Haoyu out of the brothel in ropes, to having Hongdou slap him, to forcing apologies and stinking chamber pots at dawn—not one single moment of genuine joy. "Truthfully? Not an ounce."
"Mild payback brought zero joy; crueler payback will bring even less," Master Jingguang observed. "Avenging wrath is a fool's bargain. Wisdom lies in bearing the insult and letting go clean—only release brings ease."
"Let go? Easier said than done!"
"Why cling to it?"
"He trashed my reputation, shattered my match, and robbed me of happiness—shouldn't a man like that pay?"
"Did it never cross your mind that the happiness you mourned was never meant to be yours?"
A dull ache echoed through her—maybe she and Wenyuan truly weren't meant to be—yet her stubborn pride pushed back. "If victims just bear abuse and walk away, won't scoundrels run wild and turn the world upside down?"
"Tell me: is the man you resent an irredeemable monster?"
That stopped Qianli Xun cold. Scoundrel, yes—monster? Memories flashed: apologizing earnestly to Qinggua, sweeping the courtyard stroke by stroke, absorbing every sharp barb with that sunny compliance... "Just a good-for-nothing jerk."
"Not an irredeemable monster, then. Step back one pace, and sea and sky open wide."
"Doesn't that let him off way too cheap?"
"Do you truly care for yourself, Lady Benefactor?"
"Of course!"
"Then why obsess over another person until you make yourself miserable? Someone who truly cherishes their own life spares no hours feeding poison to old grudges. Life spans only decades; wasting years nursing wrath wounds you before it ever touches your enemy. Isn't that a terrible bargain?"
That landed dead center. Look at the absurdity: Chen Haoyu was supposedly the prisoner, yet apart from day one he was grinning through chores like a kid at a fair, while she—the avenger—sat brooding under a willow tree! Wound the enemy a thousand, bleed yourself eight hundred. Not for Chen Haoyu's sake—purely for her own peace—she would wipe the slate clean.
The instant that thought settled, an actual weight lifted off her ribs. "Thank you for waking me up, Master. I let it go."
"Amitabha. Letting go brings great merit. May peace and joy attend your days, Lady Benefactor." Turning, Master Jingguang walked away up the path.
"Thank you, Master!" Qianli Xun called after her with a deep bow.
Kuqiao's face lit up. "Miss—'let it go' means you're done punishing Young Master?"
"When did Chen Haoyu buy YOU off too, rooting for him?" Qianli Xun teased.
"Never!" Kuqiao protested in a rush. "I just hated seeing you miserable ever since you learned the truth—not even revenge made you smile! Listening to the master opened my eyes too!"
Breaking into her first genuine laugh in days, Qianli Xun said, "Smart girl—got real wisdom in you! Fine, clean slate with Chen Haoyu. Tell the whole courtyard they can quit running their little praise campaign—think I didn't notice?"
"Nothing gets past you, Miss!" Kuqiao grinned.
Lighthearted again, Qianli Xun lingered to enjoy the lakeside wildflowers, weaving twin flower crowns with Kuqiao to perch on their heads. Whenever fresh young couples strolled up to tie ribbons, Qianli Xun scanned every pair—Kuqiao figured she enjoyed watching lovers, never guessing her mistress half-hoped and half-dreaded spotting Prince Yi and Mengrong.
Only as twilight gathered did she rest a final spell beneath the willow before riding home.
#CH 240
#TITLE: Second Young Master Wins His Freedom
By the time Qianli Xun reached Chen Manor, dinner was long over. Not hungry, she waved off Kuqiao's offer to lay out supper, changed into fresh clothes, and headed for Boya Study to tell Chen Haoyu face to face that his sentence was over.
Stepping out of Suxin Thatched Hall into the lantern-lit yard, a lone figure approached across the flagstones—Chen Haofei.
"Greetings, Second Sister-in-law," he bowed respectful.
"What brings you by?"
"Came to check on Second Brother."
Catching the subtext at once, Qianli Xun smiled. "Sent by the elders, right?"
Too honest to fib, Chen Haofei admitted, "Grandmother and First Aunt swore not to meddle, yet couldn't stop fretting, so they sent me to peek in on him."
"If they couldn't bear it, why put me in charge?" Qianli Xun mused, figuring two days of boot camp could hardly cure lifelong bad habits anyway. "Come along—I'm heading to Boya Study myself."
Trailing her into the back courtyard, Chen Haofei eyed Asheng and Sanbao flanking the unlocked door like temple door-gods and stuck out his tongue in secret: No wonder Second Brother calls her a tigress—even posting guards! Remind me to marry someone mild!
"You two can knock off," Qianli Xun told the guards. "No more sentry duty."
Thrilled, both bowed and left. Kuqiao pushed open the doors, letting Qianli Xun step in first with Chen Haofei right behind calling out, "Second Brother! Came to see you!"
Chen Haoyu and Qinggua stepped out of the inner room—happy to hear Haofei, and beaming wide at spotting Zhu Shuzhen herself! Throwing an arm around his cousin, Chen Haoyu grinned, "Took you long enough to visit!"
Haofei whispered in his ear, "Scared of Second Sister-in-law! Only worked up the nerve because Grandmother and First Aunt sent me to check on you."
Releasing him, Chen Haoyu boomed, "Look me over—fit as a fiddle! Your sister-in-law treats me great, plenty to eat and wear—feel sharper these last two days than ever!"
Haofei winced in silent pity—whatever brutal tricks she pulled must have scared his cousin into singing her praises!
Amused at his theater, Qianli Xun stood back watching—until Chen Haoyu swiveled toward her. "Hey! Where'd you disappear all afternoon till dark?"
"Since when do I report my schedule to you?" she shot back, then got straight to business. "Chen Haoyu, from this second on, you're free. No more guards, no more chores, and last year's rumor grudge is wiped clean. I'll draft a fresh copy of our old contract; just cooperate and put your thumbprint on it."
Joy at freedom flipped to instant alarm at "contract." "No way!"
"What, begging for more discipline?"
"I mean the contract! You burned it—no point rewriting it."
"Why not?" she asked, puzzled.
Stepping closer, Chen Haoyu said, "My thinking changed big-time these past two days. Those old terms don't fit anymore—why ink paper that's already outdated?"
Fair enough. "Fine—sleep on what terms you want and come to Suxin Thatched Hall tomorrow to hash out a new pact. Chat with your cousin; I'm turning in."
At the doorway, Chen Haoyu called after her, "Hey—you really aren't mad about last year's rumors anymore?"
Without turning back, Qianli Xun dropped a parting gem: "If a dog bites a human, does the human bite the dog back? What's the difference between them then? I'm human—I refuse to sink to a dog's level, so I'm done feuding with that dog."
Oddest thing—falling for her made even getting called a dog sound sweet! Grinning at her departing back, Chen Haoyu chuckled, "Bet you already like me—releasing me this fast and even dropping hints about staying loyal! Heh heh..."
Chen Haofei blinked in utter confusion. "Wait—where was the hint, Second Brother? Did I miss something?"
"Not a chance!" Chen Haoyu spun around with swagger. "Hear her mention a dog?"
"Yeah?"
"What are dogs famous for?"
"What?"
"Loyalty to their master! She's hinting I better stay loyal to her! Can't blame her—with my looks, girls drop like flies whenever I step out!"
Haofei gave Qinggua a helpless look: "Did Second Sister-in-law really mean that?" Qinggua just shook his head.
"Tell Grandmother and Mother it's late tonight, so I'll pay my respects first thing tomorrow morning," Chen Haoyu instructed. "And not one bad word about your sister-in-law!"
Hurrying straight back to Eldest Uncle's courtyard—where Old Madam Xia sat fretting alongside Yao Qingyan and Chen Jianglin after dark—Haofei burst through the doors announcing, "Great news! Great news!"
Both women leaned forward in relief. "What news?"
"Second Sister-in-law stopped locking Second Brother up, canceled all punishments, and wiped the slate clean on last year's rumors!"
Instantly all three smiles vanished. "Quit after two days?" Chen Jianglin groaned. "Nobody reforms in two days!"
"All our grand hopes—reforming him and sparking love—just wishful thinking," Old Madam Xia sighed. "Shuzhen never cared."
"Guess Haoyu just lacks the luck—and us too," Yao Qingyan mourned.
Realizing they wanted romance along with reform, Haofei jumped in fast. "Don't worry, Grandmother, Uncle, Aunt! Hard to read Second Sister-in-law yet, yet Second Brother is like a brand-new man! Pretty sure he's head over heels for her—even warned me not to say one bad word about her!"
Relief turned into broad laughter around the table.
"Progress—huge progress!" Old Madam Xia beamed. "Defending his wife already—no way he runs wild again!"
"Mother's right!" Chen Jianglin crowed. "Two days with Shuzhen accomplished more than I did in fifteen years!"
"True enough!" Yao Qingyan dabbed happy tears when Haofei passed along his message to visit at dawn. "When has Haoyu ever been this thoughtful? Used to vanish without a word—now he checks in polite!"
"Only with you two—he always checks in with me!" Old Madam Xia teased.
"Sure, whenever he wants a handout!" Chen Jianglin joked.
"Asking me for things proves he remembers me—when do you lot ever ask?"
Unwilling to spoil the fine evening arguing with his mother's logic, Chen Jianglin smiled and waited for morning.
Escorting Old Madam Xia back to her gate, purehearted Haofei felt zero envy over his grandmother's favoritism. As he turned to leave, Old Madam Xia caught his sleeve. "Hold on, Haofei. Grandmother believes you're going to earn that imperial degree."
"May your blessing come true, Grandmother."
"Know why I say that?"
"Because we're family, so you root for me."
"Wrong. Fifty years of watching folks taught me to read hearts. Your heart is clean and true—heaven won't shortchange you. You're the Chen clan's hope to lift our family standing."
Touched to the core, Haofei bowed low. "Thank you, Grandmother."
Bright and early next morning, Chen Haoyu stepped out of Boya Study with Qinggua—and ran straight into Matron Wei. Spooked at how she seemed to vanish during his lockdown and materialize the instant he went free, he jumped as she curtsied. "Congratulations on your freedom, Young Master."
"Haven't seen hide nor hair of you for two days—how'd you already know?"
"Seen or unseen, nothing in this courtyard escapes me."
Feeling as if her sharp eyes x-rayed his skull, he beat a fast retreat. "Gotta run!"
Matron Wei chuckled at his back: Miss hasn't budged, yet Young Master sure flipped fast—progress at last.
Passing Suxin Thatched Hall, Chen Haoyu beamed at the wooden plaque. "Funny, Qinggua—why does 'Suxin Thatched Hall' suddenly look so classy today?"
"Because Young Madam named it and sleeps inside," Qinggua deadpanned.
"Heh heh..." Scanning the courtyard, he sighed in pure bliss. "Good eye my wife has! Lotus leaves in the pond, and look at that hehuan silk tree—'harmonious union'! Think she planted it secretly hoping we'd live in wedded bliss forever?"
Watching his playboy master transform overnight into a lovesick goofball, Qinggua bit back a grin until prodded to speak. "Either way, having a tree of harmonious union right in Moxiang Courtyard means you and Young Madam are destined for lasting love!"
"Well said! First bonus I earn goes straight to you! Come on—time to visit Father and Mother!" Full of fresh drive to make something of himself, Chen Haoyu marched out of Moxiang Courtyard.
#CH 241
#TITLE: He Really Changed After All
Eager to see her grandson—guessing he would visit his parents first—Old Madam Xia walked over to Chen Jianglin's courtyard right after sunrise, eating breakfast there while waiting.
"Second Young Master is here!" Yingxue announced.
Striding right in with Qinggua behind, Chen Haoyu bowed crisp to his parents—"Father, Mother"—before dropping straight into his grandmother's arms. "Grandmother! Missed you to death!"
Stroking his head fondly, Old Madam Xia asked, "Not mad at us for bolting our gates and ignoring your cries?"
"Thank you isn't enough—why would I be mad?" His sweet obedience lit up all three faces.
Hiding a smile behind fatherly sternness, Chen Jianglin said, "Warm morning—get off your grandmother and stand straight to answer questions."
Hopping up, Chen Haoyu added, "Even before your questions, Father, I have something to ask you."
"Answer your elders first."
Yao Qingyan jumped in. "Did Shuzhen truly wipe the slate clean on last year's rumors?"
"Would I lie? I'm her husband—we're one family! Why would family stay mad at family? Right, Mother?"
Hearing "one family" roll so natural off his tongue broke even Chen Jianglin's stern mask into chuckles. Sipping tea to compose himself, he asked, "Shuzhen let you off way too light after two days—I'd have kept you grounded longer! What progress could you possibly have made in forty-eight hours?"
Chen Haoyu paused, then spoke straight. "Hard to change everything in two days, yet something shifted in me. I'm done loafing around town—I want to stay home and work. Could you assign me a real job in the family business, Father? Need to earn my own silver so I don't look pathetic when I want to buy my wife gifts!"
Surprise gave way to pure radiance on both women's faces, and Chen Jianglin broke into an unstoppable grin. "That's what you came to ask?"
"Yes, sir!"
"Done roaming for good—really ready to learn trade?"
Before Haoyu could answer, Old Madam Xia smacked her armrest. "My grandson already gave his word! Quit doubting your own son—nasty habit!"
"My apologies, Mother—I'll mend that habit!" Chen Jianglin laughed.
Tears of joy shimmered in Yao Qingyan's eyes. "Haoyu really grew up! Nobody's happier than his mother."

Chen Jianglin laughed and shook his head. "Not one stitch of work done and already asking wages! Focus on doing the job right—pay won't be short."

Meanwhile, right after Chen Haoyu left Moxiang Courtyard that morning, Matron Wei had invited Qianli Xun out for a stroll through Chen Manor's sprawling gardens. Happy to walk off breakfast and explore grounds she had barely seen since arriving, Qianli Xun strolled beside her through fragrant flowerbeds and singing birds.
"Didn't realize Chen Manor had gardens this lovely—flowers everywhere," Matron Wei admired.
Thinking of the bouquet sitting in Kuqiao's room, Qianli Xun remarked, "Even got roses."
"Didn't spot any roses—where?"
Dodging mention of Chen Haoyu's gift, Qianli Xun said, "Maids mentioned a small rose patch somewhere."

Reaching a wide lotus pond where broad leaves already floated thick across the water, they rested inside a lakeside pavilion. Gazing over the pond, Matron Wei dropped her real question out of the blue: "Miss, do you really mean to live unconsummated with Young Master forever, each going your separate way?"
Unblushing, Qianli Xun answered straight, "Our prenuptial pact spelled out non-interference."
"Word is you burned that pact."
"We'll draw up a fresh one."
"I spoil you nine times out of ten, Miss, yet on this point I must speak plain."
Knowing Matron Wei never wasted words, Qianli Xun turned attentive. "Go ahead, Matron."
"How do you find the Chen household?"
"Every single thing here is great—except Chen Haoyu."
"What if Young Master genuinely reforms?"
"Him? Reform? Fat chance."
"Short as your discipline lasted, Miss, I watched close—he's changed a great deal."
"Don't fall for it, Matron! Just his new angle to get around me."
"Not an act, Miss. He truly shifted."
Forced to admit there might be smoke behind the fire, Qianli Xun pushed back. "Even if he did, does that mean I have to sleep with him?"
"Having lived a long life, I know how hard marriage is for a woman—landing in a decent household is rarer still," Matron Wei said gently. "Chen Manor beats the Lins and Qiaos by miles. Cherish this haven, Miss. If Young Master turns worthy, try opening your heart bit by bit."
Realizing life was nudging her down this exact path made Qianli Xun balk. "I don't love Chen Haoyu."
Matron Wei sighed. "How many women under heaven ever get to marry for love?"
Just then Kuqiao hurried up. "Miss, Old Madam Xia, Eldest Master, and Eldest Madam are waiting at Moxiang Courtyard!"
Matron Wei rose. "Come greet the elders—bet they came to thank you."
Rising with heavy thoughts, Qianli Xun knew marrying into this house meant consummating and bearing children sooner or later—yet how could she take that step while another man still lived inside her chest? Shen Jianchen's parting vow at Zuiyun Tower—"I'll stay chaste for you"—wrapped around her heart with equal parts tenderness and scorching guilt toward Mengrong. Trying to shove his image away only made it sharpen.
Approaching Moxiang Courtyard, a warm scene met her eyes beneath the hehuan silk tree: Old Madam Xia reclining in the rattan chair, Chen Jianglin and Yao Qingyan chatting over Hongdou's whisked tea, and Chen Haoyu perched on a low stool leaning affectionately against his grandmother's knee.
A portrait of genuine family warmth that made Qianli Xun's chest swell. She already thought of this manor as home—if only Chen Haoyu weren't part of the package!
Mid-reverie, warm fingers closed around her hand. "Hey! Where'd you run off to? Kept us waiting!"
Snapping back, Qianli Xun jerked her hand free from Chen Haoyu. "Keep your hands to yourself!"
"Alright, alright, hands off!" He trotted back to his stool beside Old Madam Xia.
Reading every flicker on her mistress's face—loving the family, not yet ready for the husband—Matron Wei stepped up smiling. "Had I known you three were calling, I wouldn't have dragged Miss off for a walk."
Hongdou and Amei fetched two more chairs. Still gazing at the cozy tableau, Qianli Xun forgot even to step forward until Yao Qingyan walked over and took her hand. "Standing back there, Shuzhen—mad at us?"
"Never—it just looked so warm I wanted to soak the picture in and memorize it."
"If it looks warm, step right in and become part of the picture!" Yao Qingyan laughed, tugging her beneath the shade.
"Become part of the picture"—those simple words struck a deep chord. Curtsying to the elders, Qianli Xun said, "Had I known you all liked sitting under the hehuan tree, I'd have set out more chairs."
"No need—too many chairs clutter the view," Old Madam Xia said, sitting up.
"We only drop by now and then," Chen Jianglin agreed. "Sit down, Shuzhen."
Taking the chair beside Matron Wei, Qianli Xun felt Chen Haoyu's eyes glued to her face. She shot him a glare; he looked away innocently, then sneaked peeks right back—making Yao Qingyan beam inside. Clear as day her son had reformed out of sheer love for Shuzhen!
"We came today to thank you, Shuzhen," Yao Qingyan began.
"First for letting go of last year's rumors," Chen Jianglin added, "and second for straightening Haoyu out so well."
Refusing to claim false credit, Qianli Xun spoke straight. "No need to thank me. Letting go of the rumors was for my own peace of mind, and I claim zero credit for Chen Haoyu's shift—I was only taking payback, and nobody transforms from two days of boot camp."
"See? Proof I was solid gold underneath all along!" Chen Haoyu crowed.
Lounging back under the cool leaves, Old Madam Xia smiled. "Whatever your motive, the result is pure gold, so the credit is yours. For handing me back a worthy grandson, name any reward—hard as it is, Grandmother will deliver!"
About to decline, Matron Wei's pond-side warning flashed through Qianli Xun's head. Sooner or later these loving elders would push for consummation and grandchildren. Better lock down breathing room right now while holding the high ground!
"Since Grandmother offers so generously, I won't be shy. Keep gold, silver, shops, and jewels—I only ask one promise from all three elders."
#CH 242
#TITLE: Every Child Walks Their Own Fate
Before Qianli Xun finished speaking, Matron Wei already knew what was coming. Raising consummation by the pond earlier had served two aims: preparing her mistress for reality, and prompting her to negotiate smartly instead of colliding head-on with the elders later. Right on cue, Miss seized the reward offer.
"Name it," Chen Jianglin invited.
Rising to bow deeply before all three elders, Qianli Xun stated her term clear: "Please promise me, Grandmother, Father, and Mother: until I genuinely develop feelings for Chen Haoyu, never press me to consummate the marriage."
Disappointment clouded all three elders' faces, dropping heavy silence over the yard.
A sharp pang hit Chen Haoyu too—so she still felt zero spark for him—yet afraid the elders would scold her, he jumped in fast to smooth the water. "Done, done! I agree! You don't like me yet only because you haven't seen my best side! Give me time to show off my charms and you'll fall for me soon enough!"
His breezy chime broke the chill, lifting a weight off Qianli Xun's chest—for the first time, his blind cockiness sounded almost likable. Matron Wei hid a small smile: Young Master really has turned endearing.
Since her grandson yielded, Old Madam Xia spoke up. "If Haoyu agrees, why should I object? Your ideas sure differ from ordinary brides, Shuzhen—this old bone will have to get used to it."
Awkward for a father-in-law to debate bedroom matters, Chen Jianglin nudged Yao Qingyan with a look.
Still smarting from disappointment, Yao Qingyan spoke gently. "Shuzhen, we elders treated that prenuptial contract like kids playing house. Now that you're wed and Haoyu is turning around, why cling to paper?"
"I already burned the contract," Qianli Xun interjected.
Yao Qingyan brightened. "Good riddance! Then live warm together—consummation will follow naturally."
"I burned it in anger," Qianli Xun clarified. "I plan to draft a new one with Chen Haoyu."
"Over my dead body!" Chen Haoyu jumped in. "A real man's word is steel—I'll keep my promise in my heart, no need for paper chains! Relax, I won't ever force you!"
As if you could force me! Qianli Xun huffed inside.
"If it's burned, don't rewrite it," Yao Qingyan pleaded. "A wife enters a family to bear children and carry on the line. If you refuse to consummate, when will your father-in-law and I ever hold a grandchild?"
Confident a year was more than enough to win her over, Chen Haoyu coaxed his mother, "Relax, Mother! One year from today, I promise you'll be rocking a chubby grandson!"
All three elders burst into chuckles.
Unimpressed by his boast, Qianli Xun offered a blunt shortcut. "If Mother wants grandchildren fast, easy fix—I'm happy to arrange a concubine for Chen Haoyu to bear children."
All three smiles died on the spot.
"No way!" Chen Haoyu protested loud. "I'm only having kids with the woman I love!"
Sensing deadlock looming, Matron Wei stepped smoothly into the gap. "Old Madam, Master, Madam—congratulations are in order!"
Still gloomy over grandchildren, Yao Qingyan blinked. "Congratulations for what?"
"Think about it," Matron Wei laid out calm. "In the past, the second Young Master walked free he'd have bolted straight out the manor gates! Instead he stayed home chatting with elders, backed up my mistress, and even asked Master for work in the family trade—a clear change of heart! Another capable heir stepping up for the Chen clan—isn't that cause for joy?"
Old Madam Xia beamed again. "Right! Asked his father for work first thing today!"
Cheered up too, Yao Qingyan waved Shuzhen back to her chair. "Don't stay standing—sit down."
Still waiting for her in-laws' formal nod, Qianli Xun sat back down reluctantly to let Matron Wei finish.
"Everything is already shifting in the right direction on its own," Matron Wei continued. "Push too hard and things snap; flow with the grain, everyone stays relaxed, and good fruit ripens natural. None of us mortals can predict tomorrow—look at Young Master! Two days ago he camped in brothels; today..."
Catching his cue to score points with his wife, Chen Haoyu declared loud, "Never stepping foot in a brothel again!"
All three elders blossomed into grins.
"Miss's request sounded blunt," Matron Wei wrapped up, "yet that's merely how she feels today—who knows what her heart holds tomorrow?"
Chen Jianglin exhaled a wry smile. "Leave young folks' business to themselves. Parents fretting changes nothing—every child walks their own fate."
With her husband yielding and Matron Wei's wisdom ringing true, Yao Qingyan relented with a warm smile. "Fine, Shuzhen—consummation is between you and Haoyu. If Mother isn't pressing, neither will I. Case closed."
Instead of gloating, a wave of genuine guilt washed over Qianli Xun—put herself in their shoes, and any loving parents would ache hearing a bride refuse their son. Rising to bow deeply, she spoke from the heart: "Thank you for your grace, Grandmother, Father, and Mother. Words fall short—from this day on, Chen Manor is truly my home."
"Family doesn't trade stiff thanks," Old Madam Xia chuckled. "Consider your reward claimed—no asking for extras later!"
Warm laughter rippled beneath the silk tree. For the first time in his life, Chen Haoyu truly tasted family warmth, gazing over at Zhu Shuzhen and marveling how loving one woman lit up the entire world around him.
Once the elders left, Qianli Xun threw her arms around Matron Wei in gratitude. Watching from the side, Chen Haoyu realized this sharp old matron might hold the key to melting his bride's heart. When Qianli Xun returned to Suxin Thatched Hall and Matron Wei headed to the back yard, he decided to tail her for advice.
Two steps in, Chouya intercepted them. "Young Master, may I borrow Qinggua for a quick chat?"
"Knock yourself out—just don't bother me!" Chen Haoyu waved, hurrying after Matron Wei while Chouya hauled a reluctant Qinggua toward the West Courtyard with surprising strength.
Reaching the back courtyard, Matron Wei was already turned waiting. "Need something, Young Master?"
Chen Haoyu flashed a cheeky thumbs-up. "Just realized today how legendary you are, Matron—top notch!"
"Out with it, Young Master."
"You know that tigress inside out—give me the secret to making her fall for me!"
"Simple. First: never call Miss 'tigress' again."
"Done—banished forever!"
"Second: learn to genuinely care for her."
"How?"
"Copy Eldest Master."
"Easy! What else?"
"Your soft approach is working fine—keep at it." Turning, Matron Wei disappeared into Jingyi Hall.
Chen Haoyu blinked after her: She wasn't even around when I used soft tactics—how'd she know?! Must have spies everywhere!
Eager to score points with Zhu Shuzhen, he headed back to the front yard—bumping straight into Qinggua drooping like frostbitten eggplant.
"What's with the funeral face?"
"Just walked into the West Courtyard and overheard Asheng confessing to Hongdou—and she said YES!" Qinggua groaned. "Got so mad I dragged Chouya right in front of them and yelled, 'Big deal, I've got my own sweetheart—Chouya!' Regretted it the second it left my mouth!"
"Hahaha! Saves me playing matchmaker—you're fated for Chouya!" Chen Haoyu slung an arm across his shoulders. "Honestly, Chouya's a solid catch—knows martial arts, nobody dares pick on you when she's around!"
"Hongdou knows martial arts too!"
"Sure, except her heart belongs to somebody else! Marry her and you'll lose sleep worrying about wandering eyes. Chouya's devoted solely to you—zero stress! Think about it: drop Hongdou among those seven tough manservants in the West Courtyard—sleep easy?"
Qinggua shook his head. "Nope."
"Drop Chouya among them?"
"Sleep like a baby!"
"Spend all day stressing over Hongdou getting stolen and you'll mess up serving me till I boot you! With Chouya, zero drama—she'll even baby you! Which beats which?"
"Put like that... Chouya wins hands down!"
"Attaboy! Settle down with Chouya and follow me to visit Young Madam."
Tugging his sleeve, Qinggua paused. "Wait, Young Master—which type is Young Madam? Sleep-easy, or lose-sleep?"
"Don't compare me to you!"
"Yet Prince Yi literally raided your wedding..."
"Shoo! Compare yourself to me again?! I've got looks, wealth, charm—and Zhu—" Catching "tigress" on his tongue per Matron Wei's rule, he corrected fast: "Zhu Shuzhen is already my wife! What's there to worry about? Quit stalling—time to woo my bride!"
Trailing behind, Qinggua chuckled silently: Calling it "wooing" himself—Young Master sure dropped his high-and-mighty airs fast!
Slipping into Suxin Thatched Hall, Chen Haoyu found her writing at her desk as expected—wondering how short poems took page after page of ink.
"Young Master is here, Miss," Kuqiao murmured.
"Freeze right there—talk from the doorway!" Qianli Xun called without moving.
"I'm your husband and master of Moxiang Courtyard—how does standing at the door like a lackey look? Better sitting!" Plopping into a chair uninvited, he called, "Kuqiao, heard you whisk mean tea—make your young master a bowl!"
"He has Qinggua—since when do you wait on him?" Qianli Xun blocked her.
Unbothered, Chen Haoyu grinned. "Qinggua, new mission: learn tea-whisking from Kuqiao! Soon I'll set up a tea table in Boya Study and get cultured myself!"
Setting down her brush, Qianli Xun sighed. "What do you want? I'm busy."
"Hunched over a desk all day will pack fat onto your waist! Come out for a stroll with me?"
Certain now he had caught genuine feelings—yet unable to return them—she shut him down flat. "Zero interest going anywhere with you."
"Say whatever you want, I don't mind—just one small suggestion."
"Spit it out."
"Quit calling yourself 'laoniang' like some tough street dame—clashes terrible with that gorgeous face."
"None of your business! I like talking like that. Don't like it, stay out of my sight!"
"Hard to stay out of sight sharing one courtyard—and as your husband, I'm dropping by plenty."
Dreading daily pests, Qianli Xun tried sweet reason. "Look, Chen Haoyu—why not take a concubine? Agree, and I'll treat you like my best pal and even crack skulls for you if anyone messes with you outside!"
#CH 243
#TITLE: Winning Over a Wife Takes Strategy
Twice in one single day pushing concubines on him—she really was desperate to paw him off onto another woman!
Stung yet firm, Chen Haoyu refused again. "One of you is plenty—add another woman and my head will explode. Quit bringing up concubines."
Wanting to splash cold water on his sudden infatuation, Qianli Xun spoke blunt. "I've seen ten dozen guys like you: rich spoiled playboy messing around shameless, then one day pretending to turn faithful and begging for true love while expecting applause like the past never happened. Nothing turns my stomach faster. Drop the syrupy lines—I don't buy them."
Too smitten to take offense, he replied steady, "What rich playboy? I'm flat broke! Sure I acted wild before I ever met someone I truly cared for—now that I love someone, I don't want to mess around anymore. Why hate me for growing up?"
Qianli Xun let out a cool huff.
Remembering Matron Wei's second rule—"care for her"—plus how much she had loved his grilled meat skewers at the chuiwan field, Chen Haoyu tried a fresh tack. "Stuck inside Chen Manor all day must bore you silly. I'm free today—let's ride out to West Lake! I'll grill meat skewers by the water while we take in the view. Nobody roasts meat tastier than me!"
Recalling his rowdy lakeside picnic last year lit Qianli Xun's fuse straight up. "Chen Haoyu, do you have an ounce of public decency?!"
"Inviting you for skewers and lake views—what's that got to do with public decency?!"
"Last year you hauled a mob out to West Lake trampling grass and flowers, filling the air with greasy smoke, and leaving piles of trash behind! Ruining gorgeous West Lake scenery—no manners yourself, and now trying to drag me down with you?"
Chastised by the girl he loved, guilt actually pricked him. "My bad, my bad—no more grilling by West Lake, don't be mad! Tell me where you want to go and I'll take you."
"Nowhere! Disappear right now and leave me in peace!"
Striking out on care and getting lectured on littering proved wooing her would take serious skill. Since silk-shop training didn't start until tomorrow, why not visit his father right now for expert coaching?
Rising, he bowed light. "I'll leave you to your work, Wife."
"Don't let the door hit you."
Stepping outside Suxin Thatched Hall, Chen Haoyu let out a long sigh. "How on earth did I end up married to the hardest nut in Lin'an—and fall head over heels for her to boot?"
"Karma," Qinggua chimed in.
"Watch that mouth!" Habit nearly lifted his boot—only to catch himself remembering his apology.
Surprised not to get kicked, Qinggua blushed. "Just kidding, Young Master—ignore me!"
"No, explain—why karma?"
"You hooked too many girls easy before, Young Master. Heaven sending someone unbreakable like Young Madam balances the scales!"
"Fair enough—guess I'll take my medicine since I fell for her against all logic!"
Reaching his parents' courtyard, Chen Haoyu waved Yingxue off from announcing him so he could peek in and study how his father actually treated his mother.
Stepping quietly over the threshold, he beheld Chen Jianglin standing before the vanity painting Yao Qingyan's eyebrows while both beamed warmly.
"Ever since marrying you, my own hand with an eyebrow brush has gone rusty," Yao Qingyan teased.
"With me here, why should my wife ever lift a brush?"
"You spoil me rotten."
"My wife—who else should I spoil?"
Chen Haoyu's jaw dropped—his own father was Lin'an's undisputed grandmaster of sweet talk! His own clumsy lines looked like amateur hour beside this.
