"Ahem, ahem!" he coughed.
Finishing the final stroke, Chen Jianglin glanced over. "Haoyu! Come sit."
Yao Qingyan stood and patted his arm. "Not keeping Shuzhen company in Moxiang Courtyard?"
"Came to ask Father for advice."
Thrilled to see father and son bonding, Yao Qingyan grabbed her shawl. "I'll leave you men to talk—off to sit with Old Madam Xia before the storyteller arrives. Heard Master Qianli Xun wrote a thrilling new chapter!" She swept out with Yingxue.
Chen Jianglin gestured to a chair at the table. "Silk shop starts tomorrow—ask whatever business questions you have."
Instead of talking trade, Chen Haoyu let out two sheepish chuckles. "Heh heh..."
"Quit giggling and spit it out!"
"Not about business, Father—I came to learn your secret for winning over a wife! Heh heh..."
Realization broke across Chen Jianglin's face, bursting into hearty laughter. "Ha! Winning your wife is big business too—came to the right master!"
Emboldened, Chen Haoyu leaned in. "Pass down every secret trick, Father, so you get that grandson fast!"
"No magic tricks—just putting your heart into it."
"I put my heart in, yet Zhu Shuzhen doesn't bite!"
"Calling your own wife by her full name—that's putting your heart in?"
"Okay, dropping the surname!"
Seeing his son actually taking counsel to heart convinced Chen Jianglin again what a masterstroke this match was. Holding up three fingers, he laid out the code.
"First: total devotion. Nothing ruins a home faster than a wandering eye—chasing one woman today and another tomorrow leaves a wife weeping and the whole house poisoned. Look at me: ever seen a concubine under my roof?"
"Check—easy! Second?"
"Second: show up and spend time with her. Busy as trade gets, always carve out hours beside your wife. Neglect her and she suspects brothels or mistresses; unrest inside the home sinks every venture outside."
"Noted! And third?"
"Third—and strongest of all—master one skill your wife truly needs better than anyone else. The moment she needs it and thinks first of you, she can't do without you—how could she keep you out of her heart?"
Chen Haoyu shot up a big thumbs-up. "Genius, Father! No wonder Mother never quarrels with you! Painting Mother's brows is your secret skill?"
"What else?"
"How long did it take to learn?"
"Started the day we wed. Botched it awful at first and got scolded—a full year before my brush grew steady. Now she won't touch a brush herself or let maids near her face; every morning she thinks straight of me."
As a boy, Chen Haoyu had thought a grown man painting eyebrows looked sissy; now he saw sheer mastery. "Third rule's tricky—I'll have to watch Shuzhen close to figure out what she needs most, then train like crazy!"
"Seeing you pour real thought into Shuzhen gladdens my heart," Chen Jianglin smiled. "Fine girl, fierce temper—the day you melt her into gentleness, you'll know she's accepted you."
Armed with his father's playbook, Chen Haoyu bowed out and marched back toward Moxiang Courtyard wondering how to scout his wife's deepest habit—then grinned down at Qinggua. "Slip over and summon Kuqiao quietly to Boya Study! Urgent questions!"
While Chen Haoyu headed to the back yard, Qinggua tiptoed up to Suxin Thatched Hall and craned his neck past the doorframe, spying only Young Madam writing.
"Sneaking around like a thief, Qinggua?" Kuqiao's voice startled him from behind.
Spinning around with a grin, he whispered, "Hunting for you, Sister Kuqiao! Young Master just got wooing lessons from Eldest Master and needs your help on the toughest rule!"
Delighted at the groom's devotion, Kuqiao nodded. "For Miss's sake, lead the way."
Inside Boya Study, Kuqiao blinked to find Chen Haoyu voluntarily flipping through a poetry volume—even Qinggua stared: "Since when do books look tasty, Young Master?"
Setting down the Collected Poems of Wang Wei, Chen Haoyu sniffed, "Uncultured bumpkin! Never heard 'in books lie houses of gold and maidens fair as jade'?"
"Used to swear books held nothing but dog droppings!" Qinggua fired back.
"Mouthing off? Ancient history!" Spotting Kuqiao, he beamed. "Bring Sister Kuqiao a chair, Qinggua!"
"Never offered ME a chair—she's a servant too!" Qinggua grumbled.
"Comparing yourself to Kuqiao? Sit anywhere you like, Kuqiao!"
Curtsying polite, Kuqiao stayed standing. "No ceremony needed, Young Master. Ask anything that helps Miss and I'll tell all."
"See how classy she talks, Qinggua, instead of roasting her own master nonstop?" Turning keen toward Kuqiao, Chen Haoyu got down to brass tacks. "You can see I'm dead serious about your mistress, yet she won't budge. Help me out: what does Shuzhen need most every single day?"
"Need most...?" Kuqiao tilted her head.
"Something she does every single day without fail."
"Oh! Either writing poetry, or..." Catching herself before leaking huaben, she pivoted fast: "...practicing martial arts!"
Both dead ends—reading Wang Wei just now gave him a headache, and his amateur grappling couldn't scratch her paint! "Aside from those two—something smaller she'd miss if it wasn't there, pure daily habit!"
Kuqiao thought hard. "Drinking my whisked tea every morning—does that count?"
Jackpot! Chen Haoyu lit up like a lantern. "Counts ten times over! Tea-whisking I can learn! How hooked is she?"
"More habit than obsession—needs one bowl every morning. One busy day I missed making it, and she fidgeted nonstop until I whisked her a bowl."
"Brilliant! I'll master tea-whisking till she can't start a day without me! Heh heh..." Lowering his voice, he added, "Keep today's talk secret from your mistress!"
"Lips sealed, Young Master!"
Mastering tea meant hiring a real master—the female tea virtuoso at Yongtai Teahouse sprang straight to mind! Tuition meant silver, and his purse sat empty, so he trotted straight to Old Madam Xia and confessed the whole plan. Thrilled to see him investing real heart in his bride, she handed over silver on the spot—no repayment required, calling it seed money for their wedded bliss.
#CH 244
#TITLE: Eldest Cousin's Plot Goes Up in Smoke
Within twenty-four hours, news of Chen Haoyu's sudden transformation swept both younger branches. All afternoon after the storyteller left, Old Madam Xia and Yao Qingyan had beamed nonstop, crediting Shuzhen and celebrating Chen Haoyu's turnaround right in front of Madam Bao and Madam Cui.
When Chen Jiangmu got home after dark, Madam Cui sat sulking with puffed cheeks until he pried the story out of her.
"Good news for the whole clan!" Chen Jiangmu laughed. "Another capable hand joining the business!"
"Means I have to write my surname upside down!" Madam Cui pouted.
"Huh?"
"Swore to myself that Zhu girl could never reform Haoyu—if she pulled it off, I'd write 'Cui' upside down!"
"Say it out loud?"
"Just in my head."
"Then who's the wiser? Quit torturing yourself and help me change—long day."
Relaxing, Madam Cui helped shed his robe. "Lesson learned—never look down on folks too fast. Still, straightening Haoyu out in days takes serious skill."
"Fierce fists keep him trembling! Never saw a wife train a husband like that."
"Makes sense, though," Chen Jiangmu mused, sitting on the bed. "Second marriage—she can't risk another divorce, so she rolled up her sleeves to whip up a decent husband. Plus Chen men have good hearts toward their wives at core—otherwise even her fists wouldn't turn him so fast."
Hanging his robe, Madam Cui sighed. "Most Chen men, except Haodong—saw fresh bruises on Anya's neck today."
"Haodong shines everywhere except hitting his wife—shameful habit, yet Second Brother's yard isn't our place to meddle." Snuffing the lamp, they turned in.
Over in Second Branch quarters, stunned by Haoyu's sudden U-turn before he could even deploy his next move, Chen Haodong strode into his parents' room late at night. Madam Bao sat untouched before her mirror while Chen Jiangshu sat brooding on the bed edge.
"Father, is it true Haoyu starts learning trade under Manager Qiu at the silk shop tomorrow?"
"True," Madam Bao snapped. "Old Madam Xia and First Sister-in-law crowed about it all afternoon. Pushing that marriage through backfired!"
"My fault for only wanting a fierce wife to box him in," Chen Haodong gritted. "Never dreamed it'd turn out like this."
Lifting his head, Chen Jiangshu stayed calm. "So what if Haoyu steps into the silk shop? You've been learning trade since boyhood—scared he'll catch up? Relax."
"Catch me? Not in three lifetimes," Chen Haodong scoffed, though unease lingered. "Still, flipping overnight after two days? Think he's faking it just to get that tigress off his back?"
"Could be—Haoyu's been slick at putting on acts since he could walk," Madam Bao agreed.
"Guessing gets us nowhere," Chen Jiangshu decided. "Ride with him to the silk shop tomorrow and sound him out. He trusts you blind—he'll spill everything."
Agreed, Chen Haodong returned to his own courtyard, where Xiaocui met him with a bow. "Young Master, Miss asks to speak with you."
Rare to be summoned by Ye Anya, a flicker of hope crossed his face as he stepped inside—only to freeze at her stone-cold gaze as she rose. "What is it?"
"My mind is made up," Ye Anya stated. "Grant me a mutual divorce."
Thunder out of a clear sky! Chen Haodong stormed up and seized her collar. "Barren hen—I'm merciful not tossing you out already, and you dare ask for mutual divorce?! Not in a million years!"
Squeezing her eyes shut, two quiet tears escaped. "Then repudiate me."
Suspicion flared sharp. "Hanging around Haoyu's divorced wife lately—did she poison your head with this stunt?"
"Between you and me—leave outsiders out." Resolved even unto death, Ye Anya refused to flinch.
Shoving her back, he spat, "Not repudiating you yet—maybe when I feel like it."
"What will it take for you to let me go?" she pressed steady.
Her frozen tone snuffed every spark of warmth inside him. Stepping close, he hissed, "Keep your mouth shut and play the spotless wife until next year when the clan names the heir! Once the estate is mine, we'll talk divorce—get me happy enough and maybe I'll even sign a mutual divorce!"
"Give me your word?"
Seeing joy flash across her eyes at the prospect of escaping him stabbed straight through his pride. "Dying to bolt from me that bad?"
"Every waking second."
That barb—piled atop Haoyu entering the silk shop—blew his fuse wide open. Dragging her onto the bed, fists flew once more while Xiaocui wept helplessly outside the door, praying for the nightmare to end.
Next morning at dawn, Chen Haoyu dressed sharp for his first day at the silk shop. Passing Suxin Thatched Hall's closed doors, he called loud through the planks: "Wife, heading to the silk shop! First day, gotta settle in—staying till dark, don't miss me too much!"
Inside at her vanity, Qianli Xun ignored him.
"Thoughtful of Young Master to check in before leaving," Kuqiao smiled.
Sliding a hairpin into her bun, Qianli Xun muttered, "Go tell him he doesn't need to report his comings and goings to me."
Cracking the door, Kuqiao relayed the message. Chen Haoyu grinned wide. "Only saying that to spare me trouble! I can't let down her thoughtfulness—gotta report every trip so she doesn't worry I'm flirting outside! If she frets, how could I focus?"
Kuqiao hid a giggle behind her hand.
Qianli Xun marched to the doorway with a glare. "Quit calling me 'Wife'—gives me chills! Get to work and stop bugging me!"
Freshly groomed, radiant in morning light, her scowl only made Chen Haoyu glow brighter. "Seeing my bride radiant at sunrise feels like a spring breeze—I could work till midnight without tiring!"
"More greasy poetry and taste my fist!"
"Easy, Wife—heading out!"
SLAM! The door shut right in his face.
Chen Haoyu chanted calm: Not mad, not mad, zero anger!
Trotting beside him, Qinggua asked, "She shuts you down cold every time—really doesn't burn you up?"
"She's my wife—why get mad at my own wife? Look at my father—my role model!"
"Exceptions exist," Qinggua muttered. "Heard Eldest Young Master beats First Young Madam all the time."
Chen Haoyu stopped short. "Who told you that? Never heard such a thing!"
"You camped outside all year—of course you missed house gossip!"
"If that's true, I'm giving Big Brother Dong an earful!"
Outside the main gate, Chen Haodong stood beside a waiting carriage with a warm smile. "Heard you're starting at the silk shop today, Haoyu—thrilled for you! Waited to ride together."
"Awesome, Big Brother Dong!" Climbing aboard together while Qinggua took the reins, Chen Haoyu chatted bright as Chen Haodong studied him close.
"Level with me, Haoyu—did Sister-in-law actually whip you into shape?"
"Who whipped whom? I was solid all along!"
Seeing that old cheeky smirk eased Chen Haodong's nerves. "Relax—if the silk shop bores you stiff, sneak out and play! I'll cover for you."
"Appreciate you always looking out for me, Big Brother Dong! Only I'm married now—can't loaf around shaming a celebrity wife like the Poetess of Jiangnan! Gotta step up so folks don't sneer she married a bum."
Alarm jolted Chen Haodong. "Seriously reforming—not putting on a show to get her off your back?"
"Think I'm that good an actor?" Leaning close with a goofy grin, Chen Haoyu whispered, "You'll never guess, Big Brother Dong—I went and fell head over heels for that tigress! First time loving someone feels incredible—gonna straighten up and make her fall for me too! Heh heh..."
Half his grand plot just went up in smoke! Watching his loafing cousin beam in pure bliss stoked green venom in Chen Haodong's gut: why did this bum stumble into love and joy while Chen Haodong stayed stuck beating a frozen bride he secretly craved?
Masking his envy, he probed, "Dead serious? Swear you aren't pulling my leg?"
"Swear to heaven—every word true!"
No doubting his earnest grin. Fine—reformed or lovesick, Chen Haodong sneered inside, I'll dig up a few of your past dirty deeds and blow up your cozy little house!
Remembering Qinggua's rumor, Chen Haoyu asked low, "Say, Big Brother Dong—word is you hit Sister-in-law. True?"
Open secret or not, Chen Haodong denied flat. "Pure nonsense—don't listen to servant gossip."
Figuring nobody as sharp as Big Brother Dong would stoop to hitting women, Chen Haoyu let it drop.
Back in Moxiang Courtyard after breakfast, Qianli Xun tried writing her new huaben about star-crossed lovers, only for her own heart to ache until she set the brush down and had Kuqiao stow the pages—then fetch the clay figurine.
Lifting out the bare-bottomed boy, memories of Shen Jianchen brought a flicker of warmth that faded fast into hollow solitude. Surrounded by Kuqiao, ten loyal servants, kind elders, and even persistent Chen Haoyu, an icy loneliness still gripped her inside this bridal room built for two. Outsiders might call her cold for banishing her husband on her wedding night, yet she could never force herself to play loving wife without love—leaving her alone with her own shadow.
Feeling the exact ache Zhu Shuzhen must have carried centuries ago, she tucked the clay boy back into its box, smoothed fresh paper, and brushed out a ci lyric:
"Alone I walk, alone I sit, / Alone I sing, alone I drink, alone I lie down too. / Standing long, my spirit breaks— / Helpless as the faint chill creeps right through.
Who sees this longing? / Tears have washed half my faded rouge away. / Grief and sickness press in turn; / Trimming the cold lamp down to ash, no dream will come to stay." [TN: Translator's rendering of Zhu Shuzhen's "Jianzi Mulan Hua: Spring Resentment"]
#CH 245
#TITLE: Sisters-in-Law Talk of Royal Guests
Reading over the freshly inked lyric, Qianli Xun felt Zhu Shuzhen's sorrow cut deeper even than her own—weakened by illness with no beloved to offer comfort, only cold lamps and tears.
It pulled back an old memory of falling sick before her transmigration.
Qianli Xun rarely caught colds, yet when one hit, it floored her—stuffy nose, racking cough, burning fever. Once, when every disciple at Qianli Fist Manor left for a month-long film shoot out of town, she stayed solo in her twenty-second-floor apartment writing web fiction—until a brutal flu slammed into her. Muscles aching, she tucked a thermometer under her arm and collapsed onto bed: thirty-eight point six degrees. Too weak even to shake the mercury down, she cracked open her nightstand drawer for fever pills—no water nearby! Wishing she had kept one female student home, she dragged herself upright, took two wobbly steps, and slumped onto the floor, clear-headed yet drained of every ounce of martial strength.
Her phone rang on the nightstand. Hoping for a disciple, she crawled over, spotted "Shen Jianchen" on the screen, swiped the green call button, and tapped speaker.
"Hey, Qianli Xun! Heard your students left town—bored solo? Want company?"
"I'm... sick," she croaked. "Come over... door code's my birthday."
"Sick?! Hang tight—right there!"
Hanging up brought a strange flood of relief—her very first glimpse of how dependable Shen Jianchen could be—letting her slump peaceful against the bedside till consciousness slipped.
When she woke, tucked snug beneath her duvet with a cooling gel patch across her forehead, savory steam filled the room. Shen Jianchen stood beside the bed wearing an apron, holding a steaming bowl of tomato-and-egg noodles.
"Awake! Made tomato-egg noodles—best thing for a fever," he smiled, setting the bowl down and sitting beside her. "Never saw a cold flatten anyone this hard. Good thing I called!"
"Thanks... pills in the drawer—pass me some water?"
"Every pill in your drawer expired ages ago! Bought fresh medicine downstairs and already gave you a dose."
"Wait—already took it? Don't remember a thing!"
"Found you slumped on the floor half-delirious—anyone could've kidnapped you! Carried you to bed, ran down to the pharmacy, and you swallowed every pill like a good kid." Peeling off the cooling patch, he laid a warm palm on her brow. "Fever's coming down. Sit up and eat before your next dose—no taking pills on an empty stomach."
Feeling much lighter, she propped herself against the headboard, thinking for the first time: If I ever date or marry, a guy like him wouldn't be half bad.
"Not taking the bowl?" he teased holding it out. "Want me to feed you? Wouldn't mind, only scared you'd punch me!"
Snatching the bowl, she grinned. "I can feed myself!"
"Shuzhen! Get off that desk—I barely visit, come chat with me!"
Chen Wenxin's bright voice—with Yuegui behind her—yanked Qianli Xun straight back to Song Lin'an. Her first visit since the wedding! Setting her memories aside, Qianli Xun rose warmly to greet her. "Missed you, Sister-in-law!"
Scanning the tidy hall, Chen Wenxin smiled. "Noticed the courtyard looked transformed—indoors too! No wonder Haoyu shaped up so fast."
"Where's Laibao?"
"Playing over in Grandmother's yard with half the house fussing over him, so I sneaked over to see you! Barely married in and you flipped this whole manor upside down—Grandmother grinning ear to ear surrounded by Mother and both aunts, everyone singing your praises! Meanwhile here you sit solo!"
"Grandmother has plenty of company now, leaving me time to write verse so I earn my Poetess title."
"New poem?" Strolling to the desk, Chen Wenxin scanned the wet sheet and tsked. "Still writing tearjerkers like our Chen house mistreats you?!" Taking Shuzhen's hand to inspect her rosy cheeks, she scoffed, "Bright eyes, glowing skin—what 'grief and sickness'?! Just moaning without an ache!"
That blunt quip made Qianli Xun laugh aloud. "Guilty—call it moaning without an ache! Sit down, Sister-in-law."
"Sitting indoors all day is dull—let's stroll the south garden and enjoy spring!"
Walking out through the south flower garden lined with white fringe trees, blazing crimson kapoks, golden trumpets, and lush magnolias, they chatted while Kuqiao and Yuegui trailed behind gossiping.
Fallen blossoms blanketed the winding gravel path so thick no footstep could avoid crushing them. Lu You's famous lines flashed into Qianli Xun's head: "Fallen in mud and ground to dust, she seems no more, / But her fragrance is still the same." [TN: Translated by Xu Yuanchong]
Blossoms blooming, falling, turning back to earth—just like human lives, maybe even the myth of Nüwa molding humans from clay held hidden truth. Before returning to dust, petals left a fleeting scent; blessed with two vivid lives, Qianli Xun resolved to leave her own unmistakable fragrance in this Song world as well—not just Zhu Shuzhen's immortal name, yet Qianli Xun's own spark too.
"Thank you for reforming Haoyu, Shuzhen," Chen Wenxin broke into her reverie.
"Enough elders thanked me already—if you start too, I'll feel awful when everyone gets disappointed in a few days."
"Meaning?"
"Doubt Chen Haoyu's good behavior lasts a week," Qianli Xun spoke frank, safe talking straight with her sister-in-law.
"Know my little brother best," Chen Wenxin laughed. "Once he truly flips, he sticks to it!"
Unwilling to debate blind sisterly faith, Qianli Xun left it to time—even trusting Matron Wei's judgment, old habits died hard.
"Since he's turning good, try opening up to him," Chen Wenxin urged gently. "Didn't marry your brother out of grand romance either, yet look how happy we are! Don't obsess over passion—solid character counts most; affection grows after marriage."
Spotting another elder-backed nudge, Qianli Xun offered a smooth delay: "Like you said, character counts—let time test Chen Haoyu first. Once he proves solid, then we'll talk."
Satisfied with that pledge, Chen Wenxin dropped the topic and strolled quiet a spell before asking, "Guess why I came home today?"
"Tell me."
"Father-in-law sent me."
"My father? Since when do you need his orders to visit your own parents?"
"Lin'an is throwing a grand banquet inviting the Chens—he sent me to deliver details while visiting home."
"Usually an invitation card does the trick—what's special about this banquet?"
"Haven't heard?"
"Heard what?"
"Prince Yi and Princess Jiahe just got back from Bianliang!"
Back already! A jolt of tangled gladness and dread froze Qianli Xun's tongue for a long beat before she managed, "When did they arrive?"
"First thing this morning—slipped back quiet as they left! Good thing Father-in-law stayed sharp and tipped off Butler Li at Youlin Retreat to send word the instant they arrived. Father-in-law led Lin'an's officials to pay respects at dawn, and tomorrow we're hosting a welcome banquet—also serving as their Lin'an wedding feast!"
Wedding feast... married now, meaning Mengrong was formally Princess Consort Yi. "Even so, why send you in person instead of a card?"
"Think about it," Chen Wenxin prompted low.
Realization hit hard, making Qianli Xun wish she hadn't asked: before her wedding Shen Jianchen had barged into Zhu Manor forcing Zhu Xiyan to kneel; on her wedding day he had raided the bridal procession and seen Mengrong wounded. Both the Zhus and Chens walked on eggshells terrified of royal wrath.
"The Chen family is footing the entire bill," Chen Wenxin added.
Guilt pricked Qianli Xun for saddling her in-laws with the tab of a storm she hadn't asked for. "Prince Yi isn't petty—he won't hold grudges against either family, especially since he acted on his own."
"Royal pride still demands full honor," Chen Wenxin noted. "Spotted his feelings for you back at the chuiwan field! Technically the Chens snatched the woman Prince Yi wanted—no wonder both fathers started planning this lavish feast the day he left, hoping to smooth things over."
Dreading facing Mengrong too soon, Qianli Xun asked, "Who's invited?"
"Lin'an officials and top gentry, primary wives only. I'm going on your brother's coattails; you and Haoyu aren't even on the list. Only exception among the younger generation is Qiao Wenxian and Miao Zhiyu."
A quiet wave of relief washed through Qianli Xun—spared for now! Seeing Mengrong was inevitable sooner or later, just not tomorrow. Wait—why shrink like a criminal when she hadn't betrayed her? Except... didn't every secret thought of Shen Jianchen betray Mengrong a little?
#CH 246
#TITLE: Prince Yi and His Consort Return to Lin'an
The Bianliang wedding had been grand enough to satisfy Qiao Mengrong—she had wed her brother at last, His Majesty's edict leaving him no escape even with another woman in his heart.
Yet on their wedding night, he had never lifted her red bridal veil, leaving only quiet words before walking out: "Mengrong, I can stand in Zhao Pu's shoes to care for you and marry you, yet I cannot take his place in the bridal bed—because I only ever saw you as a little sister."
Left weeping alone in the bridal chamber, every tear hardened into pure venom toward Zhu Shuzhen, the thief who had stolen her brother's heart.
Next morning, he hurried to start back for Lin'an—and Qiao Mengrong hurried too, burning to launch her payback. Xilan alone lacked bite; she needed a seasoned strategist, and Matron Zou stepped right up when Qiao Mengrong spilled everything that had happened in Lin'an.
"The capital manor runs itself," Matron Zou had vowed. "I'll go to Lin'an with Your Highness and see what kind of vixen bewitched Prince Yi into walking out on his own bridal night!"
Back at Youlin Retreat after the jolting journey, Qiao Mengrong rested to regain her strength and sharpen her opening strike against her former best friend.
Shen Jianchen knew full well how deep his refusal wounded Mengrong, yet closing his eyes to consummate without love felt like turning into a beast. Maybe someday he would accept her as his true consort—just not now, not with his vow to stay chaste for Qianli Xun still fresh.
"Stay chaste"—part of him felt noble, part absurd. In a rotting dynasty ruled by a foolish emperor and corrupt ministers where a man couldn't save the realm, holding his own moral line felt like the last dignity left; yet clinging to a promise Qianli Xun might not even care about felt foolish too.
All road back from Bianliang, he had resolved to throw himself into real work: first, to escape awkward guilt facing Mengrong under one roof every day; second, to stay too busy to dwell on Qianli Xun, hoping time might let him let go and eventually accept Mengrong as his wife.
Barely settled back at Youlin Retreat, Zhu Xiyan arrived leading a pack of city officials.
"Forgive us disturbing Your Highness after a long journey," Zhu Xiyan bowed low. "Having missed seeing you off to Bianliang, we hurried straight over to beg pardon."
Annoyed yet needing a favor, Shen Jianchen waved it off. "My choice to slip out quiet—no fault on Lin'an's officials."
Bowing lower still, Zhu Xiyan continued, "Thank you for your grace! Tomorrow Lin'an's officials are hosting a welcome-and-wedding banquet in honor of Your Highness and Princess Consort Yi. We beg you both to grace us with your presence."
Sick of the emperor's extravagant court culture, Shen Jianchen frowned. "Bianliang's wedding was lavish enough—throwing another feast wastes the people's sweat and blood. Cancel it."
Every official dropped straight to his knees.
"Forgive us, Your Highness!" Zhu Xiyan pleaded. "Unable to attend your wedding in the capital, we began preparing this feast the day you left to express our devotion. Not a copper comes from public coffers—the Chen family is paying every coin!"
Seeing through it at once—the Chens buying peace after the wedding raid—Shen Jianchen relented so the family wouldn't take lingering jitters out on Qianli Xun. "Very well. My consort and I will attend tomorrow. Rise."
"Thank you, Your Highness!"
Wanting a private word, Shen Jianchen dismissed the other officials to wait in the courtyard while Zhu Xiyan stayed hunched in respectful silence.
"Since taking office as Military Commissioner of Lin'an," Shen Jianchen began, "I haven't lifted a finger for local affairs—feels like letting His Majesty down..."
Panic seized Zhu Xiyan: Wants to dig into city governance?! Pull one thread and my whole yamen unravels!
Reading the sweat on his brow, Shen Jianchen had zero illusions—from court down to counties the empire was Swiss cheese, and no single man could rewrite history. Skip saving corrupt officials; do something tangible for ordinary people instead.
"You handle civil administration, Prefect Zhu, and military posts need no meddling from me. I want hands-on work close to common folk. What post fits best?"
Huge relief washed over Zhu Xiyan. "Your Highness's love for the people moves me! One post deals straight with townsfolk, though it's far too lowly for a prince—afraid it would insult your rank."
"Name it."
"Judicial Administrator—handling criminal investigations and trials for commoners. Only Lower Eighth Rank, far beneath Your Highness!"
Music to Shen Jianchen's ears! "Lower Eighth Rank sits within your authority to transfer, Prefect. I'll take Judicial Administrator! Move the current holder to another decent post—from tomorrow on, I run Lin'an's Judicial Court."
Thrilled to hand off courtroom drudgery without losing political grip, Zhu Xiyan bowed fast. "I'll file the orders today! Still, since His Majesty named you Military Commissioner, I dare not alter your imperial title—we'll announce that Military Commissioner Prince Yi acts as Judicial Administrator on His Majesty's behalf to look after the common folk!"
Rolling his eyes inside at local flattery crediting his useless emperor-father, Shen Jianchen nodded. "Fine. I report for duty right after tomorrow's banquet."
Once the officials left, Bai Feng burst out, "Your Highness, haven't seen Kuqiao in ages—may I go visit her now?"
"Go," Shen Jianchen said, then added low, "Ask Kuqiao how she's doing."
"Yes, Your Highness." Stepping out, Bai Feng pitied Princess Jiahe—married, yet the prince's heart stayed stuck on Youqi Jushi! Still, imagining being forced to marry anyone besides Kuqiao made him understand his master all too well.
Alone, Shen Jianchen walked over to break the news to Mengrong before she heard from servants.
Waking from her nap, Qiao Mengrong stood in her small maiden yard feeling stung—married now, yet still parked in her old courtyard! As Princess Consort Yi, his main hall belonged to her as their bridal chamber. Just as she stepped out to inspect it, Shen Jianchen walked through the gate.
Rushing straight into his arms, she pleaded, "Brother, I don't want to stay in this side yard anymore—I want to move into your main hall! We're husband and wife now!"
Unwilling to say yes yet unable to push her away, he deflected. "Is Matron Zou settled in?"
"Next courtyard over," she murmured, clinging tighter.
"Mengrong, two things to tell you. First, Lin'an's officials are throwing us a wedding banquet tomorrow—come with me."
"Of course! Thoughtful of them—we must honor it." Perfect chance to rally Lin'an's noble ladies against Zhu Shuzhen!
"Second, starting tomorrow I'm acting as Judicial Administrator and staying at the Judicial Court most days, so I won't have much time here..."
Knowing he was dodging her, Mengrong stepped back with reddened eyes. "Can't stand the sight of me so much you're running away?"
"Mengrong... our wedding happened fast. Give me time to adjust, and maybe..."
"You still can't let her go! The harder you cling to her, the deeper I hate her!"
Catching her own outburst before tipping him off to her plans, she smoothed her face fast. As Princess Consort Yi, she held power now—she would win her brother AND crush her enemy. "Do as you please, Brother—I'll just move to the Judicial Court with you!"
"Too rough and cramped there for you. I promise I'll come back every week to visit."
Actually, plotting against Zhu Shuzhen worked way better without Brother watching every move! Time enough to win him later. "Alright, Brother—as you wish."
Her sudden gentle obedience stabbed Shen Jianchen with fresh guilt. Pulling her into a brief hug, he murmured, "Don't blame me, Mengrong, and don't hate Youqi Jushi. She married Chen Haoyu—she and I are over. Only because I woke up as a different man with someone already in my heart—once I let her go completely, I'll try my best to accept you."
Warm in his arms yet seething inside—he actually had to "try" to accept her?!—"Grant me one request, Brother."
Letting go, he asked, "What?"
"Let me redo your main hall as our bridal chamber."
Staying at the court six days a week anyway, why deny her this small comfort? "Arrange it however makes you happy."
At last a genuine smile touched her lips.
Leaving her yard, instead of walking to the Divine Willow, Shen Jianchen climbed the tall wooden viewing platform he hadn't visited in ages. Looking down over the canopy thick with red ribbons, he wondered if Qianli Xun had sat on his boulder while he was gone. Sitting at the wooden table with closed eyes, he breathed the distant willow breeze and replayed every shared moment since transmigrating.
Meanwhile, Qiao Mengrong summoned Matron Zou for a quick council.
"Come with me to tomorrow's banquet, Matron—and help me pick gifts for the officials' wives. Not too extravagant, not cheap, nice enough to make them thrilled and eager to follow my lead."
"With your rank, Your Highness, any gift flatters them," Matron Zou smiled. "Remember that chest of pigeon-egg pearls His Majesty gifted for your wedding? Spare change to you, priceless treasures to Lin'an's ladies!"
"Brilliant! Useless gathering dust in my trunks—pack them up!"
"Right away! I'll send servants to buy neat brocade boxes in town and pack each pearl tonight."
Thrilled to have Matron Zou handling retreat affairs and strategy alike, Qiao Mengrong felt every chess piece clicking into place.
#CH 247
#TITLE: First Day at the Silk Shop
Strolling along flower-strewn paths with Chen Wenxin, a Chen Manor maid hurried over. "Eldest Miss, Second Young Madam—someone at the gate asking for Kuqiao! Says he's Guard Bai from Prince Yi's household."
Chatting behind with Yuegui, Kuqiao had missed all mention of Prince Yi's return. Her face lit up like fireworks: "Miss—!"
Glad to let her go—and secretly curious for news of Prince Yi and Mengrong—Qianli Xun waved her off. "Run along, I don't need you here."
"Thank you, Miss!" Kuqiao bolted.
"Look at that girl sprint—forgot her own mistress the instant Guard Bai showed up!" Chen Wenxin teased.
"Getting tired, Sister-in-law—let's head over to Grandmother's before the storyteller starts." Not actually tired, just craving noisy company so Shen Jianchen's shadow wouldn't keep creeping back in.
"Heard hiring a storyteller on monthly retainer was your brainchild!" Chen Wenxin beamed as they turned back. "Now half the rich houses in Lin'an signed him up too—man dashes house to house earning way more than he ever made in Goulan Wasi! Our Chen house set a whole citywide trend!"
"Guess I ought to charge him commission!" Qianli Xun laughed.
"Count me in!"
In Old Madam Xia's buzzing yard, with maids entertaining Laibao elsewhere, they settled in to enjoy the storyteller. Hearing her own plot spun vivid by a seasoned pro pushed Shen Jianchen clean out of Qianli Xun's mind.
Chatting afterward over tea, noticing Ye Anya absent yet again, Qianli Xun seized a lull to ask, "Second Aunt, where's First Sister-in-law?"
Madam Bao's smile froze. "Hates crowds—just likes hiding in her room."
Madam Cui scoffed inside: Everybody knows Anya only hides after Haodong beats her!
Old Madam Xia set her cup down sharp. "You and Jiangshu better talk sense into Haodong! What kind of loser beats his own wife? Running a great family starts with honoring your own home—a wife is a man's treasure vault! Keep bruising and making your own vault weep, and fortune walks straight out the door!"
Unconvinced inside yet bowing her head, Madam Bao murmured, "Yes, Mother—I'll tell him."
"Telling isn't enough—make sure Haodong takes it to heart!"
"Jiangshu and I will lecture him tonight."
"A wife is a man's treasure vault"—a striking maxim that stuck with Qianli Xun, making her think of Chen Jianglin's quiet devotion to Yao Qingyan while Chen enterprises kept thriving. For one bizarre second, Chen Haoyu crossed her mind—what if he grew up to treat her like his father treated his mother? She shook her head laughing at herself: a guy who haunted brothels? No way!
When Old Madam Xia tired, the crowd dispersed and Chen Wenxin took Laibao back to Zhu Manor.
Returning alone to Suxin Thatched Hall, Qianli Xun found Kuqiao back at the tea table whisking tea with a radiant glow. Sitting on the cushion across from her, Qianli Xun fished subtle: "Back already? Did Bai Feng put on weight or slim down?"
Knowing full well who her mistress actually wanted news on, Kuqiao answered smooth while setting down the bowl, "Bai Feng says Prince Yi looks the same—only difference is he's married to Princess Jiahe now. Drink up, Miss."
Taking a sip, Qianli Xun arched a brow. "Asked about Bai Feng—why bring up Prince Yi?"
Why keep pretending with me, Miss? Kuqiao thought.
"Gone all that time—didn't Bai Feng bring you a souvenir?"
Hesitating only a breath—Bai Feng brought her a gift, nothing from Prince Yi, yet both were married now anyway—Kuqiao answered honest, "He did—a woodblock print from Bianliang!"
"Let me see!"
Fetching it from Yuening Room, Kuqiao handed over a crisp carved portrait—her own smiling likeness caught to the life!
"Thoughtful guy, Bai Feng." A quiet pang of envy tugged at Qianli Xun—Kuqiao could see her sweetheart open, accept his gifts without shame, while she and Shen Jianchen stood walled apart by twin marriages.
Suddenly Kuqiao dropped straight to her knees, bursting into sobs.
"Hey—just saw Bai Feng, why are you bawling?!"
"My heart aches for you, Miss! Boo-hoo..."
Setting the print down, Qianli Xun pulled her up onto the cushion. "Aches for what? I'm fine!"
Wiping her eyes, Kuqiao confessed, "Terrified you're heading back into the same misery as Lin Manor!"
"How? I'm not the old me."
Summoning every ounce of nerve, Kuqiao spoke straight. "Forget Prince Yi, Miss! You're both married—dwelling on him brings nothing good. The Chen family is wonderful; I'm praying you and Young Master work out!"
All at once Qianli Xun felt completely outnumbered: Grandmother, her in-laws, the Zhus, Matron Wei, the whole courtyard, even loyal Kuqiao—every last soul rooting for Chen Haoyu! How unfair was it that two days of playing nice turned the whole world into his fan club?
"Mind your own business—quit meddling in mine!"
"I'm just a maid, no right to meddle—only because you treat me so well, I want you safe! Even if you don't think of anyone else, think of Princess Jiahe—what wife can bear another woman holding her husband in her heart?"
That bull's-eye hit hard. Her face going grave, Qianli Xun stood slowly and spoke flat: "Lock that peeing clay boy away where I'll never see it. I won't touch it again."
Obeying with a heavy pinch of guilt, Kuqiao hated snuffing out her mistress's last tiny comfort.
Meanwhile, stepping down outside the Chen Silk Shop with Chen Haodong, Manager Qiu greeted them both warmly. "Both young masters gracing the silk shop—rare sight!"
Showing off his turf right away, Chen Haodong asked, "Southwest merchants here?"
"Waiting in the reception parlor, Eldest Young Master."
Turning to Haoyu with mock care, Chen Haodong said, "Learn the ropes from Manager Qiu while I close a major deal. Take good care of Haoyu, Manager Qiu—don't let Eldest Uncle down!"
"Count on me, Eldest Young Master."
Teach all you want—he'll never touch my heels! Chen Haodong sneered inside before striding off.
"First visit to the silk shop, Second Young Master—let me give you the grand tour," Manager Qiu offered.
Starting in the busy front storefront packed with customers and bolts of gauze, satin, crepe, damask, and silk floss, they passed through a back arch into a bright courtyard with blooming flowerbeds ringed by covered galleries housing bustling workshops.
Inside the Weaving Hall, rows of looms clacked nonstop as skilled weavers worked pedals and flying shuttles. "Every bolt sold upfront comes off these looms," Manager Qiu explained. "We screen nimble, hardworking girls from town and countryside, train them six months, pay generous wages, and leave them a lifelong trade—poor families line up to join."
Next came soft zither music drifting from the Embroidery Hall, where rows of nimble-fingered embroiderers bent over tall frames while a female musician played soothing melodies. "Lin'an's finest needlework! Only girls with slender, supple fingers make the cut. Two core techniques—flat stitch and couching—split by thread into gold-couched and colored silk, with sub-stitches from satin, stem, and long-and-short to gold-laying, ring-gold, velvet-pile, and silk appliqué..."
Listening to a dozen stitch names left Chen Haoyu dizzy—who knew needlework held an entire universe of craft?
Out back sprawled the vast reeling yard stacked with baskets of white cocoons, steaming cauldrons, and bamboo racks draped with gleaming reeled silk. "Half our cocoons come from our own country manor's mulberry groves, half bought from top farmers," Manager Qiu beamed. "Eldest Master hired expert growers; every summer the huge sweet mulberries go free to every weaver, embroiderer, and clerk first!"
Tour complete, Manager Qiu guided him into a neat back office. Scanning the room, Chen Haoyu asked, "So—what job do you have lined up for me?"
#CH 248
#TITLE: Starting Out Behind the Counter
Instead of answering right away, Manager Qiu took the main desk chair, dropped his polite smile, and turned stern. "Since Eldest Master placed you under me, Second Young Master, you follow every order to the letter—until you graduate, I don't care if the Jade Emperor himself walks in! See that desk? That's yours."
Chen Haoyu eyed the cramped side desk and stiff wooden stool—not even close to the big seat he had pictured! Swallowing his gripe, he stepped over to sit—only for Manager Qiu to halt him.
"Not so fast! Earning that seat takes real grit first."
Trailing along wide-eyed, Qinggua figured his master would storm right out after getting lectured like an apprentice. Instead, anger flickered across Chen Haoyu's brow, faded fast, and he asked steady, "What do I have to do?"
"Two months as a front-counter clerk, three months in the accounting room, then closing three major deals solo—pass all three, and you earn that desk to train as manager."
"So I haven't even earned that cramped seat yet?"
"Sharp ear, Second Young Master."
"Then why drag me in here?"
"So you see firsthand who runs this shop."
Half regretting volunteering for work, Chen Haoyu pictured his wife's face and gritted his teeth. "Did Big Brother Dong climb the same ladder?"
"Eldest Young Master started selling bolts upfront at age seven or eight—worked every Chen shop in Lin'an."
Steeling his jaw, Chen Haoyu nodded. "Then I'll match him! Put me wherever you want, Manager Qiu."
Manager Qiu gave an approving nod while Qinggua marveled silently: Young Master really DID grow up!
Back at Youlin Retreat, Bai Feng climbed the wooden viewing platform where Prince Yi sat alone. Eager for news yet holding his royal restraint, Shen Jianchen asked, "Saw Kuqiao? Everything alright?"
Knowing who mattered, Bai Feng got straight to the point. "Kuqiao said Youqi Jushi found out Young Master Chen spread last year's rumors."
"Tried shielding her from that pain, yet it came out anyway..." Shen Jianchen murmured. "Must have cut her deep learning she married the culprit."
"Kuqiao said she already wiped the slate clean with him."
"Wiped it clean?" Relief and sharp dread tangled in his chest.
"One more thing, Your Highness—not sure if I should say..."
"Speak."
"Kuqiao says Young Master Chen turned over a new leaf, fell in love with Youqi Jushi, and went to the Chen Silk Shop at dawn to learn trade."
"Reformed? In love with her?"
Shooting to his feet, Shen Jianchen started down the steps—then slowed halfway down. Charging off to do what? She was married; Chen Haoyu falling for her and reforming was only natural. Strength draining from his knees, he sat down right on the wooden stairs. Bai Feng quietly sat a step above.
Before long, Matron Zou walked up to the base of the steps and curtsied. "Have a moment, Your Highness? Need a word."
Walking down, Shen Jianchen led her silently back to his main hall while Bai Feng tactfully waited outside.
Inside, Matron Zou rose and bowed again before speaking bold. "Princess Jiahe is Princess Consort Yi now, Your Highness—leaving her alone in an empty bed isn't right. Consummate your marriage tonight!"
Shen Jianchen stayed stone silent.
"I watched her pour her heart out nursing you when she was still just a commandery princess! Marrying devotion like that is a rare blessing—you can't recover, spot some wildflower in Lin'an, and trample all she sacrificed!"
"I told you before—I am not Zhao Pu..."
"Stop that talk! If you aren't His Majesty's son Prince Yi, who are you? Waking from death wiped your memories, sure, yet you're a full-blooded man—how can you stay cold beside a bride fair as jade? Must be you haven't tasted wedded sweetness yet—try tonight, and tomorrow you'll be glued to her hip, hehe!"
Seeing his stony face, she dropped her chuckle and pressed harder. "Her Highness told me you fancied a poetess in Lin'an. You're a prince—fancy a woman, take her as a concubine if you like, yet never let an outsider drive a wedge between you and your primary consort! Besides, that poetess already married someone else—why break Her Highness's heart over another man's wife?"
Dead silence answered her. Sensing a brick wall, Matron Zou stood. "Said my piece, Your Highness—your call."
The instant she left, Shen Jianchen strode out into the yard and barked at Bai Feng, "Come with me to the Chen Silk Shop!"
Knowing his master wanted to size up Chen Haoyu in person, Bai Feng went to hitch the carriage.
Meanwhile, decked in plain clerk cotton upfront at the silk shop, Chen Haoyu watched shoppers stream in and crooked a finger at Qinggua. "Funny—most buyers are women, yet every clerk is a guy. Why?"
"How'd I know, Young Master? Ask me to run errands, not market strategy!"
A senior clerk finishing a sale spotted unfamiliar faces standing idle and snapped, "Hey! New hire? Quit standing like a post—greet customers! Who's he?"
"I'm his servant," Qinggua piped up.
"A clerk bringing a personal servant?!"
Dropping the act, Chen Haoyu puffed up. "I'm Chen Manor's Second Young Master—why can't I bring my servant?"
The clerk shrank three inches, grinning sheepishly. "Forgive my blind eyes, Second Young Master—right back to work!"
Bored once the guy turned obsequious, Chen Haoyu looked at Qinggua. "Silly dragging a servant while dressed as a clerk—go on home."
"Not leaving your side, Young Master! I'll grab a clerk smock and pitch in too!"
"Fair enough—go change!"
Watching seasoned clerks greet buyers with bright smiles and crisp pitches looked simple enough. When a young woman walked in, Chen Haoyu stepped right up beaming. "Welcome, Miss! Looking for anything special?"
"Fabric for an everyday robe for my father."
"Dutiful daughter! Chen shop carries everything—take your pick!"
Looking overwhelmed at towering shelves, she asked, "Not sure which weave works best—recommend something?"
Chen Haoyu pointed to a bright pastel bolt. "How about that one?"
"That's women's silk—not for my father!"
Red-faced, he pivoted fast to darker tones. "Over here—men's fabrics!"
"Tell me about the weaves so I can pick right."
Stumped—he wore fine silk daily without knowing a single loom name—he stammered, "N-nothing fancy to explain—feels nice, nice color, grab it!"
Frowning, the girl snapped, "Chen clerks always know every weave cold! Why don't you know a thing?"
Another clerk glided smoothly in. "Apologies, Miss—he's brand-new! Let me help you."
Stepping aside to listen, Chen Haoyu watched the clerk shine: "All these bolts are leno-weave gauze—fine threads, strong yet airy with open pores, ideal for summer robes. We carry horizontal, vertical, and patterned weaves; for a gentleman's everyday robe, this plain unfigured gauze hits the mark."
"Wrap it up!" the girl beamed.
Changing back in time to witness the rescue, Qinggua patted his master's arm. "First day, Young Master—you'll outshine them all soon!"
"Finally said something pleasant!"
Handing over the parcel, the clerk added smoothly, "Chen Tailor Shop sits right next door—half price sewing on our bolts, or ready-made robes one door past!"
Passing Chen Haoyu out the door, the customer tossed back, "Take notes!"
Bowing quick once she left, the clerk apologized, "Sorry to cut in on your sale, Second Young Master!"
"You saved it! What's your name?"
"Ergui, sir."
"You're my mentor now—teach me everything!"
"I wouldn't dare, Second Young Master!"
"Dare or I'll have Manager Qiu fire you!"
"Teaching, teaching right away!"
Finishing his southwest deal and escorting the merchants out, Chen Haodong spotted his cousin in clerk clothes taking notes from Ergui and sneered silently. Once the clients rode off, he marched over and grabbed Haoyu's sleeve. "Don't waste time with counter clerks—come stroll town with me and I'll teach you real trade!"
Tempted yet realistic—can't even pass clerk basics, let alone big deals—Chen Haoyu declined. "Too advanced for me yet, Big Brother Dong! Let me nail the basics first."
Afraid pushing harder would tip his hand, Chen Haodong instructed the clerks loud to take good care of his cousin and stalked outside—smiling dark at the sight of Scarface and his cronies loitering across the street right on schedule. Shooting them a sharp nod, he climbed into his carriage and rolled away.
#CH 249
#TITLE: Hard to Let Go of One Heart
Scarface swaggered through the silk shop doors with his pack of street hoodlums, freezing every clerk and sending shoppers edging toward the corners until they bounded up grinning at Chen Haoyu. Ergui slipped off to assist other buyers.
Annoyed they had spooked customers, Chen Haoyu scowled. "What are you doing in here? Step outside!"
Out on the street, before Scarface could open his mouth, Chen Haoyu lit into them: "Look at you bunch of lazy bums showing up at my workplace! Done hanging with you—I'm busy!"
"Whoa—few days gone and Young Master Chen's dressed like a shop clerk?" Scarface jeered. "Did Young Madam beat your brains loose?"
"Watch that mouth! My wife treats me great!"
Long resentful of these leeches dragging his master off while leaving him behind, Qinggua puffed up and chimed in: "Scram before I tell Young Madam to come beat you crying for your mommas!"
Ignoring Qinggua flat, one hoodlum baited Chen Haoyu: "Don't tell us you don't miss Chun Jinmo?"
A tiny twinge of guilt crossed Chen Haoyu. "She doing alright?"
"How could she be without you guarding her?" Scarface jumped in. "Crying every day! The morning after Young Madam dragged you off, Master Jiang stormed into Chunxiang Brothel—Jinmo swore she'd rather die! Good thing Master Jiang didn't force her—bought out her bookings exclusive till she warms up, promising redemption later. Madam's happy taking his silver, only Jinmo still pines for you nonstop!"
Thinking of his wife back home, Chen Haoyu steeled himself. "Pass word to Chun Jinmo: back then I was bored with an empty heart, just passing time—tell her not to take it serious. Never setting foot in Chunxiang Brothel again; tell her to move on."
Realizing the gravy train had dried up for good, one lackey whined, "If you drop us, Young Master Chen, how do we eat?"
"Quit leeching and earn honest wages!" Chen Haoyu suggested. "I'll ask Big Brother Dong to get you hauling cargo at the wharves."
Instantly every hoodlum pulled a sour grimace at the mention of manual labor.
"Look at your lazy mugs—quit bothering me!" Turning back toward the shop doors, a calm voice halted him.
"Young Master Chen."
Turning, he spotted Guard Bai standing beside Prince Yi's carriage—back from Bianliang already!
"Guard Bai? Need something?"
"His Highness invites you inside the carriage for a word."
Nobody turned down a royal summons. Chen Haoyu climbed aboard while Scarface's crew caught wind of "His Highness," paled, and melted fast down the alley. Remembering Bai Feng's lethal fists, Qinggua kept a respectful distance down the block.
Inside the carriage, Chen Haoyu bowed polite. "Had I known Your Highness returned, I'd have called in person—how did you track me to the silk shop?"
"Whoever I wish to find, I find," Shen Jianchen said calm. "Besides, Chen Silk Shop is hard to miss." Studying his plain cotton smock, he asked, "Dressed like a clerk?"
"Turning over a new leaf, Your Highness—learning family trade from the ground up."
"Truly reforming?"
"Swear it! Just chased off my old street cronies trying to drag me back to Chunxiang Brothel."
"And she... is she happy?"
Catching straight on who brought Prince Yi here, Chen Haoyu answered candidly, "Hard to tell yet—still, stick with it long enough and she'll warm up. We're married, after all."
Watching Prince Yi's lashes drop in quiet bleakness, a heavy pause stretched before Shen Jianchen asked, "Remember what you promised me outside the Qiantang Gang before I left for Bianliang?"
Oh boy—promising to hand Zhu Shuzhen over! Scared of being charged with deceiving royalty, Chen Haoyu dropped straight to his knees on the carriage floor—his first time kneeling in a moving-room box!
"I hadn't fallen for Shuzhen back then—ran my mouth reckless! Don't hold me to it, Your Highness! With your rank, wave one finger and any beauty under heaven lines up—why fight a commoner over his wife?"
"That's how low you think of me?"
Isn't it true?! Chen Haoyu yelled inside. Raiding my wedding, marrying the princess, and still pining after my wife! If you weren't a prince I'd throw hands right here! Learn from Qiao Wenxian—settled down quiet and let go!
"Chen Haoyu."
"Here, Your Highness!"
"Let me speak plain with you today," Shen Jianchen said steady. "My feelings for her never changed before, don't change today, and won't change tomorrow. Yet since fate led her to marry you, I respect her choice. Ever step back into a brothel or wrong her again, and I will not show mercy."
"Step out of line and my wife's fists will flatten me long before Your Highness lifts a hand!"
Hearing "my wife" roll off his tongue twistedwhy would they give me a hard time?"
Old Madam Xia laughed and chided him. "Nonsense again. Did you forget why your father-in-law forced you to marry the Zhu girl?"
"A real man doesn't dwell on past glories, Grandmother. Don't bring that up again, or if that tigress overhears, your grandson won't know what hit him."
To coax more silver out of her, he needed to keep her beaming, so he switched gears. "Grandmother, I always pray for your long, healthy life. At Zhu Manor today, I dug up the secret behind how their Old Ancestor has lived so long. Want to hear it?"
Guessing he was just buttering her up, Old Madam Xia played along all the same. "Of course I want to hear."
Chen Haoyu lowered his voice with mock mystery. "I wandered around the Zhu Buddhist shrine for ages, and all I heard inside was the tap of a wooden fish drum and chanting. I figure the Old Ancestor lived this long from all that drumming and chanting. Tomorrow I'll buy you a wooden fish and a string of prayer beads so you can give it a try, all right?"
"Save it. Your grandmother isn't cut out for chanting sutras. Come see me every day and keep me company—when I'm happy, long life takes care of itself."
"Deal, I'll visit you all the time." Wondering how to sic his grandmother on Zhu Shuzhen, he put on his best pitiful face. "Grandmother, you have to help me."
"Help you with what?"
"Zhu Shuzhen is bullying me."
"How is she bullying you?"
"She threw out my maids, stole my courtyard, seized my properties, and capped me at twenty taels of silver a month! I'm practically a pauper now. Step out the door and nobody believes I'm a Chen."
Old Madam Xia laughed. "Your bride has a razor-sharp tongue. Even I can't talk her down. Besides, who told you to kneel and beg her to marry you, or sign some prenuptial contract? Blame yourself for gambling with Master Jiang and near losing the whole Chen estate."
Chen Haoyu blinked in shock. "How do you know about that?"
"Your bride told me. Your parents know too."
Zhu Shuzhen! You didn't leave me a shred of face in front of my own family! Just you wait! he fumed inside.
"Grandmother, gambling was wrong, and I swear I'll never touch it again. Still, you have to teach Zhu Shuzhen a lesson for me. She's walking all over my head!"
"How should I teach her a lesson?"
"Find excuses to give her a hard time whenever you get the chance."
"She is your wife now. Giving her a hard time means giving you a hard time too."
"Grandmother, we're only husband and wife on paper."
A shadow of sorrow crossed Old Madam Xia's face. "My grandson gets married at last, only to live like this. It breaks my heart just thinking about it."
Chen Haoyu hurried to cheer her up. "Don't be sad, Grandmother. Sooner or later, I'll marry a bride you love."
Old Madam Xia spoke from the heart. "Your grandmother already likes the bride you have."
Seeing his plot to set Grandmother loose had flopped, Chen Haoyu went straight for the silver. "Grandmother, Zhu Shuzhen won't give me spending money, and I don't dare ask Father and Mother. Could you spare me a little silver?"
Open-handed as ever with her favorite grandson, Old Madam Xia sent a maid for a wooden box and pulled out a five-hundred-tael banknote. "Spend it with sense. Not one copper on courtesans or gamblers, hear me?"
Overjoyed, Chen Haoyu took the note and rained kisses over her cheeks until she beamed from ear to ear. After a few more sweet words, he tucked the banknote into his robe, sprinted out of the manor, and led Scarface and his crew off for another round of carousing.
#CH 216
#TITLE: Cheering Up Old Madam Xia
Two days later, the Chen gardeners had dredged every bit of silt and grime from the pond in Moxiang Courtyard, packed the bed with rich fertilized mud, and planted lotus roots, leaving only time to sprout fresh leaves and blossoms.
Everything now matched her taste. She held assets of her own inside the Chen household, her father-in-law and mother-in-law treated her well, and nobody came stirring up trouble. Qianli Xun's spirits soared.
She had not laid eyes on Chen Haoyu since the night of the return visit, and she cared nothing about where he went gallivanting. Her mind was on one target: winning over Old Madam Xia.
Setting her huaben aside for the moment, she brainstormed ways to keep the old lady happy. Having grown up without a grandmother before her transmigration, she had zero experience coaxing elderly relatives. She thought back to Chen Haoyu's shameless, fawning act that always had Old Madam Xia beaming, yet she had never talked like that in her life and could never pull off such buttering up.
Kuqiao walked in to find her mistress resting her chin on her hand at the desk, brush untouched. "What are you thinking about, Miss?"
Qianli Xun lowered her hand. "Just in time. Help me think of a way to put Old Madam Xia in a great mood."
Kuqiao mulled it over. "My father used to say the older folks get, the more they crave lively company. Why not think of something lively, Miss?"
Qianli Xun brightened at once. "You've got a sharp head on your shoulders, girl. We have the perfect solution sitting right under our noses: invite that storyteller over to spin tales for Old Madam Xia."
Kuqiao hesitated. "Great idea, except I'm afraid he'll recognize me. I'm the one who delivers your manuscripts to him every time."
"Send Hongdou instead. When the storyteller arrives, you stay in Moxiang Courtyard while I take Hongdou along to attend me."
"Smart plan, Miss. I'll go find Hongdou right now." Pausing mid-step, Kuqiao remembered another matter. "Miss, one more thing to ask your leave on."
"What is it?"
"Matron Wei told me to teach Hongdou how to whisk tea, so you'll have another trained hand by your side."
"If Matron Wei suggested it, don't bother asking me. Just arrange it."
"Yes, Miss."
Out in the West Courtyard, Kuqiao found Hongdou drilling the servants in fist forms while Qinggua hovered at the edge, mimicking their stances with wild, clumsy flails that almost made Kuqiao burst out laughing.
Spotting Kuqiao, Hongdou told the group to keep practicing and walked over. "Did Miss send you with an errand, Sister Kuqiao?"
"Miss wants you to go to West Third Alley, find the storyteller, and invite him to Chen Manor to tell stories for Old Madam Xia."
"Got it. I'll go right away." Hongdou turned back to the servants. "Break it up for now and get back to your chores. We'll train again tomorrow."
The servants dispersed and Hongdou hurried off. Left with nobody to copy, Qinggua chased after Kuqiao.
"Kuqiao, could you put in a word with Young Madam and ask her to teach me martial arts too?"
"Why do you want to learn?" Kuqiao asked as she walked.
Qinggua put on a woeful face. "Young Master ordered me to learn. If I don't, he'll kick me out to the West Courtyard."
Kuqiao halted. "If the young master wants you trained, tell him to ask Miss himself. I'm not meddling in your mess."
She started walking again, and Qinggua trailed after her, looking pitiful. "How is that a mess? Come on, help me out! You've seen how Young Master kicks me all the time since you moved in. If Young Madam teaches me a few moves, at least I can dodge his boots."
Half amused and half sympathetic, Kuqiao relented. "Fine, I'll mention it to Miss. Whether she agrees is up to your luck."
Qinggua escorted her back to Suxin Thatched Hall and waited outside full of hope.
Inside, Kuqiao found her mistress sitting at the tea table whisking tea with stiff, awkward strokes. "If you want tea, Miss, I'll make it. No need to trouble yourself."
"Thinking about Old Madam Xia has my head all cluttered. I have no mood to write stories or read, so I tried whisking tea to pass the time. After watching you do it every day, I figured I could manage a passable cup, yet I still made a total wreck of it." For the first time, Qianli Xun felt let down by her own hands.
That gave Kuqiao the exact opening she needed. "If you want something to pass the time, Miss, I have something you'll love."
Qianli Xun set down the tea whisk. "Spill it."
"Guess what I just saw in the West Courtyard?"
"Stop teasing and tell me."
"I caught Qinggua trying to copy the martial-arts drills, flopping all over the place—hilarious to watch. On my way back he begged me to ask you to teach him. I meant to turn him down, yet he looked so pitiful I agreed to ask."
Amused, Qianli Xun stood up. "He wants to learn martial arts? That's rich. He hasn't a scrap of martial aptitude; he can wait for his next life. Still, I've got time to kill, so I'll use him for amusement."
Kuqiao did not mind the reason; her promise was kept. Once her mistress stepped outside, she cleared away the botched tea.
Sure enough, Qinggua stood right outside the door craning his neck. The moment he spotted his young madam, his face broke into a grin. "Did you agree to teach me martial arts, Young Madam?"
Qianli Xun looked him up and down. "Why do you want to learn?"
Knowing his master and young madam were oil and water, Qinggua dared not mention Chen Haoyu's threat. "I saw how unbeatable you are, Young Madam—unafraid of Old Madam Xia above, Master and Madam in the middle, or my Young Master below. I just want to pick up a few tricks so I can dodge when Young Master swings a foot at me."
An idea clicked in Qianli Xun's head. "You have zero aptitude, so you'll never learn my fist forms—even if you memorized the motions, it'd be hollow show. I do have one move outside my fist system that requires no talent. Learn it, and no matter how Chen Haoyu kicks at you, you'll slip right past—and even kick him back if you've got the nerve."
Qinggua's heart sank at first; he had dreamed of mastering real kung fu and strutting behind his master on the streets. Still, one self-defense move beat nothing. "I'll learn it, Young Madam! Please teach me."
"Kick me," Qianli Xun ordered.
Qinggua froze in alarm. "How could I dare kick Young Madam?"
"When I tell you to kick, kick! How else can I demonstrate?"
Screwing up his courage, Qinggua aimed a kick at her.
Qianli Xun glided sideways in one smooth slide, angling her torso so his foot grazed past empty air and threw him off balance. In the same breath she stepped in, brushed his leg aside with one palm, and locked his arm with the other.
"This move is called Phantom Sidestep," she said, letting him go. "Catch that?"
Qinggua shook his head. "Too fast. Missed it."
She had him kick at her seven or eight times in a row until he grasped the footwork, then summoned Asheng to drill him over in the West Courtyard.
No sooner had she finished than Hongdou returned. "Miss, the storyteller from West Third Alley is waiting outside the courtyard."
"Bring him along. We're going to see Old Madam Xia."
Delighted to accompany her mistress—a task that usually went to Kuqiao—Hongdou asked, "Isn't Sister Kuqiao coming?"
"I gave her another chore. You're with me today." Qianli Xun headed out, Hongdou close behind.
Seeing the mistress emerge, the storyteller bowed. "Young Madam, where would you like this humble servant to perform?"
"Just follow me."
Qianli Xun led the way, Hongdou and the storyteller trailing behind. Reaching Old Madam Xia's courtyard, Qianli Xun told the two to wait outside and walked in alone.
Maids were supporting Old Madam Xia on a stroll around the yard. Only a few steps in, she spotted her granddaughter-in-law and bristled. "No manners at all! Walking right in without being announced—and you call yourself the Poetess of Jiangnan!"
Qianli Xun had braced herself to try a softer tone like Chen Haoyu's, yet that sour snap wiped out her patience on the spot. "As the Poetess of Jiangnan, I've got a broader heart than most. If Grandmother can't stand the sight of me, I won't hold it against you. I brought someone today to liven up this quiet yard."
Ignoring the old lady's glare, she directed the maids. "You two, bring out a table. You, fetch a chair."
Noticing Old Madam Xia stayed silent despite her scowl, the maids knew she did not object and hopped to work.
Once the table and chair were set, Qianli Xun stepped over and took Old Madam Xia's arm. "Set aside your temper with me for today, Grandmother. Let me help you sit."
Watching her granddaughter-in-law bustle around and fill the yard with life warmed the old lady inside, though her tongue stayed sharp. "Fine, I'll sit and see what trick you have up your sleeve."
Once Old Madam Xia settled in, Qianli Xun called toward the gate, "Hongdou, bring the storyteller in."
At the word "storyteller," Old Madam Xia's stern mask cracked, and the corners of her mouth curled upward.
Catching that flicker from the corner of her eye, Qianli Xun grinned to herself: Got you wrapped up that fast! Life in Chen Manor is about to get a whole lot smoother.
Hongdou escorted the storyteller in. The sight of a table made him feel right at home. He strode over, drew his wooden gavel and folding fan from his cloth satchel, set out his purple clay teapot, and told a nearby maid, "Trouble you to brew a pot of tea."
Old Madam Xia's smile widened. "Brew our guest a pot of fine tea."
The maid took the teapot and hurried off. Old Madam Xia glanced at her granddaughter-in-law standing beside her. "Have a seat too."
Another maid ran to bring a chair. Sitting down, Qianli Xun said, "Grandmother, this storyteller tells tales written by Master Qianli Xun. You're bound to love them."
"You went to a lot of trouble," Old Madam Xia said, her voice noticeably warmer.
When the tea arrived, the storyteller took a test sip—rich flavor, just hot enough without scalding. Satisfied, he set the pot down. "Who in Lin'an doesn't know Chen Manor brims with wealth and fortune, and Old Madam Xia enjoys boundless blessings and high renown..."
Old Madam Xia cut him off with a laugh. "Save the flattery and get to the story. Tell it well and I'll reward you handsome."
"At your command, Old Madam!" With a crisp crack of his wooden gavel, he launched in:
"In the southern heavens stood a Glazed Pagoda, where a Jade-Faced Fox lay trapped for a thousand years. Yet that fox never sat idle—making the pagoda her home, feeding on pagoda air, dressing in pagoda dust, until she grew thoroughly pagoda-soaked..."
Old Madam Xia burst out laughing. "Hah! First time I've ever heard 'pagoda-soaked.' What a hoot!"
The storyteller pressed on:
"In the southern heavens lived a True God named Xuanzhi, who gazed at the Glazed Pagoda every day after his meditations. His eyes blazed with divine radiance, and day by day the pagoda soaked up his godly power until it could bear no more. With a thunderous BOOM across the southern sky, the Glazed Pagoda shattered into splinters! Freed at last and brushed by immortal essence, the Jade-Faced Fox transformed into a young woman—though after ages inside, she stood coated in soot with tangled hair.
"Just then True God Xuanzhi appeared. Startled, the girl blurted out, 'Who are you? Decent face, though you look sour enough to curdle milk.'
"With one flick of his immortal sleeve, Xuanzhi swept every speck of dust off her, revealing a dazzling beauty. 'I saved you,' Xuanzhi announced. 'From now on, you belong to me.'
"Delighted to turn pretty yet furious at his nerve, the girl snapped back, 'What makes you say you saved me? I didn't see a thing!' She spun to bolt, only for Xuanzhi to reel her back with a tug of immortal power..."
Old Madam Xia laughed until her sides hurt. Not since her sons had married and set up separate courtyards had anyone brought her such joy.
Before long, word of the storyteller spread across Chen Manor. Chen Haofei hurried over to listen, followed by Second Aunt, Third Aunt, and Ye Anya. The courtyard filled with voices and laughter, lifting Old Madam Xia's spirits higher than they had climbed in years.
#CH 217
#TITLE: Guessing an Elder's Heart
Once the storyteller wrapped up and departed, Old Madam Xia beamed with contentment and issued her verdict. "One session isn't nearly enough. Have him come every single day from now on."
"Rest assured, Grandmother," Qianli Xun replied. "I already arranged for him to come at this exact hour every day to tell you stories."
The old lady grinned from ear to ear.
Second Aunt Madam Bao chimed in with a vinegary edge. "Who would have guessed Haoyu's bride knows how to cheer Old Madam Xia up even better than Haoyu? How I envy First Sister-in-law for landing such a clever daughter-in-law—unlike this one of mine." She shot a glare at Ye Anya beside her. "Start learning from Shuzhen, or what good did Haodong get from marrying you?"
Ye Anya kept her mouth shut and bore her mother-in-law's scolding in silence. Old Madam Xia frowned at the remark yet held her tongue. Qianli Xun kept quiet and watched; after binging enough palace-and-manor dramas in her past life, she knew inner-courtyard politics demanded brains, not fists. Madam Cui and Chen Haofei treated it as background noise, long used to watching Ye Anya get dressed down.
Madam Bao pressed her point. "Too bad my Haodong stays buried from dawn till dusk in the Chen silk shop, tea house, salt yard, porcelain firm, docks, inns, and restaurants. Unlike Haoyu and his wife, who have oceans of free time just to amuse Old Madam Xia. Don't play favorites, Old Madam, or Haodong will feel hurt."
Catching the barb, Old Madam Xia let her smile drop. "I don't need you reminding me. I keep a scale right here in my heart. Who has character, who has ability, and who contributes most to the Chen family—I see it all clear as glass."
Not to be outdone while Second Sister-in-law touted her son, Madam Cui stepped in. "Of course my Haofei can't compare with his two older cousins—one a schemer in business, the other a master at having fun and pleasing Grandmother. He buries his whole heart in his books. Next year he sits for the Metropolitan Exam, and if he passes, it's off to Bianliang for the Palace Examination. Haofei, recite a passage from the Erya for your grandmother."
"Enough, don't bother," Old Madam Xia waved it off. "I wouldn't understand a word anyway. Haofei is a good boy. Study hard and earn an official title for the Chens—that's the greatest contribution you can make."
"Yes, Grandmother," Chen Haofei answered.
"The rest of you go on back," Old Madam Xia dismissed them. "I want a private word with Haoyu's wife."
Watching them file out, Qianli Xun thought over Second Aunt's and Third Aunt's jabs and understood why Old Madam Xia doted on a good-for-nothing grandson who at least knew how to make her laugh.
Once the yard emptied, Old Madam Xia said, "Shuzhen, help me inside."
Supporting her arm, Qianli Xun felt how unsteady the old woman's legs were. Her thoughts drifted to her own Old Ancestor at Zhu Manor, spry and sturdy at one hundred and twenty, and a swell of pity rose in her chest. "Grandmother, Chen Haoyu mentioned a doctor who treats leg ailments. Another day, let me track him down for you."
Old Madam Xia chuckled. "You believe Haoyu's tall tales? He only says that to cheer me up. The Chens have silver to spare—what physician haven't we hired? We tried them all years ago. My legs are beyond cure."
Qianli Xun helped her onto the couch, slipped off her own shoes, and sat cross-legged across from her. "So starting today, Grandmother isn't mad at me anymore?"
Old Madam Xia laughed. "When was I ever mad at you?"
Qianli Xun paused a beat before realization hit. "You were pretending to be mad on purpose? Had I known, I wouldn't have racked my brains trying to butter you up!"
"In this entire manor, I have found one person with sense at last," Old Madam Xia said. "You figured out I only pick fights and act angry to make you put some effort into pleasing me. Not a single one of my sons or daughters-in-law ever caught on."
Light dawned across Qianli Xun's mind. Every time Old Madam Xia snapped at Chen Haoyu's parents, she was only fishing for attention and affection—which backfired and drove them away instead. Qianli Xun had stumbled onto the answer by sheer accident.
"Grandmother, you ought to tell the elders and all of us juniors what you like outright."
Old Madam Xia sighed. "Where's the fun in spelling it out? Anyone who keeps me in their heart figures out what to do on their own—just like you did today. From now on, in Chen Manor, I have your back. Nobody dares push you around."
Qianli Xun grinned. "Aside from you, Grandmother, nobody has tried pushing me around since I married in. Not that I'd be scared anyway, with my fists."
"Oh, listen to you brag!" Old Madam Xia laughed, then softened. "Still, I adore a woman like you—fearless under heaven, just like me in my youth. Pity I grew old."
"Are you teasing me, Grandmother? The day I stormed Chen Manor to make a scene, you looked ready to chew me out. How could you like me?" Qianli Xun felt warmed yet skeptical, recalling the frosty tea ceremony too.
"You marched in determined not to marry Haoyu—why would I force it?" Old Madam Xia explained. "Putting on a sweet face while you tore the place up wouldn't have matched the show. Besides, I hated seeing my grandson risk getting beaten by you, so I played along hoping we'd sink the match."
Qianli Xun marveled at the old woman's layers—one face outside, another inside, impossible to read. No wonder her own children stayed baffled.
Recalling that pre-wedding storm brought another question back to her mind. "Grandmother, that day you mentioned my father forced Chen Haoyu to marry me. Why did you say that?"
Old Madam Xia stiffened inside. Her granddaughter-in-law did not know; Prefect Zhu must have kept it from her. She cursed her own loose tongue from that argument. Given the girl's temper and iron fists, spilling the truth now would mean misery for Haoyu. She covered her tracks fast. "Pure nonsense. You had me so riled up that day I talked gibberish. Pay it no mind."
Spotting nothing odd on the old lady's face, Qianli Xun dropped it. "Grandmother, what did you think of Master Qianli Xun's story?"
"Marvelous! Better than anything I've ever heard!" Old Madam Xia beamed, then tilted her head. "You called the author a male scholar, yet why does it sound to me like a woman wrote it?"
Delighted by the praise—which swept away the last bitter residue of her online harassment before transmigration—Qianli Xun admired the old lady's sharp instincts. "What makes you say that?"
"A story about a young woman's heart has to come from a woman," Old Madam Xia declared.
Qianli Xun had a ready counter. "Not so fast, Grandmother. Tang Immortal Poet Li Bai wrote 'Qingping Yue,' Sage of Poetry Du Fu wrote 'The Fair Lady,' and Buddha of Poetry Wang Wei wrote 'Ballad of a Girl from Luoyang'—every one about women, and every one written by famous men."
Delighted by her granddaughter-in-law's learning, Old Madam Xia marveled at what good karma her book-hating grandson had earned in a past life to land a true talent. "True to your name as the Poetess of Jiangnan—you know everything!"
Buoyed by the compliment, Qianli Xun pitched another treat. "Grandmother, I know a blind drummer who sings folk ballads. Another day I'll bring him here to sing the tale of Cai Bojie for you."
Old Madam Xia bobbed her head like a pellet drum. "Yes, yes, yes!"
The two talked and laughed until noon, when Qianli Xun excused herself for the old lady's lunch.
Only a few paces outside Old Madam Xia's courtyard with Hongdou, Chen Haofei stepped into her path. "Greetings, Second Sister-in-law!"
"Third Brother-in-law," Qianli Xun greeted him. "What can I do for you?"
"I have a favor to beg of you, Second Sister-in-law. You must say yes!"
"Tell me what it is first, and I'll decide." Hardly knowing him, she would not sign a blank check.
"I passed the provincial exam, yet my poetry is weak and I have no name in Lin'an. When invited to poetry salons, I only tag along to fill a seat, never bringing fresh verse of my own. Now that the famed Youqi Jushi is my sister-in-law, couldn't you spare me a poem or two so I can shine at gatherings? Please, Second Sister-in-law?"
Promoting Zhu Shuzhen's poetry suited Qianli Xun just fine. "I thought it was something tough. A poem or two is nothing. Ask whenever you need more."
"I'd love them right now!"
"Come along then."
Beaming, Chen Haofei followed her toward Moxiang Courtyard.
At the courtyard gate, they found Ye Anya waiting alone.
"First Sister-in-law, what are you doing standing out here without even a maid?" Qianli Xun asked.
"Waiting to chat with you, Younger Sister," Ye Anya said. "What brings Haofei over?"
"Greetings, First Sister-in-law," Chen Haofei grinned. "Second Sister-in-law promised me two poems, so I tagged along."
"Aha," Ye Anya laughed. "Having the renowned Youqi Jushi enter Chen Manor sure makes life handy for you—no more showing up empty-handed to poetry salons."
"Of course! We're family now."
Chatting and laughing, they entered Moxiang Courtyard. Kuqiao had already laid out lunch, yet Qianli Xun sat at her desk first and brushed out two seasonal lyrics for Chen Haofei: "Xijiang Yue: Mid-Spring" and "Dielianhua: Seeing Off Spring." Chen Haofei accepted them with effusive thanks and hurried off in high spirits.
Since lunch was ready, Qianli Xun invited Ye Anya to eat with her, and Ye Anya accepted at once. Four dishes, a soup, and rice filled the table—ordinary fare by now to Qianli Xun, whose curiosity was aimed instead at why Ye Anya had come seeking her out.
Kuqiao ladled soup and served rice before stepping back to wait on them.
"You're the only woman near my age in Chen Manor, First Sister-in-law," Qianli Xun said. "We ought to visit each other often."
Ye Anya did not stand on ceremony, taking a spoonful of soup before replying. "My thoughts exact. That's why I came over to talk today."
