Qianli Xun placed a serving of vegetables into her bowl. "I'm brand-new here and don't know the ropes yet. Teach me when you have time so I don't step on toes or upset the elders."
"Word is you never wanted to marry into the Chen family, didn't consummate the marriage on your wedding night, and leave Haoyu to roam free outside," Ye Anya observed. "Yet you still put all this heart into pleasing the elders. I find that baffling."
"True, I didn't want to marry Chen Haoyu, yet fate cornered me into it. Since I'm here, I treat myself as part of the Chen household and intend to build a peaceful life."
The phrase "cornered into it" reminded Ye Anya of Prince Yi's wedding raid. Knowing an imperial prince had wanted the Zhu daughter, she still could not fathom why the Zhus had handed her to a playboy like Haoyu instead.
"To outsiders, marrying into the Chen family looks like hitting the jackpot," Ye Anya sighed. "Only you and I know the bitter taste beneath the sweet. Haoyu stays gone all day, heaven knows where, and mine looks so respectable on the surface, yet..."
Her voice trailed off. Sensing the ache behind her words, Qianli Xun placed another morsel into her bowl. "Try this dish. It's pretty good."
Ye Anya ate a bite before continuing. "I envy you, Younger Sister—strong, decisive, holding Haoyu's assets, turning this courtyard into your own sanctuary. Whereas I..."
"I only manage because Father-in-law and Mother-in-law are generous, the elders cut me slack, and I have a sister-in-law like you willing to open her heart to me," Qianli Xun deflected.
Ye Anya let out a laugh. "What a honeyed tongue—no wonder you won Old Madam Xia over so fast! I heard how you talked circles around Old Madam Xia, my mother-in-law, and Third Aunt when they came looking for a fight, leaving all three speechless. That mouth of yours spins poetry and ironclad arguments alike!"
"You flatter me, First Sister-in-law."
They chatted and laughed through lunch. Big, bustling, warm—Chen Manor had everything Qianli Xun liked in a home, marred only by the wrong groom. If only her husband were someone she loved.
That thought pulled Shen Jianchen straight to mind. He and Mengrong must still be on the road to Bianliang. By the time they returned to Lin'an, everyone would address Mengrong as Princess Consort Yi.
In silence, Qianli Xun offered a blessing: may Prince Yi and his princess consort find happiness together.
#CH 218
#TITLE: Poor, Pitiful Ye Anya
After lunch in Moxiang Courtyard, Ye Anya lingered for more conversation before taking a reluctant leave.
Her draw to Shuzhen went far beyond their shared age; her sister-in-law's life fascinated and inspired her. Securing a mutual divorce was rare enough to make other gentlewomen blush, yet when the entire city tore her name apart last year, she had kept living with spirit—where most women would have thrown themselves into the Qiantang River ten times over. Betrothed to Haoyu, she had ditched ladylike decorum and stormed Chen Manor to blow up the match, failing yet showing fierce nerve. Then on her wedding day, Prince Yi had raided the bridal procession and Princess Jiahe had been wounded—proving a man could still love her that madly even on the brink of marrying another.
During this first long chat, Ye Anya had avoided the real topic burning inside her. Instead, she had studied Shuzhen's bearing, hoping some of that courage would rub off and push her toward the step she longed yet feared to take. She resolved to visit Moxiang Courtyard often.
Stepping back into her own courtyard, she froze at the sight of her mother-in-law Madam Bao waiting with a dark face.
Ye Anya curtsied. "Mother, what brings you here?"
"High noon, and you skip lunch in your own courtyard to come strolling back past mealtime? Where have you been gallivanting?"
The word "gallivanting" stung, yet Ye Anya forced a smile. "That word is a bit harsh, Mother. I only went to chat with Shuzhen. She insisted I stay for lunch, and I couldn't refuse."
Madam Bao scoffed. "Hmph! Look at Shuzhen—married in for a handful of days and already wrapped Old Madam Xia around her finger. And you? Over two years in this house, and how many times have you visited Old Madam Xia's rooms, much less helped Haodong win her favor? And that useless belly of yours—still not a whisper of a child! No wonder Haodong has no use for you and hates coming back to this courtyard."
Sick of the lecture, Ye Anya said, "If you have no other orders, Mother, I'll head inside."
Without waiting for dismissal, she walked straight into her room.
Madam Bao seethed, turning to her maid. "Look at her! Does she act like a meek daughter-in-law? And outsiders praise her as gentle and filial, painting me as some wicked mother-in-law!" With a sharp huff, she marched off.
Inside, Ye Anya collapsed onto her bed, choking down her misery.
Her maid Xiaocui hurried over. "Miss, I went to the usual spot this morning. Young Master Cao sent a note."
Life sparked back into Ye Anya's eyes. She sat up, took the folded slip, and read the Han-era vow inked inside:
"O Heaven above! / I long to share my heart with you, / Unbroken and unfading for all my days. / Only when mountains lose their peaks, / And the great river runs dry, / When thunder crashes in dead winter, / And snow falls in midsummer, / When sky and earth fuse into one— / Only then would I dare part from you." [TN: Translator's rendering]
Ye Anya sighed. "He pours such devotion into me, yet I am another man's wife. How can I ever repay his heart?"
"You and Young Master Cao loved each other first, Miss. You were forced into marrying Young Master Chen. The way he beats and curses you—even if you can stomach living like this, I can't bear watching!"
"I can't bear it either, yet the marriage is done. What can I do?"
"Didn't you want a mutual divorce from him, Miss?"
"I do, yet walking that road isn't easy."
"The new Zhu bride went through a mutual divorce. Why not ask her how she did it?"
"That's why I went to see her today, yet the words stuck in my throat. I'll find a chance to ask her next time."
Mid-sentence, Chen Haodong strode through the door. Xiaocui snatched the slip from her mistress's fingers, shoved it up her sleeve, and shrank aside.
"Getting ruder by the day, aren't you?" Chen Haodong snapped at the maid. "Don't even greet your master?"
"Greetings, Young Master," Xiaocui stammered.
Ye Anya stood up. "You're back early today, Husband."
"What, wish I'd stayed away? Hiding someone in here who doesn't belong? Don't think I forgot your little romance with the Cao boy before we married."
Fragile yet stubborn, Ye Anya held his gaze. "What happened with him is in the past, and you knew about it before we wed. Why dredge it up now? While you're lecturing me, let's talk about you—don't think I haven't heard about Chun Jinchan and the filth you get up to outside."
Knowing a blow was coming, Xiaocui tensed in terror for her mistress.
"Get out!" Chen Haodong roared at Xiaocui.
Xiaocui dropped to her knees. "Young Master, please don't hit Miss! The bruises from last time haven't even healed!"
"Servants!" Chen Haodong shouted toward the door. Two attendants rushed in. "Drag Xiaocui out and shut the door."
They hauled the weeping maid outside and pulled the door closed.
Chen Haodong stalked toward Ye Anya. "Getting mouthier every day. Guess I've been going too easy on you."
Ye Anya backed away. "Think beating me will break me? You're wrong. Every blow just makes me despise you more!"
He lunged and seized her collar. "Mother just told me you went sucking up to Haoyu's wife. I'm warning you: stay clear of her bad habits! Her name is mud across Lin'an, and you'd better keep yours spotless. Next year the clan picks the heir to the Chen fortune—don't you dare ruin my shot!"
Ye Anya refused to yield an inch. "You wear a shiny mask for outsiders, yet I know what rotten garbage you are underneath. Someone like you thinks he's fit to inherit the Chen estate—"
SMACK! His open palm cracked across her cheek. "Shut your mouth!"
Blow after blow rained down until Ye Anya could no longer lift her arms. He flung her onto the bed and ripped at her clothes. "Beating you first, then making you do your wifely duty—nothing beats the thrill!"
Swamped in humiliation and powerless to fight him off, Ye Anya endured in stony silence.
When he finished, Chen Haodong straightened his robes and sneered down at his bruised, tear-streaked wife tangled in torn silk. "Lying there cold as ice—no wonder you can't get pregnant. Go take lessons from the courtesans at Chunxiang Brothel on how to please a man."
Only after the door slammed shut behind him did Ye Anya let the bitter tears spill over.
Xiaocui rushed back in, weeping at the sight of her. "Miss, next time just humor him and don't talk back, or you're the one who ends up hurt."
"I can't humor a man I loathe. Bending to him breaks my own heart; I'd rather take bruises on my skin than choke on misery inside. I'm leaving him. Even if he writes a letter of repudiation and casts me out, I'm ending this marriage."
Seeing firmer resolve on her mistress's face than ever before, Xiaocui felt a fierce ache of relief. Ye Anya had not known a single happy day in Chen Manor; walking out—even alone, even scorned—beat rotting here.
Over the following days, the storyteller came to Chen Manor every afternoon, filling Old Madam Xia's courtyard with laughter instead of silence.
Qianli Xun noticed Ye Anya stopped showing up, yet as a newcomer she hesitated to pry or drop by uninvited, deciding to wait and see. She also noticed Yao Qingyan and Chen Jianglin never appeared either. One afternoon, while everyone hung on the storyteller's words, Qianli Xun slipped out unnoticed.
Not far beyond the gate, she spotted Yao Qingyan pacing beneath a tree with her maid Yingxue.
Qianli Xun walked up. "Mother-in-law, you're right outside the gate. Why aren't you going in?"
"I'm afraid seeing me will put Old Madam Xia in a bad mood," Yao Qingyan admitted.
Her father-in-law and mother-in-law were wonderful people who just had zero clue how to read the old lady, turning fondness into years of friction. Time to lend a hand.
"You're overthinking it, Mother-in-law. Grandmother loves a lively crowd. If you keep her courtyard lively every day, she'll be thrilled—why would she get mad at you?"
Yao Qingyan looked doubtful. "Does that trick really work?"
"Of course it does. That's how I got Grandmother grinning nonstop and changed her whole tune toward me."
"How did you figure out what she wanted in just days, when I've been her daughter-in-law for decades and never noticed?"
"I'm not that clever—Matron Wei tipped me off."
"No wonder every gentlewoman in Lin'an envies you for having Matron Wei at your side."
Qianli Xun grinned. "What Lin'an envies most is how Father-in-law dotes on you, Mother-in-law."
Yao Qingyan laughed, then clouded over. "Outsiders envy our bond, yet Old Madam Xia can't stand it."
"Did you ever wonder if Grandmother snaps at you two for a different reason—not because you get along?"
"A different reason? I can't imagine what."
"Only after I cheered Grandmother up did I learn the truth. Every time she acted furious with me, she wasn't really mad—she just used anger to grab my attention so I'd put effort into pleasing her and keep her from feeling lonely."
Understanding struck Yao Qingyan like lightning. "That's why! No matter what Jianglin and I did, we never pleased her and only got scolded—and the more she scolded, the more we stayed away! Why didn't she just say so instead of leaving us in the dark all these years?"
"She told me spelling it out spoils the fun. She wants to feel people taking the trouble to think of her. Elders are just like children—they want attention and fuss. Visit her every day with Father-in-law, keep her yard bustling, and I promise she'll beam."
"Now I see why she adores Haoyu—not just because he looks like his late grandfather, yet because he drops by her room and sweet-talks her." Yao Qingyan clasped Shuzhen's hands. "The Chen family struck gold marrying you, Shuzhen. You barely crossed the threshold and unlocked Old Madam Xia's heart. Thank you."
The Chens struck gold, sure, while I drew the short straw! Qianli Xun thought, saying aloud, "Don't just stand out here talking. Come inside with me. Grandmother is in a great mood right now—she won't get mad."
Yao Qingyan nodded and followed her into the courtyard, where the storyteller was in full swing:
"Xuanzhi gave the Jade-Faced Fox a name: Luoying. From then on she served as a maid in his palace, tending his meals and tea. Everyone in heaven praised True God Xuanzhi's unmatched power—even the Heavenly Emperor gave him face—yet Luoying couldn't stand his icy, stone-faced gloom.
"Every day after chores, Luoying sat by the lotus pond muttering to a lotus blossom. One day she sighed, 'Oh lotus, serving that True God is dull as dirt. I want to sneak out of his palace and see the world.'
"Out of thin air came a voice: 'I'll take you out.'
"Startled, Luoying spun around. Nobody was there. She scrambled off her rock to bolt, turned, and bumped straight into a handsome young man.
"She stepped back. 'Who are you?'
"'I'm the lotus who listens to you every day,' he said. 'Call me Pretty-Boy Flower.'
"Luoying burst out laughing. 'What a cheesy name!'"
Absorbed in the tale, Old Madam Xia did not notice her eldest daughter-in-law walk up. Qianli Xun offered her seat, yet Yao Qingyan declined with a glance, waving away the extra chair a maid brought. Stepping behind Old Madam Xia instead, she laid her hands on the old lady's shoulders and began kneading them in rhythm with the tale.
Feeling the touch, Old Madam Xia glanced back, saw her eldest daughter-in-law, said nothing, and kept smiling—only now her smile held deeper contentment.
A boulder lifted from Yao Qingyan's chest. At last she knew how to warm the old woman's heart, and she could not wait to tell Jianglin tonight.
Watching from the side, Madam Bao sneered inside: Look at First Sister-in-law, sucking up to Old Madam Xia!
Madam Cui felt a twinge of sourness too, yet shrugged it off and went back to the story.
#CH 219
#TITLE: First Sister-in-Law's Secret
After the storyteller left, the younger Chens drifted back to their own courtyards. Haofei had stayed away today, so Madam Cui excused herself to check on her son. Worried that Yao Qingyan might edge her out if left alone with Old Madam Xia, Madam Bao lingered behind. Seeing Grandmother well attended and guessing Yao Qingyan wanted a heart-to-heart, Qianli Xun made her farewells and left.
The two daughters-in-law helped Old Madam Xia indoors. Joy glowed in the old woman's chest: her courtyard had come alive, her eldest daughter-in-law now understood her heart, and her eldest son would soon follow.
Once Old Madam Xia was seated, Yao Qingyan dropped to her knees. "Mother, I was wrong all these years to misread your heart. Beat me or scold me as you see fit."
Before Old Madam Xia could speak, Madam Bao grumbled, "When First Sister-in-law kneels like that, how can I stay seated?"
Ignoring Madam Bao, Old Madam Xia told Yao Qingyan, "Get up. Just come sit in my courtyard when you're free and keep an old woman company. Stop leaving me alone in here until I have to pick fights just to get your attention."
"Yes, Mother. I'll come keep you company every single day."
Yingxue helped Yao Qingyan up into a chair.
Madam Bao chimed in with mock reproach, "You could have just said you wanted company, Mother. I'll tell Haodong and his father to visit every day too, and I'll come along."
"Stop standing and sit," Old Madam Xia said. "So long as you keep me in your hearts, I'm happy."
Madam Bao sat down, and with both daughters-in-law chatting beside her—a rare treat—Old Madam Xia grinned nonstop.
With Old Madam Xia won over, Qianli Xun felt a huge load lift. Taking stock, she had property and her own courtyard, she had pacified the biggest boss in Chen Manor, her parents-in-law treated her well, and she had a friendly sister-in-law in Ye Anya. Everything was smoothing out—so why did a hollow ache still sit at the bottom of her chest?
In a wistful mood, she jotted down an address and handed the slip to Hongdou. "This is Xiaguo's family home. Go ask the old blind drummer when he's free to visit Lin'an and come to Chen Manor for me. Tell him Old Madam Xia wants to hear him sing a ballad."
Once Hongdou hurried out, quiet settled over the hall. Not knowing where Kuqiao had gone, Qianli Xun sat still and examined her own heart—and hit the reason at once. She lacked someone to love beside her.
Shen Jianchen came back to mind. Counting the days, he must be nearing Bianliang by now. Memories of everything they had been through stirred a dull ache; she cursed landing in an era where nobody held the reins of their own heart.
Kuqiao walked in to find her mistress propping her chin on her hand at the desk, wearing a glum expression. "What's on your mind, Miss?"
Skipping the question, Qianli Xun asked, "Where have you been?"
"Since the storyteller was here, I didn't dare wander out, so I stayed in the West Courtyard watching Qinggua practice."
Qianli Xun dropped her hand. "That's hardly martial arts—just one self-defense move I taught him out of pity because Chen Haoyu keeps kicking him. How's he doing?"
"With Asheng sparring against him, Qinggua looks sharp now—way smoother and faster than when you first showed him."
Having no interest in Qinggua's footwork, Qianli Xun stood. "I want to go see the Divine Willow."
Sensing her mistress's low mood, Kuqiao asked no questions and trailed along as they left Chen Manor by carriage.
Kuqiao had never quite grasped why her mistress and Prince Yi kept visiting that willow. Bai Feng had told her the tree stood close to Youlin Retreat, and Prince Yi would go sit beneath it talking to himself as though the willow could answer.
Mid-thought, Kuqiao glanced out the carriage window and spotted Huayu and Nan Shuang walking together toward Chen Manor.
"Miss, I just saw Huayu and Nan Shuang! Think they're heading to Chen Manor to ask for your poems?"
Qianli Xun ordered the driver to halt. "Call them over."
Kuqiao poked her head out the window. "Nan Shuang! Huayu! Over here!"
Both servants hurried up to the carriage.
"How did you two bump into each other?" Kuqiao asked.
"My master told me to visit Chen Manor every few days starting today to request Youqi Jushi's poems," Nan Shuang explained. "Ran into Huayu on the road, and it turns out he's on the exact same errand."
"Come to think of it, you haven't come asking since Young Master Qiao returned from Bianliang," Kuqiao remarked. "Miss is heading out right now, so come by tomorrow instead. Don't worry—plenty of poems are already written and waiting."
Huayu jumped in at once. "They were all written for my master, right? Don't cut our share short just because Nan Shuang showed up!"
"My mistress writes fast and brilliant—seven or eight pieces are already sitting on her desk," Kuqiao laughed. "Your share won't shrink, and there's plenty left over for Nan Shuang too."
Beaming, the two servants watched the Chen carriage roll on.
Qianli Xun had stayed silent while listening to every word. Now she asked, "Did Nan Shuang used to come asking for my poems before?"
"Hardly asking—he used to fish your discarded drafts out of the trash and hope to get lucky."
"Why did he stop after Wenyuan returned from Bianliang?"
Kuqiao studied her mistress for a moment before answering, "Think about it, Miss. You already know."
That nudge cleared the fog. When Wenyuan returned from Bianliang, she had fallen for him at first sight and they had loved each other—why use poems to hold on when he held her heart? Then their romance hit rocks, leaving him no mood for verses; then came the breakup beneath the Divine Willow. Now he was sending Nan Shuang for poems again, proving he had stepped past the heartbreak. Their final meeting at Zuiyun Tower had closed that chapter clean.
A smile curved Qianli Xun's lips. Funny how love worked—blissful stepping in, and somehow light and peaceful stepping out too.
Then her smile faded. Stepping onto this quiet path with Shen Jianchen had never brought her joy—more accurately, she dared not feel joy, because a single spark of happiness made her feel rotten to the bone. When would this chapter end, letting both of them draw a clean full stop and walk away smiling?
Time and again she tried to draw that period inside her heart, yet every time her hand stopped halfway. Why torture herself? Could she not even keep someone she loved tucked inside her own heart? Caught in that tug-of-war, she left Shen Jianchen right where he was.
The carriage exited the city and reached the foot of the hills. Stepping down, Qianli Xun walked toward the Divine Willow through a spring breeze drifting with willow catkins, white tufts soft as feathers scattering across the dirt path.
Drawing closer, she saw a new palette on the tree: if the red silk ribbons dressed the willow in bridal crimson, the white catkins draped a modern bridal veil over its shoulders. She chuckled at her mash-up of ancient and modern imagery; spanning a thousand years across two eras, the Divine Willow would not mind.
Across the pond, young lotus pads floated beneath a dusting of pale catkins, which coated the open water too. A scene this poetic could not go unsung—she could not let Zhu Shuzhen's gift go to waste. Lines rose off her tongue:
"Swirling through clear skies like drifting snow, / Floating free, too proud to touch the dust below. / Soft beside the blossoms, clinging to a honeybee's wing, / Wild along the country lanes, chasing a galloping hoof. / Skimming the pond to turn to duckweed far down the waves, / Teasing the breeze unseen over low courtyard walls. / Massing in white clouds to grieve the passing spring, / Hoping to blur the road home for the Lord of the East." —"Willow Catkins" [TN: Translator's rendering]
The moment she finished, Kuqiao clapped her hands. "Marvelous, Miss! Especially 'Soft beside the blossoms, clinging to a honeybee's wing'—so true to life! I just watched a bee gathering nectar on that wildflower get snagged by a catkin on the petals. It buzzed and beat its wings for ages before shaking free and flying off!"
Qianli Xun smiled. Kuqiao's praise showed how sharp Zhu Shuzhen's eye for real life had been—and sparked an epiphany. Classical poetry or modern web fiction, great writing had to stay anchored in lived reality. Back in her old life, the online backlash had started when her novels drifted too far from real life. Adapting huaben in this era, she would weave the texture of real Song life into every line—even tales of gods and foxes would feel like the listeners' own lives.
Still, she had not come here to ponder writing. Walking up to the boulder beneath the willow, she bent and blew away its blanket of catkins. Worried the stone might be chilly, Kuqiao spread a handkerchief over it and stepped back to stand watch.
Qianli Xun sat and leaned against the massive trunk. She had never seen Shen Jianchen sit here, yet she could picture him in this exact spot, leaning back, listening to his own heart. She closed her eyes and imagined him here, then thought of Bai Feng drilling that piglet to climb the tree—both absurd and tender, trying to force the impossible into happening.
After a pause, she opened her eyes. "Kuqiao, did you know Bai Feng was training a piglet to climb this willow?"
"I heard about it from Bai Feng," Kuqiao said. "Prince Yi ordered him to buy a piglet and teach it to climb trees. No idea what got into Prince Yi—teaching a pig to climb sounds crazy."
"It is absurd. He just wants to make the impossible possible, refusing to accept that what's impossible stays impossible, pouring stubborn effort into a hopeless dream." She closed her eyes again, heavy-hearted.
Kuqiao caught the undertone at once, knowing her mistress's tangle with Prince Yi better than anyone.
Sitting beneath the willow, Qianli Xun dared not pray for any romance—any wish of hers would wound Mengrong. She would lock that love at the bottom of her heart and settle down as a steady Chen daughter-in-law.
When her legs grew stiff, she rose to leave with Kuqiao. Only a few paces away, a man and a woman emerged from the back trail. She recognized the man first—Cao Ban—and started to call out a greeting before spotting the woman beside him: First Sister-in-law Ye Anya, clutching a red silk ribbon with a radiant face.
Startled, Qianli Xun swallowed her greeting and ducked behind a tree trunk with Kuqiao, peering back toward the willow.
Hand in hand, Cao Ban and Ye Anya stepped beneath the branches, tied their red ribbon onto a bough together, and folded into an embrace—looking utterly matched and at peace.
"Miss," Kuqiao whispered, "if Eldest Young Master Chen finds out, First Young Madam is finished."
"There has to be a story behind this," Qianli Xun warned in a low voice. "Swear you'll bury what we saw today in your stomach and never breathe a word to a soul."
"I swear, Miss. My lips are sealed."
Before the pair noticed them, Qianli Xun and Kuqiao slipped away.
Her own romantic tangle faded from her head, replaced by a wave of sorrow for Ye Anya. She was far from the only one denied the person she loved in this era; women like Zhu Shuzhen and Ye Anya filled this world. Homesickness for her old century hit harder than ever. Born free, you took freedom for granted; stripped of it, you grasped how hard humanity had fought across a thousand years to win it.
Going back was impossible, so she would treasure what she actually held right here.
First, family: loving parents, a devoted brother and sister-in-law, a one-hundred-and-twenty-year-old Old Ancestor turning a year older this spring, and now inside Chen Manor, Old Madam Xia and kind, reasonable parents-in-law.
Second, friendship: the three scholars from the poetry salons, Wenyuan as a confidant, Xiangrong—and Mengrong. Thinking of Mengrong brought back the slap on her wedding day and those words of hatred. Even so, Qianli Xun bore Mengrong no grudge. No matter how Mengrong treated her from here on, she remained Qianli Xun's one true confidante in this world.
#CH 220
#TITLE: Three Elders Plot the Discipline
When Chen Jianglin returned from the silk shop, Yao Qingyan told him everything that had happened that afternoon. Realization hit him like a clap of thunder: he had misread his mother for years, talking about filial piety without grasping what she needed.
Taking Yao Qingyan by the hand, he went straight to Old Madam Xia's courtyard. Having left not long ago, Yao Qingyan came along with a light step now that the old woman's frost had melted.
Expecting her eldest son, Old Madam Xia sat on her couch paging through a collection of her granddaughter-in-law's poems, frowning in puzzlement. "Shuzhen's poems are all gloom and heartbreak—nothing like her fiery temper."
A maid beside her spoke up. "Old Madam knows everything Young Madam went through before marrying into our house. After all that, how could she feel cheerful?"
"True enough," Old Madam Xia nodded. "Nobody could stay sunny after that. Now that she's a Chen, things will brighten up."
Right then Chen Jianglin and Yao Qingyan walked in. Setting the book aside, Old Madam Xia asked, "Back from work? Long day?"
Overjoyed—this was the first warm greeting his mother had given him since Wenxin was born—Chen Jianglin stepped forward to bow. "Working for our own family is never a burden, Mother."
As Yao Qingyan started to curtsy, Old Madam Xia stopped her. "My daughter-in-law already bowed to me today. Come sit across from me, Qingyan, and let him do the bowing."
Yao Qingyan straightened without hesitation and settled opposite her. Chen Jianglin finished his bow and took a side chair, waiting for his mother to speak.
"You two landed a gem of a daughter-in-law, and I got a gem of a granddaughter-in-law," Old Madam Xia said. "If she hadn't taken the trouble to read my heart, you two might never have figured out what I wanted."
"Forgive your unfilial son, Mother," Chen Jianglin said. "I misunderstood you all these years. Thank heavens for Shuzhen—she solved it the instant she arrived. Seeing how simple it was makes me all the more ashamed as head of the household."
"No need to beat yourself up. Drop by often to keep me company and fill this courtyard with life. That alone will add years to my span."
"Whenever business allows, Qingyan and I will visit every single day to keep your courtyard lively. With you in high spirits, you'll live to a hundred."
Laughter rippled through the room. Then Old Madam Xia let out a sigh. "We're all sorted out, yet my grandson is still roaming wild outside, never setting foot at home, marriage still unconsummated. This can't go on."
Emboldened by their thaw, Yao Qingyan spoke up. "If neither you nor I step in to stop him, Mother, the moment Haoyu walks back in, let Jianglin give him a proper thrashing and lock him up so he can't run wild."
Far from taking offense, Old Madam Xia blamed herself. "I spoiled him rotten because he's the spitting image of his late grandfather, and back then he was the only one who knew how to cheer me up. Whenever Jianglin tried to discipline him, I'd flare up and block it. Looking back, I only ruined the boy."
Yao Qingyan echoed her regret. "Not all on you, Mother. I worried Jianglin would beat him too hard and shielded him too."
Chen Jianglin cracked a grin. "So you're both giving me a green light to bring down the hammer on that brat?"
"I proposed it, didn't I?" Yao Qingyan said. "Discipline him however you like—I won't step in."
A sly smile curved Old Madam Xia's mouth. "I don't think it's our turn to discipline Haoyu."
Yao Qingyan caught on at once. "You mean Shuzhen?"
Old Madam Xia nodded. "She's the ideal candidate."
"Earlier, Qingyan and I handed him over to Shuzhen only because she wasn't scared of you stepping in," Chen Jianglin noted. "Now that we're all on the same page and you agree to strict discipline, why burden Shuzhen?"
"There are three big advantages to letting Shuzhen handle it," Old Madam Xia countered. "First, we already gave her the job and shouldn't take it back. Second, the three of us get peace and quiet. Third—and most important—when she disciplines Haoyu, the two will clash up close day after day. Bang two stones together long enough, and sparks are bound to fly!"
Chen Jianglin slapped his knee at the third point. "Brilliant as ever, Mother. Done."
Yao Qingyan frowned. "What about that prenuptial contract they signed about staying out of each other's business? We asked Shuzhen to rein him in, yet she brushed it off. Haoyu has been gone for days and she hasn't batted an eye, spending all her energy cheering you up instead."
Old Madam Xia winced in guilt. "My fault. On their return-visit day, he came whining about being broke, sweet-talked me, and I caved and handed him a five-hundred-tael banknote. That's why he vanished again."
Chen Jianglin smiled and broke it down for them. "Don't blame yourself, Mother. That actually proves Shuzhen already has him on a leash. Steward Fang told me Haoyu tried to draw silver from the ledger that day, and when Fang demanded Shuzhen's signed order, Haoyu didn't even dare ask her—he ran straight to you instead."
"Handing Haoyu's assets to Shuzhen really was the smartest move," Yao Qingyan said.
"She's already got him by the purse strings," Old Madam Xia chuckled. "Reining in the rest of him won't be hard."
"Just promise not to slip him any more silver, Mother," Yao Qingyan warned.
"Never again, never again."
Just then Chen Jiangshu and Chen Jiangmu walked in together. After hearing the news from their wives, neither wanted their eldest brother hogging all the filial credit; bumping into each other at the gate, they came in side by side, bowed to their mother, greeted their elder brother and sister-in-law, and took seats.
"If you ever need anything, Mother, don't keep it bottled up making us guess," Chen Jiangshu said first. "Just say the word and which of your three sons wouldn't jump?"
"Right, Mother," Chen Jiangmu chimed in. "Eldest Brother, Second Brother, and I stay buried in Chen business all day and miss details. We're blunt men—how can we guess what's on your mind?"
Any other day, those complaints would have earned a scolding, yet in her sunny mood Old Madam Xia just laughed. "When you three were babies who couldn't talk, I spent over a year guessing what each of you wanted. Now I ask you to guess my mind once, and you grumble?"
"We're happy to guess, Mother!" all three sons chorused.
Old Madam Xia turned to her second son first. "You raised Haodong into a sharp businessman, which makes me proud, yet teach him to treat his wife better. When you three married, I lectured every one of you to cherish your wives, and you all listened. Why didn't you pass that lesson to your own son? I heard Haodong hits Anya all the time."
"Rest assured, Mother," Chen Jiangshu promised. "I'll give Haodong a stern talking-to tonight and make him treat Anya right."
Next she turned to her third son. "Haofei is a good lad, pouring his heart into study. If he wins an official rank, our ancestors will beam from their graves. Still, don't let him bury himself in books alone—he needs to mix with people. Officials have to deal with people, and tact and conversation can't be learned from ink and paper."
"Sound advice, Mother," Chen Jiangmu replied. "I'll guide him. He's made real strides lately—Haoyu's wife gifted him a few poems, and he's been floating on air, running off to poetry salons every few days and mingling with scholars and exam candidates."
Old Madam Xia nodded in satisfaction, more convinced than ever that bringing Shuzhen into the family was pure luck.
They chatted until Old Madam Xia grew tired, then parted outside her gate to return to their courtyards.
Walking home, Yao Qingyan asked, "Should we send someone to bring Haoyu back?"
"He runs off all the time," Chen Jianglin replied. "We never chased him before, and we won't start now. Once his silver runs dry, he'll crawl back on his own. All we have to do is back Shuzhen when she whips him into shape."
Seven or eight days drifted by. In Moxiang Courtyard, fresh lotus pads broke the pond's surface and spread green across the water, adding bright life to the yard.
All week, Qianli Xun split her hours between keeping Old Madam Xia company and writing her huaben, forgetting Chen Haoyu existed—as if she had moved into Chen Manor just to be a doting daughter and granddaughter. Only when her mother-in-law or grandmother asked if Haoyu had come home did she recall she was married to the man she despised. When they urged her to haul him back and discipline him, she nodded aloud while refusing inside. The Chens were lovely people, just expecting way too much from her; she had zero interest in fixing a specimen like Chen Haoyu. Sensing her lukewarm reaction, the elders stopped bringing it up, though the flicker of disappointment on their faces gave Qianli Xun a twinge of guilt.
By then, Master Jiang's bruises had healed enough for action. After clearing some gang business, he figured Chen Haoyu would be lounging with Chun Jinmo at Chunxiang Brothel and marched right in with five men. He kept his crew small on purpose: last time a big crowd had drawn Commandant Lin and gained him nothing, and he had no desire to poke the authorities again.
Small crew or not, Master Jiang's swagger commanded every eye in the brothel. The madam rushed up. "Master Jiang! Come right in and take a seat!"
He dropped into a chair, leering up at Chun Jinmo dancing on stage. "Once she finishes that number, send her down to keep me company."
The madam winced. "Afraid I can't, Master Jiang. Young Master Chen booked her exclusive."
Master Jiang pushed up and stalked straight over to Chen Haoyu's table.
Chen Haoyu had spotted him the second he walked in. Counting only five thugs while three hired fighters stood behind his own chair, he stayed sprawled back, enjoying Chun Jinmo's dance without a care.
Master Jiang pulled up a chair at his table. "What are you still doing chasing Chun Jinmo, Young Master Chen?"
With the gambling slip burnt to ash, Chen Haoyu had zero fear left. "Heh! All that big rigged wager, and your plan flopped, didn't it? Sure, I married a tigress, yet I know how to tame one! She purrs like a kitten for me now—doesn't touch my freedom, meows sweet as honey, lets me go wherever I please. Jealous?"
Master Jiang bristled. "Hand Chun Jinmo over right now, Chen Haoyu, or I'll knock every tooth out of your skull!"
At a flick of his eyes, his five thugs closed in. Paid to shield their patron, Chen Haoyu's three bodyguards stepped straight into their path.
Patrons scattered for cover; Chun Jinmo froze mid-dance on stage, gazing down in alarm. Upstairs, Scarface and his pals, who had been drinking with courtesans, leaned over the railing to gawk.
"Another brawl starting," one lackey muttered.
"Next chance we get, let's tell Young Master Chen to move on from Chun Jinmo," another said. "Plenty of prettier girls in here."
"What do you know?" Scarface scoffed. "Young Master Chen is loyal in love—doesn't swap girls on a whim."
"That's what you call loyal in love? First I've heard of it."
"Shut up and watch the show."
Downstairs, fists flew. Chen Haoyu and Master Jiang stayed seated across from each other, trading sneers.
"Level with me," Chen Haoyu probed. "What did Prefect Zhu promise you to frame me into marrying his unwanted daughter?"
Master Jiang had never expected that guess—and jumped at the chance to bluff and scare the boy out of the brothel for good. "Sharp guess, Young Master Chen! Think I'm just underworld trash? I've got backers in the yamen, and Prefect Zhu is my patron! Who else would I help? He ordered me to whip you into shape and keep you out of Chunxiang Brothel—stay home with his daughter, or you're in for a world of hurt!"
Chen Haoyu shot to his feet in fury. "Prefect Zhu thinks he's high and mighty, meddling in my private fun? I'll come here every single day just to drive him crazy!"
Before he could curse more, he saw his three bodyguards gaining the upper hand, and his rage melted into a cackle. "Look at your worthless thugs, getting wiped across the floor by my three guards! Hahaha!"
Seeing his five men pushed back step by step, Master Jiang stood to salvage face before the crowd. "Stop!"
Both sides broke off. Master Jiang jabbed a finger at Chen Haoyu. "You get a pass today! Next time you won't be so lucky!" Then he shouted up at the stage, "Chun Jinmo! Sooner or later, you're mine!"
Turning to the three bodyguards, he flashed a thumbs-up. "Fine fighting, boys. The Qiantang Gang's doors stay open for you anytime. See you around!"
#CH 221
#TITLE: Haodong Plays His Trump Card
Burned in public, Master Jiang needed someone to pay the tab, and his mind went straight to Chen Haodong.
All that elaborate scheming for the eldest Chen nephew had bombed: Chen Haoyu was not caged by his fierce wife, and Master Jiang felt played for a fool. The silver Chen Haodong paid did nothing to salve his bruised pride.
That afternoon, Chen Haodong was busy at the silk shop, where booming orders from the southwest kept him tied down day after day.
Mid-ledger, a gang burst through the door, sending the manager and clerks scrambling in terror. Recognizing Master Jiang's stormy face, Chen Haodong hurried forward. "Master Jiang! What brings you here?"
"If you don't want the whole shop knowing what you've been up to," Master Jiang growled, "find us a private room."
Guessing the reason, Chen Haodong ushered him straight into the rear warehouse. Part of Master Jiang's crew guarded the door while the rest filed inside.
Bolts of silk towered to the rafters, the air heavy with the tart scent of raw fabric. The second the door clicked shut, Master Jiang waved his hand and his men jumped Chen Haodong. Having no martial training, Chen Haodong could only curl up and take the punches.
When it was enough, Master Jiang called, "Hold it!" His thugs stepped back.
Wincing in pain, Chen Haodong gasped, "Barging in and beating me without a word—where's the justice in that?"
"Beating you is getting off easy!" Master Jiang barked. "You conned me into setting a trap to marry Chen Haoyu to that tigress, promising she'd lock him down so Chun Jinmo was mine! Instead she lets him run wild at Chunxiang Brothel every day—and I just ate dirt trying to take him on!"
"Even so, you got every tael I promised. You didn't lose out."
"Your petty silver doesn't come close to paying for my lost face and bruised temper!"
"Nobody wants Haoyu caged by that fierce wife more than I do," Chen Haodong hurried to explain. "I never saw that prenuptial non-interference pact coming! Still, I've got a trump card left. Give me a few days, Master Jiang, and Chun Jinmo is all yours."
Master Jiang crouched beside him. "Not jerking me around again?"
Chen Haodong crooked a finger. "Lean in and listen."
As Chen Haodong whispered in his ear, a wide grin split Master Jiang's face. "Haoyu was behind that? Hah! All right, I'll trust you one more time."
Tossing a bottle of salve into Chen Haodong's lap, Master Jiang led his crew out.
Chen Haodong pocketed the salve, hauled himself up, warned the shop manager and clerks not to breathe a word to the Chen elders, and rode home by carriage.
The bruises were superficial; two days of rest cleared most of them. All the while, Chen Haodong plotted how to leak Haoyu's rumor-mongering straight to Zhu Shuzhen's ears.
A servant stepped in. "Eldest Young Master, Second Master is back and wants to see you."
An idea clicked. Chen Haodong beckoned him closer. "Come here. I've got an errand for you."
"At your command, Eldest Young Master."
Chen Haodong pressed a tael of silver into his palm. "Take this—more waiting once it's done." After murmuring instructions in his ear, he added, "Pass it to someone in Moxiang Courtyard today."
"Yes, Eldest Young Master."
Once the servant left, Chen Haodong rose to go see his father—only to run into Ye Anya walking in with Xiaocui.
Her cool, blank face devoid of any wifely warmth grated on his nerves at once. "Where were you?"
"Out on the street buying rouge and powder."
"Hmph! Since when do you wear rouge for me? Sneaking out to meet your lover and dolling up for him?"
Hit dead-on, Ye Anya felt a jolt yet kept her face stone-calm. "If you have nothing else, I'm going inside."
From their wedding day on, that icy front had driven Chen Haodong wild. He had assumed claiming her in bed would soften her into smiling and clinging to him, yet consummation and countless rough nights had changed nothing; not a spark of warmth ever reached her eyes.
Her cold detachment tripped his need to dominate all over again. Stepping into her path, he grabbed her wrist and barked at Xiaocui, "Out!"
"Young Master, please don't!" Xiaocui cried.
"Get out!" he roared.
Too weary to struggle, Ye Anya spoke in a flat voice. "Go outside, Xiaocui, and close the door."
Xiaocui obeyed, shutting the door behind her.
Yet Ye Anya's lifeless compliance killed his appetite on the spot. He flung her hand away. "Cold as a slab of rock in bed. I won't touch you again."
Ye Anya breathed out in relief—only for Chen Haodong to whirl back from the door, haul her against his chest, and crush his mouth down on hers. Gasping for air, unable to shove him off, she endured his bruising kiss until he pulled back, holding her tight.
"Chen men treat their wives well—Father even lectured me to be kinder to you," he muttered. "Yet every time I look at you, all I want is to break you and own you. Can't you stop acting like a block of ice? Maybe I'd be nicer to you."
Ye Anya stayed mute.
He dropped his arms. "Father wants me. I've got to go."
The second the door clicked shut, revulsion twisted Ye Anya's face; she grabbed a silk handkerchief and scrubbed her mouth clean.
Outside Moxiang Courtyard, the bribed servant lurked until Asheng stepped out. "Asheng!"
Asheng halted. "What do you want?"
The servant drew him aside. "Got something huge to tell you—about your Young Madam and Second Young Master."
"They're doing fine," Asheng said with caution. "What's there to tell?"
"Remember last year when the whole city tore your mistress's name to shreds?"
"Pure slander! Miss is nothing like what they said."
"Too bad she's still kept in the dark, clueless about who started those rumors."
"You heard something?"
"I've worked in Chen Manor for years—of course I know who spread them."
"Spill it so I can help Miss teach that blind fool a lesson!"
Checking both ways, the servant lowered his voice. "It was your own young master—Second Young Master Chen! Didn't see that coming, did you? Your mistress married the exact man who ruined her reputation."
Asheng stared in disbelief. "Where did you hear that?"
"Overheard Second Master and Eldest Young Master talking. Sat heavy on my chest, so I figured I'd pass it to someone in Moxiang Courtyard—ran right into you. Feels better getting it off my chest. Got chores to run!"
Left frozen in place, Asheng reeled. If the shock hit him this hard, what would it do to Miss? Should he tell her or keep quiet? Deciding to think it over after his errand, he walked on.
Meanwhile, a Qiao family carriage halted outside Chen Manor. Xiaguo stepped down first, followed by Aimo helping the blind drummer out.
Xiaguo took his arm. "Grandfather, Miss is married into the Chen family now. Remember to call her Young Madam."
The old man nodded. "You've drilled that into me ten times—my ears are calloused! Are the Chens as rich as the Qiaos?"
"In silver, the Chens are Lin'an's richest—the Qiaos can't touch them," Xiaguo explained. "In prestige, the Qiaos are imperial kin, and the Chens can't match that."
"Each has its own shine, leagues above country folk like us," the drummer chuckled. "Mind your place in the Qiao household and live steady."
"You're not sore about me being a concubine anymore, Grandfather?"
"I made peace with it. What good is grumbling now that you're married in? Long as you live well, your parents and I are glad."
"Come on, Miss is probably waiting."
Having given the storyteller the day off for the blind drummer's performance, Qianli Xun was working on her huaben in Suxin Thatched Hall until a maid announced Concubine Xia of the Qiao household. Dropping her brush, she had Kuqiao stow the manuscript and hurried out to greet them.
Meeting them in the courtyard, Qianli Xun took the old man's arm. "Thank you for making the trip, Elder. Few artists still sing drum ballads like yours, so I sent for you special to perform for our Old Madam Xia."
"Young Madam showed endless kindness to our Xiaguo. Say one word and this old man comes running."
"Would you like to rest first, or head straight to Grandmother's courtyard?"
"I sat enough in the carriage. Let's go sing for Old Madam right away."
"Then let me walk you over."
Xiaguo spoke up. "I'll wait right here, Miss. Once you get him settled, come back and let's chat."
Qianli Xun nodded and called Hongdou to host Concubine Xia inside Suxin Thatched Hall.
Stepping in, Xiaguo looked around before sitting. "Why do the furniture and layout look identical to Wangyue Pavilion? Felt like I stepped straight back into her maiden room."
Seating herself at the tea table to measure out tea powder, Hongdou explained, "It looked nothing like this when Miss first arrived. She redid the entire place and hauled all her furniture over from Wangyue Pavilion."
"So that's it." Noticing Hongdou whisking tea, Xiaguo arched a brow. "You learned how to make tea too?"
"Matron Wei told Sister Kuqiao to teach me. She said Sister Kuqiao will marry Guard Bai sooner or later, so I should train to take over serving Miss up close."
Xiaguo settled onto the cushion opposite her. "Passable form, though you need more practice."
"I just started, still clunky, though Miss says it tastes decent."
"Being a maid in Miss's service brings pure luck," Xiaguo mused. "Look at me—half a mistress in Qiao Manor, married to the man I love. Even Kuqiao is marrying an imperial prince's guard, way better than some rich house's manservant. Know Youfan?"
"No."
"Know Nan Shuang?"
"Sure. He stopped by yesterday to ask for Miss's poems for Young Master Qiao."
Xiaguo sneered. "Youfan is Miao Zhiyu's maid. Not half as lucky as us—Nan Shuang has her spinning in circles, and she's grinning like a fool."
Finishing the whisked tea, Hongdou offered the bowl. "Please enjoy, Concubine Xia."
Xiaguo took a sip. "Not bad at all." She glanced back at Aimo. "Start learning to make tea once we're home."
"Yes, Concubine Xia—I'll need you to teach me!" Aimo beamed.
"Of course. I may not match Yongtai Teahouse's tea masters, yet I beat Kuqiao hands down—the pupil outshining the teacher. Stay loyal to me, and I'll arrange a far better future for you than Youfan will ever see."
"Thank you, Concubine Xia!"
Right then Qianli Xun walked back in. "What's got you all grinning?"
Setting down her empty tea bowl, Xiaguo stood to greet her. "You're back, Miss! I've got heaps to tell you."
Before Xiaguo opened her mouth, Qianli Xun already knew it would be Qiao household gossip—zero interest to her. Still, for the blind drummer's sake, she might as well spare an hour to listen to Xiaguo chatter.
#CH 222
#TITLE: Dull Chatter with Xiaguo
Chatting with Xiaguo promised to be dull enough; stuck indoors without a view would make it unbearable. "Let's go talk under the hehuan silk tree in the yard."
Matron Wei had already had a rattan chair and wooden table placed beneath the tree. Hongdou fetched a second chair for Xiaguo, Kuqiao set down a platter of seasonal fruit and stood by to wait on them, and Hongdou wandered off to the West Courtyard to watch Qinggua practice—he had the sidestep almost nailed now and should have no trouble dodging his master's boots.
Though summer had not arrived yet, the midday sun packed heat. Sitting in the dappled shade beneath the leaves spared a woman's complexion, leaving Xiaguo pleased.
She praised the courtyard first. "I glanced around on your wedding day, Miss—not a single tree stood here. Look at it now: every chrysanthemum you love, lotus pads sprouting in the pond, and this lush hehuan tree. Yard and hall alike scream that you rule the roost."
"Chen Haoyu promised me this courtyard before the wedding. My turf, my taste—otherwise looking at it every day would drive me nuts."
Xiaguo sighed. "Being a primary wife sure beats everything. As a concubine in Qiao Manor, I could never dream of this."
"At least you married the man you love," Qianli Xun consoled her.
That hit the sweet spot. Formidable and admired as her former mistress was, she had married a stranger, whereas Xiaguo had won her heart's desire. A proud smile lit Xiaguo's face. "There's one piece of news you have to celebrate for me."
Leaning back in the rattan chair with closed eyes to soak in the leafy breeze and flecks of sunlight, Qianli Xun asked, "What news?"
"Wenyuan has shared my bed," Xiaguo confessed with a shy blush.
Eyes still shut, Qianli Xun quirked a lip. "Sharing bedroom secrets right in front of me—no shame at all."
"I think of you as family, Miss. He consummated his marriage with Miao Zhiyu too—keeps the scales even. Miao Zhiyu acts politer to me now, though she still slips barbs into everything she says."
Having zero appetite for another household's drama, Qianli Xun stayed silent.
"You don't know, Miss," Xiaguo went on. "Miao Zhiyu acts the perfect gentlewoman on the outside, yet her heart isn't half that kind. Every few days she hunts for excuses to pick on me. Good thing I'm no fool—most of the time Wenyuan sides with me, so she can't touch me."
Feeling obliged to answer, Qianli Xun spoke without opening her eyes. "Hard to judge whether someone is good or bad—it all depends where you stand. At poetry salons, Miao Zhiyu seemed poised and refined; during last year's rumors, she even defended me behind my back. As for now, I won't rush to judge since I don't live under her roof every day."
Taking that as agreement, Xiaguo warmed up further. "She may share salon ties with you, Miss, yet she doesn't really like you. Every few days Wenyuan sends Nan Shuang for your poems, and it drives her up the wall. Just yesterday she confronted him to his face, asking if he still can't get over Youqi Jushi..."
Hearing that a few of Zhu Shuzhen's poems were sparking fights in Wenyuan's home made Qianli Xun crack her eyes open and gaze at the garden, wishing the scenery could erase Xiaguo's chatter.
Xiaguo rattled right on. "Wenyuan told her he's moved on—I believe him, yet Miao Zhiyu doesn't. She ordered him to stop sending Nan Shuang for poems, and he refused. Given my bond with you, of course I backed Wenyuan, so he's been spending most nights in my room lately. Miao Zhiyu is livid, and the madder she gets, the happier I am!"
Gazing up at the sprouting branches of the hehuan tree, Qianli Xun tried picturing its summer blooms, yet Xiaguo's voice cut through every thought. She wanted this talk over now.
"Xiaguo, pass a message to Wenyuan: tell him to stop sending Nan Shuang for poems."
"No way!" Xiaguo refused on the spot. "It's his one hobby—I won't spoil his mood."
"Then next time Nan Shuang comes, I'll just turn him away." Qianli Xun shut her eyes again.
"No way!" Xiaguo protested again. "When did you ever care what Miao Zhiyu thinks, Miss? Proves her love for your verse was fake all along. Guess who she's joined at the hip with these days?"
Wenyuan was hardly the only one requesting poems, Qianli Xun thought, yet no other household turned verse into a battlefield. The fault lay not in Zhu Shuzhen's poems, yet in human hearts; when someone wanted to pick a fight, flat looked round. Her own conscience stood clear—she was spreading Zhu Shuzhen's art, not Qianli Xun's feelings. Deciding Xiaguo had a point, she let out one word: "Who?"
"Lin Jue's wife, Bai Meiruo." Mentioning Lin Jue curdled Xiaguo's face—she had not forgotten him pawing her and tying her up when she was a maid. "She drops by Qiao Manor nonstop, and Miao Zhiyu drags her around introducing her to all her close friends. I can't stand Bai Meiruo, though Lin Jue's concubine seems decent enough from the one time I met her."
Qianli Xun popped her eyes open. Barely ten days since she ran into Bai Meiruo, and Lin Jue already had a concubine? "Don't tell me it's Chun Jinqiao from Chunxiang Brothel?"
Xiaguo gasped. "You heard already? News flies fast!"
News flies fast? I'm the one who pitched the idea! Qianli Xun thought.
"Bai Meiruo may be nasty, yet she goes all out for Lin Jue," Xiaguo said. "Used her own private dowry silver three days ago to buy Chun Jinqiao out of the brothel and set her up as his concubine. Yesterday Miao Zhiyu dragged me to a banquet requiring every wife to bring her concubine. Thought she was being nice—turned out to be a pack of primary wives gathering just to mock and lecture concubines! That's where I met Chun Jinqiao."
Qianli Xun closed her eyes a third time to enjoy the spring air. "They actually throw banquets like that? Skip them from now on."
"First time—didn't know better. Next time Miao Zhiyu tries dragging me along, I'll refuse flat. Still, I met concubines from all the big Lin'an houses there and found out they host private gatherings of their own. I chipped in to join their circle, so I won't lack company anymore!" A smug smile lit Xiaguo's face; she had found her tribe, a whole club where they could trade gossip and complain about primary wives.
Eyes shut, Qianli Xun murmured a classic line. "Old Master Laozi got it right: 'Good fortune hides within disaster, and disaster lurks within good fortune.'"
Baffled by the quote, Xiaguo fumbled for an answer until a maid from Old Madam Xia's courtyard arrived to rescue them both.
"Young Madam, the elder has finished his ballad. Old Madam Xia wants to chat with him and keep him for lunch, and sent me to invite you and Concubine Xia over."
Thrilled for an exit from wife-versus-concubine politics, Qianli Xun rose from her rattan chair. "Come on, let's eat at Grandmother's."
The lively meal in Old Madam Xia's courtyard left Xiaguo zero opening for petty complaints. Afterward, Qianli Xun escorted the blind drummer and Xiaguo to the front gate.
The old drummer left with a heavy purse—enough silver from the generous Chens to cover a full year without trudging from village to village in wind and sun. Climbing into the carriage, he marveled aloud.
Xiaguo pouted. "No need to marvel, Grandfather. Even without Chen silver, what I send home is plenty. Quit wandering the countryside singing!"
"Your own path in Qiao Manor isn't easy—stop sending us all your silver and save a nest egg so you can stand tall there. Remember to stay on good terms with your in-laws and primary wife. Harmony makes a house thrive."
"You've told me a dozen times, Grandfather. I remember."
Returning to Moxiang Courtyard, Qianli Xun spotted Asheng pacing restlessly in the yard. "Something up, Asheng?"
He turned, opened his mouth to speak, hesitated, and choked it back. "Nothing, Miss. Heading to the West Courtyard to drill Qinggua." He hurried off like a man carrying a secret.
Qianli Xun blinked. "What's gotten into Asheng?"
"Word is Asheng has a crush on Hongdou," Kuqiao said. "Probably wanted to ask you to betroth her to him."
Qianli Xun chuckled. "He likes Hongdou? If he's too shy to say it, let's pretend we didn't notice." Dismissing it, she headed indoors to write.
Halfway to the West Courtyard, Asheng ran straight into Hongdou. Bursting with the secret, he grabbed her arm and pulled her into a quiet corner.
"What are you dragging me for?"
"I'm about to burst!"
"Go hit the latrine then!" Hongdou teased.
"Not that kind of burst—a secret eating me alive!"
Long aware of Asheng's crush, Hongdou assumed he had finally worked up the nerve to confess, and heat crept up her cheeks. "Go on then. I'm listening."
Asheng dropped his voice. "Remember last year's rumors about Miss?"
Disappointed that no confession was coming, Hongdou huffed, "Of course I remember. Why dig up ancient history?"
Checking that nobody was nearby, Asheng blurted out, "A servant from Eldest Young Master's courtyard just told me the young master himself started those rumors!"
Disappointment flipped to shock. "What? Second Young Master spread them?!"
"Keep your voice down!"
"What do we do?" Hongdou fretted. "Poor Miss—she hated marrying him already. If she finds out he wrecked her match with Young Master Qiao, it'll crush her! Yet keeping her in the dark like a fool feels cruel too."
"That's why I'm torn. Tell her or not? You decide."
"I don't know either."
"What are you two whispering about over here?" a voice asked.
Both spun to see Matron Wei, just back from checking the shops. Exchanging a glance, they agreed Matron Wei's brain beat theirs hands down. After bowing, Hongdou said, "Come back to your room first, Matron. Asheng and I have huge news."
Inside Matron Wei's quarters, before she could sit, the pair spilled every detail.
Matron Wei sank onto her couch in shock. Sharp as she was, she had never guessed the groom was the culprit. Yet looking back, every piece snapped into place. Last year, she had wondered why the Chen family did not blink at citywide scandal when arranging the match. Prefect Zhu cared above all for face and had once told Madam Xiang he was investigating the rumor-monger—only for the probe to vanish overnight and turn into a rushed betrothal to the Chens. Prefect Zhu had caught the culprit and forced the match, thinking it salvaged Zhu honor while landing his daughter a rich husband—leaving Shuzhen clueless and trapped.
"You two go on back," Matron Wei said. "Let me think this over."
"Yes, Matron."
Stepping outside, both breathed easier. "Handing that headache to Matron Wei takes a ton off my shoulders," Asheng sighed.
Still sore from thinking he was about to confess, Hongdou snapped, "Enjoy your relief then. I've got work to do!" and marched off.
Asheng scratched his head at her retreating back. "Weird girl—fine a second ago, now snapping my head off out of nowhere."
#CH 223
#TITLE: The Culprit Is the Groom
Tell her mistress that the groom started the rumors, or keep it buried? Matron Wei sat on the edge of her couch weighing both sides.
Keep quiet, and since even servants knew, Shuzhen would find out sooner or later. Tell her, and fresh resentment would poison whatever peace remained between husband and wife.
Her mind replayed an encounter in the garden on her way back from errands earlier that afternoon. Walking along the Chen Manor path, she had heard Yingxue calling from a pavilion where Yao Qingyan sat resting and waving her over.
Guessing First Madam had waited there on purpose, Matron Wei stepped up, curtsied, and took a seat by the stone table. "Busy as I am, I'm nothing next to the Chen masters."
"I owe you thanks for helping Shuzhen—and helping me in the bargain," Yao Qingyan smiled.
Having forgotten her offhand remark, Matron Wei looked puzzled. "Which matter does Madam mean?"
"You help Shuzhen so much you lose track! I mean cheering up Old Madam Xia."
Matron Wei smiled in recognition. "Just a passing word I dropped. Credit goes to Miss for taking it to heart."
"You have brains, and Shuzhen has heart." Yao Qingyan's smile gave way to a frown. "Now I need your brains on another headache."
"What troubles Madam?"
"Haoyu and Shuzhen. Married, unconsummated, living separate lives—him roaming wild outside, her acting like he doesn't exist. At this rate, will I ever hold a chubby grandson?"
Matron Wei had known this day would arrive; a prenuptial contract could only stretch so far inside a traditional clan. "Patience, Madam. These things take time."
"Set grandsons aside for now—the urgent job is getting Haoyu under control. Old Madam Xia, Jianglin, and I all agreed to hand his discipline to Shuzhen. We asked her already, yet she nodded polite and ignored it, and now we feel awkward bringing it up again. Please, Matron, figure out a way to make Shuzhen willing to rein Haoyu in."
Now the pavilion ambush made total sense. "Raising a son is normally an elder's job," Matron Wei noted dryly. "Asking a bride to raise her own husband—few folks would believe it."
"I feel ashamed as a mother dumping my own failure onto my daughter-in-law," Yao Qingyan admitted. "Yet Old Madam Xia, Jianglin, and I talked it through, and handing him to Shuzhen has huge upsides—above all, rubbing up against each other every day. Strike two stubborn stones together enough times and sparks fly, let alone two living people! Don't you agree, Matron?"
Half amused, Matron Wei understood their bind. Old Madam Xia had spoiled the boy too long to play tough, Yao Qingyan lacked the stomach for harshness, and Chen Jianglin's strictness collapsed whenever his mother and wife intervened. Shuzhen was the ideal enforcer—sparing the three elders conflict while potentially reforming the boy and warming the marriage. Clever scheme. And honestly, whipping out a decent husband by her own hand might not hurt Shuzhen either. Still, Shuzhen honored contracts and had zero interest in babysitting Chen Haoyu.
"Good plan, Madam, except I doubt Miss will bite."
"That's why I'm begging you, Matron! Find a way to make her willing."
"I never push Miss into anything she dislikes..."
Yao Qingyan stood and stepped right in front of her. "Refuse me and I'll kneel right here until you say yes!"
Horrified at the sight of a mistress bending her knees to a servant, Matron Wei jumped up and caught her arms. "You'll shorten my life, Madam! I'll agree—no promises she'll listen, yet I'll try my best."
Overjoyed, Yao Qingyan squeezed her hands. "With you on the case, it's as good as done!"
Back in her own room, Matron Wei finished connecting the dots. If she told Shuzhen the truth, her mistress would erupt and lock Chen Haoyu down tight, ending his wild days on the spot—disciplining him even without calling it discipline. Knowing her mistress, fierce fists or not, she would never maim or kill him, just put him through the wringer he had earned ten times over. Matron Wei did not expect romance overnight, yet a good husband beat a bad one—and looking at how Chen Jianglin cherished his wife, Chen Haoyu had solid family stock underneath the rot. If Haoyu ever treated Shuzhen half as well as his father treated Yao Qingyan, Matron Wei would smile in her sleep.
Mind made up, Matron Wei stepped outside and glanced across the yard at Boya Study. "Miss already banished him to the back courtyard right across from me—what can't she handle? Helping her whip up a decent husband is nothing to hesitate over."
Inside Suxin Thatched Hall, Qianli Xun was deep into her writing. Having finished her previous arc, she had dropped adapting her old modern web novels to launch a brand-new tale inspired by her own heartache and the sight of Ye Anya and Cao Ban beneath the willow: star-crossed lovers fighting out of wretched marriages for real happiness. Ideas poured onto the paper.
Three or four pages in, Matron Wei walked in. Qianli Xun laid down her brush and hurried over. "Same courtyard, yet I haven't seen you in days—missed you!"
Glancing at the desk, Matron Wei teased, "Didn't have Kuqiao hide your manuscript today, Miss?"
Qianli Xun tugged her into a chair. "You knew all along and stayed mum, letting me put on a whole act!"
Weighing how to break the news, Matron Wei stayed silent to draw her mistress's curiosity.
"Why so quiet, Matron?"
"There is a matter I turned over and over, and decided I must tell you."
"What is it?" Qianli Xun leaned forward, intrigued.
"Last year's rumors."
"Those died down ages ago. Are people gossiping again?"
"The culprit behind them just surfaced."
Before Qianli Xun could speak, Kuqiao bristled beside her. "You know who it was, Matron? Tell us right now so I can march over and curse their ears off!"
"Who was it?" Qianli Xun pressed. "How did you find out?"
"How doesn't matter," Matron Wei said with caution. "What matters is what you plan to do once I name them."
"Need you ask? That scum ruined my life—two words: payback!"
"Right! Payback!" Kuqiao cheered.
"Out with it, Matron. Who?"
Steeling herself, Matron Wei gave two words: "Young Master."
"Chen Haoyu?!" Qianli Xun stared.
Matron Wei nodded.
Kuqiao froze silent, watching shock harden into fury on her mistress's face. Qianli Xun's fingers clamped around the wooden armrest—CRACK! The solid camphorwood snapped clean off in her grip.
Young Master is dead meat! Kuqiao winced inside.
Qianli Xun shot to her feet, paced two steps, and whipped back around. "If even you found out, Matron, with my father's reach he must have known ages ago! He knew, and still pushed me blind into marrying Chen Haoyu! I'm marching back to Zhu Manor right now to have it out with him!"
Matron Wei stood and blocked her. "What good does yelling at Prefect Zhu do now that the wedding's done? Think about how to deal with Young Master first."
That snapped Qianli Xun back to focus. Storming Zhu Manor fixed nothing. "Fine, my father gets a pass for now. Anyone else can slide—never Chen Haoyu! I'm collecting every cent for making me the laughingstock of Lin'an! Kuqiao!"
"Here!"
"Fetch Hongdou!"
Moments later Hongdou rushed in.
"Take men and scour every brothel and gambling den in Lin'an until you find Chen Haoyu," Qianli Xun barked. "Report back the second you spot him—I'm going in person to beat him senseless and drag him home in ropes!"
"No need to scour, Miss," Hongdou said. "I already know where he is."
"Chunxiang Brothel?"
Hongdou nodded.
"Round up the crew. We're hitting Chunxiang Brothel!"
Without another word, Qianli Xun stormed out of Suxin Thatched Hall.
Matron Wei let out a sigh. "Here comes the fireworks."
Kuqiao blinked. "Why do you sound like you're enjoying the show, Matron?"
"Nonsense! Stow the manuscript before someone sees it, and get that broken chair swapped out."
Before tidying up, Kuqiao caught Matron Wei's sleeve in alarm. "Matron, I'm scared—Miss already divorced once. You don't think she's heading for a second mutual divorce?"
"Wish something good for Miss instead of keeping 'divorce' glued to your tongue! Sure, this groom is a mess, yet this second marriage is nothing like the first—the Chens aren't the Lins. Just sit back and watch."
Matron Wei stepped out, leaving Kuqiao muttering to herself. "Matron always talks in riddles, though if she isn't worried, Miss must be fine. Besides, Young Master asked for it—Miss'll beat his hide raw!" She got busy clearing the pages and replacing the chair.
Qianli Xun marched out of Moxiang Courtyard toward the front gates flanked by ten servants—three maids and seven men—turning heads all down the paths.
Near the main gate, she ran right into Chen Haodong returning home. Guessing his scheme had landed, he put on a bright smile and stepped up. "Where are you off to with an army, Younger Sister-in-law?"
With nothing to hide from the Chens, Qianli Xun answered flat, "Hunting Chen Haoyu."
"Send servants if you want him back. Why march out in person?"
A sudden question hit her: had everyone in Chen Manor known except her? "Did Eldest Cousin know Chen Haoyu spread those rumors about me last year?"
Bullseye! Chen Haodong rejoiced inside, happy to pour oil on the tigress's blaze. "Since you found out, I won't hide it. Everyone in Chen Manor knew. That's the exact reason the clan overlooked your damaged name and prior divorce. A real man owns up to his mistakes. Besides, Prefect Zhu marched in last year with a whip, dragging a hog-tied Haoyu to Eldest Uncle and Eldest Aunt and forcing the betrothal on the spot. They had no choice except to agree."
Whatever Chen Haodong's game was, he had laid out the whole chain of events. Zhu Xiyan had known all along and hidden it just to offload a disgraced daughter and patch up Zhu Manor's prestige, caring nothing for her happiness.
Too furious for words, Qianli Xun brushed straight past Chen Haodong without a reply.
Grinning wider, Chen Haodong called after her, "He's at Chunxiang Brothel, Younger Sister-in-law—don't look in the wrong spot!"
Mission accomplished, Chen Haodong strolled back to his quarters humming inside, ready for the show.
#CH 224
#TITLE: Hog-Tied and Locked Away
Blazing with rage, Qianli Xun tossed ladylike image to the wind, hopped off the carriage with ten servants at her heels, and stormed straight into Chunxiang Brothel. Seeing their mistress march in without blinking, Hongdou and the other two maids dropped their shyness and followed right behind.
Inside, the usual bustle hummed—music on stage, wine flowing, patrons flirting—until every jaw dropped at the sight of a well-bred young lady barging in with ten servants, three of them young maids.
Recognizing her at once, the brothel madam gasped under her breath, "Mother of mercy! Young Master Chen's tigress tracked him here!" Hurrying over, she forced a smile. "Looking for Young Master Chen, Young Madam?"
"Where is he?" Qianli Xun's face promised bruises within sixty seconds.
No sense shielding a husband from his own wife. "Upstairs with Chun Jinmo."
"Lead the way." Her voice crackled with cold fury.
Still hoping to tip her patron off, the madam spotted Scarface on the landing and yelled, "Master Scar! Tell Young Master Chen his wife's here!"
Scarface had already seen them and bolted inside the room to warn him.
"Right this way, Young Madam," the madam gestured.
Barely two steps toward the stairs, Chen Haoyu's bark echoed down. "Zhu Shuzhen! What are you doing barging in here? Get back home!"
Qianli Xun glanced up to see him descending the stairs while tugging his disheveled robe straight—plain as day what he had just been doing—with the three bodyguards from the manor gate trailing behind.
Remembering the rumors and staring at his smug, punchable face, Qianli Xun snapped. Using her light-foot technique, she vaulted straight up the staircase, snatched Chen Haoyu by the collar, dropped back to the floor in one swoop, and shoved him flat on his backside.
Humiliated before a packed room, Chen Haoyu blustered from the floor. "Acting tough in public? I'm letting it slide out here—wait till I get home and teach you a lesson!"
Having already tasted the seven servants' fists and seeing the wife outclassed them all, the three bodyguards traded one glance and bailed. Stepping up to Chen Haoyu, they bowed. "Family business, Young Master Chen—we'll sit this one out. See you around!"
Abandoned by his guards, Chen Haoyu scrambled up, only for Qianli Xun to bark, "Tie him up!"
Asheng whipped out rope, and with two helpers trussed Chen Haoyu tight in three seconds flat.
"Zhu Shuzhen, you've lost your mind!" Chen Haoyu roared. "I'm your husband! Bullying your own husband in public—people will laugh their heads off!"
Sure enough, patrons craned their necks grinning at the spectacle.
Having no desire to linger, Qianli Xun snapped, "Haul him out!"
Just as she pivoted for the door, a soft voice called from behind. "Hold on, Young Madam!"
Turning back, Qianli Xun saw a slender, pretty woman swaying down the stairs like a willow in the breeze—Chun Jinmo, no doubt.
Chun Jinmo curtsied before her. "Blessings upon you, Young Madam."
"What do you want?"
"I've read your poems, Young Madam—tender, wistful, full of feeling. Meeting you in person, you don't match your verse at all."
"Not in the mood for poetry talk. Excuse me." Qianli Xun turned to leave.
Chun Jinmo stepped across her path. "Wait, Young Madam—not poetry. I heard you signed a prenuptial contract with Young Master Chen promising not to meddle in each other's lives. Why storm in here today and treat your husband like a criminal?"
Hearing that Chen Haoyu had blabbed their contract to a courtesan lit a fresh fuse. "Who the hell are you to stick your nose in my business? What contract? Never heard of it! Save your breath!"
Turning a third time, Qianli Xun halted as Chun Jinmo hurried forward and dropped to her knees before the whole crowd.
"I didn't touch a hair on you—what are you kneeling for?"
"Young Madam, since being sold to Chunxiang Brothel, Young Master Chen is the only man I've ever served. He has sheltered me all this time. If he stops coming, my life here will turn to hell. Have mercy and let him go, Young Madam—I'll owe you a debt of gratitude forever!"
The sight of her kneeling melted Chen Haoyu's heart. "Look how pitiful she is, Zhu Shuzhen! You hate my guts and live happier without me, and the Chen clan has plenty of other sons, yet Jinmo can't survive without me—I'm everything to her! Untie me right now and quit making a scene!"
With revenge fresh in her blood, Qianli Xun leaned close to him. "Starting today, the more you want something, the harder I'll block it. Want to protect her? I'll make sure you never lay eyes on her again."
Turning down to Chun Jinmo, she spoke plain. "Sure, you've got it rough, and I'm not heartless, yet I'm in no mood to play nursemaid. Ever wonder when I needed pity? Where were you when I was getting torn apart, and what was Chen Haoyu doing? I'm no saint and no savior. Kneeling to me buys you zero."
With that, she marched her crew out of Chunxiang Brothel.
At the doorway, Chen Haoyu craned his neck back to shout, "Hang tight! I'll be back in no time!"
Left weeping on the floorboards, Chun Jinmo felt her chest go hollow. With a wife that fierce, clinging to Young Master Chen was over. Would she really have to yield to a brute like Master Jiang?
The brothel madam hurried over and lifted her up. "Jinmo, you're a courtesan—face facts. Any patron who calls your name and pays silver gets served, unless you get lucky like Jinqiao and land a man willing to buy you out as a concubine. I heard you dropped hints to Young Master Chen plenty of times and he never gave you a straight answer. He's just playing around, and with that tigress at home, forget redemption. Find another patron who might actually free you. Master Jiang isn't half bad—older and rough-looking, sure, yet he's genuinely hooked on you and fought Young Master Chen over you how many times? Word is he doesn't even have a primary wife yet. That's a real shot."
Her words sank partway in; wiping her eyes, Chun Jinmo climbed back upstairs.
Back in Suxin Thatched Hall at Moxiang Courtyard, Qianli Xun sat behind her desk glaring at Chen Haoyu trussed upright in a chair.
Acting unbothered, he smirked. "Staring at me like that—never seen a handsome man before? Or did you miss me after a few days apart?"
"Hongdou! Slap him twice for me!"
"Zhu Shuzhen, are you out of your mind?!" Chen Haoyu barked.
Hongdou froze. "Miss, I don't dare—he's the young master."
"Touch me and I'll sell you straight to Chunxiang Brothel!" Chen Haoyu threatened.
Hongdou shrank back.
"What's your game today, Zhu Shuzhen?" Chen Haoyu demanded. "We signed a contract not to interfere! Did a dog eat your precious contract spirit?"
Qianli Xun picked up a sheet from her desk. "Here's your contract. Look close." Popping the lid off her incense burner, she rolled the sheet tight and dropped it inside; flames licked up and reduced it to gray ash in seconds.
Eyes bulging, Chen Haoyu waited until she replaced the lid before shouting, "You burned it! That voids everything! Hand back my properties, restore my courtyard and rooms, and pack your bags to the back yard—I'm moving back in here!"
"Are you hearing yourself, Chen Haoyu? Think I'd burn that contract if I planned on handing back a single brick or coin? Dream on!"
"Aren't you scared I'll tell Grandmother and my parents so they haul you over the coals?!"
"You'd have to get out of this courtyard first!"
Sensing something different from before—when she had wanted peaceful coexistence—Chen Haoyu swallowed his bluster and asked, "Did you swallow gunpowder today? I haven't done a thing to cross you since we wed. Why pull this?"
That lit her up all over again. "Forgotten your own filthy deeds already, Chen Haoyu?!"
A chill prickled his spine. Burning the contract, foaming at the mouth—had she found out about the rumors? He probed with caution. "Did you hear something?"
Itching to smash his face in, Qianli Xun stood, balled her fists, and stalked toward him. "Last year, you spread filth across Lin'an, wrecked my marriage prospects, and turned me into a citywide joke! Time to settle that tab!"
Terror iced his veins—she knew! I'm a dead man! Seeing her fist whistle toward him, he squeezed his eyes shut. CRASH! He hit the floor in a shower of splinters—she had smashed the chair out from under him instead.
Exhaling in relief, he cracked his eyes open and blustered back. "Your own fault for bullying me nonstop! If you hadn't picked on me, I'd never have spread rumors! Besides, folks gossiped over your own line—'falling asleep in his arms, fully dressed'—"
"Hongdou! Slap him now!" Qianli Xun roared.
Ordered twice, Hongdou hesitated no longer. Stepping up, she declared, "Even if you sell me to a brothel, Young Master, I'm hitting you for Miss!"
SMACK! SMACK! Two stinging palms landed square on Chen Haoyu's cheeks.
Standing by, Kuqiao felt furious for her mistress yet winced at the sound.
Bound tight and unable to rub his throbbing face, Chen Haoyu hissed, "Damn maid! Why swing so hard?!"
Qianli Xun crouched and tapped his reddening cheek. "I meant to pound you into pulp and settled for two slaps instead. Getting off that light, and you're still whining?"
Unmoved, Chen Haoyu spat, "Zhu Shuzhen! I'm repudiating you!"
"Divorce me? Not a chance! From today on, I have two goals in Chen Manor: live my best life, and make yours pure hell."
"H-how do you plan to torture me?" Fear crept into his voice.
"Everything you love doing, I forbid," Qianli Xun said, spacing out every word crisp and clear. "Everything you hate doing, I force you to do."
"You—you—" Speech failed him.
