Qianli Xun stood. "Guards! Lock Chen Haoyu in Boya Study out back!"
Asheng and another servant hauled him into the back courtyard, shoved him into Boya Study, and untied the ropes. The instant his arms came free, Chen Haoyu lunged to deck Asheng and bolt, only for Asheng to block the doorway. "Better behave, Young Master. Crossing Miss won't end pretty."
Outside, shutters slammed shut and hammers drove wooden planks straight across the windows.
Chen Haoyu rushed over roaring, "Stop that! I own this courtyard!"
Then the door pulled shut and a heavy padlock clicked home.
Chen Haoyu pounded the wood shouting, "Zhu Shuzhen! This isn't over! Just you wait! This is Chen Manor—not Zhu Manor, and not your Wangyue Pavilion!"
A familiar voice floated through the shutter crack. "Young Master? Young Master, you all right?"
For the first time in his life, Qinggua's voice sounded like heaven. Chen Haoyu pressed his face to the window. "Qinggua, thank goodness! That tigress is torturing me half to death! Run tell Old Madam Xia, Master, and Madam right now—tell them I'm divorcing her! Go!"
"Count on me, Young Master! On my way!"
Qinggua sprinted into the front yard aiming for the gate—only to freeze beside the lotus pond at a sharp call.
"Going somewhere, Qinggua? Running to tattle for your master?"
Skidding to a halt, Qinggua scrambled for a fib. "Misunderstanding, Young Madam! Just looking for an open spot to practice that Phantom Sidestep you taught me!"
"You've got it down pat—no need to practice. Since I'd hate for you to lack a bed, starting today you're bunking inside Boya Study with Chen Haoyu." To stop leaks, Qianli Xun had no other choice.
"Young Madam, Young Master messed up, not me! Don't drag me in—I'm fine sleeping in the West Courtyard!"
"Your master gets lonely in there. Keep him company." Grabbing his scruff, Qianli Xun marched him straight back to Boya Study.
Hearing the padlock turn, Chen Haoyu lit up, expecting Grandmother to storm in and set him free—only for Qinggua to get shoved through the doorway before the door slammed and locked again.
"Sent you some company so you won't get lonely, Chen Haoyu!" Zhu Shuzhen called from outside.
Chen Haoyu hammered his fists against the door screaming, "Zhu Shuzhen! The second I get out of here, I'm divorcing you for sure!"
#CH 225
#TITLE: Matron Wei Soothes the Elders
After pounding the door and shouting himself hoarse to zero effect, Chen Haoyu needed a punching bag. Spinning around, he laid eyes on Qinggua's wide-eyed innocent face and flared up worse.
"I sent you to fetch Grandmother, Father, and Mother! How did you end up locked in here too?!"
"Don't blame me, Young Master! Young Madam's eyes are sharp—she caught me in the front yard, saw right through me, and tossed me in here."
"You idiot! Couldn't you make up an excuse?"
"I did! She didn't buy it, said I should keep you company." Qinggua edged closer. "Young Master, why not just play nice from now on? When Young Madam says east, don't go west. Fighting her gets you nowhere and drags me down too..."
Already fuming, Chen Haoyu snapped and launched a vicious kick. "Daring to look down on me too?! I'll kick the daylights out of you!"
Qinggua glided sideways without breaking a sweat, leaving Chen Haoyu spinning off balance. Another kick—missed! Three, four more kicks—Qinggua slipped every single one.
Ditching kicks, Chen Haoyu used his grappling moves and snagged Qinggua by the arm. "Dodge that! Where'd you learn those tricks?"
"Mercy, Young Master! Mercy! Young Madam taught me Phantom Sidestep!"
"Zhu Shuzhen again!" Letting go, Chen Haoyu landed a boot square on Qinggua's backside before he could turn. "To hell with that!"
Qinggua stumbled forward onto the floorboards, bruised pride more than bruised skin, and stayed sitting on the floor. "Quit beating on me, Young Master. No matter how raw you kick me, we're still locked in. Think of a way out instead!"
Mad as he was, Chen Haoyu knew he had brought this on himself. The real goal was getting word to his parents and grandmother; once the elders stepped in, Zhu Shuzhen would have to unlock the door.
He dropped into a cushioned chair. "Which of the servants in this yard are you tight with?"
Qinggua puffed up with pride. "Every last one! While you were gone, I drilled with them in the West Courtyard every day—just Phantom Sidestep, since Young Madam said I lack aptitude for real fist forms. Hanging out all day made us close. You don't know, Young Master, I even... I fell for Hongdou, and I think she likes me too..." A blush crept up his neck.
"Hongdou falling for a face like yours? Quit dreaming!" Chen Haoyu scoffed. "Tell me which of those ten servants is closest to you so we can get them to pass a message."
Crushed by the jab, Qinggua pouted and forgot the mission. "You always look down on me, Young Master! First maid I ever like, and you cut me down. Look how good Young Madam treats her servants—you should learn a thing or two from her!"
"Since when do you lecture your master? Talk business or I'll smack you!"
Qinggua stuck out his lower lip. "All ten are friendly with me, except they take orders from Young Madam. I can't boss them around."
Chen Haoyu stalked over and grabbed his shirtfront. "Half an hour of breath wasted for that?! Fine—your punishment is standing by the door shouting 'Zhu Shuzhen, I'm divorcing you!' Nonstop!" He shoved Qinggua over to the door. "Yell!"
Sprawled by the threshold, Qinggua whimpered, "Young Master, she's married to you, not me! How can I yell that? And I'm a servant—how dare I shout Young Madam's full name?"
Chen Haoyu raised a boot. "Yell, or I'll stomp you into meat paste!"
"I'll yell, I'll yell! Don't stomp!" Scrambled to his feet, Qinggua leaned against the door and murmured, "Zhu Shuzhen, I'm divorcing you."
"Louder!"
"Zhu Shuzhen, I'm divorcing you."
"Louder still!"
Squeezing his eyes shut, Qinggua belted it out: "Zhu Shuzhen! I'm divorcing you!" Over and over without pause.
Satisfied, Chen Haoyu strolled into the bedroom, flopped onto the bed, and drifted off to sleep.
Across the back yard inside Jingyi Hall, Matron Wei sat listening to the racket, caught Qinggua's chanting, and stood up. "Time I paid Old Madam Xia a visit."
Over in Old Madam Xia's rooms, her three daughters-in-law were chatting when a maid burst in panting. "Old Madam! Trouble! Huge trouble!"
"Watch your tongue," Old Madam Xia chided. "What's got you frantic? Catch your breath and speak."
Slowing down, the maid reported, "Just now I saw Second Young Madam march Second Young Master through the gate tied up like a hog! Looks like he's in for a rough time!"
Worry hit Old Madam Xia and Yao Qingyan at the same instant.
Thrilled that her son's trap had sprung, Madam Bao put on a horrified face. "What outrage! Barely married in, and she's trussing up her own husband?! You have to step in, Old Madam, or folks will say Chen men let women walk all over them!"
Madam Cui chimed in. "First Sister-in-law, you need to step in and teach that Zhu girl how a daughter-in-law behaves. Wild as Haoyu is, you and Eldest Brother are right here—it's not her place to discipline him."
Old Madam Xia swallowed her jitters. "Stop stirring the pot, you two. I handed Haoyu's discipline to Shuzhen, and I trust her. However she handles him, Jianglin and Qingyan are not to interfere—and neither will I."
Itching to rush over and check, Yao Qingyan held herself back. "I'll listen to Mother."
With both grandmother and mother sick with worry, conversation died. Finding no more fun to stir, Madam Bao and Madam Cui bowed out together.
Outside the gate, Madam Bao tutted. "No idea what Eldest Brother and Sister-in-law saw in that Zhu girl—poetess or not, foul temper and ruined name."
"Drop the act, Second Sister-in-law," Madam Cui teased. "A bad match for Haoyu only helps Haodong. You're laughing up your sleeve."
"Nonsense. Even with a saint for a wife, Haoyu couldn't touch my Haodong. My boy learned every trade from his father and uncles since boyhood, while Haoyu just plays around and your Haofei won't lift a finger for business—leaving all the heavy lifting to Haodong."
Stung by the dig at Haofei, Madam Cui stiffened. "Keep busy, Sister-in-law. I have things to attend to."
Madam Bao sneered at her back. "Generations of Chen merchants, and instead of teaching your boy trade, you dream of imperial exams and capital offices! Good luck with that!" Eager to carry the good news to her son, she hurried off, barely glancing at Matron Wei heading the opposite way.
Inside, heavy silence gripped Old Madam Xia and Yao Qingyan while maids stood mute, until a voice announced from outside: "Old Madam, First Madam, Matron Wei from Second Young Madam's courtyard requests an audience."
Color returned to both women's faces. "Show her in at once!" Old Madam Xia called.
Matron Wei stepped in and curtsied.
"Bring a seat," Old Madam Xia ordered. "You haven't dropped by my courtyard since my granddaughter-in-law married in."
Reading the fretful worry on both faces—brave when handing over discipline, softhearted the moment it began—Matron Wei bowed her head. "My oversight, Old Madam. Please forgive me."
"Understandable—running Shuzhen's entire courtyard keeps you busy enough."
Noticing Old Madam Xia's forced smile, Matron Wei moved to set their minds at rest. "Thank you for understanding, Old Madam. I caught a breather today and came to pay my respects—and give you an update on Miss and Young Master."
Both women spoke in one breath: "How is Haoyu?"
"Look how panicked you two are—afraid Miss is abusing Young Master?"
"Not abusing," Yao Qingyan hedged. "I just hate seeing him suffer."
"I spoiled him from the cradle," Old Madam Xia sighed. "Can't stand seeing him bear a shred of hardship. I know it ruined him, yet my heart still aches."
"All the more reason handing discipline to Miss was the smartest choice," Matron Wei said. "Right now she has him locked in the back courtyard—windows boarded, door padlocked, servants bringing meals and water."
"That's going too far!" both women cried in unison.
"Discipline doesn't have to be that harsh!" Yao Qingyan fretted. "How can Haoyu stand it?"
Seeing their panic, Matron Wei decided the truth was needed. "When Madam stopped me in the garden earlier asking me to persuade Miss to rein Young Master in, Miss had zero interest. You know why she changed her mind? Not my silver tongue—she just found out one huge secret."
"What secret?" Old Madam Xia asked.
"That Young Master himself spread last year's rumors about Miss."
Old Madam Xia and Yao Qingyan traded stricken looks. "A secret like that couldn't stay buried forever," Old Madam Xia groaned. "Maybe it's better she knows, yet poor Haoyu is in for misery now! Go back and coax Shuzhen—discipline him if she must, just don't let her go too far."
"Haoyu acted reckless ruining her name like that," Yao Qingyan fretted. "What if Shuzhen loses her temper and forgets her own strength?"
"Since you entrusted Young Master to Miss, trust her all the way," Matron Wei urged. "I watched her grow up—no soul is purer or kinder..."
"Yet Wenxin told me after losing her memory, Shuzhen turned fierce—nothing like before!" Yao Qingyan cut in.
"Different on the surface, Madam, yet the kindness in her bones never changed. Haven't you felt that yourselves since she married in?"
Both elders nodded.
"Furious as she is about the rumors wrecking her Qiao match, she'll never maim Young Master—only teach him a proper lesson. Put your minds at ease and pretend you know nothing. Just picture him off gallivanting outside like usual. Think of all the scrapes and bruises he got into out there without your knowing—didn't he bounce right back?"
Recalling Haoyu coming home bruised and that rigged gamble with Master Jiang, both women exhaled.
Yao Qingyan hardened her resolve. "Matron Wei is right. We'll pretend he's off gallivanting."
Still, one doubt lingered for Old Madam Xia. "From what you say, Shuzhen locked him up out of spite over the rumors, not to reform him. Will that really get us what we want?"
"Whether spite or discipline, Old Madam, the methods match and the results will match too. Wait and see—Miss will whip out a fine grandson for you. And just like First Madam said, strike two stubborn stones together enough times and sparks might fly!"
That coaxed chuckles from both elders, sweeping the gloom away.
Before leaving, Matron Wei gave one final warning. "While Miss disciplines Young Master, neither of you must step in. If he cries for rescue, harden your hearts and ignore him. One soft moment, and all of Miss's work goes up in smoke."
Steeling their hearts, both women nodded in firm agreement.
#CH 226
#TITLE: Hongdou Delivers Dinner to Boya Study
By dusk, Qinggua's voice had shriveled to a croak, though he dared not stop whispering, "Zhu Shuzhen, I'm divorcing you."
A rumble of snores rolled from the bedroom. Qinggua brightened. "Young Master's asleep! I can take a break—throat's dry as sawdust. Time for tea."
Crossing to the wooden table, he poured a cup and tested it with his lips. "Stone cold, and nobody brought hot water. Whatever, I'm parched." He gulped it down and peered through a shutter crack. "Pitch black outside and my stomach's howling. Where's dinner?"
Right on cue, the padlock rattled. Qinggua bounced toward the door as it swung open and Hongdou walked in carrying a food carrier in one hand and a pot of hot tea in the other.
"Hongdou, you made it!" Taking the teapot to set on the table, Qinggua eyed the open doorway for a dash—only for the door to click shut behind her.
Hongdou set down the carrier and unpacked two plates of vegetables and two bowls of rice. "Miss sent dinner. Where's Young Master? Call him out to eat."
Already roused by the padlock, Chen Haoyu strolled into the front room and glared at Hongdou. "The day I get out, I'm selling you off to pay you back for those two slaps!"
Having already swung once and backed by her mistress, Hongdou did not flinch. "Miss holds my deed of sale, Young Master. You can't touch me."
Stung by a maid's lip, Chen Haoyu barked, "Go tell Zhu Shuzhen I'm divorcing her!"
"You had Qinggua screaming it all afternoon—every soul in Moxiang Courtyard heard, so why repeat it? Miss already answered: whatever you want, she blocks. Want to divorce her? Not a chance!"
Chen Haoyu raised a fist. Qinggua jumped between them. "Don't fight Hongdou, Young Master—we need her to bring our meals!"
That boiled his blood over. Forgetting Qinggua's new trick, he swung a boot—and Qinggua slipped sideways without effort. "Quit kicking me, Young Master, it won't work. I only held back because I care about you; anyone else and I'd have flipped them over already."
Unable to beat Hongdou and now stripped of his one punching bag, Chen Haoyu clenched both fists and hissed, "Zhu Shuzhen, I'll make you pay for this!"
Half laughing, Hongdou said, "Better eat up, Young Master. I'm waiting to take the bowls back."
Starving and powerless, he dropped into a chair and stared at the table. "Only two dishes? I eat five dishes and a soup minimum! Tell Zhu Shuzhen to send more!"
"Miss said every complaint you make cuts the portions smaller."
"Fine, forget I spoke!" Swallowing his rage, he picked up his chopsticks—and froze. "All greens? Not a scrap of meat?!"
"Miss said while you're locked up, it's vegetarian only. No meat."
Too mad for words, Chen Haoyu dug in.
Famished and seeing the second rice bowl meant for him, Qinggua boldy sat across the table and reached for chopsticks.
Chen Haoyu bristled. "Who gave you leave to eat at the same table as me?!"
Dropping the chopsticks, Qinggua stood and stared longingly at the food, swallowing saliva. "Young Master, I yelled all afternoon for you—even without merit I earned sweat! My belly's hollow—just let me grab a few bites!"
"Let Qinggua sit and eat with you, Young Master," Hongdou put in. "Miss's orders."
"Hear that, Young Master? Young Madam's orders!"
Chen Haoyu had almost softened at Qinggua's sad face, yet hearing Zhu Shuzhen's name stiffened his spine. "You're my servant and take my orders—Zhu Shuzhen doesn't count! Sit down and eat with me and I'll tan your hide!"
Daring not sit, Qinggua hovered beside the table watching every bite with aching eyes, praying his master would leave enough behind.
At last Chen Haoyu finished—leaving half of each plate untouched—glared at Hongdou, and retreated to the bedroom. Qinggua dove into the chair and wolfed down the rest.
Helping Hongdou stack the dishes afterward, Qinggua fished for an opening. "Hongdou, what do you think of me?"
Packing empty bowls into the carrier, Hongdou shrugged. "So-so."
"What does so-so mean?"
"Not bad, not great."
Unsatisfied, Qinggua pressed, "Do you like a not-bad, not-great guy like me?"
Blunt as he was, Hongdou did not even blush since she felt nothing for him. "What's rattling around in that head of yours all day, Qinggua? Plenty of maids in Chen Manor might take a shine to you."
Handing her the cold teapot, Qinggua said, "I don't care about anyone else. I only care if you like me."
Holding the carrier in one hand and the pot in the other, Hongdou paused. "Like you..."
Qinggua's heart leaped.
"...or don't like you..."
His heart plummeted.
"...honestly, I have no idea."
Crestfallen yet stubborn, he trailed her to the door. "I'm a solid catch! Hang around me more and you'll see. Marry me, and nobody will spoil their wife better."
Hongdou laughed. "Since you're such a prize, I'll advertise for you around Moxiang Courtyard—and if nobody bites here, across all of Chen Manor. Bound to find you a wife!"
Before Qinggua could blink, the door opened, shut, and padlocked from outside.
Qinggua pressed against the door calling, "Hongdou, be my wife, okay?"
No answer came from outside—only a mocking voice from behind. "Got any shame left? She just turned you down flat and you're still groveling? I'm embarrassed for you!"
Qinggua spun around. "Stop sneaking up on me like a ghost, Young Master! Nearly gave me a heart attack!"
"Daring to talk back? Tired of working for me?"
Stuck inside with hours to kill, Chen Haoyu sat by the table. "Come sit. Let's chat."
Flattered, Qinggua hopped onto a stool. "What about, Young Master?"
"Chasing Hongdou like that won't get you anywhere."
"Teach me how, Young Master!"
"Know why girls flock to me?"
That stumped Qinggua; he racked his memory. "Young Master, I've never seen a girl genuinely like you—all I remember is you snatching country maidens to serve as maids, like all the girls who used to be in this yard, and in the other Chen houses..."
Chen Haoyu raised a fist. "Talk more garbage and taste my knuckles."
Qinggua ducked back. "Just stating facts!"
Chen Haoyu lowered his fist. "Sure, I got reckless before, yet I haven't pulled anything like that in over half a year. Can't a guy turn over a new leaf?"
"True enough—since last year you've stuck to Chunxiang Brothel. Must be nicer girls there. Got a sweetheart inside?"
Chun Jinmo crossed Chen Haoyu's mind. "Sort of. Hey, we're talking about you—how did we get onto me?"
"You asked why girls flock to you! Far as I see, girls only flock to you for your silver."
"Bingo! At last you used your brain. That's why you need silver—flash money and Hongdou will throw herself at you without you lifting a finger."
Qinggua shook his head. "Wrong, Young Master. You're swimming in silver, and Young Madam still has zero interest—she even locked you up! Besides, a girl hooked on silver isn't genuine. Even if I had silver, I'd pretend to be broke so I'd know Hongdou liked me for real."
Those blunt words stung Chen Haoyu in an unexpected spot. Deep down he knew every country maid he had claimed and every courtesan who smiled at him bent to his silver—maybe that was why he had never truly loved anyone. Bought affection held no thrill; life was just dull, so he killed time with what silver could buy.
Seeing his master fall mute, Qinggua winced. "Did I put my foot in it again? Mad at me, Young Master?"
To his surprise, Chen Haoyu spoke with strange calm. "Looks like you know love better than I do. Forget my advice—chase Hongdou your own way. Still, anyone can see she isn't into you. Don't waste your heart."
"Thanks for the warning, Young Master, yet today was just warming up! Once we're out, I'll pull out every stop—Hongdou will be mine sooner or later!" Qinggua beamed with confidence.
Leaving him to his optimism, Chen Haoyu returned to the real problem: escaping. Night had fallen, yet neither Grandmother nor his parents had appeared. Had Zhu Shuzhen hidden him? No—a maid from Old Madam Xia's courtyard had seen him hauled in hog-tied! Grandmother should have stormed over hours ago.
"Qinggua, why hasn't Grandmother come to rescue me?"
"Maybe Old Madam doesn't know you're locked in here."
"Impossible—her maid saw me dragged in! Usually Grandmother would be banging down the door by now. Did something happen while I was away?"
Qinggua scratched his head. "Actually, huge things happened."
"What things?"
"While you were gone, Young Madam hired a storyteller to come every single day and spin tales for Old Madam Xia—kept her laughing nonstop. Today she even brought an old blind drummer, and Old Madam was so thrilled she ate extra bowls of rice! And the biggest thing—"
"What's the biggest thing?!" Chen Haoyu tensed.
"Young Madam smoothed things out between Old Madam Xia and Master and Madam! Now Second Master, Third Master, and their wives visit Old Madam Xia every single day too. Maids from her yard say the place buzzes with laughter now, and Old Madam, Master, and Madam can't stop praising Second Young Madam!"
Chen Haoyu slammed a fist onto the table. "Sneaky! Beyond sneaky! Buying off my entire family behind my back—no wonder nobody came to save me! Did a fancy new granddaughter-in-law make Grandmother stop spoiling me, and Mother stop caring?!"
Qinggua snickered under his breath.
"I'm fuming and you're snickering? Asking for a beating?"
Qinggua jumped clear, which somehow broke Chen Haoyu into a laugh. "Relax, just messing with you. Sit back down—I'm bored."
Sliding back onto the stool, Qinggua grinned. "Don't be mad, Young Master. I only laughed because for the first time ever, you just called Young Madam a 'good granddaughter-in-law and good daughter-in-law'!"
"Use your ears! Was that a compliment? Quit yapping and help me figure a way out. Wait—got it! Put that face of yours to work: seduce one of Zhu Shuzhen's maids so she unlocks the door and sneaks me out. Skip Kuqiao and Hongdou—there are two other maids, plain-looking, bound to bite the second you flirt!"
Qinggua pulled a face. "My looks don't hold a candle to yours, Young Master, and I have zero interest in those two maids—besides, Young Madam's maids are tough nuts."
"What, expecting me to seduce them myself?"
"If you tried, Young Master, guaranteed success!"
Chen Haoyu raised a palm. "Want a smack?"
Qinggua ducked with a grin. "Heh, my looks are too plain, Young Master."
Lowering his hand, Chen Haoyu dangled bait. "Put in a little charm now, and once we're out, I'll help you land Hongdou."
Qinggua's eyes lit up. "Swear it? No lying!"
"A gentleman's word stands solid as a four-horse chariot!"
"Deal! I'll sacrifice myself for you, Young Master."
"Now you're talking!"
#CH 227
#TITLE: Using Discipline as Cover for Revenge
Having dragged Chen Haoyu home in ropes from Chunxiang Brothel, Qianli Xun feared zero backlash from the Chen elders. Part of her even hoped they would storm over so she could ask them straight out why they had pushed this marriage knowing Chen Haoyu started the rumors.
Yet night fell without a shadow from any elder—even though Old Madam Xia's maid had witnessed everything. Unable to fathom their silence, Qianli Xun let it go.
With the culprit locked away, her white-hot fury cooled into a rare, heavy ache. Unable to focus on her huaben, she sat at her desk reliving the darkest stretch of her life in this era—the citywide slander, the silent tears, the crushing sense that every road forward had dead-ended. Chen Haoyu had engineered every bit of it, and she had ended up married to him. Thank heavens they had never consummated the marriage, or regret would have eaten her alive.
Memories of those dark weeks brought back the people who had carried her through: her family, Mengrong, and Shen Jianchen.
Her family's warmth had kept her standing. Zhu Xiyan never visited Wangyue Pavilion, yet without his nod her mother, brother, and sister-in-law could never have stepped out of Zhu Manor. Harsh on the surface, her father loved her in his own clumsy way, and arranging the Chen match was his idea of fixing things. Matron Wei had stopped her from confronting him, and now the urge was gone; yelling at Zhu Xiyan would not turn back the clock.
During that dark winter, Mengrong had visited Wangyue Pavilion two or three times—few visits, yet proof the world had not thrown her away, someone willing to sit beside the brazier and share secrets. That was when Qianli Xun had vowed to count Mengrong her best friend for life.
Later, learning Prince Yi was Shen Jianchen explained everything—the gifts, the treats, waiting outside Wangyue Pavilion in his carriage while Mengrong visited. A debt of feeling she could never repay in this lifetime. Because of Mengrong, she had turned him down flat; yet she could not deny that having an imperial prince see her worth while the whole city spat on her name had rebuilt her spine—a real-life knight riding in when she hit rock bottom.
"Kuqiao, go fetch that gift Prince Yi sent to Wangyue Pavilion last year."
Kuqiao racked her brain. "Miss, I don't remember Prince Yi sending a gift."
"A peeing clay boy."
Light dawned on Kuqiao's face. "Oh, right! That bare-bottomed clay doll! What do you want it for, Miss?"
"Less talk, go find it."
Kuqiao tried recalling where she had tucked it—her mistress had glanced at it once and had it put away, never asking since, though it might have been packed in the move to Chen Manor. "I'll check the storage room. Everything you don't use often goes in there."
Left alone, feeling hollow and restless, Qianli Xun spread a sheet of paper and brushed out a quatrain:
"How many springs have come and gone before, / Yet none brought half the bitterness of this year. / Lonely moon perched on the crabapple bough, / Shining down on a clear night—what am I to do?" —"Ten Miscellaneous Spring Poems, No. 1" [TN: Translator's rendering]
As she set her brush down, Kuqiao returned cradling a wooden box and placed it beside her. "Took some digging, yet I found it."
Kuqiao lifted the fresh sheet and blew on the damp ink. "I'll store this away for next time Nan Shuang or Huayu stops by."
The character for "bitterness" and "hate" jumped out at her. "Do you hate Young Master, Miss?"
Drawing the box close, Qianli Xun lifted out the bare-bottomed peeing figurine, and a genuine smile broke across her face—the cheeky little doll made smiling impossible to resist. "Hate him? Of course I hate him. He put me through hell."
Blowing again on the ink, Kuqiao relaxed at seeing her mistress smile; she worried less for Chen Haoyu than for her mistress carrying venom into a second marriage. "Long as you're smiling, Miss, I'm glad."
Once the ink dried, Kuqiao put the poem away, noting her mistress's eyes still fixed on the clay doll. Remembering the clay figurine Bai Feng had given her, Kuqiao murmured, "Wonder when Bai Feng and Prince Yi are getting back to Lin'an?"
That poked straight at Qianli Xun's own tangled wish—longing for Shen Jianchen to return yet dreading facing Mengrong. "I'd rather they stay in Bianliang and never come back."
Catching her meaning and eager to steer away from the wedding raid, Kuqiao changed track. "Miss, are you really keeping Young Master locked up forever?"
Setting the doll back inside its box, Qianli Xun closed the lid. "Locked up for now. Haven't decided how long."
Unexpected tears welled up in Kuqiao's eyes, and she started sniffling.
Qianli Xun glanced over. "Why are you crying all of a sudden?"
"I'm heartbroken for you, Miss!" Kuqiao sobbed. "Your first marriage was misery, you fought so hard for a mutual divorce, and now you're married to the very man who spread your rumors! How are you supposed to live like this? Waaah..."
Her tears pricked Qianli Xun's own ache. Without crying, she spoke low and flat. "Chen Haoyu is going to pay."
"He's your husband now, Miss!" Kuqiao wept on. "To outsiders, you're one household—rising together, sinking together! If he pays a heavy price, it splashes right back onto you. I don't know what you're supposed to do! Waaah..."
"Quit crying, you're giving me a headache." Qianli Xun handed her the box. "Set this on the shelf where I can grab it anytime."
Wiping her cheeks, Kuqiao tucked the box onto the shelf.
"Go get some rest. I want to sit alone for a bit."
Obeying, Kuqiao withdrew to Yuening Room.
Finding the hall stuffy, Qianli Xun stepped into the courtyard and walked to the pond's edge. Young lotus leaves floated small across the dark surface; under moonlight, the water held only silver reflection and ink-black shadow.
Kuqiao's warning—"rising together, sinking together"—was plain truth. Hate Chen Haoyu as she did, marrying him had been her own choice. Exhausted, bowing to fate, or trying to give Mengrong back her brother, she had come into Chen Manor intending for it to be her final stop, never once contemplating a second divorce. Hearing Chen Haoyu threaten to repudiate her today had stung not from fear of divorce, yet from how jarring the words sounded.
How could she vent her fury while still protecting the home she meant to keep?
Then the elders' words clicked: they had begged her to discipline him! A cool smirk tugged at her mouth. "Then I'll take revenge under the banner of discipline. Hope you never reform, so I can discipline you for life—and if you actually do turn decent, I become Chen Manor's savior with a rock-solid seat in this house!"
Trying to picture loudmouthed Chen Haoyu reformed—like Wenyuan or Shen Jianchen—made her chuckle aloud. With her plan clear, her mood lifted. Tomorrow she would pay the elders a formal visit to state her terms on disciplining him, assuring them while warning them not to meddle in her payback—er, discipline.
Inside Yuening Room, Kuqiao watched her mistress's silhouette through the window, sighed, latched the shutters, and told Hongdou, "I'm terrified Miss is going to end up divorcing again."
Lying awake on the second maid's bed, Hongdou shook her head. "Relax, Sister Kuqiao. Miss gets along great with the Chen elders; they'd never let her go."
Sitting on the edge of Hongdou's bed, Kuqiao fretted. "Young Master spread those rumors, so Miss won't go easy on him. Yet he's Old Madam Xia's apple of her eye, and First Madam dotes on her son. Fond as they are of Miss, blood runs thicker than water."
Hongdou rolled over. "Quit borrowing trouble. Matron Wei isn't sweating—why are you?"
True enough: Matron Wei had stepped out once after the groom got locked up and stayed serene ever since. Relaxing, Kuqiao asked, "Did Young Master curse Miss when you brought dinner?"
Hongdou rolled back. "Nonstop! Swear those two were sworn enemies in a past life dragged into one bed this time. Wonder which one wins?"
"Need you ask?" Kuqiao crowed, forgetting her worry. "Miss will mop the floor with him!"
Now Hongdou turned thoughtful. "What's the fun in husband and wife fighting forever? I want Miss happy with a good husband. Eldest Master and First Madam are such wonderful people—how did their son turn out nothing like his father? Imagine if Young Master treated Miss half as well as Eldest Master treats First Madam."
Yawning, Kuqiao blew out the candle, shed her outer jacket, and climbed into bed. "Worrying won't fix it. All we can do is pray Young Master straightens out fast so Miss gets a good life."
That night, when Chen Jianglin returned from the tea shop, Yao Qingyan recounted every event of the day.
"Locking him up was overdue!" Chen Jianglin cheered. "I wanted to do it years ago, except you and Mother kept shielding him."
Helping him out of his outer robe, Yao Qingyan confessed, "When I first heard, Mother and I panicked. Good thing Matron Wei came by to reassure us—she told us Shuzhen found out Haoyu spread those rumors, and that's why she locked him up."
Sitting on the edge of the bed, Chen Jianglin sighed. "Paper can't wrap fire—Shuzhen was bound to find out. Better now than later. After a stunt that dirty, locking him up is getting off light; he deserves a sound whipping."
When Yao Qingyan bent to remove his shoes, he waved her off. "I'll get them. Climb into bed and rest, Wife."
Removing her hairpins at the vanity, Yao Qingyan undressed, blew out the lamp, and slid under the quilt. "I'm more scared of her fists than a whip. What if she cripples him?"
"Put your heart at ease. Tough as her fists are, has she thrown one punch since crossing our gate? No—she's polite, sharp, and thoughtful, and transformed the whole household in days."
"So she brought us good fortune?"
"No question! Looking back, her divorce from Lin Jue and the fallen-through Qiao match were Heaven saving her straight for the Chen family! Hahaha!"
"Can't agree with you there," Yao Qingyan teased. "The Zhu-Chen match only happened because of Haoyu's rumors."
"Which means fate rigged it so Haoyu won himself a marvelous wife! Hahaha!"
Half unconvinced yet cheered by her husband's optimism, Yao Qingyan sent up a silent prayer that Shuzhen and Haoyu would thaw toward each other.
#CH 228
#TITLE: One Branch Frets While Another Laughs
Where one branch worried, another laughed. Inside Chen Jiangshu's quarters, all three beamed.
"Hahaha! With Haoyu locked down, his wild days are over!" Chen Haodong crowed. "About time—why should I break my back earning silver while he burns through it doing nothing? That tigress paid off big."
"Great news indeed," Chen Jiangshu mused, "yet it puzzles me why Old Madam Xia and First Sister-in-law haven't lifted a finger. Don't they know?"
"Of course they know!" Madam Bao said. "I was sitting right there when a maid ran in reporting it—you should have seen their faces!"
"Then why didn't they charge over to stop it? Nothing like their usual selves."
"Bet the Zhu girl's fists scared them off."
Chen Jiangshu shook his head. "Mother has weathered real storms—she wouldn't flinch at a young bride. Remember when you and Third Sister-in-law riled her up to march over? She marched right over without fearing any fists."
"Then I'm stumped," Madam Bao admitted.
"My guess," Chen Haodong offered, "is since the Zhu girl just smoothed things over between Grandmother and the elders, Grandmother and First Aunt held back to save her face. Better they don't meddle—if the Zhu girl got pressured into releasing Haoyu, my whole scheme would flop."
"Fair point," Chen Jiangshu nodded. "Let's just hope they don't lose their nerve tomorrow."
"Even if they try, they won't stop her," Madam Bao scoffed. "That girl's tongue is deadlier than her fists. When Grandmother marched in to scold her, she twisted three clear faults until we couldn't find a single flaw and almost agreed with her! Fearless creature. Now that she knows Haoyu ruined her name, not even Old Madam Xia and First Sister-in-law could hold her back."
Both father and son chuckled at Madam Bao's breakdown.
"Spot on, Wife," Chen Jiangshu praised. "Never again will I say women have long hair and short sight."
"Mother grew up a refined scholar's daughter—of course she reads situations sharp as a blade," Chen Haodong added.
Praised by the two men who mattered most in her world, Madam Bao glowed.
With night deepening, Chen Haodong bid his parents goodnight and headed back to his own courtyard. Buoyed by his triumph, desire stirred in him—too late to bother heading out to Chun Jinchan.
Glancing at Ye Anya's dark room, he bristled at finding she had gone to bed without waiting up for him.
He rapped hard on the door. Knock, knock, knock!
Lying awake inside after sending Xiaocui to bed, Ye Anya knew who it was and pulled the quilt over her head without stirring.
Knock, knock, knock! Silence answered. Snapping in fury, Chen Haodong kicked the door open, stormed past the screen in the dark, and yanked Ye Anya upright out of bed. "Why didn't you open the door?!"
Numbed by too many beatings, Ye Anya felt no fear. "Don't you know? Why ask?"
SMACK! His palm cracked across her face. "You're my wife—your duty is waiting up and tending me to bed, not crawling under the covers alone like I don't exist! Show me half a scrap of warmth and I wouldn't hit you!"
Ye Anya gave a bitter laugh. "Before we even wed, I heard you were messing around with brothel courtesans. Looking at you turns my stomach—why would I wait on you?"
He shoved her back onto the mattress and pinned her down. She did not fight back, just turned her head away with an icy stare that sent a chill off her skin in the moonlight.
"I'm a man—what's wrong with playing around with a few women? Learn from Lin Jue's wife: gentle, sensible, even dipped into her own silver to buy Chun Jinqiao's freedom—"
PTUI! Spittle hit his cheek. "Want me like that? Wait for your next life—no, not even then!"
Wiping his cheek with his sleeve, Chen Haodong snarled, "The icier you act, the more I want to take you. I'm in a good mood tonight, so I'll go easy."
Shutting her eyes, Ye Anya endured while he took his pleasure. Not one joyful night since her wedding; when would this hell end, and when could she belong to the man she loved? Thoughts of Shuzhen rose—brazen enough to haul Haoyu out of a brothel and padlock him indoors. Tomorrow she would go talk to her.
Over in Third Master Chen Jiangmu's room, husband and wife chatted as they readied for bed.
Removing her hairpins at the vanity, Madam Cui sighed. "Eldest Brother and Sister-in-law never should have made this match for Haoyu. Look at the poor boy suffering now."
Sitting with his feet soaking in a basin of hot water poured by a maid, Chen Jiangmu shrugged. "You know why—Prefect Zhu showed up at the door, leaving Eldest Brother zero choice. Done is done."
Setting her pins in the box, Madam Cui crouched beside the basin and washed her husband's feet with both hands. "Still blows my mind Haoyu spread those rumors last year. Why would he even target the Zhu girl when they never crossed paths?"
Eyes closed as he enjoyed her massage, Chen Jiangmu murmured, "Haoyu roams outside day and night—who knows what scrapes he gets into?"
"Thank heavens our Haofei has sense," Madam Cui said, splashing warm water over his ankles. "Never gave me a day of grief, nose buried in his books."
"I'd rather he learn family trade, though his heart is set on study."
Finishing up, Madam Cui rose and dried her hands on a towel handed by a maid while another maid brought a towel for Chen Jiangmu's feet. Once the maids withdrew, they climbed into bed and doused the lamp.
"Haofei's two older cousins each hold strong cards—one charms Old Madam Xia, the other runs circles in business," Madam Cui sighed in the dark. "Competing head-on isn't in your blood or Haofei's. Taking the imperial exams opens a brand-new road. Merchants always rank below officials; if Haofei wins an appointment, we become an official's parents—real prestige."
Rolling onto his side facing away, Chen Jiangmu muttered, "True enough. That's why I back him even if it isn't my dream."
"Who do you think will end up inheriting the Chen fortune?"
Chen Jiangmu yawned. "Count Haofei out."
"I mean between Haodong and Haoyu—who do you want?"
"Isn't it obvious?" he mumbled.
"You mean Haodong?" Hearing only snores in reply, Madam Cui whispered to the ceiling, "Right now, Haodong looks like a sure thing."
At dawn, Chen Haodong headed straight out to the silk shop, leaving Ye Anya breathing free—she wished he would stay gone forever, roving outside like Haoyu. Too restless to sleep in, she ate a quick breakfast and walked over to Moxiang Courtyard with Xiaocui.
Having worked out her "revenge via discipline" plan the night before, Qianli Xun was heading out to declare her stance to the elders when she spotted Ye Anya at the courtyard gate.
"First Sister-in-law! Early visit means something important—my errands can wait. Come on in and talk!"
Admiration flickered in Ye Anya's eyes at Shuzhen's resilience. Storming a brothel in fury yesterday, glowing bright and unbothered this morning—how did a woman this spirited write such aching, wistful poetry? Maybe pouring sorrow onto paper kept her soul sunlit.
"Am I catching you at a bad time?"
Qianli Xun linked arms and led her inside. "Never a bad time for you, First Sister-in-law."
"Then let me sit inside and speak from the heart."
Sensing private matters ahead, Qianli Xun guided her straight into the inner chamber, where a woven rug supported a low square tea table flanked by low wooden stools—almost like sitting on the floor. Without needing to be told, Kuqiao began whisking tea in the outer hall.
Seated, Ye Anya opened with yesterday's news. "Heard you locked Haoyu up. Such nerve—aren't you afraid Grandmother, Eldest Uncle, and First Aunt will scold you?"
"If you heard, they certainly heard too—and not one of them has come knocking," Qianli Xun remarked. "Either their consciences are guilty, or they secretly approve."
Ignoring the elders' motives, Ye Anya sighed in admiration. "You're fearless and sharp, doing whatever you set your mind to. I envy you so much."
"Haven't you heard folks call me a tigress behind my back?" Qianli Xun joked.
"Whatever they mean by it, I take it as high praise," Ye Anya smiled. "How many women under heaven dare haul their husband out of a brothel in ropes and lock him up? That takes real spine."
"You're the only soul in Chen Manor who sees it that way."
Ye Anya paused, gathering her nerve. "Shuzhen, I meant to ask your advice last time, yet felt too shy on our first visit. Today I'm swallowing my pride to ask outright—please guide me."
Remembering the scene beneath the Divine Willow, Qianli Xun kept her tone careful. "No need for formality. Speak straight, First Sister-in-law."
Ye Anya took a breath. "You went through a mutual divorce once. Could you tell me how you managed it?"
Just then Kuqiao walked in carrying two bowls of whisked tea, catching the question—and knowing at once from the willow encounter this was no idle curiosity. Too late to retreat, she set the tea bowls down with stiff composure.
"Wait in the outer hall, Kuqiao," Qianli Xun instructed, "and keep everyone out."
At Ye Anya's nod, Xiaocui stepped out behind Kuqiao.
Qianli Xun studied the desperate hope in Ye Anya's eyes. She had no desire to recklessly blow up someone else's marriage without knowing the whole truth. "A few days ago, I went out to the Divine Willow outside the city—and stumbled onto an unexpected sight."
Catching her meaning, Ye Anya dropped all pretense. "Since you saw us, you know why I'm asking about mutual divorce."
"How long has this been going on?"
"Before I ever married into the Chen family, we loved each other. Yet the Ye and Cao families have feuded for generations, so my father blocked us and betrothed me to the Chens. For a stretch I tried accepting my fate—until the very day before our wedding, when Xiaocui heard Chen Haodong was consorting with a courtesan. Disgust took root in my bones, and I haven't stopped loathing him for a single day."
Rolling up her sleeve, Ye Anya revealed mottles of purple and blue bruises across her forearm. "Because I turn cold, whenever Chen Haodong wants... wants me, he uses his fists. My body is never without bruises. I can't endure another day like this, so I thought of mutual divorce—yet I don't know where to begin. Since you walked that road, I came to ask you."
Reaching across, Qianli Xun drew the sleeve back down over the bruised skin. "I didn't know you were enduring hell, First Sister-in-law. Are you certain you want to take the step of mutual divorce?"
Ye Anya nodded without hesitation. "My mind is iron. Otherwise I'd never have dared ask."
Knowing firsthand the gauntlet a Song woman faced to break a marriage, Qianli Xun looked at Ye Anya's fragile frame and worried she would get crushed. "Mutual divorce is brutal, First Sister-in-law. Think long and hard first."
#CH 229
#TITLE: Laying Out the Harsh Truth Upfront
Ye Anya drained her tea bowl in one gulp, dabbed her lips with a silk handkerchief, and met Shuzhen's eyes. "Don't worry for me, Younger Sister. If you truly wish me well, tell me how to end this marriage."
Thinking back over her own bruising path since arriving in the Song, Qianli Xun felt a sharp pang. Next to Ye Anya, she had been lucky—neither Lin Jue nor Chen Haoyu could lay a finger on her, whereas her sister-in-law bore Chen Haodong's fists in silence. She owed her the honest truth.
"In this era, mutual divorce is an uphill battle. I threw everything I had at it, and even then it only worked because Prince Yi stepped in to pressure my father and Lin Jue."
"Prince Yi helped? That tough?" Anxiety shadowed Ye Anya's face.
Qianli Xun took a sip of tea. "Yes. Sometimes I think if Prince Yi hadn't come to Lin'an, I might never have broken free of Lin Jue." Memories of Shen Jianchen drifted back—helping her the instant he arrived, pushing Qiao Manor to propose, helping squash the citywide rumors...
Noticing Shuzhen's silence, Ye Anya ventured, "Did Prince Yi already have feelings for you back then?"
After the wedding raid, the question was natural enough. Wanting to stay honest without sparking fresh gossip, Qianli Xun said, "You're asking because of the wedding raid. Whatever Prince Yi felt back then I couldn't say, yet nothing improper ever passed between us. Princess Jiahe was my closest friend—how could I betray her? What happened on my wedding day blindsided me too."
"Both of us are trapped women," Ye Anya sighed.
Steering off Prince Yi, Qianli Xun returned to the point. "If you truly want mutual divorce, First Sister-in-law, you must persuade Eldest Cousin and win consent from both sets of parents. If even one side refuses, it stalls dead."
Twisting her handkerchief in silence, Ye Anya sank into worry.
Looks like she'll back off, Qianli Xun thought.
Yet after a moment, Ye Anya lifted her head. "I'll find a way to persuade them one by one. If all else fails, I'll push Chen Haodong into repudiating me."
Remembering Kuqiao's warning from her earliest days in this world, Qianli Xun cut in sharp. "Do you have unmarried sisters at home?"
"Two younger sisters."
"Then never let your husband repudiate you!"
"I know being cast out ruins my sisters' marriage prospects, yet I cannot survive another year like this. Worst comes to worst, the Ye clan can disown me as their daughter."
Moved by the steel beneath her soft skin, Qianli Xun clasped her hands. "You're rarer than gold in this era, First Sister-in-law. Just swear one thing: plan every move before striking, and protect yourself first."
Ye Anya gripped her hands back. "Thank you, Shuzhen. Watching you gave me the nerve to fight for my own life."
Words failed Qianli Xun, haunted by a quiet fear that her modern influence might bring Ye Anya danger rather than rescue.
Seeing Ye Anya out beyond Moxiang Courtyard's gate, Qianli Xun whispered a silent wish: "Hope First Sister-in-law finds happiness." Why happiness rather than a successful divorce? Because whether the divorce succeeded or failed—whether she fled to the man she loved or stayed trapped fighting on—happiness was what she needed most.
Setting Ye Anya's struggle aside for the moment, Qianli Xun turned toward her own pending errand: Old Madam Xia's courtyard. Every morning after breakfast her parents-in-law sat there now, letting her address everyone in one sweep.
Voices floated from the hall as she entered the yard. When a maid moved to announce her, Qianli Xun raised a hand. "No need. I'll go right in." Unannounced, she would catch the elders' raw expressions before they could put on polite masks.
Recognizing Second Uncle's voice inside, Qianli Xun stepped boldly across the threshold. Conversation died on the spot.
Old Madam Xia, Yao Qingyan, and Chen Jianglin all greeted her with warm smiles—relieving her at once, though she had come braced to bring up the rumors regardless. Second Aunt and Third Aunt wore pinched smirks waiting for fireworks, proving household harmony remained skin-deep. Second Uncle and Third Uncle hid their feelings better, yet both flicked one glance at her and dropped their eyes—clear proof they knew Chen Haoyu was locked up.
"Shuzhen, come sit," Old Madam Xia welcomed her.
Instead of sitting, Qianli Xun dropped straight to her knees, Kuqiao kneeling right behind her.
"What are you kneeling for?" Old Madam Xia asked.
"Grandmother, yesterday I dragged Chen Haoyu home in ropes from a brothel and locked him in the back courtyard. I believe I did nothing wrong, yet fearing the elders might disagree, I kneel first to beg pardon."
Before Old Madam Xia could answer, Chen Jiangmu burst out, "If you know you did wrong, go unlock Haoyu right now instead of kneeling here for show—"
Old Madam Xia raised a hand, silencing her third son. "What wrong did you commit? Get up at once."
Rising with Kuqiao, Qianli Xun pressed on purpose, "Grandmother, Father-in-law, Mother-in-law—you truly don't blame me?"
"When did we ever blame you?" Chen Jianglin said. "We handed Haoyu's discipline to you. Handle him however you see fit."
"We heard yesterday and didn't lift a finger to stop you," Yao Qingyan added. "That proves we stand behind you. Discipline him your way."
"And I give you my word," Old Madam Xia chuckled. "While you whip Haoyu into shape, none of us three will drag your feet."
She had expected Chen Jianglin's backing, yet Old Madam Xia and Yao Qingyan's total hands-off blessing caught her off guard.
Chen Jiangshu and Madam Bao traded a glance, finding the elders' logic laughable. Catching her husband's cue, Madam Bao piped up, "Yesterday when Mother and First Sister-in-law heard Haoyu was tied up, they were frantic—how did you turn calm overnight? Oh, I remember! When I lingered outside yesterday, I saw Matron Wei walk in. She must have talked you round! That matron by Shuzhen's side is really something."
Whatever barb Madam Bao meant to plant, it cleared Qianli Xun's puzzle at once. Good old Matron Wei—clearing the minefield behind the scenes before she even thought to worry.
"Shuzhen isn't your daughter-in-law—stay out of it," Old Madam Xia snapped.
Madam Bao pursed her lips and fell mute, and Madam Cui swallowed whatever she had meant to add.
Old Madam Xia turned back with a warm smile. "Sit down now; why keep standing?"
Qianli Xun stayed on her feet. Since discipline was settled, she still meant to air the rumor business and get the acid off her chest. "I'd better keep standing, Grandmother, because what I say next might upset you."
Guessing right away, Old Madam Xia beat her to the punch. "About Haoyu spreading those rumors?"
"Yes."
"All water under the bridge. You're married in and we're one family now. No sense digging up old dirt."
Those smooth words—"one family"—nearly dulled her edge until Chen Haoyu's smug face flashed across her mind.
"I just want to know why," Qianli Xun pushed back. "Chen Haoyu ruined my name and destroyed my chance at happiness. Why did the elders still push this match—forcing two enemies into marriage? Isn't that shoving me into a pit?"
Her blunt volley landed like a cannonball—alarming some elders while delighting others watching the drama.
Chen Jianglin let out a heavy sigh. "We understand your resentment, Shuzhen. When Prefect Zhu marched in with Haoyu tied up and laid out what he'd done, I was furious and flustered. Prefect Zhu proposed the betrothal, and it sounded right at the time—Haoyu caused the mess, so Haoyu owed you responsibility."
"Plenty of ways to take responsibility! Why pick marriage? Shoving me into a fire pit while dressing it up as noble duty!"
Yao Qingyan rose and clasped Shuzhen's hands. "How is Chen Manor a fire pit? Have you suffered a single grievance or hardship since crossing our gate?"
Honestly? No—even Old Madam Xia's earlier scolding had been theater. Yet bitterness still churned in her gut. "Chen Manor is fine and the elders treat me well, except Chen Haoyu—we're oil and water, nowhere near the man I want."
"Then whip him into the man you want!" Yao Qingyan grinned. "Won't that be perfection?"
Old Madam Xia and Chen Jianglin burst out laughing.
Inside, Madam Bao sneered: Couldn't raise your own son, so you expect his bride to work miracles—what a joke!
Madam Cui snorted in her head: Never heard of a wife reforming a husband. If this Zhu girl pulls it off, I'll write my surname Cui upside down!
Chen Jiangmu found it absurd too, yet kept quiet seeing his eldest brother beaming.
Holding back no longer, Chen Jiangshu spoke up. "Mother, Eldest Brother, why not put Haoyu in our shops under my wing to learn trade? I can keep him in line—sounds better to outsiders than letting a brand-new bride discipline her husband. Tough as Shuzhen's fists are, fists alone don't build character."
Madam Bao knew her husband meant not one word of it; he was jabbing Eldest Brother's failed parenting and mocking their blind faith in Shuzhen.
"Shuzhen suits me fine," Old Madam Xia shut him down. "Discussion closed."
Having no real desire to babysit Haoyu, Chen Jiangshu yielded at once. "Whatever Mother deems best is best."
Old Madam Xia turned back to Shuzhen. "I know you hated marrying into this house, and learning Haoyu started those rumors boiled your blood all over again. Yet nobody held a blade to your throat to make you step into that bridal sedan. Maybe this really is your fate with Haoyu—a bitter tangle right now, yet Grandmother believes you've got the grit to turn a bad match into a golden one."
Still holding her hands, Yao Qingyan echoed, "Mother is right—bad fate can turn sweet. Put those rumors behind you, Shuzhen. Good years lie ahead. If anger still burns, use discipline as an outlet to blow off steam..."
Listening to them spin fantasies of reforming a rake and turning bitter fate into romance nearly made Qianli Xun laugh out loud. Seizing Yao Qingyan's own words, she laid her warning on the table.
"Since Mother-in-law called it blowing off steam, I'll hold you to that. From now on, disciplining Chen Haoyu is my way of venting. If I fail to mold him into the saint you all dream of, Grandmother, Father-in-law, and Mother-in-law, don't regret today's choice."
Chen Jiangshu gloated inside: Vent all you want—my son will cheer you on!
Madam Bao laughed up her sleeve: Smooth talk, First Sister-in-law—dug your own pit and jumped straight in!
Third Uncle and Third Aunt thought the new bride brazen beyond belief, yet held their tongues to watch the sparks fly.
Letting go of Shuzhen's hands, Yao Qingyan caught herself and winced. "I only said 'venting' as a figure of speech—don't take it literal!" Retreating to her chair, she shot an anxious look at Chen Jianglin.
Qianli Xun knew her words had cut sharp, yet harsh terms belonged upfront. She meant to torture Chen Haoyu for payback, not enroll him in moral finishing school; spelling it out now kept the Chen elders from blaming her later.
#CH 230
#TITLE: Qinggua Seduces Ugly Maid
Catching Yao Qingyan's panicked glance, Chen Jianglin knew she regretted her slip. Clearing his throat to steady his wife and put Shuzhen at ease, he spoke up. "Shuzhen has only been in our house a short while, yet she opened all three brothers' eyes to what Mother needed. That alone proves she has both a thoughtful mind and a kind heart."
"Kind heart" brought Matron Wei's assurance straight back to Yao Qingyan, and her shoulders dropped in relief. Shuzhen was decent at her core; she would never turn cruel.
"Where there's a will, there's a way," Chen Jianglin continued. "I trust you, Shuzhen. Even if you fail to reform him, I won't blame you or regret it. Either he turns around and we all celebrate, or he doesn't and I wash my hands of him—every child carves their own fate. All I ask is that once I'm gone, whoever leads the Chen clan leaves Haoyu a warm bowl of rice, and that you don't abandon him, Shuzhen."
Fair and heartfelt as his words were, Qianli Xun could not stay bitter at the elders; Chen Haoyu had spread the rumors, not his father.
Chen Jiangshu and Madam Bao lit up at their eldest brother's subtext: Eldest Brother had written Haoyu off as heir, Haofei wanted exams, leaving the Chen empire straight in Haodong's lap. Smug smiles curved both their lips.
Chen Jiangmu broke in at once. "What talk is that, Eldest Brother? With the Chen fortune, when would Haoyu ever scrape by on a single bowl of rice? Even if he roams wild his whole life, coming home means meat and fine dishes every day."
"Too right!" Madam Cui chimed in. "How could Mother and you two ever let Haoyu go hungry? You'll leave him a fat share, his cousins will look out for him, and worst comes to worst he has his wife—between her dowry and Haoyu's properties, Shuzhen ranks among the wealthiest brides in Lin'an! Haoyu won't lack a thing."
Watching her granddaughter-in-law's cool face, Old Madam Xia sensed she had zero real interest in reforming Haoyu and felt a dull ache. Irked by Third Uncle and Third Aunt's chatter, she snapped, "Enough! I'm not dead yet, and you're already planning Haoyu's funeral rations? A virtuous wife beats ten thousand acres of fertile land. Haoyu earned blessings in ten past lives to marry Shuzhen—with a wife like her, why worry about his future?"
Virtuous wife? Qianli Xun mused inside. Stuck with a grudge against Chen Haoyu, this virtuous wife is stuck playing the neighborhood tigress!
Virtuous wife my foot—a roaring tigress! Madam Bao fumed silently.
Madam Cui chuckled in her head: Pretty as a peach blossom on the outside, yet swinging iron fists and hog-tying her husband—Old Madam's bar for "virtuous" sits in the dirt!
"Shuzhen," Old Madam Xia went on, "if you're satisfied with your in-laws and this old woman, put Haoyu's old rumors behind you. Good or bad, yesterday is gone; look forward. Focus on disciplining Haoyu—skip daily morning greetings, this big family isn't short one face, and stop worrying about entertaining me since the storyteller already knows the path here every afternoon. Handle Haoyu however you like without reporting to us. Run along now."
Old Madam Xia dismissed her before bitterness could spill further and hand Second Aunt and Third Aunt fresh gossip; loyal as those two were to their own husbands, both had narrow hearts that feasted on others' woes.
Qianli Xun curtsied and walked out. Along the path home, she felt the trip had been a wash: Matron Wei had already settled the elders, yet the knot in her chest remained untied. Best to skip morning calls for a few days until her temper cooled so she would not snap at kind elders. Time to dream up proper ways to torture Chen Haoyu under the cover of discipline.
Meanwhile, back in Boya Study, Hongdou had delivered breakfast first thing. Once they finished eating, Chen Haoyu shot Qinggua a meaningful look.
Taking his cue, Qinggua sidled over as Hongdou stacked the bowls. "Hey, could you send Ugly Maid over for me in a bit?"
"What do you want Ugly Maid for?"
"Don't get the wrong idea—I'm not sweet on her, just have something to tell her."
Long aware that Ugly Maid had a massive crush on Qinggua, Hongdou jumped at the chance to steer him off her own back. "Hang tight, I'll send her over. She can't go inside, though—talk through the window."
"Window's fine!" Qinggua saw her to the door until the padlock snapped shut.
"Why pick Ugly Maid?" Chen Haoyu asked.
Qinggua spun back. "Your mission is tough, Young Master—Ugly Maid is my best shot. One listen to that name tells you she's plain, way easier to charm."
"What's the other maid called?"
"Amei."
"Amei—means pretty, right? Must be a looker."
"Average, nowhere near Hongdou. She's Asheng's younger sister."
"Brother and sister both slaving for Zhu Shuzhen—hopeless."
Qinggua pushed back. "Born rich, Young Master, you don't know what poor families live through. Landing a job in a wealthy manor makes poor folks cry with joy—and serving a fair mistress like Young Madam who even teaches brother and sister martial arts? Everybody envies them."
"Shoo, shoo! Quit praising Zhu Shuzhen in front of me! You're my man—don't let her buy you off."
"Relax, Young Master, loyal to the bone!"
Right then Ugly Maid's voice floated through the shutter. "Qinggua? Sister Hongdou said you wanted me?"
Ugly Maid was not truly hideous—just plump with narrow, squinting eyes that looked less striking than the other maids, earning her the nickname.
"She's here—go turn on the charm!" Chen Haoyu whispered, settling into a chair to enjoy the show.
For his master—and for that promise to help land Hongdou—Qinggua steeled his stomach and pressed up to the shutter. "Ugly Maid, Young Madam locked me in here and I haven't seen you for eight or nine shichen! Asked Hongdou to call you just so I could hear your voice."
Chen Haoyu wrinkled his brow: Didn't know Qinggua could spin lies without blinking—better watch him later! Ugh, corny enough to curdle soup!
A shy flutter answered from outside. "I thought you had eyes for Sister Hongdou! Never guessed you felt that way about me... honestly, I like you too."
Qinggua froze stiff. Fake bait had hooked a real heart; he had never realized she carried a torch for him, leaving him tongue-tied.
Jumping up in excitement, Chen Haoyu hissed beside his ear, "Say something! She's hooked—this is a cakewalk!"
Prodded by his master, Qinggua stammered, "Then... we're two hearts beating as one..."
"Get to the point!" Chen Haoyu poked him.
"I'm dying to see you, yet I'm locked inside! Could you open the door for me?"
Ugly Maid hesitated. "I want to see you too, yet Miss locked you up. What if I beg her to let you out when she gets back?"
"No use—Young Madam won't budge! Heaven knows how long she'll keep me in here. When will I ever hold you? I miss you, Ugly Maid!"
"I miss you too!"
"I didn't even do anything wrong, and she locked me up keeping us apart..."
"Wait right there, Qinggua! I'll go swipe the key and let you out!"
Hearing her footsteps scurry away, master and servant slapped palms in triumph.
"So who sneaks out, Young Master—me or you?"
"Me, obviously! Let's see—should I run straight to Grandmother and my parents, or bolt outside the manor? Straight outside! Hide somewhere Zhu Shuzhen will never track me down—yes!"
Moments later, the padlock clicked open. Both men lunged for the door—only for Ugly Maid to slip inside and slam the wooden door shut behind her, cutting off every inch of escape.
Launching straight at Qinggua, she wrapped him in a bear hug. "Qinggua! I'm over the moon you like me too!"
Squirming inside her grip, Qinggua gritted his teeth for freedom's sake.
With the door shut from inside, Chen Haoyu crept over while Ugly Maid was distracted and reached for the latch—only for Ugly Maid to pivot, still hugging Qinggua, and block the door solid. "Going somewhere, Young Master?"
Impressed by the grit of Zhu Shuzhen's maids, Chen Haoyu tried bluffing. "Let me out, or I'll order Qinggua to dump you! He's my servant and obeys every word I say!"
Releasing the hug to clasp Qinggua's hand, Ugly Maid stood firm. "Save the threats, Young Master! Qinggua and I love each other—nobody can tear us apart!"
"Let me out and I'll give you my blessing to be together!"
"Don't need your blessing. I'm taking Qinggua out; you stay put inside."
Qinggua stepped in. "Let go a second, Ugly Maid—let me tell Young Master something."
She obeyed at once. Leaning to his master's ear, Qinggua whispered, "Hang tight, Young Master! Let me slip out first, then I'll bring help from outside to free you!"
Chen Haoyu nodded and waved at Ugly Maid. "Fine, take Qinggua. I'll stay here enjoying my locked-up vacation."
Watching a brief blade of sunlight flash through the open door before it clicked shut and the padlock rattled back into place, Chen Haoyu lunged up yelling, "Don't forget to find Old Madam Xia, Qinggua!"
"Count on me, Young Master!"
Outside, Ugly Maid clung to Qinggua's arm refusing to let go. Helpless, he nudged her. "Better put that key back before someone notices!"
She released him at last. "While Miss is out, go hide in the west pavilion and wait for me. I'll sneak the key back to Asheng in the West Courtyard!"
The second Ugly Maid scurried off, Qinggua bolted straight out of Moxiang Courtyard toward Old Madam Xia's rooms—ducking behind a garden rockery halfway when Qianli Xun and Kuqiao strolled past, then sprinting full speed once they cleared.
Back in Old Madam Xia's hall, the elders had dropped the tense talk and were chatting while waiting for the storyteller; all three brothers had cleared their morning business to stay and listen with their mother.
Bursting through the unguarded door, Qinggua threw himself face-down on the floor and squeezed out loud wails. "Old Madam! Save Young Master! Young Madam locked him up! Waaah!"
"Haoyu's wife went way too far!" Chen Jiangmu jumped in. "Mother, while we're all here, lead us over and make her unlock him!"
"Yes, Mother, go save Haoyu!" Madam Cui seconded.
Old Madam Xia lifted one hand to cut them off. "Quit bawling, Qinggua. Go back and tell Haoyu that from today on, his parents and I are washing our hands of everything inside his courtyard. Good or bad, he's on his own."
Qinggua's wails choked off mid-sob. Blinking in shock, he stammered, "You can't abandon him, Old Madam! Young Madam's fists are lethal—Young Master might not survive!"
Hiding their glee behind wooden faces, Chen Jiangshu and Madam Bao stayed silent—thrilled to leave Haoyu roasting.
Getting nowhere with Old Madam Xia, Qinggua crawled toward Chen Jianglin. "Master! He's your own flesh and blood—you can't stand by!"
"Tell Haoyu I'm thrilled he's locked up," Chen Jianglin said flat. "Why would I rescue him? He made his bed; now lie in it."
Qinggua swung toward Yao Qingyan. "Madam—"
Hardening her heart, Yao Qingyan cut him short. "Not another word! Haoyu's fate rests in his wife's hands. Stop pestering me with Moxiang Courtyard's business!"
"Servants!" Old Madam Xia called. Two attendants hurried in. "Escort Qinggua out."
Dragged past the courtyard gate just as the storyteller strolled up, Qinggua lingered until the clack of the gavel and laughter drifted over the wall, then let out a long sigh and slunk away.
#CH 231
#TITLE: The Torture Plan Begins
Returning from Old Madam Xia's courtyard, Qianli Xun stepped into Moxiang Courtyard just as Ugly Maid hurried past with pink, glowing cheeks.
"Miss," Ugly Maid curtsied in haste.
"Why all the rushing?"
Guilty, Ugly Maid stammered, "N-nothing, Miss—got chores, won't keep you!" and scampered off.
Qianli Xun blinked. "What's up with Ugly Maid today?"
"Looked scared you'd scold her," Kuqiao guessed.
"Nah, looks more like she's racing off to a secret tryst," Qianli Xun joked, dismissing it.
Reaching Suxin Thatched Hall, she turned her mind back to Chen Haoyu—time to launch payback. "Go grab the key to Boya Study."
While Kuqiao ran to the West Courtyard, Qianli Xun strolled into the back yard. Glancing at Jingyi Hall's shut door—Matron Wei must be out running errands again—she felt a surge of quiet gratitude for everything the matron handled behind the scenes. Then she faced Boya Study. Keeping Chen Haoyu cooped up forever solved nothing and gave zero satisfaction; better to sit down and spell out his daily torment.
Kuqiao returned with the key and unlocked the heavy padlock.
Inside, Chen Haoyu had been pacing the front hall waiting. Hearing the key turn, his chest leaped—Grandmother had come to set him free! He bounded to the doorway expecting Old Madam Xia's sympathetic face—only for Zhu Shuzhen and Kuqiao to step in alone.
He craned his neck past them. Empty yard.
Qianli Xun smirked. "Still waiting for the Chen elders to ride in on white horses? News flash: they handed full authority to discipline you straight to me—which gives me a free pass to put you through hell."
"Liar! Grandmother adores me and Mother's softhearted—they'd never hand me over to you!" Seeing the door standing open, he made a break for it.
Qianli Xun slid across the threshold. "Trying to bolt? Not a chance. Leave this door wide open all day—long as I'm standing here, you aren't taking one step past it."
Shaking a furious finger in her face, Chen Haoyu choked on rage before collapsing back into a chair. Catching his breath, he snapped, "Fine, spell it out—what will it take to let me out?"
"I came here today to let you out."
Suspicion narrowed his eyes. "You're turning generous?"
"Not even close." Turning to Kuqiao, she said, "Write down every word I say."
Kuqiao seated herself at the desk and spread a fresh sheet.
Qianli Xun faced Chen Haoyu. "Starting today, you can step out of Boya Study—yet you cannot set one foot outside Chen Manor."
"On what grounds?!"
"On the grounds that you can't beat me in a fight, and the Chen elders gave me full command."
"I don't buy your one-sided story!"
"Believe it or not, behave yourself and listen up."
Chen Haoyu clapped both hands over his ears. "Not listening! Not listening! Do your worst!"
Fed up with his whining, Qianli Xun darted forward and tapped two acupoints. He froze solid—mute and stiff as a statue, able only to glare daggers.
"Nice and quiet. Now let's go over your rules. First, your monthly allowance is cut to zero. Want spending money? Earn it yourself."
Unable to speak, Chen Haoyu clenched his jaw inside: Cutting off even my twenty taels?! Never earned a single copper in my whole life!
"Second, here is your wage sheet. One: jog ten laps around Chen Manor's main loop every day—ten wen. Two: memorize assigned passages from the Hundred Schools classics and classical poetry every day—thirty wen. Three: complete one manual labor chore every day—fifty wen. Four: apologize face-to-face to someone you bullied—one tael of silver per person."
Improvised on the spot—equal parts torment and character-building, every single item something Chen Haoyu loathed. She nodded in satisfaction. "Four rules for starters; I'll tack on more whenever inspiration strikes. Got all that, Kuqiao?"
Kuqiao laid down her brush. "Every word, Miss."
"Great. Get Chen Haoyu's thumbprint on it."
Frozen helpless, Chen Haoyu watched Zhu Shuzhen pry his fist open, mash his thumb into Kuqiao's red ink paste, and stamp it hard onto the paper, turning his face purple with trapped rage.
With the seal dry, Qianli Xun unblocked his acupoints.
He lunged at once swinging a wild punch. "Zhu Shuzhen! I'm not doing a single one of those!"
Qianli Xun caught his wrist and twisted his arm clean behind his back. "Glad you reminded me! Forgot the penalties. Skip one task, empty my chamber pot for one day. Skip two, two days. Skip all four, ten days straight. Keep resisting, and you empty my chamber pot for life!"
Wincing in pain, Chen Haoyu barked, "Chen Manor has clean latrines everywhere! Nobody uses chamber pots for heavy business—only urine jugs! Eat that!"
"Easy fix!" Qianli Xun grinned. "Just for you, I'll switch to a chamber pot for every single trip and stink you right out of your boots!"
Outmatched in fists and tongue alike, Chen Haoyu shifted tactics and went meek. "Look, Zhu Shuzhen, I'll apologize right now, okay? Let it go! Spreading rumors was wrong—hit me, curse me, just don't leave me crippled!"
Seeing him fold, Qianli Xun released his arm. "Kuqiao, go call Hongdou."
Jotting down the chamber-pot penalty on the signed sheet, Kuqiao hurried out.
Relieved the door was staying unlocked, Chen Haoyu slumped back into his chair. "Biggest mistake of my life was marrying you, Zhu Shuzhen. What about you—regret marrying me too?"
Since choosing to enter Chen Manor, Qianli Xun had banned regret from her vocabulary. "Whether I regret it is none of your damn business."
"Bet you regret it to your bones," he pushed. "Why not get a mutual divorce and set yourself free? Look how crazy Prince Yi is for you—man like that wouldn't blink if you divorced twice. Let's sit down like civilized folks and arrange a mutual divorce, yeah?"
The words "mutual divorce" pricked an unexpected ache in her chest. She had fought through one divorce hoping for peace, only to hear her second husband toss the same words right back. She had neither the heart nor the fight left for a second divorce.
Spotting that flicker of sorrow, Chen Haoyu lit up and teased, "Wait—did you fall for me? Can't bear to leave me? Makes sense! Tall, dashing, irresistible to every woman in Lin'an—of course you'd fall for me! Since you're smitten, quit torturing me and treat me sweet; maybe I'll take a shine to you too, heh!"
Snap—the gloom vanished in a flash of disgust. "Shut your filthy mouth! Want a divorce? Tough luck—I'm blocking it on purpose! Wait until I've tormented you to my heart's content and cooled off, then maybe I'll think about it."
Unfazed, he kept smirking. "Heard you moved heaven and earth to divorce Lin Jue, yet when I hand you divorce on a silver platter, you refuse? What else could it be except falling for me? I never turn away a beauty—why not throw yourself into my arms right now?"
Sleazy leering always tripped Qianli Xun's fist reflex. WHAM! One clean punch landed square on his left cheek.
Purple bloomed across his face at once. Clapping a hand over his eye, he yelped, "Are you crazy?!"
Qianli Xun shook out her knuckles. "You're the crazy one! Tease me with that sleazy face again and watch what happens!"
Sweat stung the swelling bruise, forcing his hand down. "Fierce like that—what on earth did Qiao Wenxian and Prince Yi ever see in you?!"
Hongdou walked back in behind Kuqiao, both biting back grins at the giant shiner ringing the young master's eye. Kuqiao collected the rules sheet while Hongdou asked, "What are your orders, Miss?"
"Assign two men right now to shadow Chen Haoyu all day and make sure he completes every task on this list."
"On it, Miss." Taking the sheet from Kuqiao, Hongdou hurried out to pick the watchers.
"Can I walk out now?" Chen Haoyu asked.
"Not until your babysitters get here."
So long as the door stayed unbolted, he could run straight to Grandmother and weep his case. Wait—where was Qinggua? He had slipped out hours ago! Why hadn't Grandmother stormed in? Had Zhu Shuzhen really bought off his whole family?
"Did Grandmother and my parents really put you in charge of disciplining me?"
"Every word," Qianli Xun said smugly. "Swore they wouldn't lift a finger to interfere."
"Don't buy it!"
"Suit yourself. Think I'd unlock your door if I were scared of you crying to the elders?"
Hongdou returned with Asheng and another male servant. "Miss, Asheng and Sanbao will watch Young Master from here on." Handing the list back to Kuqiao, she added, "Both memorized every line."
Pleased with the pair, Qianli Xun gave clear orders. "Shadow Young Master nonstop. Do not let him step outside Chen Manor—anywhere inside the grounds is fine. Daytime he roams free; once he goes to bed at night, lock the door again so he doesn't sneak out after dark."
"Yes, Miss!" both servants answered.
Turning to Chen Haoyu with a cool huff, she waved him off. "You're free to go."
Chen Haoyu bounded straight out the door. "Ah, the sweet air of freedom!" Spinning back, he jabbed a finger at her. "Just wait, Zhu Shuzhen—I'm heading straight to Grandmother!"
Asheng and Sanbao fell into step right on his heels.
Yet as payback rolled into motion, Qianli Xun felt zero triumph. Chen Haoyu's mention of divorce and Prince Yi had pulled Mengrong straight back into her chest—Mengrong's hatred on the wedding day, the exact reason she had surrendered to this marriage and refused to break it.
Returning to Suxin Thatched Hall, she sat staring blankly at her desk while Kuqiao stowed the rules sheet and stood quiet watch beside her.
#CH 232
#TITLE: No Rescue, Time to Run Laps
After striking out at Old Madam Xia's courtyard, Qinggua dared not show his face back in Moxiang Courtyard—and forgot his date with Ugly Maid completely—choosing instead to kill time wandering the gardens until nightfall.
Strolling past the west garden, he glanced up and spotted Ugly Maid waiting in the pavilion, jolting his memory. What a bust—failed to save Young Master and hooked myself on the line instead! Better bolt; stand her up and she'll take the hint.
Doubling back toward Moxiang Courtyard to lurk until dusk, he ducked behind the fresh bamboo flanking the gate—only to see his master stride right out seconds later with Asheng and Sanbao in tow.
Figuring his jailbreak was old news now, Qinggua popped out from behind the bamboo. "Young Master! Young Madam let you out!"
Blaming Qinggua for vanishing with zero rescue, Chen Haoyu swung a foot before remembering Phantom Sidestep and pulling back, raising his fists instead. "Sneak out and lounge around while leaving me locked up? Come here so I can pound you!"
Qinggua hopped clear. "You're out now, Young Master—why stay mad?"
"What good is being out with two shadows glued to my back?!"
Qinggua eyed Asheng and Sanbao with a grin. "Beats rotting behind locked shutters."
"Quit yapping and come with me to tattle to Grandmother!" Chen Haoyu strode off.
Qinggua jumped in his path. "Save the trip, Young Master! I already went! Old Madam Xia said she's washing her hands of your courtyard; Master said he's thrilled you're locked up and you made your own bed; Madam said your life is in Young Madam's hands and not to bother her again!"
Convinced Qinggua was spinning tall tales, Chen Haoyu shoved him aside and marched straight toward Old Madam Xia's courtyard.
Inside her hall, the storyteller had left along with Second and Third Uncles' families, leaving Chen Jianglin and Yao Qingyan chatting with Old Madam Xia when a maid hurried in. "Old Madam, Second Young Master is out and heading right this way!"
"Bolt the main gate," Old Madam Xia ordered, "and tell him to stop pestering me."
Noticing Yao Qingyan's stricken look, she added, "Lock your own courtyard gates when you get home too. Don't go soft—one weak moment ruins everything." Pressing a hand to her chest, she sighed, "My heart aches right here, yet for Haoyu's own good, we hold the line."
Yao Qingyan bit her lip and stayed silent.
"My failure raising him put you both in this bind," Chen Jianglin said. "Everything rides on this stretch—we harden our hearts together." Both women nodded.
Reaching his grandmother's bolted gate, Chen Haoyu barked at Qinggua to pound on it. No door swung wide; instead a maid called through the wood, "Go on back, Second Young Master. Old Madam is staying out of your affairs from now on."
"A servant talking back to me?! Watch me have Grandmother sell you off tomorrow!"
"I wouldn't dare, Young Master—Old Madam's exact words."
Switching gears on the spot, Chen Haoyu put on loud, theatrical wails. "Grandmother! Don't abandon me! That tigress let me out only to torture me worse—two goons shadowing me nonstop, endless chores, and she's making me empty her chamber pot! Waaah! If you don't save me, your grandson won't make it out alive! Waaah!"
At "empty her chamber pot," Yao Qingyan gasped. "How can Shuzhen make him do that?! Haoyu has never emptied his own washbasin in his life!"
Old Madam Xia surged half out of her chair. "No, that's too much!" Pausing, she sank back down with a groan. "Hold firm... maid, bring cotton wads and plug my ears!"
The maid stuffed cotton into her ears, though his wails still seeped through. Seeing the old woman hold fast, Yao Qingyan swallowed her protest.
Only Chen Jianglin stayed cool as stone. "No pain, no steel. Too much pampering turned Haoyu soft—left unchecked, he'd sink lower than a night-soil hauler. Emptying a chamber pot lets him off easy!"
