Hearing zero response inside, Chen Haoyu cranked up the drama. "Waaah! Grandmother! Zhu Shuzhen is out for blood! Yesterday she had Hongdou slap my face twice—still stinging! Waaah! Just now she punched my eye black and blue without even giving me salve, and cut my allowance to zero! Waaah!"
Wailing until his throat turned raw brought dead silence. Realization sank in: Grandmother was really not opening that gate.
Dropping the tears, he yelled, "If Grandmother won't stand up for me, I'll go find my mother!"
"Master and First Madam are right inside Old Madam's room," the maid called back. "They told me to tell you to head straight back and obey Second Young Madam."
Every last hope shattered. Chen Haoyu grasped at last what a sharp operator Zhu Shuzhen was—buying over his whole family in one sweep.
Asheng stepped forward. "Time to run your laps, Young Master. Skip them and it's chamber-pot duty."
Chen Haoyu threw a punch at Asheng's jaw. "A servant bossing me around?!"
Asheng blocked his wrist without breaking stride. "Save your breath, Young Master."
Spinning around, Chen Haoyu swung at Sanbao, who stepped clear with ease. "No use, Young Master."
Abandoned by his family and outmatched by two servants, Chen Haoyu swung his boot at Qinggua in blind fury—who dodged in panic and accidentally bumped his master's shoulder, sending Chen Haoyu staggering back.
"Qinggua! Tired of living—shoving your own master?!"
"Accident! Slipped, Young Master—don't take it to heart!"
Not take it to heart?! Chen Haoyu lunged to clobber him, only for Asheng to step between them. "Don't waste daylight, Young Master. Start running."
Qinggua sent up silent prayers of thanks.
Abandoned, outmatched, powerless—for the first time in his pampered life, Chen Haoyu felt utter helplessness and sank into a squat right on the flagstones.
Qinggua crept closer in concern. "You all right, Young Master?"
SMACK! Chen Haoyu slapped him across the cheek.
Clapping a hand to his face, Qinggua whimpered, "Picking on me again, Young Master!"
His pent-up steam vented in that single smack, Chen Haoyu pushed himself up. "Who else can I bully—those two?!"
Picturing a reeking chamber pot turned his stomach sour on the spot. A wise man bends before a storm; better just run the laps.
"Hey! Chen Manor's huge—where do I run?"
"I set the pace in front, Sanbao guards the rear, and you stay between us following me," Asheng explained.
Refusing to suffer alone, Chen Haoyu barked at Qinggua, "You! Run with me!"
"I hate running, Young Master—too tiring!"
"Look at them—not even my servants, and they're running! My own lackey acting like a coward? Move it, or forget my help landing Hongdou!"
For Hongdou, Qinggua bit the bullet. "If you're running, Young Master, I'm right beside you!"
Along Chen Manor's wide main drive, the absurd parade took off: Asheng pacing ahead, Sanbao bringing up the rear, Chen Haoyu and Qinggua puffing between them.
Passing servants froze, pointing and whispering, filling Chen Haoyu's chest with raw humiliation—though gasping for air left him zero breath to curse them out. Along the west lane near Xinglong Pavilion, clerks bolder than house servants grinned and jeered, "Taking up morning sprints, Second Young Master?"
Panting too hard to snap back, Chen Haoyu wheezed at Asheng, "Can... can we... take a breather?"
Without looking back, Asheng kept striding. "Not even one lap down and already whining? You've got ten to go—push through and your legs will loosen up."
"QINGGUA! FREEZE RIGHT THERE!"
A furious girl's roar stopped the entire squad dead in its tracks—blessed relief to Chen Haoyu's burning lungs.
Storming off the west path came Ugly Maid. After waiting in the pavilion until realizing Qinggua had played her like a fiddle, rage drove her out hunting answers, right into the jogging parade.
Her stormy glare cracked Chen Haoyu up. "You're toast, Qinggua."
"I only turned on the charm for you, Young Master!" Qinggua hissed. "Help me out here!"
"Wise man bends before a storm—sweet-talk her first!" Chen Haoyu whispered back.
Plastering on a sheepish grin, Qinggua trotted over. "Sorry to keep you waiting, Ugly Maid! I wanted to come to the pavilion, yet look—Young Madam released Young Master and ordered me to jog with him!"
Ugly Maid narrowed her eyes. "Really?"
"Would I lie? Ask Young Master!"
"You and Young Master breathe out the same nose—I'm not asking him! Sanbao, tell me straight: did Miss order Qinggua to jog?"
Sanbao told the plain truth. "Miss only ordered Young Master to jog. Young Master dragged Qinggua along."
Ugly Maid whirled on Qinggua, fists balled. "Lying to me again!"
"No, no! Whether Young Master or Young Madam gives an order, how can I say no?"
"And saying you liked me—was that a lie too?" Unbothered by the audience, Ugly Maid fired straight.
Chen Haoyu settled in with a grin; dull jogging had just turned into front-row theater. Asheng, who had worried Qinggua liked Hongdou, exhaled in relief.
Qinggua weighed his two futures fast: confess the lie and eat a bruising right here, or play along and stay stuck with Ugly Maid for life. One beating versus a whole lifetime—no contest!
Just as he opened his mouth to confess, Ugly Maid warned, "If you lied to me, I'll shadow you every waking day so you never marry anyone else—until you marry me! Run to the ends of the earth and I'll chase you there!"
Even I feel sorry for Qinggua now, Chen Haoyu winced inside.
"Ugly Maid's crazy about you, Qinggua—don't play games with her," Sanbao chimed in.
"Relax, Ugly Maid, Qinggua takes feelings serious," Asheng backed him up.
Weighing survival now against trouble later, Qinggua caved. "Every word came from my heart, Ugly Maid! Head back now—I've got to help Young Master finish his laps, or he gets stuck emptying Young Madam's chamber pot, and guess who'll end up carrying that bucket!"
Hearing him stand by his confession turned Ugly Maid pink with joy. Stopping herself from hugging him in front of onlookers, she beamed. "Fine, keep jogging with Young Master—I'll head back!" and dashed off shyly.
"Show's over, Young Master," Asheng called. "Back to running."
Sighing as his comic relief vanished, Chen Haoyu dragged his aching legs back into motion along Chen Manor's main loop.
#CH 233
#TITLE: Fighting Back Gets Nowhere
Chen Manor sprawled wide enough that three or four laps wrecked a man's lungs, let alone ten. Panting, muscles burning, hearts full of resentment, Chen Haoyu and Qinggua slowed to a trudging shuffle on the final two laps while Asheng and Sanbao kept pace at a brisk walk.
"Young Master," Qinggua gasped, "Young Madam only... made you run... let me sit down!"
"No... way!" Chen Haoyu wheezed. "Jogging alone... looks too pathetic... having you beside me... softens the blow."
Qinggua shut up and kept slogging.
Rounding a bend, Chen Haoyu looked up and spotted Chen Haodong standing dead center in the road wearing a wide smile.
Inside, Chen Haodong rejoiced: Watching you run laps like a hound is pure bliss! Time to stir the pot and blow your feud with that tigress sky-high!
Spotting his elder cousin like a drowning man spotting driftwood, Chen Haoyu found fresh strength, bolted forward, and threw his arms around him. "Brother Dong! I've been running forever and not a single Chen elder cares—only you have my back!"
Putting on a mask of deep concern, Chen Haodong patted his shoulder. "Heard what happened and ran straight to Grandmother, yet her gate was bolted tight, and Eldest Uncle's too. Nobody else dares cross Old Madam Xia, so I waited out here to help you brainstorm."
Asheng and Sanbao stopped respectfully to wait, giving Qinggua a blessed breather.
"Hurry, give me a plan!" Chen Haoyu begged, stepping back. "How do I dodge that tigress's punishments?"
Instead of answering right away, Chen Haodong eyed his swollen cheek. "What happened to your face?"
"The tigress punched me!"
Pound him black and blue! Chen Haodong cheered silently while saying aloud, "Hang on—let me give those two lackeys a piece of my mind."
Striding up to Asheng and Sanbao, Chen Haodong barked, "Blind dogs! Daring to bully Second Young Master Chen in broad daylight—who gave you the gall?! Wait till I tell Old Madam Xia and have you both sold to a country farm for good!"
When Sanbao moved to argue, Asheng checked him and answered even-voiced, "Eldest Young Master may not know, yet our mistress received approval from Old Madam Xia, First Madam, and Eldest Master to discipline Young Master, and assigned us to supervise."
Putting on a furious scowl, Chen Haodong waved them back. "Step aside and wait right here! My brother and I are going to sit in that pavilion. If Younger Sister-in-law has an issue, tell her to come see me!"
Linking arms with Chen Haoyu, he marched him toward the pavilion.
"Brother Dong, you're a legend!" Chen Haoyu flashed a thumbs-up.
"You're disgracing every Chen man alive," Chen Haodong tutted as they sat. "Let me teach you how to keep a wife in line."
Chen Haoyu sighed. "Think I want to lose face? Zhu Shuzhen's fists are monstrous, and her lackeys too—can't fight those two, can't outrun them, so I had to fold."
Chen Haodong leaned in to fan the flame. "Be a real man—never fold, fight back! Tough as Younger Sister-in-law is, she won't dare cripple you or put your life at risk. Use your brain: why did Grandmother and First Aunt wash their hands of it? Because they know for a fact she won't truly hurt you! So what are you scared of? Push right back!"
Light flared across Chen Haoyu's face. "Of course! How didn't I see that?! No wonder you're the smart one, Brother Dong, with a gentle, refined wife at home! Screw the last lap—I'm marching straight back to Moxiang Courtyard to defy Zhu Shuzhen to her face!"
"That's the spirit!" Chen Haodong beamed. Watching his pumped-up cousin swagger off, he chuckled inside: Go poke that hornet's nest—your big brother is grabbing a front-row seat!
Qinggua hurried up to meet him. "Rested up, Young Master? One lap left—I'll run it with you."
"Who said I'm running?!" Chen Haoyu spun on Asheng and Sanbao. "Listen up! I'm skipping the last lap and heading straight back to Moxiang Courtyard. Let's see what Zhu Shuzhen does about it!"
Unwilling to rough up a young master, Asheng and Sanbao trailed behind with wry sighs. "Skip the tasks and it's chamber-pot duty, Young Master," Asheng warned.
"Empty my foot! I'm not touching any pot—see what she does!"
Back beside him, Qinggua whispered, "What did Eldest Young Master say to turn you fearless overnight?"
"Pure gold!" Chen Haoyu grinned.
Back in Moxiang Courtyard, three maids stood lined up in a row. Chen Haoyu vaguely recognized them from Third Uncle's courtyard—he had pinched their cheeks once upon a time—yet brushed past without caring, heading toward the back yard until a maid stepped across his path.
"Young Master, Miss says once you finish jogging, apologize to these three maids, then memorize the Analects and Wang Wei's poems, then dust her bedroom."
Recalling Chen Haodong's tip that she dared not maim him, Chen Haoyu kept his swagger. "What's your name? Don't recognize you."
"Amei. I helped fight Master Jiang's thugs for you and went with Miss to haul you out of the brothel—you just never noticed me, spending all your nights outside since the wedding."
"Ah, Amei—Asheng's sister! Think you two siblings can boss me around? Forget it! Go tell Zhu Shuzhen I'm not scared of her, and I'm boycotting every single chore!"
Just as he pivoted for Boya Study, Qianli Xun's cool voice halted him. "So you're dying to empty my chamber pot, Chen Haoyu? Didn't realize you had such quirky hobbies."
He spun to face her. "Let me repeat myself: I'm not doing one chore you set, and I'm sure as hell not touching your chamber pot!"
Qianli Xun closed the gap in a flash and locked his arm behind his back. "Doing it or not?"
"Ow, ow! No means no! You won't cripple me and you won't kill me—what's left to fear?! Do your worst!"
Caught off guard that he had spotted her hard limit, Qianli Xun shoved him loose. "Not a copper in your pocket—don't you want to earn silver?"
Rubbing his shoulder, he smirked. "Stuck indoors with free food and bed—what do I need silver for? Keep it!"
"Then I'll lock you inside Moxiang Courtyard forever!"
Sensing he had her cornered, Chen Haoyu grinned wider. "Fine by me! I'll become a full-time homebody. Seen every sight, eaten every dish, had all the fun in Lin'an—never tried being a recluse before. Sounds great!"
Dead pigs do not fear boiling water, Qianli Xun thought, watching his smug grin. Then a lethal idea struck her.
"Refuse today's rules, and I'll have a wooden placard made reading 'I AM A GIANT SCUMBAG,' hang it around your neck, tie you up like a hog, and have my men parade you around every lane in Chen Manor—and then down the main streets of Lin'an every single day! Your pick: follow the list, or go on citywide parade?"
Chen Haoyu's hair nearly stood on end. "Y-you—what do you gain parading me through the streets?! I'm your husband on paper!"
The wilder he got, the brighter she smiled. "You said it—on paper! You lose face, not me! Long as I get even for last year's rumors, I'm thrilled! Did you think of your wife once while camping out at Chunxiang Brothel? Why should I care about my husband?"
Grasping for a comeback, he put on a teasing smirk. "Wait—did you fall for me? Man as dashing as me, totally natural..."
"Which ear heard me say I like you? I only like torturing you! Asheng, go fetch a wooden board!"
"Zhu Shuzhen! Pushing it too far, aren't you?!"
Stepping right into his face, she raised her knuckles. "Haven't even warmed up! Want another black eye?"
Brother Dong's advice had bombed in three rounds flat. Knowing Zhu Shuzhen always kept her threats—and imagining his face paraded down Dongren Street beneath that sign—Chen Haoyu waved the white flag. "Fine, fine, put the board away! I'll obey! I messed up spreading those rumors, so call it my debt to you."
"Why didn't you say so from the start? Amei, take Chen Haoyu to apologize to those three maids."
Grumbling inside—convinced Zhu Shuzhen was his mortal nemesis, and remembering Master Jiang's claim that Prefect Zhu framed him—he tossed over his shoulder, "Your father is a sly old fox, Zhu Shuzhen. Ruined my life."
Ignoring the nonsense, she snapped, "Less talk, start apologizing!"
Stopping before the three maids, Chen Haoyu looked them over with a scowl. "All I did was squeeze your hands and cheeks once—and I have to apologize? Level with me: how did the tigress dig you three up?"
One maid giggled. "Hongdou told us Second Young Master planned to apologize to every servant he'd ever bullied, so we came over curious to see it for ourselves!"
"You came for kicks while I suffer the indignity of apologizing to servants!"
"Apologize, Young Master," Amei reminded him.
"Busybody!" Glancing back at Zhu Shuzhen's icy glare, he choked out, "Sorry."
Never having heard a master apologize to a maid, all three burst out giggling.
"One doesn't cover three people—two more," Amei prompted.
"Sorry! Sorry!"
"Don't get handsy with maids again, Second Young Master," one teased, "or you'll run out of breath saying sorry!" The three skipped off thrilled.
Turning back, Chen Haoyu grunted, "Happy now, Zhu Shuzhen?"
"Just getting warmed up—nowhere near happy."
Watching with envious eyes, Qinggua stepped up to Qianli Xun. "Young Madam, can I get in line for an apology too?"
"Of course," Qianli Xun said. "He bullies you nonstop—owes you a mountain of apologies."
Qinggua beamed.
Hearing his own lackey volunteer for the line snapped Chen Haoyu's last nerve. He swung a ferocious kick—missed clean as Qinggua hopped clear—and overbalanced straight onto his backside.
Qinggua hurried over to help him up. "Why still kicking me, Young Master?"
Snatching Qinggua's collar, Chen Haoyu roared, "Anyone else can demand an apology—never you!"
"Young Madam already said yes!"
"You're my servant! Obey me alone!"
Qinggua bobbed a meek nod.
Losing interest in their circus, Qianli Xun turned indoors, Kuqiao signaling Asheng before following her.
Shoving Qinggua off, Chen Haoyu scrambled up with Qinggua's help as Asheng said, "Time for Boya Study and your memorization, Young Master."
Shaking his fist at Asheng and Sanbao, Chen Haoyu growled, "Haunting me like ghosts—one day I'll flatten you both!"
Still, outnumbered and outmatched, he trudged toward Boya Study needing an outlet for his bruised pride. "Qinggua, walk in front of me."
"Why?"
"Do as you're told and quit yapping!"
Unsuspecting, Qinggua stepped ahead—and Chen Haoyu put all his weight into his right boot, punting straight at Qinggua's rear. "Take that, Zhu Shuzhen!"
#CH 234
#TITLE: One Tear Reveals True Feeling
Without eyes in the back of his breeches, Qinggua took the boot dead center, pitched forward off balance, and headed straight for a face-plant into the flagstones.
In a flash, Ugly Maid darted out and caught him upright. "You okay, Qinggua?"
"Saved my nose—thanks, Ugly Maid!"
Releasing him, Ugly Maid turned and curtsied stiffly. "Young Master, could you please stop picking on my Qinggua?"
Blocked from venting, humiliated all morning, surrounded by Zhu Shuzhen's remodeled courtyard and her trained lackeys—and now even Qinggua had someone standing up for him while he had nobody at all—a hot sting rushed into Chen Haoyu's eyes. Not saying a word, he turned and walked toward Boya Study, Asheng and Sanbao trailing behind.
Ugly Maid blinked. "Qinggua, did you see that? Look like Young Master was about to cry?"
"Cry? No way! My master makes other folks cry—never shed a tear in his life!"
Amei strolled over. "I saw it too. Young Master looked crushed, eyes red as a rabbit's. Running into a wife as tough as Miss, who wouldn't cry?"
Ignoring Amei, Ugly Maid tugged Qinggua's sleeve. "Meet me at the west pavilion when you're free!"
"No shame at all, Ugly Maid—I'm standing right here!" Amei laughed.
"Then make yourself scarce and let us talk!" Ugly Maid nudged her off toward the West Courtyard.
Worried about his master—and eager to ditch Ugly Maid—Qinggua backed away. "Got to go check on Young Master!" and bolted toward the back courtyard.
Letting him run, Ugly Maid muttered at his back, "Gets kicked nonstop and still chases after him—must enjoy being beaten! Next time I'm not saving you."
Along the path to Boya Study, Chen Haoyu blinked hard to hold back the burn, yet one hot tear slipped down his cheek anyway. Halting, he wiped it away with his sleeve—and froze as an old night of drinking with his pals rushed back into his head.
They had been carousing at Juxiang Tower, trading coarse jokes until talk turned to love. One after another, his wealthy friends named a girl who had stirred their hearts—everybody except Chen Haoyu.
"Plucked half the flowers in Lin'an, Brother Chen—never felt real love for a single one?" one friend asked.
With a girl tucked under each arm, Chen Haoyu had grinned. "Fun's fun—why ruin it with love?"
"Always wondered what kind of woman could actually hook your heart, Brother Chen," another prodded.
Waving off the two girls to sit aside once the whole table pestered him, Chen Haoyu had turned half-serious. "Since you're dying to know: no idea how much I bawled as a baby, yet since I grew sense, I haven't shed a tear. The first girl who ever makes me cry—that's the one I'll fall for."
"What if she's ugly?" someone teased.
"With my standards? An ugly girl never gets past my gate, let alone makes me cry!"
Standing alone on the path, Chen Haoyu asked himself in disbelief: Wait... did I fall for the tigress?!
He shook his head hard. Impossible! We're mortal enemies! Why did a tear slip out then? No, no—just overthinking a drunk boast from years ago!
Puzzled, he stepped into Boya Study while Asheng and Sanbao took post outside.
Hongdou stood tidying the desk and bowed. "Young Master, Miss picked out this stack of books for you—start with the Analects and Wang Wei's poems. Five chapters of the Analects and five poems every day, then report to Suxin Thatched Hall for Miss to test you."
One glance at the towering stack made Chen Haoyu's skull throb, cursing Zhu Shuzhen inside: Hateful tigress! No chance in hell I'm falling for you!
"Best start reading right away, Young Master."
Rubbing his growling belly, he protested, "Ran all morning on an empty stomach! Bring me lunch first, then I'll memorize."
"Start reading while I fetch your meal."
After Hongdou left, Qinggua crept in to find his master staring at an unprecedented pile of books. Grinning, he sidled up. "Young Master, Ugly Maid and Amei swear you cried—true?"
"Scram! Quit pestering me—none of your business!"
"Guess it's true! I know you're hurting, Young Master, yet with the elders staying out and Young Madam this fierce, suffering is all you get. Want a bright idea?"
Staring bleakly at the texts, Chen Haoyu murmured, "What bright idea could you have?"
Qinggua leaned across the desk. "Head-on clashing flopped every time—why not try going soft?"
Chen Haoyu's eyes snapped wide. "Didn't know you had brains in there! Keep talking!"
Energized by the praise, Qinggua ran with it. "You two are husband and wife! Turn on real husbandly warmth—tough as Young Madam is, she's still a woman who likes sweet, caring words. Pour on enough tenderness and her heart melts, no way she keeps swinging fists! Mold yourself into a model husband, and once she sees your good side, she'll want a real marriage and stop tormenting you!"
Chen Haoyu mulled it over. "Sweet words I can pull off, yet being a model husband? Never tried—where do I even start?"
"Eldest Master is a model husband! Copy how he treats First Madam!"
SLAP! Chen Haoyu hit the desk in excitement. "Right! Living blueprint right under my nose—copy my father!" Then his gaze dropped back to the book stack and deflated. "Wait—do I still memorize these?"
"Of course!" Qinggua flipped the top book open before him. "Think about it: when has Eldest Master ever crossed First Madam?"
"Never—except Mother never bullies Father! The tigress is bullying me! I hate reading, and feeling forced makes my blood boil!"
"Calm down, Young Master." Qinggua patted his back to soothe him. "Think why Young Madam is furious—you wronged her first! Everyone knows you spread last year's rumors."
"Even you know about that?!"
"Every servant in Chen Manor knows! Picture a young lady cursed by the entire city—she must have cried oceans behind closed doors, and it wrecked her Qiao marriage too! Honestly, can't believe you pulled something that rotten, Young Master."
"Not all my fault! She wrote 'falling asleep in his arms, fully dressed' herself—she ruined her own name!"
Qinggua paused mid-pat. "Sure, she wrote it—yet who leaked that line to the whole street? Regular folks don't read scholar poetry! Without your rumor campaign, nobody on the street would have heard it."
That hit home. Commoners never touched literary verses; his spite had turned a private poem into a public stoning. His sin ran deeper than he had admitted. "Fine, fine—my fault. I'll read."
Opening the Analects, he groaned at the tedious ancients leaving headaches for future generations. After Hongdou brought lunch and he ate his fill, drowsiness washed over him until his eyelids drooped and he slumped head-down on the desk, snoring away.
Standing watch, Qinggua sighed—and began nodding off on his feet too until a sharp poke jolted him awake.
Ugly Maid stood whispering beside him. "Come on—west pavilion!"
Sick of dodging her and worried Hongdou might get the wrong idea, Qinggua steered her away from his sleeping master and cooked up an excuse. "Stop looking for me, Ugly Maid."
"Why?"
"Young Master is getting tormented by Young Madam—zero mood for romance."
"That's his business, not ours!"
"Wrong! When Young Master's happy, I'm happy; when he's miserable, I'm miserable!"
"So you won't meet me at the west pavilion until Miss and Young Master make up?"
Qinggua nodded firm.
"That'll take forever!"
"Then either quit looking for me, or help Young Master make peace with Young Madam!"
"Impossible—guess I'll stay away then." Slumping in defeat, Ugly Maid shuffled out.
Puffed up at shaking her off so clean, Qinggua paused—wait, did Ugly Maid's pessimism mean his master and young madam would feud forever, and his soft-tactics plan was doomed?
Just then Chen Haoyu mumbled in his sleep: "Zhu Shuzhen... just wait... I'll beat you... flat..."
Sleep-talking, Qinggua chuckled—then froze as his master murmured softer: "I... like... you..."
Eyes popping wide, Qinggua leaned close and whispered, "Who do you like, Young Master?"
"Zhu... Shu... zhen..." slurred from Chen Haoyu's lips.
Mumbled as it was, every syllable came clear. A wide grin broke across Qinggua's face. "Young Master fell for Young Madam without even knowing it while awake! Hilarious! Hope they really make up so life gets back to normal."
In his dream, Zhu Shuzhen punched Chen Haoyu straight into a pit, jolting him upright in a cold sweat. Rubbing his eyes, he asked, "What hour is it?"
"Hour of the Monkey—mid-afternoon."
"Already?! I haven't memorized a single line—what do I do?!"
"Keep cramming!"
Before he could grab the book, Hongdou stepped in. "Study time's up, Young Master. Report to Miss for recitation."
"Give me a little longer!"
"No! Miss sets the clock, nobody changes it!"
"Fine, no need to yell!" Dragging his feet, Chen Haoyu headed out with Qinggua trailing behind, bracing for an explosion.
#CH 235
#TITLE: Soft Tactics, Soft Tactics, Use Soft Tactics
Stepping into Suxin Thatched Hall, Chen Haoyu breathed in the crisp scent of ink and paper—and for the first time in his life found it pleasant.
Seated by the desk sipping tea, Zhu Shuzhen looked breathtaking when she was not scowling. No wonder Prince Yi lost his head over her; even Chen Haoyu's pulse fluttered. Shaking his head to snap out of it, he silently scolded himself.
"Miss, Young Master is here," Hongdou announced.
Setting down her tea bowl, Qianli Xun waved Hongdou off.
Unable to peel his eyes away, Chen Haoyu mused: If the tigress turned gentle, she'd make a dream wife—smart, pretty, and lethal in a fight. Anyone outside messes with me, she'd clean their clock!
"What are you gawking at, Chen Haoyu?"
Her sharp bark shattered the daydream. "Came to see you—who else should I look at, Kuqiao or Qinggua?"
"Save the lip. Recite what you memorized."
"Time was too short. Didn't memorize any."
"None?! I gave you over an hour and you didn't memorize one single poem?!"
Chen Haoyu gave a sheepish nod.
"Kuqiao! Fetch the birch ruler!"
Kuqiao handed over the wooden ruler. Rising, Qianli Xun marched over. "Hold out your palm!"
To his own astonishment, Chen Haoyu extended his hand like a contrite schoolboy.
His total lack of resistance threw Qianli Xun off stride. "Why acting so docile all of a sudden?"
Seizing his shot at soft tactics, he smiled. "No more fighting back. Whatever you tell me to do, I'll obey."
That sucked every drop of fun out of striking him. "Not worth dirtying my hands smacking yours—need them intact to clean my rooms."
Bullseye! Soft tactics worked like magic! Behind his back, Chen Haoyu flashed Qinggua a secret thumbs-up, leaving the servant beaming from ear to ear.
Returning the ruler to Kuqiao, Qianli Xun resumed her seat. "Dust every corner of this hall inside and out—no help from Qinggua. Stay a full yard clear of my desk."
Playing the soft game smooth as silk, Chen Haoyu agreed. "Dusting's a breeze, no help needed—surely Qinggua can rinse the rag for me?"
Unnerved by this sudden personality swap, Qianli Xun snapped, "Quit stalling and get to work." Picking up her brush, she returned to her huaben, ignoring him.
Qinggua rolled up his master's sleeves and handed over a damp cloth. Wiping shelves and screens with surprising care, Chen Haoyu stole glances at Zhu Shuzhen's focused profile—nothing like a tigress when engrossed in ink.
He recalled spying on her and Qiao Wenxian by West Lake last year, leaning soft in a frail scholar's arms on the boat bow. Back then he could not fathom how a fierce brawler melted like butter for a bookworm; now he understood—love unlocked her tender side. Now that she belonged to Chen Manor, if he could make her fall for him, she might turn soft as a kitten!
Yet gloom hit right after. Look at her past rivals: Qiao Wenxian had poetic fame and heartthrob looks; Prince Yi had imperial blood and top-tier fists. What did Chen Haoyu have?
Spotting Qinggua—whose looks matched Ugly Maid yet who chased Hongdou fearless—Chen Haoyu waved him close for a whispered pep talk.
"If someone told you you're way out of Hongdou's league, would you quit chasing her?"
"No way! Who cares what folks say? I like her—that's all that matters!"
Another thumbs-up from Chen Haoyu had Qinggua glowing. And Qinggua had a point: brilliant as Qiao Wenxian and Prince Yi were, Zhu Shuzhen had married him! Heaven itself put her in his court. Why sweat it? Go all out and win her over!
Fired up, he scrubbed every beam and sill spotless within an hour. Kuqiao ran a fingertip across the woodwork and nodded in surprise. "Aside from haunting brothels, Young Master dusts as well as any maid."
"Watch that tongue," Chen Haoyu said loud enough for the desk to hear. "I'm done with brothels for good. A married man belongs at home—hanging out at brothels invites gossip and hurts his wife's heart."
Glancing toward Zhu Shuzhen, he saw she stayed unmoved, setting down her brush only to tell Qinggua, "Call Asheng in." Kuqiao tucked her fresh pages away.
While waiting, Chen Haoyu watched Zhu Shuzhen flip open a book and lose herself in reading. What was so captivating about ink on paper? To win her respect, he needed to master some books too—starting tomorrow, he would memorize for real!
Asheng stepped in. "Report on his laps," Qianli Xun ordered.
"Eight and a half laps, Miss. Stopped twice—once to watch drama, once to chat with Eldest Young Master in a pavilion."
"Then out of four tasks, you finished two," Qianli Xun declared. "Starting tomorrow, Chen Haoyu, two straight days emptying my chamber pot. Clear?"
Heat flared in his chest—only for him to chant a mantra inside his skull: Soft tactics, soft tactics, use soft tactics! Like magic, the anger evaporated, replaced by a sunny smile. "Whatever my wife commands, I obey."
That tripped Qianli Xun up worse than a slap. "Don't call me that!"
"How should I call you? Teach me, Wife."
"Saying it again?!"
"Shuzhen."
"Swallowed bad medicine? Put my surname back!"
"Zhu Shuzhen."
Same three syllables, yet rolling off his tongue with an unfamiliar warmth that gave her chills. One day of discipline could never turn a leopard spotless—this had to be a new ploy! Hard fists she could counter blindfolded; honeyed compliance left her off balance. Stay sharp, don't buy the act!
"Kuqiao, bring his pay."
Kuqiao placed the coins in his palm. "One tael of silver and fifty wen, Young Master. Miss keeps her word—hope you accept tomorrow's penalty just as good."
Embracing soft tactics all the way, Chen Haoyu handed the silver right back to Kuqiao and faced Zhu Shuzhen. "If this is punishment, how can I take wages? Keep every copper—I accept every penalty without complaint."
Both maid and mistress stared in shock.
"What do I do with this, Miss?" Kuqiao asked.
Refusing to bend to his stunt, Qianli Xun said, "Take it to the West Courtyard and split it among the servants—call it silver Chen Haoyu earned for them."
Spotting her bait, Chen Haoyu chanted his mantra twice more and broke into a broad grin. "Listen to Young Madam! Split it among yourselves—starting tomorrow I'll earn even more for you all! Don't leave Qinggua out!"
"Thank you, Young Master!" Qinggua cheered.
Left baffled and outmaneuvered, Qianli Xun pivoted fast. "Tomorrow's schedule: besides emptying my chamber pot, finish all laps and memorization. For manual labor, sweep the entire main courtyard—Asheng inspects, and fail means another chamber-pot day. For apology—apologize to Qinggua in front of every servant in Moxiang Courtyard."
Fearing his master's temper, Qinggua hurried to wave it off. "Skip me, Young Madam—picking on others is wrong, picking on me is fine!"
One round of his mantra kept Chen Haoyu breezy. "Nonsense, Qinggua. Tomorrow I apologize to you fair and square."
Holding up her frosty front, Qianli Xun still noticed the purple swelling on his cheek. "Kuqiao, bring him a bottle of bruise salve."
Kuqiao pocketed the silver and fetched a small porcelain vial from the inner room. "Top-grade salve, Young Master—one coat tonight and the bruise vanishes by morning."
Chen Haoyu grabbed it beaming; first time the tigress had ever shown concern! Keep this pace up and his misery would end in no time.
Unable to stomach this bizarre new Chen Haoyu another second, Qianli Xun shooed him out. "Get back to Boya Study and quit annoying me!"
Once the room emptied, Kuqiao ventured, "Miss, doesn't Young Master seem like a whole new person?"
"Illusion—pure illusion! Think Chen Haoyu reforms in forty-eight hours? Just a fresh scheme! Wait two days and the mask drops. Besides, I haven't finished paying him back—I don't want him reforming yet!"
"He's your husband, Miss. Him turning decent only helps you."
"You don't want me getting revenge?"
"Of course I do! If anyone else had spread those rumors, I'd slap them myself—yet he's our young master! I hate seeing you face a second divorce. If he turns into a good husband and treats you right, doesn't everybody win?"
"Even if he turned into a saint, it's got zero to do with me." Coexisting in peace was her outer limit; falling for Chen Haoyu or sharing a bed was out of the question.
Back in Boya Study after nightfall, Qinggua dabbed salve across his master's cheek, gushing, "Soft tactics worked wonders, Young Master! Young Madam couldn't even stay mad at you!"
"Sharpest brain on you, Qinggua—once life gets back to normal, big reward waiting."
"Skip the reward—just keep your word and help me win Hongdou!"
Chen Haoyu winced. "Hongdou's cold as ice toward you. Why not pick Ugly Maid—she's already throwing herself at your feet!"
Setting down the salve bottle, Qinggua shook his head firm. "Don't want easy—I want Hongdou."
"Fine, fine. Once I win Zhu Shuzhen over, I'll play matchmaker for you two."
Today marked the sharpest twist of Chen Haoyu's whole life—a day he would never forget, nor the first woman who had ever brought a tear to his eye. He could not explain why an idle boast among drinking buddies had come true, yet loving a woman felt dizzying and sweet; every flaw that had once grated on him in that tigress now seemed charming.
A goofy chuckle slipped out of him. "Heh heh..."
Staring at his master giggling alone on the eve of chamber-pot duty, Qinggua shook his head in disbelief.
#CH 236
#TITLE: A Bouquet of Roses to Confess His Heart
Not until Asheng pulled the door of Boya Study shut and clicked the padlock home did Chen Haoyu snap out of his dreamy grin. "Locking me in again? Afraid I'll sneak off to Chunxiang Brothel—why not just admit you like me? Relax, even if you chased me out with a broom, I wouldn't set foot near Chunxiang Brothel!"
Qinggua laid a palm on his master's forehead. "No fever—why talking delirious?"
Chen Haoyu swatted his hand aside. "Quit poking! No fever here!"
"You actually think locking your door means Young Madam likes you and fears you visiting brothels?!"
"What else?"
"Think soft tactics fried your brain, Young Master?"
"Not delirious—dead serious!"
"You're really done with Chunxiang Brothel for good?"
Propping his chin on his hand with a dreamy grin, Chen Haoyu sighed, "What's left to see at a brothel? Bored of it. Right now all I want is staying home in Moxiang Courtyard."
Qinggua grinned—certain now. "Awesome! Good days ahead for us!"
"Wait—one second ago you called me delirious, now you're cheering?"
Edging back within dodging range, Qinggua probed, "Young Master... did you fall for Young Madam?"
Far from snapping, Chen Haoyu beamed. "That obvious? Even you spotted it! Who'd ever believe I fell for the tigress—feels like a dream even to me."
"Sure feels unreal," Qinggua agreed, pouring a cup of tea. "Cursing her out at noon, head over heels by nightfall—isn't that a bit fast?"
"Ever hear the phrase 'changing in the blink of an eye'?"
Remembering the afternoon nap, Qinggua mused, "Think back, Young Master—maybe you fell for her ages ago and just didn't realize."
Chen Haoyu traced it back: from the brawl at Yongtai Teahouse to the run-in in the bamboo grove, her name had spun nonstop inside his skull while he plotted revenge—no other woman had ever occupied his mind a tenth as much. Had she moved into his heart back then, hidden behind spite until one tear blew the cover off? Every piece fit!
"Didn't know you could read my soul so sharp, Qinggua!"
Puffed up by another compliment, Qinggua confessed, "When you fell asleep at the desk today, you called her name in your sleep and said you liked her—heard every word."
Glowing even brighter at having accidentally married the woman he loved, Chen Haoyu declared, "Starting tomorrow, I'm turning over a new leaf to make Zhu Shuzhen see me with brand-new eyes!"
"No need to wait till tomorrow—your soft talk already had Young Madam off balance today!"
"Heh heh! Found her Achilles' heel at last! Keep pouring on soft tactics until she melts into a sweet kitten right in my arms—instead of punching me, she'll use those fists to guard me! Heh heh..." Drool practically threatened the corner of his mouth as he daydreamed.
At dawn, Asheng and Sanbao unlocked Boya Study and woke him up. Never an early riser, Chen Haoyu nearly cursed—then remembered love, hopped up full of pep, dressed with Qinggua's help, and both tied cloth strips across their noses and mouths.
Outside Suxin Thatched Hall, Asheng tapped the door. Kuqiao cracked it open, set a chamber pot on the threshold without a word, and shut it fast.
A wall of stench rolled out. Asheng and Sanbao clapped hands over their noses and turned away; even behind cloth masks, Chen Haoyu and Qinggua gagged.
How does someone that pretty produce a smell this lethal? Chen Haoyu wondered. Ah well, love covers small flaws! "Quit freezing, Qinggua—grab it and dump it!"
Dutifully holding his breath, Qinggua hauled the pot off toward the latrine while Asheng and Sanbao backed clear until the air thinned.
Indoors, Kuqiao swung a censer of incense to clear the air, grumbling, "Vile stench! Really doing this again tomorrow, Miss?"
Already dressed and staring blankly at the tea set, Qianli Xun answered, "One more day."
"Praying Young Master aces every single chore today—otherwise I'm stuck trekking out every dawn to scoop foul dung into a pot until Suxin Thatched Hall turns into Stinky Dung Hall!"
Her own stomach still churning from the odor, Qianli Xun stayed mute, lost in thought.
Noticing her mistress sitting silent since waking, Kuqiao paused with the censer. "Look gloomy, Miss—feeling unwell?"
Qianli Xun looked up. "Kuqiao, am I right or wrong taking payback on Chen Haoyu?"
"Right, of course! He spread those rumors—deserves every bit!"
"Then why don't I feel even a spark of joy doing it?"
"Because you're softhearted, Miss—hate watching people suffer."
Checking her own chest, Qianli Xun shook her head. "Not just softhearted. Making him dump a stinking pot stinks us out right alongside him. Hurting someone backfires straight onto yourself—wonder if it's even worth it?"
"Mean you don't want payback anymore?"
"Want it? Of course I want it. Just wondering what's the point when it brings me zero happiness."
Unsure how to answer, Kuqiao waited until the hall smelled clean and the crowd had moved on, then threw open doors and windows for fresh air.
After breakfast, Chen Haoyu set off on his ten laps—cheerful and light-footed today, amazed to find jogging actually felt invigorating once his legs warmed up. Passing Chen Haodong midway, he waved without slowing. "Got laps to finish, Brother Dong—can't chat or I'm stuck on chamber-pot duty! See you!"
Watching his cousin jog off grinning, Chen Haodong scowled: Grinning through punishment?! My advice must have tanked! Seeing him happy drives me nuts—need a nastier trick!
Jogging past the gardener's quarters, Chen Haoyu spotted a bright patch of roses—unnoticed yesterday, sparking an instant idea today. "Qinggua, tell the gardener to cut me a fresh bouquet of roses!"
Thrilled to ditch jogging, Qinggua darted off and got the gardener to trim a fine bunch, tucked into a plain porcelain vase with water to spare thorns. Counting his master only five laps in, Qinggua ducked into a quiet wooden gallery, set the vase on a bench, leaned against a pillar, and drifted off to sleep—until a splat of bird droppings hit his cheek, jolting him awake. Wiping his face with plucked leaves and checking the sun, he snatched the vase and sprinted back to the finish line.
Minutes later, Chen Haoyu trotted up with Asheng and Sanbao and collapsed onto a roadside stone, panting yet grinning.
"Solid run today, Young Master," Asheng praised.
Spotting Qinggua hurrying up cradling the vase, Chen Haoyu smiled. "Lovely blooms, shabby vase—swap it into my green celadon vase back at Boya Study."
Once he caught his breath and switched vases, he carried the bouquet himself to Suxin Thatched Hall, ordering Asheng and Sanbao to wait outside while bringing only Qinggua in.
Inside, Kuqiao stood whisking tea with her back turned, and Qianli Xun wrote absorbed at her desk, neither noticing him enter. Cradling his green vase of roses, Chen Haoyu watched the "tigress" work—every angle delightful now, regretting every past clash.
Turning with a finished bowl of tea, Kuqiao jumped at finding him grinning silly at her mistress. "When did you walk in, Young Master?!"
"Few minutes back. Didn't want to interrupt."
Qianli Xun set down her brush and looked up. "What do you want?"
"Brought you flowers."
Eyes landing on the crimson roses, Qianli Xun blinked in total shock.
"Set them on Young Madam's desk, Qinggua," Chen Haoyu instructed.
As Qinggua approached, Qianli Xun snapped out of her daze, flipped her manuscript pages face-down fast, and watched the vase land beside her inkstone. Kuqiao stood frozen still holding the tea bowl.
Having received heaps of bouquets in her modern life, roses alone did not sway her; what baffled her was Chen Haoyu pulling this stunt. "What game are you playing, Chen Haoyu?"
Before speaking, he broke into a goofy grin. "Heh heh..."
"Stop giggling and talk!"
Suppressing his grin, he beamed. "Clear as daylight—still can't tell?"
"Tell what? Spit it out or get lost!"
"Even glaring you're gorgeous! Since you want it plain, I'll swallow my pride right in front of the servants: Zhu Shuzhen, I like you! Heh heh..."
Kuqiao's eyes nearly popped out of her skull, tea bowl still frozen in midair.
Convinced this was pure theater, Qianli Xun scoffed. "Think a cheap act like this buys you a free pass? Dream on!"
No mantra needed today—Chen Haoyu kept smiling easy. "Makes sense you don't buy it after all our fights. Time will prove I'm head over heels for you! Hahaha—who knew I'd end up marrying the woman I love? Neither Qiao Wenxian nor Prince Yi got this lucky! Heh heh..."
His goofy giggling gave Qianli Xun goosebumps. Wait—is he actually serious? True or fake, never fall for it! "Quit laughing!"
He snapped his mouth shut at once. Kuqiao finally remembered to set the tea bowl down.
Qianli Xun took a long swallow to hide her fluster and set the bowl back. "Per yesterday's schedule, you owe Qinggua an apology. Do it right here."
Expecting him to bristle now that the moment arrived, she watched him agree without blinking. "Gladly!" Turning to Qinggua, he spoke warm and clear. "I bullied you nonstop, Qinggua, and I was dead wrong. Right here in front of Young Madam, I say sorry—never laying a hand or foot on you again. Know this too: rough as I was, deep down I've always counted you my one true right-hand man."
"One true right-hand man" burst Qinggua's tear ducts wide open. "Young Master! Never knew I meant that much to you—kick me all you want, I'll take it! Waaah..."
"Calling you a glutton for punishment fits! My word stands—never punching or kicking you again." Turning back to Zhu Shuzhen, he beamed. "Apology done. Satisfied?"
Repeating silently that it had to be an act—who had coached him into this maddening tactic?—she nodded stiffly. "Task two passed."
"Aced task one too—even Asheng praised me! Whatever you order from here on, zero pushback! Mind you, that chamber pot this morning sure reeked—heh heh! Didn't mind a bit! Heh heh..."
Unable to bear another chuckle, Qianli Xun waved him toward the door. "Nothing else? Get out and quit bugging me!"
"Yes ma'am! Off to memorize my books! Heh heh..." Chen Haoyu skipped out on cloud nine.
#CH 237
#TITLE: The Servants Hold a Secret Council
Watching Chen Haoyu skip out, Kuqiao glanced at the vase of roses. "Miss, could Young Master really have fallen for you?"
Qianli Xun glared at the blooms. "Don't swallow that bait—pure trickery! Too bad it won't work on me. Think a bunch of flowers and a sleazy grin buys forgiveness? Not in a million years!"
"Yet he looked thrilled out of his mind—hardly looked tormented at all."
"Means my punishments are too soft. Time to cook up something nastier."
Torn between siding with her mistress and doubting the whole mess, Kuqiao stayed quiet until Qianli Xun ordered, "Toss those roses out."
Lifting the vase, Kuqiao sighed. "Too pretty to dump—if you don't want them, Miss, I'll put them in Yuening Room."
Setting the vase inside Yuening Room, Kuqiao stepped back out right into Ugly Maid grabbing her sleeve. "Sister Kuqiao, quick—need to talk!"
"About what?"
"Huge deal!"
"Spill it or I'm walking."
Leaning to her ear, Ugly Maid whispered, "About Miss and Young Master's future happiness!"
That caught Kuqiao's ear at once. "Where?"
"West Courtyard."
"Hang on—let me tell Miss so she doesn't wonder where I ran off to."
"Meet you there!" Ugly Maid darted off.
Inside Suxin Thatched Hall, Qianli Xun had resumed writing and waved Kuqiao off without looking up. Heading to the West Courtyard, Kuqiao spotted Ugly Maid waving from the doorway of the servants' dining hall instead of Qin'an Lodge.
"Thought it was just us two," Kuqiao laughed as she walked up. "Looks like a full house."
"Everyone except the three men Matron Wei took on errands!"
"What got you playing matchmaker for Miss all of a sudden?" Kuqiao teased.
Ugly Maid turned bright red. "Miss's happiness decides mine! Qinggua said he won't be with me until Young Master and Miss make up!"
"Here I thought you were purely selfless—turns out you've got skin in the game!" Kuqiao laughed as Ugly Maid blushed deeper.
Inside the dining hall stood three tables; two male servants, Jiaxiang and Fulu, jumped up to greet Kuqiao as Miss's head maid. Right behind came Hongdou, Amei, Qinggua, and Asheng, filling the room with chatter. Ugly Maid boldly pulled Qinggua onto the bench beside her, forcing him to watch Hongdou sit next to Asheng across the table.
Once everyone settled, Kuqiao looked around. "Asheng and Qinggua both here—who's watching Young Master?"
"Sanbao's got him covered," Asheng said.
"Don't worry, Sister Kuqiao," Qinggua piped up. "Young Master obeys every word now—burying his nose in books like his life depends on it. Never saw him study this hard in all my years with him!"
"Awesome!" Ugly Maid clapped. "With a little push, they'll patch things up—and then Qinggua and I can..." Embarrassment swallowed the rest of her line.
Realization hit Qinggua: his own brush-off had sparked this whole summit! Torn between rooting for his master and dreading Ugly Maid's clutches, he glanced at Hongdou—who sat beaming beside Asheng without sparing him a blink.
"Every council needs a leader," Kuqiao noted. "Who's chairing?"
"Ugly Maid called us—she chairs," Hongdou proposed.
Straightening up—giving Qinggua breathing room—Ugly Maid took charge. "Aside from Qinggua, we all belong to Miss and want her happy. Since finding out Young Master started those rumors and starting payback, Miss hasn't smiled once—Sister Kuqiao knows best."
Kuqiao sighed. "Who could smile marrying the man who slandered her? The question is helping Miss get past this wall. None of us want her going through a second divorce—landing in-laws as wonderful as Eldest Master and First Madam is rare as gold."
Murmurs of agreement circled the table.
Qinggua grinned. "Good news—they already took a giant leap! Sister Kuqiao heard Young Master confess his love today!"
Every jaw except Kuqiao's hit the floor. "What?! Young Master confessed?!"
"Sure did," Kuqiao confirmed, "though Miss didn't buy a word and wants to ramp up the torture. Honestly, I can barely believe it myself."
"Hard to believe!" the rest chorused.
"It's gospel truth!" Qinggua insisted. "He even said he loves her in his sleep!"
"I believe Qinggua!" Ugly Maid backed him up.
"I coached him to ditch fighting and try soft talk and copy Eldest Master—and he actually agreed! What else proves he's fallen hard?"
"Looks genuine then," Kuqiao sighed, knowing full well who still lingered in her mistress's heart. "Trouble is, Miss doesn't feel that way."
Asheng cut to the core. "Young Master turned around; the lock now sits on Miss. Get her to warm up to him, and everybody lives happy."
"Quiet guy, straight to the bullseye," Hongdou beamed at him.
Watching them make goo-goo eyes irked Qinggua. "He only reached that bullseye because of my setup!"
Ignoring him, Hongdou pitched a plan. "Starting today, let's back Young Master! Hunt for every good trait he shows and drop praise in Miss's ears nonstop—especially Sister Kuqiao! Hear enough good things, and Miss's view of him will soften bit by bit."
"Will that work?" Amei worried. "Miss hates rumor-mongers to the bone—would she let it go that easy?"
Stumped, the group fell silent until Kuqiao rallied them. "No better plan on the table—nothing to lose trying Hongdou's trick!"
"Count me in!" Ugly Maid cheered, and every hand went up.
Wrapping up the meeting, Ugly Maid declared, "Remember our three-word motto: Praise Young Master! Qinggua, go tell Young Master to put his best foot forward so we've got real ammo to brag about!"
"Will do," Qinggua muttered, eyes glued to Hongdou.
Walking back toward Boya Study with Asheng, Qinggua poked him. "Asheng... you sweet on Hongdou?"
Caught off guard, Asheng admitted straight, "Yeah... I like her."
"Hate to break it to you," Qinggua fibbed, "Hongdou likes me."
Asheng tensed. "Wait—isn't Ugly Maid the one glued to your hip?"
"Just because Ugly Maid likes me doesn't ban other girls from liking me! I'm still single!" Before Asheng could challenge him, Qinggua bolted inside Boya Study.
Left frowning at the door, Asheng puzzled over it until Sanbao asked what was wrong.
"Sanbao, think Hongdou likes Qinggua?"
"No way!" Sanbao scoffed. "Ugly Maid likes Qinggua—Hongdou likes ME!"
Asheng blinked in shock—stumbled right onto another rival! Time to confess to Hongdou fast before somebody beat him to the punch.
Inside, Chen Haoyu sat reciting books with fierce concentration while Qinggua poured tea, baffled by the classical chatter. Setting the book down at last, Chen Haoyu barked, "Where'd you vanish to? Sneaking off with Ugly Maid?"
"Never—if I sneak off, it's with Hongdou! Huge news, Young Master: every servant in Moxiang Courtyard just vowed to sing your praises to Young Madam! Show off every good trait you've got so they've got material!"
"Hold on—aren't they all Zhu Shuzhen's lackeys? Why root for me?"
"Because they love Young Madam and don't want her divorcing again! Once I told them you fell for her, they teamed up to help win her heart!"
Chen Haoyu shot to his feet. "Awesome! Come on—time to showcase my finest trait right in front of Zhu Shuzhen!"
"Which trait?"
"My steel-trap memory!"
Stepping out, Chen Haoyu waved at Asheng and Sanbao. "Quit tailing me like hawks—not going anywhere!"
Still obeying orders, they followed behind, Asheng scanning his master for praiseworthy traits and coming up blank aside from a handsome face. "Sanbao, see any good traits on Young Master?"
Sanbao shook his head. "Drawing a blank."
"Do good looks count?"
"Guess so."
Stopping outside Suxin Thatched Hall, the guards waited while Chen Haoyu stepped inside—disappointed at first to see the desk empty, then lighting up when he spotted Zhu Shuzhen at the tea table holding a peeing clay doll with a soft smile across her lips.
Staring spellbound, Chen Haoyu thought: With a beauty this radiant at home, why did I ever roam outside? Yesterday I cursed Zhu Xiyan; today I'd bow to him for handing me the Poetess of Jiangnan!
"Young Master is here," Kuqiao announced to alert her mistress.
Eyes still locked on Zhu Shuzhen, Chen Haoyu offered, "Love clay dolls? Once I'm out, I'll buy you a mountain of them and fill the whole room!"
Passing the doll to Kuqiao to stow, Qianli Xun rose and walked up. "Penniless as you are, buying them with air? Weigh your own pockets before bragging."
"Once your mood lifts and you let me out, I'll ask Father to put me to work in the shops—earn monthly wages and buy you all the dolls you want!"
Two days of discipline and he was talking about joining the family business? Real or fake, she shot right back. "I've got deeper pockets than you—why need you buying anything? Besides, one clay doll charms the eye; a whole room turns my hall into a toy stall!"
"Flaring up again? My bad, okay? Cool down and hear me recite!"
Meeting zero pushback drained her venom before it could fire. Fine—let's hear him recite and wait for a slip to roast him on.
#CH 238
#TITLE: Praising the Young Master Nonstop
Chen Haoyu launched into the "Xue Er" chapter of the Analects—and instead of stopping after ten short lines, recited the entire opening chapter start to finish.
Short as the chapter was, Qianli Xun had to crack open the book to track him; he rolled through every word without a single stumble, winning her grudging admiration.
Finishing, he beamed with pride. "How about that? Beat the quota!"
Setting the Analects down, Qianli Xun kept her cool. "Big deal—probably drilled it into your skull at private school as a kid."
"Sure I went to school, yet my brain was miles away—knew the book's title and zero lines inside! Ask Brother Dong if you don't believe me!" Reaching for a chair—figuring today's gold-star showing earned a seat—he froze mid-bend at her bark.
"Done reciting? No sitting! Stand straight!"
He straightened up. "Can't you ease up on your own husband? A little tenderness goes a long way."
Qianli Xun rose and circled him twice, sizing him up: Huh, he really does have brains when he applies himself. Caught in her close orbit, breathing in her faint scent, Chen Haoyu melted—first time she had ever studied him like this!
"Impressed? Hit the jackpot marrying me, didn't you?"
Where on earth did this blind arrogance come from? None of the Chen elders had it! "Less bragging, recite your poems!"
"Fair warning—hate poetry, so I only did the required quota." Still, he rattled off ten Wang Wei masterpieces including "Autumn Evening in the Mountains" and "Farmhouse on the Wei River" without dropping a syllable.
Deciding the assignment had been too easy, Qianli Xun sneered, "Too simple for you? Fine—next up, memorize the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries!"
Chen Haoyu blinked. "Complete Library of the Four Treasuries? Never heard of it."
Oops! Time-travel slip—the Qing dynasty's Siku Quanshu would not exist for centuries! Refusing to own the blunder, she bluffed straight through. "A loafer like you barely knows three books—no shock you haven't heard of it! Fine, I'll take pity: memorize the Records of the Grand Historian instead!"
Han-dynasty Shiji—solid Song syllabus, and long enough to make him weep!
Sure enough, his face fell. "You already stacked books on my desk—why swap midstream? Shiji is endless—you're just trying to bury me!"
His groan delighted her. "My discipline, my rules. Can't I change my mind?"
"Fine, your call—on one condition!"
That snapped her temper back. Eyes flashing, she glared at him. "You dare set conditions?! When you spread rumors and got the whole city cursing my name until heaven and earth went deaf, who did I get to set conditions with?! Now a couple of books make you whine? Forget it—not granting a single condition!"
Mentioning the rumors pricked genuine guilt in Chen Haoyu. "Okay, okay—zero conditions! Torment me however you want, I'll take every hit until your anger cools... just tell me how long till it cools?"
"Never!" she snapped. "Not in this entire lifetime!"
A huge grin lit his face. "A whole lifetime? That means you're sticking with me for life! Hahaha—I beat Qiao Wenxian and Prince Yi combined!"
Her fury splashed off him like a pebble hitting a lake—zero ripples, leaving her stewing alone. Turning her back before staring at his goofy grin weakened her resolve, she snapped, "Drop the act! Think I don't see through your ploy? You won't get your way!"
"Think whatever you like—off to sweep the yard so the servants earn wages! Besides, I hate making you mad now. Heh heh..."
Heading for the door, he crossed paths with Hongdou and Amei carrying lunch trays and paused. "Seeing how good I did today, Zhu Shuzhen, can I stay and eat lunch with you?"
She whipped around. "In your dreams! I'd share a table with a street beggar before sharing one with you!"
Unfazed, he kept grinning. "No rush—since you're sticking with me for life, we'll share plenty of tables sooner or later!" and breezed out before she could fire back.
Setting the dishes out, Hongdou and Amei traded a quick look before Hongdou began. "Lunch is served, Miss. Let me report Young Master's behavior today while you eat: polite and respectful to every servant, focused hard on his books without a single nap!"
"Didn't kick Qinggua once today either!" Amei chimed in. "Really seems like he's turned good!"
Missing their conspiracy, Qianli Xun rolled her eyes. "Split a few copper wages and already bought off? Don't let surface polish fool you—one good day proves nothing. Time reveals true hearts. Run along; Kuqiao's got me."
Shooting Kuqiao a quick glance, both maids slipped out.
Setting chopsticks and ladling soup, Kuqiao waited for a smooth opening. "Miss, haven't spotted Matron Wei for two days."
"Out handling shop business dawn to dusk—haven't seen her either."
Kuqiao put on a wistful sigh. "Men handle outside affairs, women handle inside—if you had a dependable man by your side, Matron Wei wouldn't have to wear herself out running around town."
Qianli Xun dropped her chopsticks. "How long have you followed me to still talk narrow nonsense like that, Kuqiao? Women hold up half the sky! Who matches Matron Wei's brains? Who's the Poetess of Jiangnan? Then look at Chen Haoyu—a hollow shell in men's robes, bullying girls and haunting brothels! World full of men like him, we're better off with women!"
Her mistress had teed up the topic herself—perfect! "Young Master isn't that hopeless, Miss. Did great today, swore off brothels, even wants to join family business—proves your discipline worked magic!"
Setting her soup spoon down, Qianli Xun scoffed. "Use your head! Twenty years a playboy, reformed in forty-eight hours? Something smells fishy—it's a scheme!"
Half nodding yet remembering Qinggua's secret, Kuqiao lowered her voice. "Heard something from Qinggua—not sure if I should say..."
"Already brought it up—spill it."
"Qinggua told me yesterday Young Master murmured in his sleep that he loves you, Miss... and says that's why he changed overnight."
Qianli Xun's spoon paused midair, then sank back into the bowl. "You believe Qinggua's tall tales?"
Kuqiao kept quiet after dropping the seed. Qianli Xun finished her soup at half speed, rose without another word, and disappeared into the bedroom.
After clearing trays and eating in the West Courtyard, Kuqiao walked back across the front yard—passing Chen Haoyu sweeping briskly with his own hands while refusing Qinggua's help under Asheng and Sanbao's watch—and found her mistress lying fully dressed on the bed.
"Let me help you shed your outer robe for a nap, Miss."
Qianli Xun sat straight up. "Can't sleep. Come out with me."
"Where to?"
"The Divine Willow."
Knowing her mistress only sought the willow when tangled inside, Kuqiao asked no questions.
Walking past the sweeping groom, Qianli Xun studied the crisp swish of his broom—no hint of faking there. What if he really had changed out of love? Where did that leave all her pent-up fury?
Just then Asheng and Sanbao stepped up and bowed.
"Miss, Young Master's putting real muscle in," Sanbao reported. "Every inch he swept shines spotless!"
"And I noticed Young Master's actually quite a catch," Asheng added—"tall, solid build, handsome face!"
Now the lightbulb went off: every servant had ganged up to hype Chen Haoyu! Putting on a stern frown, she barked, "Whose servants are you—mine or Chen Haoyu's?"
"Yours, Miss!"
"Then quit pitching for him!"
Silenced, they watched her march out. "Easy does it," Asheng sighed to Sanbao. "Takes time."
Overhearing every word, Chen Haoyu grinned at them. "Appreciate it, boys! Keep talking me up and I won't shortchange you!"
"Words only stretch so far—keep earning them, Young Master," Asheng chuckled as Chen Haoyu went back to sweeping.
Near the main gate, Ugly Maid popped out on her way back from placing kitchen orders. "Going out, Miss?"
"Taking a walk." Qianli Xun moved to brush past—only for Ugly Maid to hop square in front of her.
"Miss, got to tell you one thing: Young Master really changed! Way better than before!"
Another cheerleader?! Had Chen Haoyu bribed her entire staff?! Not wasting a syllable, Qianli Xun sidestepped her and kept striding.
"I'm telling the truth, Miss!" Ugly Maid yelled at her back until Kuqiao waved her frantically to shut up and run back toward Qinggua.
Riding out toward the hills, mistress and maid sat in unbroken silence. Her first outing since the wedding made city streets sound distant and odd. Learning Chen Haoyu's guilt, she had picked mild, corrective payback assuming his anger and misery would bring relief—instead, zero relief came, and his goofy smiles and confessions only made her gloomier. Heaven itself seemed to rob her of even a clean taste of revenge.
#CH 239
#TITLE: Light and Free After Letting Go
At the foot of the mountain path, the carriage halted and Kuqiao stepped down first to offer her hand. Guessing from her mistress's silence that Chen Haoyu's sudden goodness had bottled up her grudge with nowhere to go, Kuqiao kept gentle watch. Seeing her maid's cautious concern, Qianli Xun rested her palm on Kuqiao's hand to reassure her as she stepped down.
Pilgrims streamed up and down the slope—young and old heading to burn incense at the hilltop nunnery. Before transmigration, Qianli Xun had sneered at superstition; now she no longer mocked it. People needed an anchor for their hopes, just as she sought peace beneath the Divine Willow without burning a single stick of incense.
Walking toward the tree, she noticed fewer catkins drifting now. Counting days, over half a month had passed since Prince Yi and Mengrong rode to Bianliang—and half a month since her own wedding. Married already, or riding home? Either way, she prayed happiness would dissolve Mengrong's hatred.
Wait—dissolve hatred? A blunt question struck her: Why wish Mengrong would let go of hating me, while I cling tight to hating Chen Haoyu? All the way here she had been cooking up wilder tortures—dangling him down a dry well three days on a rope, burying him neck-deep in a field for passersby to poke, stripping him to his undershorts with smeared charcoal on his face and acupoints locked to beg on the street—all because of last year!
Reaching the willow, she found four young couples tying red silk ribbons onto the boughs; ribbons had doubled since her last visit, spring stirring romance everywhere. Envy tugged at her—however their futures turned out, right now those lovers stood hand in hand pinning bright hopes onto the wind. How she wished she and Wenyuan had tied one ribbon back when love burned sweet; maybe the willow's blessing would have spared all this.
Once the couples drifted away, quiet returned. Stepping beneath the canopy, cool breath off the trunk and leaves washed over her, easing the tight knot in her chest—though not erasing it. She spoke aloud to the tree.
"Tell me what to do, Divine Willow. Marrying someone I disliked was bad enough; learning he started the rumors made me want to slice him to ribbons... yet overnight he flipped from fighting back to bending low, and..." Leaving out his confession, she sighed. "Now I can't bring myself to strike hard, yet letting my grudge fade unanswered sticks in my craw."
A breeze swept across the slanting sunset, swaying willow fronds until red ribbons tangled tight around slender twigs. Stirred by the view, one of Zhu Shuzhen's poems rose to her lips:
"A thousand high green strands sway in the warm breeze, / Veiled in mist and smoke east of the market bridge. / Knotting hidden bitterness in the slanting evening sun, / Snapping parting sorrows amid the fine spring rain." —"Willows" [TN: Translator's rendering]
"Fine verse!"
A familiar voice spoke from behind. Turning, Qianli Xun saw the elderly nun from the mountain nunnery—still unaware she stood before Master Jingguang—and bowed. "Greetings, Venerable Master! Fate brings us together again."
Hands folded over prayer beads, Master Jingguang chanted, "Amitabha. Fine verse indeed, Female Patron, though ill-matched to the scene. This willow stands by a pond outside the city—why speak of 'east of the market bridge'? Under bright clear skies, why 'snapping parting sorrows amid the fine spring rain,' when no friend or lover parts from you here?"
"Just lines that popped into my head, Master—don't read too much in."
"Not mere whim. 'Knotting hidden bitterness in the slanting evening sun'—bitterness sits inside your heart, and you recite to vent it. Yet venting never cures a wrathful heart."
Hit square in the chest, Qianli Xun asked, "Then what cures it? Please guide me, Master."
"No grand teaching—only passing along the Buddha's wisdom. Two words disarm a wrathful heart: patient endurance."
"Just swallow it? No—I can't watch the man who hurt me walk off unscathed! I want payback until he begs on his knees!"
"You reject endurance because you have not seen that wrath has no independent nature—it arises only from conditions. Whatever depends on conditions is empty illusion. Why let an illusion chain you?"
"Illusion?" Qianli Xun shook her head. "My pain was real, and his citywide slander was real! Your teachings fly too high, Master—I'm an ordinary mortal tangled in mortal feelings."
"Have you taken revenge on the one who sparked your wrath?"
"I have—only I'm too softhearted, picked mild punishments, and he ended up grinning right through them! Leaves me itching for harsher payback yet unable to strike."
Listening nearby, Kuqiao prayed silently that the nun's words would reach her mistress.
"You possess a kind nature," Master Jingguang said. "That kindness drew our paths together beneath this willow to hear the Dharma. Tell me: since beginning your revenge, have you felt happy?"
Qianli Xun searched her chest. From dragging him out of Chunxiang Brothel to slapping his cheeks, forcing apologies, and making him dump a reeking chamber pot—not one single moment of genuine joy. "Honestly... not happy at all."
"Mild revenge brought no joy; harsher revenge will bring even less. Acting on wrath is never wisdom. True wisdom is enduring, then letting go completely—only letting go sets you free."
"Easy to say! How do I just let go?"
"Why cling so tight?"
"He ruined my name and wrecked my marriage—stole the happiness meant for me! Shouldn't I hate him and make him pay?"
"Have you ever considered that what you took for your happiness never belonged to you in the first place?"
A hollow ache echoed inside her—maybe Wenyuan was never hers to keep—yet she pushed back. "If victims just endure and let go, don't bad people run wild while the world falls to pieces?"
"Tell me—is the man you hate a monster guilty of heinous evil?"
That stopped her cold. Chen Haoyu was a spoiled mess, sure, yet heinous evil? Pictures flashed past: apologizing earnest to Qinggua, sweeping the courtyard stroke by stroke, nodding meekly at her scolding. "Just a worthless playboy."
"Hardly an irredeemable monster. Take one step back, and the sky opens wide."
"Doesn't that let him off way too easy?"
"Do you truly care for yourself, Patron?"
"Of course!"
"Then why keep your mind glued to another person until you make yourself miserable? Someone who truly cherishes herself has no spare moments to stew over others. Life spans a few brief decades—why burn your days in wrath that wounds your own heart before touching your foe? A losing trade from start to finish."
Those words unlocked the bolt inside Qianli Xun's chest. Look at the absurdity: Chen Haoyu was the one being punished, yet after day one he was jogging, grinning, and whistling through Moxiang Courtyard while she sulked beneath a willow tree! Harm the foe a thousand, bleed eight hundred yourself. Not for Chen Haoyu—for her own peace and joy—she would drop the grudge and wipe last year's slate clean.
The instant she let the thought settle, weightless relief flooded her limbs. "Thank you for waking me up, Master. I'm letting it go."
"Amitabha. Letting go brings great merit. May peace and joy follow your days." Turning, Master Jingguang walked away.
"Thank you, Master!" Qianli Xun bowed to her receding figure.
Kuqiao bounced closer beaming. "Letting it go means you're done feuding with Young Master?"
"When did Chen Haoyu buy you off too?" Qianli Xun teased.
"Never bought me off! Just hated seeing you miserable since you found out—even punishing him didn't make you smile. Hearing Master's words cleared it right up!"
The first bright smile in days lit Qianli Xun's face. "Got a sharp root of wisdom yourself, girl. Done feuding with Chen Haoyu—everybody can go back to normal and drop that chorus of 'Praise Young Master' you all thought I didn't notice!"
"Nothing slips past you, Miss!"
Lighthearted again, Qianli Xun wandered the lakeside picking wildflowers with Kuqiao to weave matching flower crowns. Whenever young couples strolled up to tie ribbons, her eyes flicked over them—Kuqiao thinking she enjoyed the bustle, only Qianli Xun knowing she searched for two faces, torn between aching to see Prince Yi and Mengrong and dreading the moment they returned.
Only when twilight deepened did she sit a brief while beneath the willow, then ride home to Chen Manor.
#CH 240
#TITLE: The Chen Heir Regains His Freedom
By the time they reached Chen Manor, dinner was long over. Not hungry, Qianli Xun waved off Kuqiao's offer of food, changed into fresh clothes, and headed for Boya Study to settle things face-to-face with Chen Haoyu.
Stepping out of Suxin Thatched Hall, she spotted a figure walking through the lantern light and paused until Chen Haofei emerged into view.
"Greetings, Second Sister-in-law," he bowed.
"What brings you here?"
"Came to check on Second Brother."
Sharp as ever, Qianli Xun read right past it. "The elders sent you, didn't they?"
Too honest to fib, Chen Haofei nodded. "Grandmother and First Aunt talk tough, yet their hearts ache—can't step in themselves, so they sent me to peek."
"If their hearts ache, why put me in charge?" Knowing the elders would be let down after two days of discipline, she waved him along. "Since you're here, come with me to Boya Study."
Trailing behind her, Chen Haofei remembered his parents whispering about how fierce she was and prayed silently never to land a formidable wife himself. Reaching Boya Study, seeing Asheng and Sanbao posted outside like twin door gods made him stick out his tongue—no wonder Second Brother called her a tigress!
"You two can stand down," Qianli Xun told the guards. "No need to watch him anymore."
Thrilled, Asheng and Sanbao chorused "Yes, Miss!" and withdrew.
Kuqiao pushed the door wide. Qianli Xun stepped in first, followed by Chen Haofei calling, "Second Brother! Came to see you!"
Chen Haoyu and Qinggua emerged from the inner room—pleased at Haofei's voice, then lighting up like lanterns at spotting Zhu Shuzhen right behind him.
Hugging his cousin, Chen Haoyu grinned as Haofei whispered in his ear, "Was scared of Second Sister-in-law, only came because Grandmother and First Aunt were frantic about you!"
Releasing him, Chen Haoyu declared loud, "Take a good look—I'm thriving! Your sister-in-law treats me great, plenty to eat and wear, feel sharper than ever!"
Poor Second Brother, Haofei pitied inside—she must have broken him bad to make him praise her like this!
Watching his slick act, Qianli Xun waited—only for Chen Haoyu to pivot and challenge her: "Hey! Where'd you disappear all afternoon till dark?"
"Since when do I report my schedule to you?" she shot back, then laid out her verdict. "Listen up, Chen Haoyu: starting right now, you're free. No more lockups, and our old grudge is wiped clean. I'll draw up a fresh copy of our prenuptial contract—just press your thumbprint on it."
Joy at freedom flipped to instant alarm at "contract." "No way!"
"What, begging me to keep disciplining you?"
"The contract! You burned it—no point writing another!"
"Meaning?"
Stepping closer, Chen Haoyu met her eyes. "My head's in a whole new place these past two days. Those old terms don't fit anymore—why bother rewriting them?"
That sounded reasonable enough. "Fair point. Sleep on it tonight and come to Suxin Thatched Hall tomorrow to hammer out new terms. Chat with your cousin—I'm turning in."
At the doorway, Chen Haoyu called after her. "Hey! Really not mad about the rumors anymore?"
Without glancing back, Qianli Xun tossed him a crisp line. "If a dog bites a human, does the human bite the dog back? What's the difference between them then? I'm human, not turning into a dog—so I'm done feuding with that dog."
Funny how love warped a man: insulted to his face, he still beamed at her back. "You totally fell for me—releasing me this fast and hinting I need to stay loyal! Heh heh..."
Chen Haofei stared baffled. "Second Brother, where did you hear a hint in that? Did you mishear?"
"Never mishear!" Chen Haoyu spun back beaming. "Heard her mention a dog, right? What's a dog's number-one trait? Loyalty to its owner! She's hinting I stay loyal to her! Makes sense—dashing as I am, girls swoon everywhere I walk, natural she's possessive!"
Haofei glanced wryly at Qinggua. "Was that what she meant?"
Qinggua gave a helpless wave.
"Tell Grandmother and Mother it's late so I won't disturb them tonight," Chen Haoyu instructed Haofei. "I'll visit first thing tomorrow—and not one bad word about your sister-in-law, hear?"
Haofei hurried straight back to Eldest Uncle's courtyard, where Old Madam Xia was waiting with Chen Jianglin and Yao Qingyan. After two gritty days holding the line behind bolted gates, twilight jitters had sent Old Madam Xia pacing to her eldest son's rooms to check on her grandson—Did ten laps break him? Did apologizing to maids crush his pride? Chen Jianglin had chosen kindhearted, discrete Haofei to check, while secretly admiring Shuzhen's pinpoint discipline after getting updates from servants.
Haofei burst in calling, "Good news! Great news!"
"Spill it!" Old Madam Xia leaned forward.
"Second Sister-in-law freed Second Brother, dropped all punishments, and wiped the rumor grudge clean!"
Smiles vanished from all three faces. "Quit after two days?" Chen Jianglin frowned. "Two days can't reform Haoyu!"
"All our hopes of reforming him and sparking romance—just wishful thinking," Old Madam Xia sighed.
"Guess Haoyu lacked the luck, and us too," Yao Qingyan echoed.
Catching on that they wanted romance alongside reform, Haofei jumped in bright. "Don't lose hope! Hard to tell where Second Sister-in-law stands, yet Second Brother is a brand-new man—looks head over heels for her, and ordered me not to say one bad word about her!"
Laughter burst across the room at once.
"Huge progress!" Old Madam Xia crowed. "Already shielding his wife—think he'll keep running wild?"
"Mother's right!" Chen Jianglin beamed. "Shuzhen achieved more in two days than I managed in fifteen years!"
"Did he send any message?" Yao Qingyan asked.
"Said it's late tonight, so he'll visit you all first thing tomorrow morning."
Tears of joy pricked Yao Qingyan's eyes. "Never saw him this thoughtful—used to vanish without a word, now making formal morning calls!"
"Speak for yourselves—he always visited me," Old Madam Xia teased.
"Usually to wheedle silver out of you, Mother," Chen Jianglin chuckled.
"Asking me for things proves I'm in his heart—when did you lot ever ask me for anything?"
Too happy to argue, Chen Jianglin grinned and let it ride.
As Haofei escorted Old Madam Xia back to her gate, she halted him. "Wait a second, Haofei. Grandmother believes you're going to pass and win high office."
"May your blessing come true, Grandmother."
"Know why I say that?"
"Because we're family and you root for me."
"Not just that. Past fifty, I've read plenty of hearts. Your heart is clean and pure—Heaven won't let you down. You're the one who'll lift the Chen name to new heights."
Realizing how high he stood in her heart, Haofei bowed low. "Thank you, Grandmother."
"Run along and get some sleep."
Early next morning after breakfast, Chen Haoyu stepped out of Boya Study with Qinggua—right into Matron Wei. Unnerved by how she vanished during his punishment and popped up the instant he was freed, he jumped as she curtsied. "Congratulations on regaining your freedom, Young Master."
"Didn't see hide nor hair of you for two days—how'd you already know?"
"Seen or unseen, nothing in this courtyard escapes me."
Feeling her eyes X-ray straight through his skull, Chen Haoyu bolted fast. "Keep busy—got errands!"
Matron Wei chuckled at his back. "Miss hasn't budged an inch, yet Young Master turned around fast—progress at last."
Passing Suxin Thatched Hall, Chen Haoyu paused grinning at the plaque. "Qinggua, why does 'Suxin Thatched Hall' suddenly look elegant and classy to me today?"
"Because Young Madam named it and lives inside," Qinggua nailed it.
Chen Haoyu chuckled and surveyed the whole yard. "Everything in here looks top-notch! Lotus pads in the pond, and that hehuan silk tree—'harmonious union,' what an auspicious name! Think she planted it secretly hoping we'd stay devoted forever? Hahaha!"
Qinggua sighed inside: once a shameless rake, now a lovestruck goofball living in cloud cuckoo land! Nudged by his master's expectant glare, he played along. "No doubt, Young Master—that tree guarantees lifelong harmony!"
"Well said! First wages I earn, first reward goes to you! Come on—time to see Father and Mother!" Full of fresh drive to make something of himself, Chen Haoyu strode out of Moxiang Courtyard.
#CH 241
#TITLE: So He Really Did Change
Eager to see her grandson, Old Madam Xia went straight to her eldest son's courtyard for breakfast to wait for him there. Mid-chat, Yingxue announced Second Young Master—and Chen Haoyu bounced through the door with Qinggua, bowed to his parents, and threw his arms around his grandmother. "Missed you to death, Grandmother!"
Old Madam Xia stroked his hair fondly. "Missed you too. Not mad at us for bolting the gates?"
"Grateful—how could I be mad?" His cheerful tune delighted all three elders.
Hiding his grin behind a stern mask, Chen Jianglin barked, "Warm day—quit leaning on Grandmother and stand straight to answer questions."
Chen Haoyu stood up smart. "Even if Father didn't ask, I've got something to ask you."
"Answer your elders first."
