Yao Qingyan jumped in. "Did Shuzhen truly let go of the rumor grudge?"
"Why wouldn't she? I'm her husband—we're one family, and family doesn't hold grudges! Right, Mother?"
Hearing "one family" roll off his tongue broke Chen Jianglin's stern mask too, laughter echoing round the room. Taking a sip of tea to steady his face, Chen Jianglin asked, "She let you off way too easy after two days. Any actual progress?"
Chen Haoyu paused, then spoke earnest. "Hard to grow much in two days, yet one thing shifted: I'm done roaming outside. Want to stay home—could Father assign me real work in the family business so I can earn my own silver? Hate having empty pockets if I want to buy my wife a gift someday!"
Shock gave way to pure joy on Old Madam Xia's and Yao Qingyan's faces. Unable to hold his straight face, Chen Jianglin beamed. "That's what you came to ask?"
"Yes, sir!"
"Done roaming for good, and ready to learn trade?"
Before Haoyu could answer, Old Madam Xia scolded her eldest son. "My grandson already said yes—quit doubting your own boy!"
"My mistake, Mother, I'll mend my ways!"
Tears of joy shimmered in Yao Qingyan's eyes. "Haoyu really changed—nobody's happier than your mother!"
Seeing how thrilled his parents were stung Chen Haoyu with an unfamiliar blush of shame over how much grief he had caused them before. Brushing past it, he pressed, "When do I start, Father?"
"Anytime you're ready."
"Soon as possible!"
"With southwest orders booming, the silk shop is swamped," Chen Jianglin decided. "Report there—I'll tell Manager Qiu to take you under his wing. Sharp veteran; learn everything he teaches."
"Done! Uh... what's the monthly pay?"
Chen Jianglin laughed and shook his head. "Haven't lifted a finger and already counting coins! Learn the work first; silver follows."
"Starting today?" Old Madam Xia protested. "Once he gets busy, I'll barely see him—let him start tomorrow!"
At Mother's word, Chen Jianglin agreed at once, and all three decided to walk over to Moxiang Courtyard together to thank Shuzhen for her miracle.
Earlier that morning, right after Chen Haoyu left, Matron Wei had invited Qianli Xun out for a walk to digest breakfast and see Chen Manor's blooming gardens for the first time.
Birds sang among flower-laden paths. "Never realized Chen Manor held gardens this gorgeous," Matron Wei marveled.
Thinking of Chen Haoyu's bouquet, Qianli Xun murmured, "Packed with flowers—even roses."
Matron Wei scanned the beds. "Don't see any roses—where?"
Dodging the bouquet story, Qianli Xun said, "Maids mentioned a small rose garden somewhere."
Matron Wei shifted to her real reason for the walk. "Letting go of the rumor grudge in just days—even at my age, I admire your breadth of heart, Miss."
"What good was holding on? Only tortured myself. Letting Chen Haoyu off the hook let me off the hook too—whole world looks brighter without that weight."
"Rare wisdom for someone so young."
"Not me—the elderly nun up by the mountain nunnery opened my eyes."
"Plenty hear sermons; few wake up. You've got real insight, Miss."
They traded playful compliments and laughed as they reached a wide pond thick with large lotus pads, pausing to rest inside a lakeside pavilion.
Gazing at the leaves, Matron Wei dropped a quiet question. "Do you plan on leaving your marriage unconsummated forever, Miss—living separate lives?"
Unflustered, Qianli Xun answered crisp, "Our prenuptial contract spelled it out: zero interference."
"Heard you burned it."
"We'll write a new one."
"I always indulge you, Miss, yet on this point I have to speak plain."
Knowing Matron Wei never wasted breath, Qianli Xun turned attentive. "Go ahead, Matron."
"How do you find the Chen family?"
"Wonderful—aside from Chen Haoyu."
"What if Young Master genuinely reforms?"
"Him? Reform?"
"From what I've watched, brief as your discipline was, he shifted deep."
"Don't buy it, Matron—just a new stunt to disarm me."
"I don't think it's an act. He really changed."
Pause. "So what if he did? Does that mean I have to sleep with him?"
"As someone who's lived long, marrying well is rare as a phoenix feather, Miss. The Chen house outclasses the Lins and Qiaos tenfold—don't throw it away. If Young Master turns good, try opening the door to him step by step."
Her chest tightened. "Yet I don't love Chen Haoyu."
Matron Wei sighed. "How many women in this world ever get to marry the man they love?"
Before she could reply, Kuqiao ran up. "Miss! Old Madam Xia, Eldest Master, and First Madam are waiting in Moxiang Courtyard!"
"Come on," Matron Wei rose. "Bet they came to thank you."
Rising with heavy thoughts, Qianli Xun knew consummation and heirs came with marriage—yet how could she take that step while another man still lived inside her chest? Shen Jianchen's vow at Zuiyun Tower—"staying chaste for you"—warmed and stabbed her in the same breath. What about Mengrong? Forcing his shadow out only made him loom clearer.
Back in Moxiang Courtyard, a warm family tableau waited beneath the hehuan silk tree: Old Madam Xia stretched back in the rattan chair, Chen Jianglin and Yao Qingyan sipping Hongdou's whisked tea at a side table, and Chen Haoyu perched on a low stool leaning affectionately against his grandmother.
Warmth washed over Qianli Xun—this bustling multi-generation family was everything she cherished, truly feeling like home already... if only Chen Haoyu weren't in the frame!
Mid-thought, fingers wrapped around her wrist. "Hey, where'd you wander off to? Kept us waiting!"
Snapping back to see Chen Haoyu holding her hand, she shook him loose at once. "Keep your paws off me!"
"Okay, okay, hands off!" He retreated straight back to his stool beside Grandmother.
Matron Wei noted it all silently—fond of the home, not ready for the husband—and stepped in smooth. "Had I known you three were visiting, I wouldn't have dragged Miss out walking."
Hongdou and Amei brought two extra chairs. Matron Wei sat at Old Madam Xia's invitation, while Qianli Xun stayed standing a step away, soaking in the scene so deep she forgot to bow.
Yao Qingyan rose and walked over. "Why hanging back, Shuzhen—mad at us?"
"Not at all—the scene just looked so lovely I wanted to memorize it."
Taking her hand, Yao Qingyan smiled. "If it's lovely, step inside and become part of the picture."
"Become part of the picture"—a simple line that hit like philosophy. Why stand outside admiring warmth when she could step in? Letting Yao Qingyan draw her under the hehuan shade, she curtsied to the elders. "Had I known you liked sitting here, I'd have set out more chairs."
"No need," Old Madam Xia waved. "Too many chairs clutter the charm—one rattan lounger and one table look perfect."
"We don't drop by every day—keep your courtyard tidy. Sit down!" Chen Jianglin urged.
Settling beside Matron Wei, Qianli Xun felt Chen Haoyu's glued-on gaze, shot him a glare—which he blithely ignored, sneaking peeks the second she looked away. Watching from across the table, Yao Qingyan glowed inside: plain as day her son had reformed out of sheer love! Shuzhen really was Chen Manor's lucky star.
"We three came to thank you, Shuzhen," Yao Qingyan said.
"First for letting go of those old rumors," Chen Jianglin added, "and second for turning Haoyu around."
Refusing false credit, Qianli Xun spoke straight. "No thanks needed. Dropping the rumors was for my own peace, and I take zero credit for Chen Haoyu—I only meant to pay him back, not reform him. Nobody truly changes in two days anyway."
"See?" Chen Haoyu puffed his chest. "I was solid stock all along—needed zero reforming!"
Leaning back in the dappled shade, Old Madam Xia smiled. "Intentions aside, the results shine bright—credit belongs to you. Name any reward you want for giving Grandmother back a fine grandson, and even if it's tough, I'll deliver!"
About to decline, Qianli Xun caught Matron Wei's gaze and remembered the pavilion warning about consummation. Sooner or later these kind elders would press for grandsons—better lock in breathing room right now while they were offering a blank check!
"Since Grandmother offers a reward, I won't be shy. Keep gold, silver, land, and jewels—I only ask the elders for one promise."
#CH 242
#TITLE: Each Generation Carves Its Own Fate
Before Qianli Xun opened her mouth, Matron Wei already knew what was coming—that was the exact reason she had nudged her mistress by the pond earlier, preparing her to ask smoothly instead of clashing head-on later.
"Name it," Chen Jianglin invited.
Standing to bow before all three elders, Qianli Xun spoke clear and firm. "I ask Grandmother, Father-in-law, and Mother-in-law to promise never to press me to consummate my marriage with Chen Haoyu before I truly develop feelings for him."
Silence dropped over the table as disappointment dimmed all three elders' faces.
A pang hit Chen Haoyu too—proof she had not fallen for him yet—yet fearing the elders might scold her, he jumped straight in to smooth things over. "Deal, deal! I promise! Only reason you don't like me yet is you haven't seen my best traits—once I show them off day by day, you'll fall for me soon enough!"
His breezy chime broke the chill. Qianli Xun exhaled in relief, finding his blind cockiness oddly bearable for the first time, while Matron Wei hid a small smile—the young master was growing genuinely likable.
With her grandson speaking up, Old Madam Xia nodded. "If Haoyu agrees, I won't oppose it. Still, your ideas are nothing like other brides'—takes this old head time to adjust."
Awkward discussing bedroom matters with a daughter-in-law, Chen Jianglin nudged Yao Qingyan with a look.
Still glum that Shuzhen was so picky, Yao Qingyan spoke up. "We treated your prenuptial contract as young folks playing games, Shuzhen. Since you're wed and Haoyu is mending his ways, why let a scrap of paper stand between you?"
"I already burned the contract," Qianli Xun noted.
Yao Qingyan lit up. "Good riddance! Then build a real life together—consummation comes naturally soon enough!"
"Burned it in a temper—I plan to write a new one with Chen Haoyu."
"Count me out!" Chen Haoyu protested. "A real man's word weighs nine tripods—I'll keep my promise in my heart, no need for paper chains! Relax, I won't force you into bed."
As if you could force me! Qianli Xun scoffed inside.
"Don't bother rewriting it, Shuzhen," Yao Qingyan urged. "A wife enters her husband's house to carry on the line. Without consummation, when will your father-in-law and I ever hold a grandson?"
Confident he would win Zhu Shuzhen inside twelve months, Chen Haoyu grinned at his mother. "Relax, Mother—guaranteed grandson in one year flat!"
All three elders burst out laughing—until Qianli Xun cut in cool: "If Mother-in-law is in a hurry for grandsons, easy—I'll happily help Chen Haoyu take a concubine to bear children."
Smiles vanished on the spot.
"No way!" Chen Haoyu snapped. "I only have children with the woman I love!"
Seeing stalemate looming, Matron Wei stepped in smooth as oil. "Congratulations, Old Madam, Master, and Madam!"
"Congratulations on what?" Yao Qingyan sighed.
"Any normal morning, Young Master would have bolted past the manor gate at dawn. Freed after days of discipline, instead of running wild, he sits chatting with his elders, stands up for his wife, and steps up as a working Chen heir—isn't that worth celebrating?"
"Too right!" Old Madam Xia brightened. "Even begged his father for a job in the business today!"
Yao Qingyan smiled too, forgetting her gloom, and gestured to her daughter-in-law. "Quit standing, Shuzhen—sit down!"
Since only Grandmother had yielded so far, Qianli Xun sat back down watching Matron Wei work her magic.
"Everything is already flowing in the right direction," Matron Wei continued. "Rushing spoils it; going with the flow keeps hearts light and brings happy outcomes naturally. None of us see tomorrow—look at Young Master! Two days ago he haunted brothels, and today..."
Right on cue, Chen Haoyu vowed loud, "Never stepping foot in a brothel again!"
All three elders bloomed with pride.
"Miss's request sounded blunt today, yet that's today's feeling—who knows how her heart shifts tomorrow?" Matron Wei added smoothly.
Chen Jianglin nodded at last. "Leave young folks' business to young folks. Parents fretting changes nothing—each generation carves its own fate."
With her husband yielding and Matron Wei's wisdom ringing true, Yao Qingyan let go with a warm smile. "Forget it, Shuzhen—consummate when you please. If Mother stays out of it, so will I. No more bringing it up!"
Hearing their generous surrender stirred unexpected guilt in Qianli Xun; standing in their shoes, any parent would ache hearing a bride refuse their son. Rising, she bowed deep. "Thank you for your grace, Grandmother, Father-in-law, and Mother-in-law. Words can't repay this—from today on, Chen Manor is my true home."
"One family doesn't talk like strangers," Old Madam Xia beamed. "Consider your reward paid—no asking for extras later!"
Laughter filled the shade beneath the hehuan tree. For the first time in his life, Chen Haoyu savored true family warmth—glancing across at Zhu Shuzhen, amazed how loving one person turned the whole world bright.
Once the elders left, Qianli Xun threw her arms around Matron Wei in gratitude, while Chen Haoyu watched eyes sparkling—this matron held superpowers! Time to ask her for tips!
As mistress returned to Suxin Thatched Hall and Matron Wei headed to the back courtyard, Chen Haoyu started trailing the matron—paused briefly when Ugly Maid asked to borrow Qinggua, waving them off ("Take him, just don't bug me!") while Ugly Maid hauled a reluctant Qinggua toward the West Courtyard.
Reaching the back yard, Chen Haoyu found Matron Wei already waiting. "Need something, Young Master?"
Flashing a big thumbs-up, he grinned. "You're number one, Matron! Teach me—you know her better than anyone. How do I make the tigress fall for me?"
"Easy. Rule one: stop calling Miss 'tigress.'"
"Never again!"
"Rule two: learn how to care for her."
"How?"
"Watch Eldest Master."
"Got it! Anything else?"
"Your soft tactics are working fine—keep at it." Turning, Matron Wei stepped into Jingyi Hall.
Left blinking in awe, Chen Haoyu muttered, "She wasn't even in the room when I used soft tactics—how did she know?! Must have spies everywhere!"
Hurrying back to the front yard to charm Zhu Shuzhen, he bumped into Qinggua trudging up looking like a frost-wilted eggplant.
"What's with the funeral face?"
"Over in the West Courtyard I overheard Asheng confess to Hongdou—and she said yes!" Qinggua groaned. "Got so mad I marched Ugly Maid right in front of Hongdou yelling 'Fine, I've got a sweetheart too—Ugly Maid!' Regretted it the second it left my mouth!"
"Hahaha! Saves me playing matchmaker—you and Ugly Maid are meant to be!" Throwing an arm over his shoulder, Chen Haoyu laid out brotherly logic. "Ugly Maid's a solid pick—knows kung fu, nobody dares touch you when she's around."
"Hongdou knows kung fu too!"
"Sure, except her heart belongs elsewhere—marry her and she'd stray sooner or later. Ugly Maid only has eyes for you! Drop Hongdou among those seven male servants in the West Courtyard—sleep easy?"
Qinggua shook his head. "Nope."
"Drop Ugly Maid among them?"
"Sleep like a baby!"
"With Hongdou, you'd fret every time she spoke to another man, slack off serving me, and risk getting replaced! With Ugly Maid, zero worries—and she'll wait on you hand and foot! Which wins?"
"Put like that... Ugly Maid wins!"
"Bingo! Settle down with Ugly Maid. Now come along—time to butter up my wife!"
Qinggua tugged his sleeve. "Wait, Young Master—which kind is Young Madam? Sleep-easy, or fret-all-night?"
"You and me aren't in the same league!"
"Didn't Prince Yi raid your wedding?"
"Scram! Comparing your mess to mine—I've got everything! Besides, the tig—er, Zhu Shuzhen is already my wedded wife! What's to fret over? Move it, time to win her over!"
Trailing behind, Qinggua snickered inside: Using "butter up" for his own wife—Young Master sure dropped his price tag!
Slipping into Suxin Thatched Hall, Chen Haoyu found Zhu Shuzhen writing nonstop at her desk as expected—wondered how short poems took all day to write.
"Young Master is here," Kuqiao alerted her.
Qianli Xun glanced up. "Freeze right there—talk from where you stand!"
"Come on, I'm your husband and master of Moxiang Courtyard—standing like a lackey looks ridiculous!" Dropping into a chair uninvited, he called, "Kuqiao, heard your whisked tea is top-notch—make your young master a bowl!"
"He's got Qinggua—since when do you wait on him?" Qianli Xun snapped, halting Kuqiao.
Unruffled, Chen Haoyu grinned. "New chore, Qinggua: learn tea whisking from Kuqiao! Soon I'll set a tea table in Boya Study and try out this classy hobby myself."
Qianli Xun laid down her brush. "Spit it out—I'm busy."
"Hunched over a desk all day will give you a spare tire around your waist! Come on, let me take you out for a stroll."
Certain now he was making a play for her—and equally certain she had zero interest—she refused flat. "Zero interest strolling with you."
"Say what you want, I won't get mad—got one suggestion though."
"Speak up or get lost."
"Quit calling yourself 'this old lady'—doesn't match your gorgeous face."
"None of your business! I like talking like that—hate it, stay out of my sight!"
"Can't stay out of sight—same courtyard, bumping into each other nonstop, plus you're my wife! Expect plenty of visits!"
Dreading daily interruptions, Qianli Xun switched to sweet persuasion. "Tell you what, Chen Haoyu—take a concubine, okay? Say yes, and I'll treat you like my best pal and even jump in to beat up anyone outside who messes with you!"
#CH 243
#TITLE: Winning a Wife Takes Method
Twice in one day she had tried pawning him off onto a concubine—how desperate was she to hand him away?
Swallowing the sting, Chen Haoyu turned her down flat. "One wife fills my hands—why invite another headache? Quit bringing up concubines."
Eager to splash cold water on his sudden devotion, Qianli Xun spoke blunt. "I've seen plenty of types like you—spoiled rich playboys, fickle and shameless, waking up one morning playing reformed saint hunting one true love while fishing for applause like their filthy past never existed! Makes my stomach turn. Save the syrupy lines—I don't buy them."
Nothing she threw could bruise him now. "What rich playboy? I'm dead broke! I never met anyone worth settling down for before, so I ran wild. Now I found the one I love and want to straighten out—why hold that against me?"
Qianli Xun gave a scornful huff.
Remembering Matron Wei's rule two—care for her—and how she had devoured his grilled skewers at the chuiwan match, Chen Haoyu lit up. "Cooped up in Chen Manor gets dull. I'm free today—let me take you to West Lake! We'll grill skewers by the shore and take in the view—nobody grills meat tastier than me!"
Memories of his noisy lakeside picnic last year lit a fuse. "Got zero civic decency, Chen Haoyu?!"
"Inviting you for skewers and lake views—what's civic decency got to do with it?!"
"Last year you and your gang trampled flowers, smoked out the shore, and probably left heaps of trash behind—ruining gorgeous West Lake! Trashing nature yourself and trying to drag me along?!"
Scolded by the woman he loved, Chen Haoyu sheepishly conceded. "My bad, my bad—no more grilling by West Lake! Don't stay mad. Where do you want to go? I'll take you anywhere."
"Nowhere! Vanish right now and quit pestering me!"
Struck out again—clearly winning her heart was going to take serious strategy. Since he did not start at the silk shop until tomorrow, time to go pick his father's brain. Standing, he smiled. "Leave you to your work, Wife."
"Don't let the door hit you."
Stepping outside Suxin Thatched Hall, Chen Haoyu groaned. "How did I marry the toughest woman on earth—and go crazy enough to fall for her?!"
"Karma," Qinggua chimed in.
"Watch your lip!" Out of habit his leg twitched, yet remembering his promise to Qinggua, he kept his boot planted.
Surprised not to get kicked, Qinggua turned sheepish. "Just kidding, Young Master."
"No, explain—why karma?"
"You hooked way too many girls easy before, Young Master. Heaven sending an impossible nut like Young Madam balances the books!"
"Fair point—I'll take my medicine since I went nuts falling for her."
Reaching his parents' courtyard, Chen Haoyu waved Yingxue quiet and slipped inside unannounced to study his father's playbook up close.
There sat Chen Jianglin at the vanity, deftly penciling Yao Qingyan's eyebrows while both traded soft smiles.
"Since marrying you, I've lost all skill at doing my own brows," Yao Qingyan teased.
"Why lift a brush while I'm here?"
"You spoiled me rotten."
"Who else should I spoil except my wife?"
Watching in awe, Chen Haoyu realized his father was the undisputed king of sweet talk—his own lines sounded childish next to that! He cleared his throat: "Ahem!"
Finishing the brow, Chen Jianglin glanced over. "Haoyu! Come sit."
Yao Qingyan rose and took his arm. "Not keeping Shuzhen company in Moxiang Courtyard?"
"Came to ask Father for advice."
Thrilled to see her boy transformed, Yao Qingyan smiled. "Leave you two men to talk—I'm off to Old Madam Xia's. Storyteller's due soon with Master Qianli Xun's brand-new tale!" She left with Yingxue.
"Sit," Chen Jianglin invited. "Starting at the silk shop tomorrow—ask anything you need to know."
Chen Haoyu gave a sheepish chuckle before blurting out, "Not about business—came to ask your secret for winning over a wife! Heh..."
Chen Jianglin burst out laughing. "Winning your wife is just as big as business—came to the right teacher!"
Emboldened, Chen Haoyu leaned forward. "Pass down every trick, Father, so you hold a grandson faster!"
"No magic tricks—just putting your heart in."
"I put my heart in! Zhu Shuzhen won't bite!"
"Calling your own wife by her full name isn't putting your heart in."
"Dropping the surname starting now!"
Seeing his boy drop all defiance warmed Chen Jianglin's chest—marrying the Zhu girl had been pure genius. He held up three fingers. "Winning a wife takes three pillars. First: absolute devotion. Nothing ruins a home faster than a wandering eye leaving your wife in tears. Look at me—ever took a concubine?"
"Easy, I can do that. Second?"
"Second: show up beside her. Busy as work gets, carve out time for your wife so she never sits home wondering if you're chasing women or visiting brothels. A worried wife means a stormy house, and a man with a stormy house fails at everything."
"Noted! Third?"
"Third—and biggest: master one skill your wife needs every day, and do it better than anyone else. When she reaches for you first every single time she needs it, she can't live without you—and your place in her heart is locked."
Chen Haoyu flashed a huge thumbs-up. "Genius, Father! No wonder Mother never fights with you! Painting Mother's eyebrows—that's your secret skill?"
"What else?"
"How long did it take to learn?"
"Started on our wedding day. Clumsy at first—your mother laughed at me—yet after a year my strokes turned smooth, and she stopped touching a brow pencil or letting maids near her face. Every morning she calls for me."
Years back, Chen Haoyu had scoffed at a grown man doing his wife's makeup; now he bowed to his father's genius. "Pillar three takes homework—I need to watch Shuzhen close, spot what she needs daily, and master it."
"Glad to see you putting real heart into Shuzhen," Chen Jianglin smiled. "Good girl with a fiery streak—the day she turns gentle around you, you've won."
Armed with his master plan, Chen Haoyu bowed out and marched home pondering how to uncover Zhu Shuzhen's daily habit—then snapped his fingers at Qinggua. "Go sneak Kuqiao over to Boya Study! Important intel needed!"
Back at Moxiang Courtyard, Chen Haoyu waited in Boya Study while Qinggua crept up to Suxin Thatched Hall, craning his neck through the doorway until Kuqiao tapped his shoulder from behind. "Peeking like a thief, Qinggua?"
"Looking for you, Sister Kuqiao! Young Master just got master-level wife-wooing secrets from Eldest Master and needs your help on the toughest step!"
Pleased at his master's sincerity, Kuqiao followed along—and walked into Boya Study to find Chen Haoyu reading Wang Wei's poems on his own without being forced!
Even Qinggua stared. "Books actually fun now, Young Master?"
Setting down the volume, Chen Haoyu tutted. "Uncultured bumpkin—ever hear 'inside books wait golden houses and jade beauties'?"
"Used to say books held nothing but dog crap, Young Master!"
"Asking for trouble bringing up old quotes?" Spotting Kuqiao, he beamed. "Bring a seat for Kuqiao, Qinggua!"
"Never offered me a seat—why seat her?"
"Comparing yourself to Kuqiao? Sit anywhere, Kuqiao!"
Kuqiao curtsied. "No need for formality, Young Master. Anything good for Miss, ask away."
"Hear that, Qinggua? Same rank, ten times the tact—stop exposing my flaws and learn from her!" Turning back to Kuqiao, he got straight to business. "You can see I'm dead serious about your mistress, yet she won't budge. Tell me: what does Shuzhen need most every single day?"
"Every day?" Kuqiao thought hard. "Aside from writing poems... and practicing martial arts..." (biting back huaben).
Both dead ends—poetry baffled him and his grappling moves crumbled before her fists. "Aside from those two—some daily routine where if she misses it, her whole day feels off?"
Kuqiao brightened. "Does drinking my whisked tea count?"
Chen Haoyu shot out of his chair! "Count?! Bullseye! I can learn tea whisking! How hooked is she on your tea?"
"Less obsessed, more habit—starts every morning with a bowl. One busy morning I missed making it, and she fidgeted nonstop until I whisked her a bowl and she relaxed."
"Jackpot! I'm mastering whisked tea till she can't live without me! Hahaha! Keep this secret from her for now, Kuqiao!"
"My lips are sealed, Young Master."
To beat Kuqiao's skills, he needed a real master—the female tea artist at Yongtai Teahouse! Tuition took silver, and his purse was bone dry, so he marched straight to Old Madam Xia to ask for a loan to repay from his future shop wages. Hearing he was learning a skill just to win over his bride, Old Madam Xia beamed, handed over the silver outright as a gift, and called it seed money for her future great-grandson.
#CH 244
#TITLE: Haodong's Scheme Collapses
Within a single day, word of Chen Haoyu's overnight transformation reached Second Uncle and Third Uncle's courtyards. At the afternoon storytelling session, Old Madam Xia and Yao Qingyan had beamed nonstop, praising Shuzhen and calling Haoyu's reform a blessing for the Chen clan right in front of Madam Bao and Madam Cui.
When Chen Jiangmu came home after dark, Madam Cui sat pouting in silence until he pried the story out of her.
"Good news indeed," Chen Jiangmu chuckled. "Another steady Chen son pitching in on family business."
"Means I have to write my surname upside down!" Madam Cui grumbled.
"Huh?"
"Swore inside my head that if the Zhu girl actually reformed Haoyu, I'd write 'Cui' upside down!"
"Say it out loud?"
"Just in my head."
"Then nobody knows—why beat yourself up? Help me out of my robe; long day."
Relaxing, Madam Cui helped him undress. "Lesson learned—never underestimate folks again. Reforming Haoyu in days flat—that Zhu girl has real tricks."
"Got fists that scare him straight—first time I've seen a wife whip a husband into shape!"
"Makes sense too," Chen Jiangmu mused sitting on the bed. "Second marriage after a divorce—she can't afford a second split, so she hardened her heart to mold a decent husband. Helps that Chen men cherish their wives deep down, or nobody could have flipped him that fast."
Hanging his robe, Madam Cui scoffed. "Except Haodong! Spotted fresh bruises on Anya's neck today."
"Haodong shines everywhere else—beating his wife is rotten, yet Second Brother's yard isn't ours to meddle in." Blowing out the candle, they turned in.
Over in Chen Jiangshu's room, disbelief hung thick. Madam Bao sat untouched at her vanity while Chen Jiangshu brooded on the bed, Chen Haodong pacing before them.
"Father, is it true Haoyu starts under Manager Qiu at the silk shop tomorrow?"
"True—Old Madam Xia and First Sister-in-law bragged all afternoon," Madam Bao groaned. "Pushing his wedding backfired!"
"My fault," Chen Haodong kicked himself. "Just wanted him miserable under a fierce wife—never dreamed of this!"
Chen Jiangshu looked up. "So he joins the silk shop—what threat is he? You've worked business since childhood; worried he'll catch up?"
"Never in a million years," Chen Haodong scoffed, then frowned. "Still, flipping overnight in two days? What if he's just faking reform to dodge the tigress's fists?"
"Makes sense—Haoyu's been slick at putting on shows since he was a toddler," Madam Bao agreed.
"Guessing gets us nowhere," Chen Jiangshu said. "Sound him out tomorrow and find out if it's real before making our next move."
Agreeing, Chen Haodong decided to ride with Haoyu to the silk shop next morning; his trusting cousin never hid a thing from him.
Stepping back into his own courtyard, Chen Haodong met Xiaocui bowing in the dark. "Young Master, Miss asks to speak with you."
Surprised by her first invitation, a flicker of warmth lit Chen Haodong's chest—only to freeze dead at Ye Anya's icy stare inside. "What do you want?"
"My mind is set," Ye Anya spoke level. "Grant me a mutual divorce."
Like a bolt from clear sky! Chen Haodong lunged forward and snatched her collar. "Barren hen—I spared you repudiation, and you dare ask for mutual divorce?! Not in a million years!"
Closing her eyes as two tears slipped free, Ye Anya murmured, "Then repudiate me."
Suspicion flared. "Been cozying up to Haoyu's divorced wife lately—did she put this poison in your head?!"
"Between you and me—leave everyone else out." Ready even to die, she would not step back.
He shoved her clear. "Not repudiating you yet—maybe when I feel like it."
"What will it take for you to cast me out?"
Her dead-cold eagerness snuffed every spark of warmth inside him. Stepping close, he hissed, "Shut up about divorce, play the perfect wife until next year when the Chen heir gets named—then we'll talk. Catch me in a good mood, maybe I'll even grant mutual divorce."
"Give me your word?"
The flare of relief on her face stabbed straight through his pride. "That desperate to get away from me?"
"Every waking breath I want out."
Already sore over Haoyu joining the silk shop, that blade pushed Chen Haodong past breaking. Yanking her onto the bed, he rained blows down while Xiaocui wept helpless outside the door: "When will this nightmare ever end?"
Next dawn, Chen Haoyu rose bright and early for his first day at the silk shop. Passing Suxin Thatched Hall's shut doors, he called through the wood, "Wife, heading to the silk shop! First day takes getting used to, so I'll stay till dark—don't miss me too much!"
Doing her hair at the vanity, Qianli Xun ignored him.
"Pretty thoughtful, reporting before leaving," Kuqiao smiled.
Sliding a hairpin home, Qianli Xun snorted. "Go tell him to quit reporting his schedule to me."
Cracking the door, Kuqiao delivered the message—only for Chen Haoyu to beam. "My wife's just trying to spare me trouble! Wouldn't dream of skipping reports—leave her fretting I'm chasing skirts outside and I'd get zero work done!"
Kuqiao hid a giggle behind her sleeve until Qianli Xun marched to the door scowling. "Quit yelling 'wife,' gives me hives! Move along and quit pestering me!"
Freshly dressed and radiant in morning light, she made Chen Haoyu glow. "One glimpse of my radiant wife at dawn feels like spring breeze—won't feel tired all day!"
"Keep spouting mush instead of moving and taste my fist!"
"Going, going!" SLAM! The door shut in his face.
Chen Haoyu chanted under his breath: "Not mad, not mad, not a drop mad!"
Trailing behind, Qinggua blinked. "Brushed you off flat, Young Master—really not mad?"
"She's my wife—why fight her? Chen men don't snap at their wives! Father's my blueprint."
"Not all Chen men," Qinggua muttered. "Heard Eldest Young Master beats First Young Madam all the time."
Chen Haoyu stopped dead. "Who told you that? Never heard a word!"
"Always out partying—when did you ever listen to manor news?"
"If that's true, I'm having words with Brother Dong!"
Outside the main gate, Chen Haodong stood waiting by a carriage with a bright smile. "Heard you're starting at the silk shop—waited special so we can ride together!"
"Awesome!" Climbing aboard while Qinggua drove, Chen Haoyu beamed as his cousin studied him close.
"Did Younger Sister-in-law really whip you into shape?"
"Who needed whipping? I was sharp all along!"
Relaxing at his familiar swagger, Chen Haodong smiled easy. "If the shop bores you, slip out and play—I'll cover for you."
"Appreciate you always watching out for me, Brother Dong, yet I'm a married man now. Can't stay a loafer—she's the famous Poetess of Jiangnan! If I keep partying, folks will mock her for marrying a deadbeat."
Chen Haodong tensed. "You're serious—not just faking to dodge her fists?"
"Think I could act this good?" Leaning close, Chen Haoyu grinned. "Never guess it, Brother Dong—I went crazy and fell head over heels for the tigress! First time loving anyone feels wild—going all out to win her heart too! Heh heh..."
Half the grand plot lay in ashes—and hot envy burned in Chen Haodong's gut. How did this spoiled fool stumble into loving his own bride while Chen Haodong's love for Ye Anya rotted into fists and hatred?
Masking his venom, Chen Haodong probed, "Dead serious? Not pulling my leg?"
"Swear to heaven!"
Force-smiling, Chen Haodong plotted inside: Fall for her all you want—I'll dig up enough dirt from your past to blow your cozy marriage sky-high!
Remembering Qinggua's whisper, Chen Haoyu asked low, "Hey, Brother Dong—heard rumors you hit Sister-in-law. True?"
"Pure servant gossip," Chen Haodong brushed it off smooth. "Don't listen to trash."
Convinced no standout gentleman like Brother Dong could hit a woman, Chen Haoyu dropped it.
Back in Moxiang Courtyard after breakfast, Qianli Xun returned to her new huaben about star-crossed lovers—only for her own ache to stall her brush. Having Kuqiao stow the pages, she asked for the peeing clay doll again, smiling faintly at memories of Shen Jianchen before gloom returned.
Surrounded by loyal maids, friendly elders, and a smitten husband knocking at her door, bone-deep loneliness still wrapped around her. This was supposed to be a bridal chamber shared with a beloved partner, yet she walked in and out alone. Banishing her husband out back might look cold to outsiders, yet forcing herself into a loveless bed was worse. Even with Chen Haoyu changing, loving him felt miles out of reach—leaving her sharing the exact solitude Zhu Shuzhen had known in this same century.
Setting the clay doll back in its box, she spread fresh paper and brushed out a ci lyric:
"Walking alone, sitting alone, / Singing alone, drinking alone, and sleeping alone. / Standing still in heavy sorrow, / Helpless as the light spring chill creeps in. / Who sees this grief? / Tears wash half the faded rouge from my cheeks. / Sorrow and sickness follow close behind; / Trimming the cold lamp wick down to ash, no dream will come." —"Jianzi Mulan Hua: Spring Resentment" [TN: Translator's rendering]
#CH 245
#TITLE: Sisters-in-Law Speak of Royal Guests
Reading back through Zhu Shuzhen's lyric, Qianli Xun felt the poetess's deeper despair—sick in bed with no warm arms beside her, only tears for company.
It dragged back a memory of falling sick before her transmigration. Rarely ill, whenever a cold caught Qianli Xun it knocked her flat—stuffy nose, cough, raging fever. One month her entire Qianli Fist Manor troupe flew out of province for a film shoot, leaving her solo in her twenty-second-floor apartment writing novels. A brutal flu ambushed her; every muscle throbbed, the thermometer read 38.6°C, and she lacked even the strength to shake the mercury down. Fever meds sat in the drawer, yet water sat out of reach. Trying to stand—years of kung fu useless against a virus—she took two wobbly steps and crumpled onto the floorboards, head spinning too hard to rise.
Her phone buzzed on the nightstand. Praying a disciple had called, she crawled over—and saw Shen Jianchen's name flashing. Too miserable to be proud, she swiped the green answer button and hit speaker.
"Hey, Qianli Xun, heard your crew went filming. Bored alone—want company?"
"I'm... sick," she croaked. "Come over... door code is... my birthday."
"Sick?! Hang tight—on my way!"
When he hung up, rare comfort washed over her; leaning her head against the mattress on the floor, she blacked out.
When she woke, tucked warm under her duvet with a cooling gel patch across her forehead, savory steam filled the room—Shen Jianchen standing beside her in an apron holding a steaming bowl of tomato-egg noodles.
"Awake! Made tomato-egg noodles—best thing for a fever," he said, setting the bowl down and sitting by her bed. "Never saw anyone catch a cold this fierce—good thing I called!"
"Thanks... grab me water for the fever pills in the drawer."
"Checked already—every box was expired! Ran downstairs to the pharmacy for fresh ones and already got them down you."
"Wait—I took meds? Zero memory!"
"Found you slumped on the floor half-conscious—somebody could've kidnapped you without you noticing! Lifted you into bed, ran for fresh medicine, and you opened your mouth like a good kid without fighting." Peeling off the cooling patch, he felt her brow. "Fever dropped a bit. Sit up and eat before your next dose—don't take pills on an empty stomach."
Propping herself up against the headboard, feeling lighter already, a sudden thought crossed her mind: Shen Jianchen isn't half bad—if I ever decide to date or marry, someone like him works.
He held out the bowl with a tease. "Not taking it? Waiting for me to spoon-feed you? Happy to oblige, though you'd probably deck me."
Snatching the bowl, she shot back, "Got two hands of my own—who needs feeding?!"
"Shuzhen! Quit hiding at your desk—I came all this way, come chat with me!"
Chen Wenxin's bright voice broke the memory as she walked in with Yuegui—her sister-in-law's first visit since the wedding.
Shaking off the past, Qianli Xun jumped up to greet her. "Missed you, Sister-in-law!"
"Even the yard felt fresh walking in, and look at this room—no wonder you flipped Haoyu overnight!" Chen Wenxin glanced around, clearly straight from the elders' rooms.
"Where's Laibao?"
"Playing at Grandmother's with the maids—snuck over to catch up with you. You've transformed the whole manor! Before, elders barely visited Grandmother; now Mother and both aunts gather there laughing nonstop, giving you all the credit—while you sit cooped up alone in here!"
"Grandmother's got plenty of company, freeing me to write poems and live up to my title."
"Fresh lyric?" Stepping to the desk, Chen Wenxin read the ink and frowned. "Why still writing doom and gloom like the Chens mistreat you?" Catching Shuzhen's hands, she teased, "Rosy cheeks, bright eyes, healthy as a horse—what 'sorrow and sickness'? Pure melodrama!"
Qianli Xun burst out laughing. "Call it melodrama then! Sit down and chat."
"Sitting indoors wastes gorgeous spring—let's walk the gardens!"
Strolling through the southern garden beneath snow-white fringe trees, crimson kapok, yellow trumpet trees, and blooming magnolias while Kuqiao and Yuegui chatted behind them, they walked a footpath carpeted in fallen petals. Impossible not to tread on them—bringing Lu You's famous plum-blossom couplet straight to mind: "Fallen to mud and ground to dust, / Only their fragrance lingers unchanged." [TN: Translator's rendering]
Petals bloomed brilliant, dropped to soil, and left behind a breath of scent—just like human life returning to earth. Having walked two lifetimes without knowing which was dream and which reality, she had left messy web novels and loyal fist disciples behind in her first world; here, even if known only as Zhu Shuzhen, she wanted Qianli Xun to leave her own lasting scent before parting.
"Thank you for reforming Haoyu, Shuzhen," Chen Wenxin broke into her reverie.
"Got enough thanks from the elders already—don't stack yours on, Sister-in-law, or everybody's in for a letdown."
"Meaning?"
"Bet Chen Haoyu won't last a week." Blunt words she kept from elders slipped easy to Wenxin.
"Nobody knows my kid brother like me—once he flips for real, he sticks."
Letting time settle the bet, Qianli Xun kept silent as Wenxin added, "Since he's turning good, try opening your heart to him. I wasn't madly in love when I married your brother either, yet look how happy we are! Good character matters most; love grows after marriage."
Spotting a gentle lobby from the elders, Qianli Xun offered a neat stall. "If character matters most, let time test Chen Haoyu first—once I'm convinced, we'll talk."
"That's all I wanted to hear!" Satisfied, Wenxin walked quietly beside her through the petals before asking, "Know why I visited Chen Manor today?"
"Tell me."
"Father-in-law sent me."
"My father sent you to visit your own maiden home?"
"Lin'an's hosting a major banquet inviting the Chens—he sent me to pass word in person."
"Usually they just send an invitation card. What's special about this banquet?"
"Haven't heard?"
"Heard what?"
"Prince Yi and Princess Jiahe got back from Bianliang!"
Back already! Joy and dread collided inside Qianli Xun's chest before she managed, "When did they arrive?"
"First thing this morning—slipped in quiet just like they left. Good thing Father-in-law kept sharp and told Butler Li at Youlin Retreat to tip him off the second they arrived. He led Lin'an's officials to pay respects at dawn, and tomorrow throws a grand welcome-and-wedding banquet for the royal newlyweds."
Wedding banquet—they were husband and wife now, and Mengrong was Princess Consort Yi. "Still, why send you in person instead of a card?"
"Think about it," Wenxin prodded gently.
Memory stung: Prince Yi kneeling outside Zhu Manor trying to block the wedding, raiding the bridal procession, Mengrong bleeding on a blade—both Zhu and Chen houses walking on eggshells praying royal wrath would not fall.
"Chen Manor is footing the entire banquet bill," Wenxin added.
Guilt tightened Qianli Xun's chest. "Prince Yi isn't petty—he wouldn't punish either family over his own impulsive stunts."
"Royal pride still demands grand face," Wenxin sighed. "Anyone at the chuiwan match saw his heart—marrying you meant Chen Manor beat an imperial prince for the bride! Father and Father-in-law started planning this feast the day Prince Yi left just to smooth every feather."
Dreading facing Mengrong before she was ready, Qianli Xun asked, "Who's invited?"
"High officials and elites with primary wives only—I go thanks to your brother. You and Haoyu aren't on the list. Only young exception is Qiao Wenxian bringing Miao Zhiyu alongside Master and Madam Qiao."
Qianli Xun let out a long silent breath—spared for now. Facing Mengrong was inevitable sooner or later, just not tomorrow. Wait—why shrink like a criminal when she had never betrayed Mengrong? Yet thinking nonstop about Shen Jianchen—did that really leave her hands clean?
#CH 246
#TITLE: Prince Yi and Princess Jiahe Return to Lin'an
The Bianliang wedding had been grand enough to please Qiao Mengrong—married to Brother at last under His Majesty's edict, even if another woman occupied his heart.
Yet on their wedding night, Brother never lifted her red bridal veil. He left only one sentence before walking out: "Mengrong, I can step into Zhao Pu's shoes to look after you and marry you, yet I cannot take his place in the bridal bed—because in my heart you have always been my little sister."
Left alone in the bridal chamber, Qiao Mengrong wept rivers—and every tear hardened her hatred for Zhu Shuzhen, the thief who had stolen Brother's heart.
The morning after the wedding, Brother rushed to head back to Lin'an—and Qiao Mengrong rushed right alongside him, burning to launch her payback. Needing a sharp elder ally besides Xilan, she told Matron Zou everything that had happened in Lin'an, and the matron signed on at once. "Plenty of stewards watch Prince Yi's Manor in the capital. I'll ride to Lin'an with Your Highness and see for myself what kind of fox bewitched Prince Yi out of his own wedding bed!"
Travel-worn back at Youlin Retreat, Qiao Mengrong rested to gather strength and plot her strike against her former confidante.
Shen Jianchen knew full well how deeply his choice cut Mengrong—yet shutting his eyes and bedding a girl he viewed as a sister would make him feel lower than a beast. Maybe one day he would open his heart and make her his wife in truth, just not today—and besides, he had sworn to Qianli Xun to stay chaste.
The vow felt both noble and absurd. In a rotting dynasty steered by a foolish emperor and corrupt ministers where a man could not save the realm, keeping personal honor stood as small nobility. Yet Qianli Xun might not even care, leaving him married by fate while guarding fidelity for another man's wife—crazy to anyone watching.
All along the road back from Bianliang, he decided he needed real work: first to keep from sitting face-to-face with Mengrong in awkward guilt, and second to fill his hours so Qianli Xun might fade from his mind—freeing him at last to accept Mengrong as his true wife.
Hardly settled indoors, Zhu Xiyan arrived with a delegation of Lin'an officials. "Forgive us disturbing Your Highness after your long journey! We missed seeing you off to Bianliang, so we hurried over the instant word came to beg pardon."
Calling it disturbing yet barging right in anyway—still, since he needed a favor from Prefect Zhu, Shen Jianchen waved it smooth. "My fault for slipping out unannounced. No blame on Lin'an's officials."
Bowing deeper, Zhu Xiyan announced, "Out of devotion to Your Highness, Lin'an's officials prepared a welcome and wedding banquet tomorrow for Your Highness and Princess Consort Yi—please honor us with your presence!"
Disgusted by the lavish waste modeled on his imperial father's court, Shen Jianchen frowned. "The Bianliang wedding was lavish enough. Throwing another banquet burns the people's sweat and blood—cancel it."
Terrified, Zhu Xiyan and his aides dropped straight to their knees. "Because distance barred us from Bianliang, we wanted to make it up to Your Highness and began preparations the day you left! Not one copper comes from taxpayers—the Chen family is paying the entire bill!"
Understanding at once—Chen Manor buying peace after his wedding raid—Shen Jianchen nodded to keep the Chens from taking any anxiety out on Qianli Xun. "Then Princess Consort Yi and I will attend tomorrow. Rise."
"Thank you, Your Highness!"
"Everyone else step outside," Shen Jianchen ordered. "I need a private word with Prefect Zhu."
Alone with the bowing prefect, Shen Jianchen began, "Since taking post as Military Commissioner of Lin'an, I've stayed idle—feels like letting His Majesty down."
Panic spiked in Zhu Xiyan's chest: Prince Yi meddling in city governance?! One dig into the ledgers and I'm toast!
Spotting the prefect's sweat, Shen Jianchen knew Lin'an's books were rotten top to bottom—just like the whole Song court, beyond one man's repair. Better spend his energy helping ordinary citizens directly. "City administration stays yours, Prefect Zhu, and military posts don't need me hovering. I want hands-on work close to the common people. What post fits?"
Flooded with relief, Zhu Xiyan answered fast, "Your concern for the people humbles me, Your Highness! There is a post dealing straight with citizens, though far too lowly for a prince..."
"Name it."
"Judicial Inspector—rank eight-B, investigating and trying criminal cases among the populace. Far beneath Your Highness's station."
That clicked instant interest. "Rank eight-B sits within your authority to reassign. I'll take Judicial Inspector—move the current holder to another decent post, and from tomorrow I run Lin'an's Judicial Office."
Thrilled, Zhu Xiyan agreed on the spot. "I'll file it today! Since His Majesty sealed your title as Military Commissioner, I dare not alter your formal rank—we'll announce that Your Highness is temporarily acting as Judicial Inspector on His Majesty's behalf to inspect the people's welfare."
Irritated at dragging the foolish emperor into his civic work yet keeping his face neutral, Shen Jianchen nodded. "Fine. I report for duty after tomorrow's banquet."
Once the officials left, Bai Feng burst out, "Your Highness, haven't seen Kuqiao in ages—can I go visit her right now?"
"Go," Shen Jianchen said, then added low, "Ask Kuqiao how she's doing."
"Yes, Your Highness." Hurrying off, Bai Feng felt a tug of pity for Princess Jiahe—yet imagining being forced to marry someone else while loving Kuqiao, he understood his master's stubborn heart.
Knowing he would stay at the Judicial Office most days, Shen Jianchen went to explain in person before Mengrong spiraled.
Having woken from a nap, Qiao Mengrong stood surveying her cramped maiden courtyard with bitter eyes—married now, yet still parked in a side room! As Princess Consort Yi, Brother's main quarters belonged to her as their bridal chamber. Just as she stepped out to inspect it, Brother walked through her gate.
Throwing her arms around his waist, she pleaded, "Brother, I don't want this little yard anymore—I want to move into your quarters. We're married now!"
Unable to say yes or coldly refuse, Shen Jianchen sidestepped. "Is Matron Zou settled in?"
"In the yard next door," she murmured, clinging tight.
"Two things to tell you, Mengrong. First, Lin'an's officials are hosting a wedding banquet for us tomorrow—come with me."
"Of course!" Mengrong hugged tighter—a golden chance to rally Lin'an's noble wives for her revenge against Zhu Shuzhen!
"Second—starting tomorrow, I'm stepping in as acting Judicial Inspector and will stay at the yamen office most days, so I won't be home much..."
Her arms fell away as red misted her eyes. "Can't even stand the sight of me—hunting excuses to stay away?"
"Mengrong... our wedding came fast. Give me time to adjust, and maybe—"
"You still can't let her go! The tighter you cling to her, the deeper I hate her!"
Catching her own outburst before revealing her plots, she reigned her tears in fast. With the title of Princess Consort Yi, she could win Brother's heart and crush her enemy both. "Do whatever you like, Brother—I'll just move into the yamen with you!"
"The yamen quarters are bare and rough—unfit for you. I promise I'll come back once a week to see you."
Actually, having Brother away at the yamen kept him from spotting and blocking her revenge against Zhu Shuzhen—plenty of time to win him over afterward! "I'll listen to you, Brother."
Her gentle compliance pierced Shen Jianchen with fresh guilt. Folding her into a brief embrace, he murmured, "Don't blame me, Mengrong, and don't hate Youqi Jushi. She's married to Chen Haoyu—over for good. Blame this reborn Zhao Pu for carrying someone inside his heart. Once I clear her out, I'll try my best to accept you."
Resting against his chest, Mengrong seethed inside: Every time you shield her, I hate her ten times worse! She stole your heart so hard you have to "try" to accept your own wife!
"Grant me one wish, Brother," she whispered.
Stepping back, he asked, "What wish?"
"Let me redecorate your main quarters as our bridal chamber."
Since he would live at the yamen and visit weekly, why deny her? "Decorate it however you please."
At last a genuine smile touched her lips.
Leaving her courtyard, Shen Jianchen detoured up the wooden viewing platform overlooking the Divine Willow, watching the red ribbons flutter in the breeze and closing his eyes at the table to drift back through every memory shared with Qianli Xun.
Meanwhile, Qiao Mengrong summoned Matron Zou. "Come with me to tomorrow's banquet, Matron—and help me pick gifts for the officials' wives. Not too extravagant, not cheap, nice enough to win their loyalty."
"With your rank, any gift honors them," Matron Zou smiled. "Better yet, His Majesty gifted a chest of pigeon-egg pearls for your wedding—ordinary trinkets to Your Highness, priceless treasures to Lin'an wives!"
"Brilliant! Those pearls just gather dust with me."
"I'll have servants buy delicate brocade boxes in town and pack them individually for tomorrow."
Delighted, Qiao Mengrong congratulated herself for bringing Matron Zou along—she now had a master strategist running Youlin Retreat behind her.
#CH 247
#TITLE: First Day at the Silk Shop
Still strolling the petal-strewn garden with Wenxin, Qianli Xun paused as a Chen maid hurried up. "Eldest Miss, Second Young Madam—Guard Bai from Prince Yi's household is at the gate asking for Kuqiao."
Chatting behind with Yuegui, Kuqiao had missed the news of Prince Yi's return and gasped bright-eyed: "Miss...!"
Eager herself to pick up scraps of news about Prince Yi and Mengrong, Qianli Xun waved her off. "Go on—I don't need you here."
"Thank you, Miss!" Kuqiao sprinted away.
"Look at that girl—one mention of Guard Bai and her mistress vanishes from her head!" Wenxin teased.
"My feet are tired, Sister-in-law—let's go sit at Grandmother's and catch the storyteller." Not really tired, just craving a noisy crowd to drown out Shen Jianchen's name.
"Heard hiring the storyteller by the month was your brainstorm!" Wenxin laughed. "Now half the rich houses in Lin'an hire him on retainer—sprints from manor to manor earning ten times what he made at Goulan Wasi! Chen Manor started a whole city trend!"
"Guess I ought to charge him a commission!"
"Second that!"
Arriving at Old Madam Xia's courtyard just as the gavel cracked—with maids taking Laibao off to play—the sisters-in-law settled in. Listening to her own plot performed live drowned out every stray thought until the tale ended and family chatter resumed, where Qianli Xun noticed Ye Anya missing once again.
Finding an opening, she asked, "Second Aunt, where's First Sister-in-law?"
Madam Bao's smile died. "Never likes crowds—prefers hiding in her room."
Madam Cui smirked inside: Everyone knows Anya only hides when Haodong's left fresh bruises!
Old Madam Xia turned stern on Madam Bao. "You and Jiangshu lecture Haodong—hitting a wife brings zero honor! Leading the Chen estate starts with putting your own house in order, and that starts with cherishing your wife. A wife is a man's treasure vault! Keep your vault bruised, weeping, and terrified, and how do you expect big fortune to stick?"
Unconvinced yet obedient, Madam Bao murmured, "Yes, Mother. We'll talk to him tonight."
"Not your ears—his heart needs to hear it!"
A wife is a man's treasure vault—Qianli Xun marveled at the phrase, picturing Chen Jianglin hovering devoted around Yao Qingyan while Chen wealth still swelled nonstop. A wild fleeting thought flickered—what if Chen Haoyu treated her like that? She snorted at herself at once; brothel-hopping slime turning into a dream husband? No thanks!
Once Old Madam Xia tired and Wenxin headed home with Laibao, Qianli Xun returned alone to Suxin Thatched Hall, where Kuqiao sat whisking tea with a glowing face.
Sitting on the floor cushion beside the tea table, Qianli Xun tested the waters casual. "Saw Bai Feng? Put on weight or lost some?"
Seeing right through the detour, Kuqiao handed over a bowl of tea. "Bai Feng says Prince Yi looks the same—only difference is he's wed to the princess now."
Taking a sip, Qianli Xun arched a brow. "Asked about Bai Feng—why bring up Prince Yi?"
Keep pretending! Kuqiao thought.
"Gone all that time—didn't Bai Feng bring you a souvenir?"
Hesitating—Bai Feng had brought a gift for her, nothing from Prince Yi for Miss, though both were married now anyway—Kuqiao admitted, "Yes—a Bianliang woodblock print."
"Let's see!"
Fetching it from Yuening Room, Kuqiao handed over a crisp carved portrait catching her own likeness to the life.
"Thoughtful guy," Qianli Xun murmured, struck by quiet envy—Kuqiao could love open and proud while she and Shen Jianchen stayed locked behind separate wedding vows.
Suddenly Kuqiao dropped straight to her knees, sobbing. "Miss... waaah!"
"Just saw your sweetheart—what's with the tears?!"
"Heartbroken for you, Miss! Waaah!"
"Save the tears—I'm thriving! Get up and sit!"
Wiping her eyes, Kuqiao sat down. "Terrified your Lin Manor misery is repeating all over again!"
"Not a chance—I'm not who I was back then."
Gathering her nerve, Kuqiao spoke straight. "Let Prince Yi go, Miss! You're both married—stop holding onto him. Chen Manor is wonderful; I'm praying you and Young Master work out!"
Realization hit Qianli Xun: she was standing one against the world—Chen elders, Zhu family, Matron Wei, every maid down to Kuqiao all rooting for Chen Haoyu! Resentment flared: why did two days of decent behavior turn everybody into his fan club while she got pressured to hand herself to a man she didn't love?!
"Meddling busybody—stay out of my heart!"
"I'm just a maid, Miss, yet I care about you too much to stay quiet! Even setting everything else aside, think of Princess Jiahe—what wife wants another woman holding her husband inside her heart?"
That arrow hit dead center. Qianli Xun's face turned grave as she stood up. "Pack that peeing clay doll out of my sight. I won't touch it again."
Nodding, Kuqiao felt a stab of guilt for snuffing out her mistress's last tiny keepsake.
Meanwhile, Chen Haoyu had stepped down at the silk shop with Chen Haodong, greeted by Manager Qiu. Showing off his turf, Chen Haodong headed straight into the guest room for a big southwest merchant deal while tossing a smooth nod to Manager Qiu: "Take good care of Haoyu for Eldest Uncle!"
